source.title: Relative p-adic Hodge theory: Foundations
readSections: arXiv v5 (211 pp.): §0 Introduction and §§1–9 (pp. 3–203), read line by line with their proofs (checkpoint 1: §§0–3; checkpoint 2: §§4–7; checkpoint 3: §§8–9, by four readers in parallel — §§8.1–8.3, 8.4–8.6, 8.7–8.9 and 9 — whose drafts were merged and checked)
Appendix A of part II (arXiv 1602.06899v3), the authors’ errata for this paper

sourceVersions.note: PDF dated 2 May 2015, posted 9 May 2015 as the version to appear in Astérisque; all page and statement numbers refer to it. LaTeX source SHA-256 60a23edf57d786eda37cca317f533d567c54cb06250f1512d2e3405491e7377d.
Not obtained: the SMF text is paywalled and the eScholarship copy (escholarship.org/uc/item/8td3s4r6) returned HTTP 403, so findings are scoped to arXiv v5.
Part II, whose Appendix A records the authors’ errata for this paper.

summary: Kedlaya and Liu build relative p-adic Hodge theory on Witt vectors and nonarchimedean analytic geometry. They compare the Gel’fand spectra of Banach rings with Huber adic spectra, set up the perfectoid correspondence between perfect uniform Banach F_p-algebras and perfectoid algebras (compatible with rational localization and finite étale covers), and prove slope theory over relative Robba rings, including semicontinuity of the slope polygon and a slope filtration theorem. They relate ϕ-modules over relative Robba rings to vector bundles on relative Fargues–Fontaine curves and to étale Z_p- and Q_p-local systems on perfectoid and analytic spaces, with (pro-)étale cohomology. The extraction is complete: three checkpoints cover the introduction and chapters 1–9, 412 items after the independent review (26 library, 185 planned, 201 missing; the extraction had 409: 23, 171, 215). Chapters 1–3 give algebraic preliminaries, spectra of Banach rings and the perfectoid correspondence. Mathlib has much of the commutative algebra, the seminorm theory, perfect rings, Witt vectors of perfect rings, inverse perfection and Fontaine’s θ. The Huber-ring and adic-spectrum material is planned in the Tau Ceti AdicSpaces roadmap (layers 0–4); the Gel’fand spectrum in TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic TB.0; the perfectoid correspondence, tilting of adic spectra and almost purity in PerfectoidSpaces P1–P3, which name this paper as a source; henselian-pair and finite étale inputs in P5; Beauville–Laszlo patching in RelativeFarguesFontaine RF4. Missing from chapters 1–3 are some commutative algebra (Fitting ideals, descent of projectivity), the étale local systems and pro-étale site of a scheme (§1.4), the Gel’fand–adic comparison, affinoid systems, finite étale descent along rational coverings, glueing squares and Kiehl glueing for vector bundles on sheafy rings, the uniform-ring results of §2.8, Katz’s correspondence between lisse sheaves and ϕ-modules over a perfect ring, the Gauss norms on Witt vectors, the functoriality and descent statements of the perfectoid correspondence, and preperfectoid algebras. Chapter 4 reviews Kedlaya’s slope theory over the Robba ring and the extended Robba ring of a perfect analytic field, all planned in PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.0–RD.2. Chapter 5 builds the relative extended Robba rings of a perfect uniform Banach F_p-algebra and proves their sheaf and Kiehl-glueing properties, relative perfectoidness and finite étale functoriality; only the lifting of rational localizations and almost purity are planned (RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0:integral-Y, PerfectoidSpaces P0 and P3). Chapter 6 identifies ϕ-modules over these rings with ϕ-bundles and with vector bundles on Proj of the graded ring of Frobenius eigenvectors, planned in VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB1–VB2 and RelativeFarguesFontaine RF1 and RF3. Chapter 7 studies slopes in families: rank and degree, pure models, openness of the pure locus, semicontinuity and boundedness of the slope polygon, and the slope filtration where the polygon is constant; VB4 plans semicontinuity and the constant-polygon filtration for perfectoid bases. Chapter 8 globalizes to adic and perfectoid spaces: spectral and taut spaces, the real quotient, vector bundles on sheafy affinoids for the adic and finite étale topologies, perfectoid spaces and the global perfectoid correspondence (§§8.1–8.3); étale ℚ_p-local systems on preadic spaces and their correspondence with ϕ-modules over perfect rings, purity in families and ϕ-cohomology (§§8.4–8.6); and the relative Fargues–Fontaine curve FF_X, GAGA, ampleness and relative B-pairs (§§8.7–8.9). Most of §§8.1–8.3 and §8.7 is planned (DiamondsAndVStacks D0, AdicEtaleGeometry A1, AdicSpacesPartII R5, PerfectoidSpaces P2–P3, RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0–RF4, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0–VB2 and VB4); missing are the local-system side, the ampleness theory beyond positive twists and the relative B-pairs. Chapter 9 builds the pro-étale site of an arbitrary preadic space with its structure and period sheaves, identifies étale local systems with ϕ-modules, vector bundles on FF_X and B-pairs, compares pro-étale cohomology with ϕ- and B-pair cohomology, and recovers Fontaine's, Cherbonnier–Colmez's and Berger's equivalences over a p-adic field; the atlas plans the classical (ϕ, Γ) equivalences (PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology PG.1–PG.3) and the perfectoid, slope-zero case of the local-system comparison (VB4), not the general relative period sheaves. The missing items go as sources to the existing layers that should own them, in twenty-five routes; no Part II or new roadmap is needed. 144 mistakes are recorded (116 new, 28 in the authors’ errata); the independent review confirmed E1–E90 and added E91–E144. For chapters 1–7, 31 are new, among them a false Corollary 2.5.13 (it needs A^+ = A°, as the paper’s own Remark 2.4.9 shows), a failing step in Remark 2.3.15(e), a reversed inclusion in the proof of Proposition 2.4.24, a gap in the proof of Proposition 3.5.9, a citation of Scholze’s covering conjecture to the wrong paper in Remark 3.1.17, a false description of the φ^a-invariants of the extended Robba ring in Lemma 4.2.10 (they are W(L^{φ^a})[p^{−1}], which is Q_p for a = 2 and L the completed perfection of F_p((t))), and wrong exponents in the proof of Proposition 6.2.4. The other 22 are already in the authors’ errata in part II, among them the false equivalence in Definition 2.8.1 and the incomplete proofs of Propositions 3.6.11 and 3.6.19. For chapters 8–9, 31 are new, among them a false Theorem 8.5.8(b) (it needs a complete subring, as 8.5.3(b) and 8.5.6(b) have), a false Proposition 8.2.14 (the real quotient does not determine A⁺), Lemma 9.3.4 (W(Ō⁺) is only almost acyclic), a slope normalization error for L_X when a > 1 (Definition 8.8.18, Lemma 8.8.19), and Conjecture 8.8.20(b), false for sections with repeated zeros; six more are in the errata (Definition 8.1.6, Remark 8.1.7, Proposition 8.2.20, Theorem 8.3.5, Theorem 8.6.4, Proposition 9.2.6). The independent review (REV-PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15) found many chapter 2–3 items already planned as packet nodes of AdicSpacesPartII, AdicEtaleGeometry and PerfectoidSpaces, and three already in Tau Ceti (Henkel’s open mapping theorem, Spa and its spectrality); it moved the pro-étale site of a scheme and two scheme-cohomology inputs to SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2, rejected route 9 (its only item is planned at ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H1:henselian), and added among others three errors in stated results of §§2–3: Remark 2.3.9 (a uniform unit does not make A an algebra over F_p((z)) unless A is uniform), Remark 2.4.7 (ε < c is not enough), and Theorem 3.3.7(c) (it needs z̄₀ ∈ R^×, which the errata impose only from §3.6 on).

prerequisites.citation: K. S. Kedlaya, Nonarchimedean geometry of Witt vectors, Nagoya Math. J. 209 (2013), 111–165
prerequisites.why: [87]: the maps λ and μ between the Gel’fand spectra of a perfect ring R and of W(R) (Lemmas 4.1–4.2), which underlie the perfectoid correspondence (§3.3), the closedness of principal ideals generated by primitive elements (Theorem 5.11), and Banach-ring lemmas cited in §§2.2–2.3 (Gauss norms, Lemma 1.20). Bhatt–Scholze, Henkel, Buzzard–Verberkmoes, Mihara, Berkovich, Bosch–Güntzer–Remmert, Gabber–Ramero, Katz (p-adic properties of modular schemes and modular forms), Scholze and Scholze–Weinstein are already cited by the atlas.

prerequisites.citation: K. S. Kedlaya, Slope filtrations for relative Frobenius, Astérisque 319 (2008), 259–301
prerequisites.why: [kedlaya-relative] in the paper’s bibliography, cited fourteen times in chapters 4–7: the slope filtration and Dieudonné–Manin statements over the extended Robba ring (Proposition 1.2.7, Theorems 1.6.5 and 1.7.1), faithfully flat descent of φ-modules (§3, Proposition 3.2.2, Theorems 3.1.2–3.1.3, which Remark 4.3.6 corrects in Proposition 3.3.2), and the successive approximation of Proposition 2.5.8 used in Proposition 7.3.6. The atlas does not cite it.

prerequisites.citation: R. Rodriguez, Preperfectoid algebras, PhD thesis, University of California, San Diego, 2014
prerequisites.why: Source of Theorem 5.3.9, which the paper attributes to Rodriguez with its proof: ℰ̃_R, ℛ̃^{bd,r}_R and ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R are relatively perfectoid, so their adic Banach extensions are stably uniform and sheafy with the Tate sheaf and Kiehl glueing properties; the paper then deduces Kiehl glueing for the sheaf ℛ̃^{[s,r]} on Spa(R, R⁺) (Theorem 5.3.13). The atlas does not cite it. The eScholarship PDF returned HTTP 403 here, so the thesis itself was not read.

prerequisites.citation: A. J. de Jong, Étale fundamental groups of non-archimedean analytic spaces, Compositio Math. 97 (1995), no. 1–2, 89–118
prerequisites.why: [33]: the étale fundamental group of a non-archimedean analytic space, whose continuous representations give the étale ℚ_p-local systems of Definition 8.4.3 that are not isogeny ℤ_p-local systems (Remark 8.4.9, Example 8.5.17).

prerequisites.citation: L. Berger, Construction de (φ,Γ)-modules : représentations p-adiques et B-paires, Algebra Number Theory 2 (2008), no. 1, 91–120
prerequisites.why: [12]: B-pairs over a p-adic field and their equivalence with (φ,Γ)-modules over the Robba ring (Definition 9.5.7, Theorem 9.5.8), which §§8.9 and 9.3 generalize to relative B-pairs.

items.name: Finite projective modules: direct summands, finitely presented flat and pointwise free
items.statement: For a module M over a ring R, the following are equivalent: (a) M is finitely generated projective; (b) M is a direct summand of a finite free module; (c) M is finitely presented and pointwise free (M ⊗ R_p free for every maximal, equivalently every prime, ideal p); Let M be a module over a ring R. M is pointwise free if M ⊗_R R_p is free over R_p for every maximal (hence every prime) ideal p; M is locally free if there are f_1, …, f_n ∈ R generating the unit ideal with each M ⊗_R R[f_i^{−1}] free over R[f_i^{−1}]; M is projective if it is a direct summand of a free module. The following are equivalent [Bourbaki, AC II.5.2, Thm. 1]: (a) M is finitely generated and projective; (b) M is a direct summand of a finite free module; (c) M is finitely presented and pointwise free.

items.name: Finite projective modules via locally constant rank and Zariski-local freeness
items.statement: For M finitely generated over R, the following are equivalent to M being finite projective: (d) M is pointwise free of locally constant rank; (e) M is locally free, i.e. there are f_1, …, f_n generating the unit ideal with each M[f_i^{−1}] free. For R reduced, finitely generated of locally constant rank suffices.
items.locator: §1.1, Definition 1.1.2 (d)–(e) and the reduced case, pp. 11–12
items.note: Mathlib has the pieces for finitely presented M (rankAtStalk, Module.isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk, Module.FinitePresentation.exists_free_localizedModule_powers, Module.Free.away_of_finite_of_flat_of_rankAtStalk_constant) but not the equivalences for finitely generated M or the reduced case.

items.name: Fitting ideals detect finite projective modules of constant rank
items.statement: For M finitely presented, the Fitting ideals Fitt_i(M) are finitely generated, increasing, eventually equal to R, and commute with base change; M is finite projective of constant rank n iff Fitt_i(M) = 0 for i < n and Fitt_n(M) = R.
items.note: Neither library has Fitting ideals of modules.

items.name: Faithfully flat modules and their criterion by maximal ideals
items.statement: M is faithfully flat if it is flat and M ⊗_R N ≠ 0 for every nonzero R-module N; equivalently, injectivity is preserved on finite modules and M ⊗ N ≠ 0 for finite N ≠ 0. A flat ring map R → S is faithfully flat iff every maximal ideal of R is the contraction of a maximal ideal of S (Lemma 1.1.4).
items.note: Mathlib defines faithful flatness by m·M ≠ M for maximal m, which is the criterion with finite test modules; Lemma 1.1.4 is iff_flat_and_proper_ideal for M = S (mS ≠ S exactly when m is contracted from a maximal ideal of S).

items.name: Étale maps and the tensor category FÉt(R)
items.statement: A ring map is étale if it is of finite presentation and formally étale (EGA IV 17.3.1); A morphism of schemes is étale if it is locally of finite presentation and formally étale (EGA IV 17.3.1); a ring map is étale if the corresponding morphism of affine schemes is. FÉt(R) is the tensor category of finite étale R-algebras, with all R-algebra morphisms as morphisms; these morphisms are themselves finite étale. Every S ∈ FÉt(R) is finite, finitely presented and flat, hence finite projective, as an R-module. A faithfully finite étale R-algebra is a finite étale R-algebra that is faithfully flat over R, equivalently of positive rank everywhere (Lemma 1.1.4 and going-up). FÉt(R) is the category of finite étale R-algebras, with base change FÉt(R) → FÉt(S). Every S ∈ FÉt(R) is finite projective over R.
items.locator: §1.2, Definition 1.2.1 and the paragraph after it, pp. 12–13
items.note: Finite étale is written [Algebra.Etale R S] [Module.Finite R S]; projectivity combines flatness with finite presentation.

items.name: The trace-pairing criterion for finite étale algebras
items.statement: An R-algebra S that is finite projective as an R-module is finite étale over R iff the trace pairing S → Hom_R(S, R), x ↦ (y ↦ Tr_{S/R}(xy)), is an isomorphism. A faithfully finite étale algebra is one of positive rank everywhere.
items.note: Mathlib has the trace form over fields (traceForm_nondegenerate) but not the criterion over rings; the paper uses it pointwise in Lemma 3.6.20. Review (status changed from missing to planned): Planned by the packet node AdicSpacesPartII:R3/etale-iff-trace-pairing-perfect; the R3 stage text says 'Construct trace for finite locally free algebras …'. The 'faithfully finite étale' clause is a definition.

items.name: Morphisms out of a finite étale algebra are idempotents
items.statement: For U ∈ FÉt(R) there is an idempotent e_{U/R} ∈ U ⊗_R U mapping to 1 under multiplication and killing its kernel. For any R-algebra V, ψ ↦ e_ψ = (1 ⊗ ψ)(e_{U/R}) is a bijection from R-algebra maps U → V to idempotents e ∈ U ⊗_R V for which Γ(e) : V → e(U ⊗_R V), x ↦ e(1 ⊗ x), is an isomorphism.
items.note: Neither library has the diagonal idempotent of a finite étale algebra or the description of Hom sets by idempotents; Mathlib has FÉt(R) (CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale) but not its Galois-category structure. Partly planned (independent review): The diagonal idempotent (Def 1.2.2) is constructed in the packet node AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal, whose sources cite KL Definition 1.2.2. Lemma 1.2.3's bijection Hom_R(U, V) ↔ idempotents appears there only in geometric form ('every section of a finite étale morphism is an open and closed immersion'). Mark it as partially planned. The item stays missing because the rest is not planned.

items.name: Idempotents modulo an ideal in the Jacobson radical
items.statement: Let I be contained in the Jacobson radical of R. (a) Distinct idempotents of R are not congruent modulo I. (b) For any integral extension S of R, IS is contained in the Jacobson radical of S.
items.note: Mathlib lifts idempotents only along nil kernels (existsUnique_isIdempotentElem_eq_of_ker_isNilpotent). The proof of (b) has a sign slip: 'P(T−1)' should be 'P(T+1)' (finding E91).

items.name: Full faithfulness of base change on finite étale algebras
items.statement: (a) If R → R′ is such that an element of an invertible R-module M generating M ⊗ R′ generates M, and for every S ∈ FÉt(R) each idempotent of S ⊗_R R′ comes from a unique idempotent of S, then FÉt(R) → FÉt(R′) is rank-preserving and fully faithful. (b) If I lies in the Jacobson radical of R and idempotents of S/IS lift to S for every S ∈ FÉt(R), then FÉt(R) → FÉt(R/I) is rank-preserving and fully faithful.
items.note: P5 plans the finite étale approximation and full faithfulness arguments through Gabber–Ramero. Review: P5's text ('full faithfulness through graph approximation', for cofiltered limits of affinoid perfectoids, ECD 6.4) does not plan the abstract criterion of Prop 1.2.5. Prop 1.2.5 is used explicitly as a proof step of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-approximation: 'idempotents of B ⊗ A lift uniquely (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.2.4(a) and Proposition 1.2.5)'. That too is only a proof-step citation, so this is a weak 'planned' either way.

items.name: Henselian pairs: Greco's root criterion
items.statement: Let R be a ring and I an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical of R. Then (R, I) is henselian in the sense of Definition 1.2.6 if and only if every monic polynomial f = Σ_i f_i T^i ∈ R[T] with f_0 ∈ I and f_1 ∈ R^× has a root in I (Greco, Thm. 5.11); i.e. it suffices to check the factorization-lifting condition for ḡ = T.
items.note: Mathlib’s HenselianRing is the root-lifting form. The instance that I-adically complete pairs are henselian is IsAdicComplete.henselianRing (RingTheory/Henselian.lean, line 170), which the declaration index omits.

items.name: Henselian pairs: lifting coprime factorizations
items.statement: A pair (R, I) of a ring and an ideal is henselian if (a) I is contained in the Jacobson radical of R and (b) for every monic f ∈ R[T], every factorization f̄ = ḡ h̄ in (R/I)[T] with ḡ, h̄ monic and coprime lifts to a factorization f = gh in R[T]. If R is I-adically complete, (R, I) is henselian (Hensel's lemma). A local ring (R, m) is henselian if (R, m) is a henselian pair.
items.note: The equivalence with the root-lifting form is proved in Mathlib only for local rings (HenselianLocalRing.TFAE). Review (status changed from missing to planned): Planned by the packet node ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/henselian-pair-characterisations (Lean `HenselianRing.tfae`). It proves the equivalence of Mathlib's simple-root definition with KL's coprime-factorization definition (Stacks 15.11.1). Route 9, which sends item 11 to P5, is therefore redundant.

items.name: Finite étale algebras over a henselian pair (Gabber, Elkik)
items.statement: For a henselian pair (R, I), the base change functor FÉt(R) → FÉt(R/I) is a tensor equivalence.
items.note: P5 cites Gabber–Ramero 5.4.53 for exactly this input. Review: P5's GR 5.4.53 is the R[1/t] vs R̂[1/t] statement, not FÉt(R) ≃ FÉt(R/I). The H1:henselian node plans Gabber's affine proper base change ('for every n ≥ 0 the restriction map H^n(X_et, F) → H^n(Z_et, i^*F) is bijective'), from which Theorem 1.2.8 follows (n = 0, 1). Theorem 1.2.8 itself is used but not stated as a node (A1/finite-etale-approximation and A1/strict-localisation-analytic cite it as input).

items.name: Finite étale algebras over a direct limit
items.statement: For a direct system of rings R_i with limit R, base extension induces a tensor equivalence from the 2-colimit of the FÉt(R_i) to FÉt(R) (EGA IV 17.7.8 and 1.8.4.2).
items.note: Review: The packet nodes AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-algebras-filtered-colimit and PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-filtered-colimit-of-rings state Remark 1.2.9 exactly.

items.name: Cofibred categories, descent data and effective descent morphisms
items.statement: For a functor F : 𝓕 → C, a pushforward of E along f is a universal morphism over f with source E; F is cofibred if pushforwards exist and compose. For f : X → Y in C with pushouts, a descent datum along f is M over Y with an isomorphism π_1^*M ≅ π_2^*M satisfying the cocycle condition on Y ⊔_X Y ⊔_X Y; f is an effective descent morphism if every descent datum comes from X and morphisms descend bijectively.
items.note: Definition 1.3.1 misprints 'objects (resp. morphisms) in 𝒞' for 'in 𝓕' (finding E92).

items.name: Faithfully flat descent for modules
items.statement: Every faithfully flat ring map R → S is an effective descent morphism for modules (extension of scalars is comonadic), Zariski covers being a special case. Every faithfully flat ring map R → S is an effective descent morphism for the cofibred category of modules over rings (Theorem 1.3.4; SGA1 VIII 1.1), Zariski covers R → ⊕ R_i being a special case (Example 1.3.3). For f : R → S faithfully flat, an R-module U is finite iff U ⊗_R S is a finite S-module, and an R-algebra U is finite étale iff U ⊗_R S is a finite étale S-algebra (Theorem 1.3.5).
items.note: Mathlib states effective descent in comonadic form; the descent-datum form is a TODO in Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Descent.lean.

items.name: Finite projective modules descend along faithfully flat maps
items.statement: Along a faithfully flat ring map R → S, an R-module M is finite projective iff S ⊗_R M is finite projective over S.
items.note: Mathlib records this as missing (module docstring of RingTheory/Etale/Descent.lean: descent of projectivity, Stacks 058B); flatness and finiteness descend, but finite presentation of modules does not yet.

items.name: The Beauville–Laszlo theorem
items.statement: Let t ∈ R be a non-zero-divisor with R t-adically separated and R̂ the t-adic completion. (a) For flat M, 0 → M → M[t^{−1}] ⊕ (M ⊗ R̂) → M ⊗ R̂[t^{−1}] → 0 is exact. (b) Finite projective modules over R[t^{−1}] and R̂ with an isomorphism over R̂[t^{−1}] glue uniquely to a finite projective R-module; R → R[t^{−1}] ⊕ R̂ is an effective descent morphism for finite projective modules.
items.locator: §1.3, Proposition 1.3.6, pp. 16–17; new proof in Remark 2.7.9, p. 58

items.name: Glueing data over an exact square of rings
items.statement: For a commuting square R → R_1, R_2 → R_12 with 0 → R → R_1 ⊕ R_2 → R_12 → 0 exact, a glueing datum is (M_1, M_2, M_12) with isomorphisms M_i ⊗ R_12 ≅ M_12; its glued module is M = ker(M_1 ⊕ M_2 → M_12).
items.note: RF4 plans the algebraic patching argument for nonnoetherian rings.

items.name: Surjectivity lemma for finite glueing data
items.statement: For a finite glueing datum with M ⊗ R_1 → M_1 surjective: M_1 ⊕ M_2 → M_12 is surjective, M ⊗ R_2 → M_2 is surjective, and a finitely generated submodule M_0 ⊆ M already surjects onto M_1 and M_2.

items.name: Glueing of finite projective modules over an exact square
items.statement: If M ⊗ R_1 → M_1 is surjective for every finite projective glueing datum, then (a) M is finitely presented and M ⊗ R_i ≅ M_i, and (b) if moreover the image of Spec(R_1 ⊕ R_2) → Spec(R) contains Maxspec(R), M is finite projective.
items.note: A notational slip in the proof (finding E1).

items.name: Glueing of finite étale algebras over an exact square
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 1.3.9(b), FÉt(R) → FÉt(R_1) ×_{FÉt(R_12)} FÉt(R_2) is an equivalence.

items.name: Étale Z_p-, isogeny Z_p- and Q_p-local systems on a scheme
items.statement: On the small étale site of X, a lisse sheaf of Z/p^n-modules is a sheaf of flat Z/p^n-modules represented by a finite étale X-scheme; a Z_p-local system is an inverse system (T_n) of such with T_{n+1}/p^n ≅ T_n; isogeny Z_p-local systems form its isogeny category; a Q_p-local system is a descent datum in isogeny Z_p-local systems for the étale topology. Over X_fét the Z_p- and isogeny categories are the same, the Q_p-category in general not.

items.name: Local systems and representations of the étale fundamental group
items.statement: For X connected with geometric point x, Z_p-local systems are equivalent to continuous representations of π_1^ét(X, x) on finite free Z_p-modules, and isogeny Z_p-local systems to continuous representations on finite-dimensional Q_p-vector spaces; a tensor equivalence FÉt(A) ≅ FÉt(B) induces tensor equivalences Z_p-Loc(Spec A) ≅ Z_p-Loc(Spec B) and Z_p-ILoc(Spec A) ≅ Z_p-ILoc(Spec B), but is not by itself sufficient to give Q_p-Loc(Spec A) ≅ Q_p-Loc(Spec B) (an isomorphism of étale topoi would suffice).

items.name: Q_p-local systems need not come from isogeny Z_p-local systems
items.statement: The natural functor Z_p-ILoc(X) → Q_p-Loc(X) is fully faithful but not always essentially surjective. Example (1.4.5): for X two copies of P^1_k (k any field) glued along {0, ∞}, glueing the trivial rank-one local systems on X − {0} and X − {∞} by the identity on one copy of P^1_k − {0, ∞} and multiplication by p on the other gives a rank-one Q_p-local system V that is not an isogeny Z_p-local system (the corresponding character of π_1^ét would have image containing p^Z, hence noncompact). Example (1.4.6): X is a degree-2 finite étale cover of the irreducible, non-normal nodal curve Y (P^1_k with 0 and ∞ glued), and V ⊕ τ^*V descends to a rank-two Q_p-local system on Y (τ the deck involution). Remark 1.4.9: for X normal and noetherian, Z_p-ILoc(X) → Q_p-Loc(X) is an equivalence. carry a rank-one Q_p-local system (identity on one branch, multiplication by p on the other) that is not an isogeny Z_p-local system; descending V ⊕ τ^*V along the degree-2 étale cover gives an irreducible (non-normal) example. For X normal and noetherian, Z_p-ILoc(X) → Q_p-Loc(X) is an equivalence.

items.name: The lattice schemes L_m(T)
items.statement: For a Z_p-local system T on X and m ≥ 0, the functor of pairs (T′, ι) with ι : T_Y ⊗ Q_p ≅ T′ ⊗ Q_p and p^mι, p^mι^{−1} integral is represented by a finite étale X-scheme L_m(T); it carries a finite étale inclusion scheme I_m(T), a sum-of-lattices operation, and descent along faithfully finite étale covers.

items.name: Descent of isogeny Z_p-local systems along finite étale covers
items.statement: Every faithfully finite étale ring map R → R′ is an effective descent morphism for isogeny Z_p-local systems.
items.note: Notational slips in the proof (finding E2; also 'identity morphism on T′' for T′_i and 'descent datum from V' for V′, finding E93). The final step's reduction to 'R and R′ local' cannot be arranged (R′ finite étale over a local R is only semilocal, e.g. R′ = R × R); it works with R local and R′ viewed as a finite π_1(Spec R)-set (finding E94).

items.name: Weakly étale morphisms and the pro-étale site of a scheme
items.statement: f : Y → X is weakly étale if f and its diagonal are flat (e.g. ind-étale algebras). X_proét is the site of weakly étale X-schemes with fpqc coverings; U ↦ Map_cont(U, T) is a sheaf (the constant sheaf F_T), and locally constant sheaves are those locally of this form.
items.note: Review (status changed from missing to planned): SF.2 owns the pro-étale site of schemes. It does not name weakly étale morphisms or the constant sheaves F_T explicitly. Item 28 (Bhatt–Scholze local systems as locally free F_{Z_p}-modules) is not planned by SF.2's text, so keep 28 missing. The reviewer's lead is thus half confirmed.

items.name: Local systems as locally free sheaves on the pro-étale site (Bhatt–Scholze)
items.statement: For any scheme X, Z_p-Loc(X) (resp. Q_p-Loc(X)) is equivalent to the category of locally free F_{Z_p}-modules (resp. F_{Q_p}-modules) of finite rank on X_proét.
items.note: Bhatt–Scholze, The pro-étale topology for schemes, §6.8.

items.name: Local systems with coefficients in a finite extension
items.statement: For F finite over Q_p one defines o_F-, isogeny o_F- and F-local systems as the Q_p-objects with an o_F-action; for F = Q_{p^d} unramified these are Z_{p^d}-Loc(X), Z_{p^d}-ILoc(X), Q_{p^d}-Loc(X).

items.name: Semilinear ϕ-actions and ϕ-cohomology
items.statement: For a ring S with endomorphism ϕ, a semilinear ϕ-action on an S-module M is an isomorphism ϕ^*M ≅ M. H^0_ϕ(M) = ker(ϕ − 1), H^1_ϕ(M) = coker(ϕ − 1), H^i_ϕ = 0 for i ≥ 2; these are the Ext groups Ext^i(S, M) over the twisted polynomial ring S{ϕ}, computed by 0 → S{ϕ} → S{ϕ} → S → 0. For a ϕ^d-action, H^i_{ϕ^d}(M) = H^i_ϕ(M ⊕ ϕ^*M ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ (ϕ^{d−1})^*M); a finite projective M has a dual ϕ-module.
items.note: The ring S in Remark 1.5.6 is misprinted as R (finding E4). Weakly planned: VB0 (isocrystals over a field) and PG.0 (étale φ-modules over cyclotomic rings) plan semilinear φ-structures only in special rings. No stage or packet node plans φ-cohomology H^i_φ as Ext over S{φ}; the closest is PG.3's Herr complex for (φ, Γ)-modules. In Definition 1.5.4, H^i_ϕ(M) = Ext^i_{S{ϕ}}(S, M) is computed by applying Hom_{S{ϕ}}(−, M) to the resolution, not by tensoring M over S with it (finding E95).

items.name: Finitely generated ϕ-modules are quotients of free ϕ-modules
items.statement: If M is a finitely generated S-module with a semilinear ϕ-action, there is a finite free S-module F with a semilinear ϕ-action and a ϕ-equivariant surjection F → M; if M is finite projective, there is a finite projective ϕ-module N with M ⊕ N free.
items.note: The block-matrix proof (det D = 1) was checked; its “bottom left block” should read “top left block” (finding E3, corrected in part II).

items.name: Nonarchimedean seminorms on abelian groups, domination and equivalence
items.statement: A (nonarchimedean) seminorm on G is α : G → [0, ∞) with α(g − h) ≤ max{α(g), α(h)} and α(0) = 0; a norm if α(g) = 0 only for g = 0. α dominates α′ if α′ ≤ cα; mutual domination is equivalence.
items.note: Domination and equivalence are the inequalities themselves; Mathlib has no named relation for them.

items.name: Bounded, isometric and submetric homomorphisms
items.statement: For ϕ : G → H with seminorms α, β: ϕ is bounded if β∘ϕ ≤ cα for some c, isometric if β∘ϕ = α, and submetric if β∘ϕ ≤ α.

items.name: Strict and optimal homomorphisms of seminormed groups
items.statement: With the quotient seminorm ᾱ on image(ϕ), ϕ is strict if ᾱ and β are equivalent there, almost optimal if they coincide, and optimal if moreover lifts of minimal norm exist. Compositions of strict maps are strict when the first is surjective or the second injective.
items.note: Mathlib has strictness only topologically (Topology.IsStrictMap) and quotient maps of normed groups (NormedAddGroupHom.IsQuotient). The item follows the intended definition of optimal (almost optimal plus minimal lifts); the printed definition omits "almost optimal" (finding E96).

items.name: Separated completion of a seminormed group
items.statement: The separated completion Ĝ is the quotient of the Cauchy sequences by the kernel of lim α(g_i); G → Ĝ is isometric, and injective iff α is a norm.
items.note: Mathlib’s completion of a seminormed group is normed; the map is isometric (norm_coe) and injective for a norm (coe_injective, T0).

items.name: Submultiplicative, power-multiplicative and multiplicative seminorms
items.statement: On a ring: submultiplicative α(gh) ≤ α(g)α(h); power-multiplicative in addition α(g²) = α(g)²; multiplicative in addition α(1) = 1 and α(gh) = α(g)α(h). The trivial norm is power-multiplicative iff A is reduced and multiplicative iff A is a domain; a submultiplicative α dominates a power-multiplicative α′ iff α ≥ α′ pointwise.
items.note: Mathlib’s ring seminorms need not be nonarchimedean (IsNonarchimedean is separate). The statements about the trivial norm in Example 2.1.6 are immediate.

items.name: The subring o_A, the ideal m_A and κ_A
items.statement: For a submultiplicative seminorm with α(1) ≤ 1: o_A = {α ≤ 1} is a ring, m_A = {α < 1} an ideal and κ_A = o_A/m_A; for a field with a multiplicative norm these are the valuation ring, its maximal ideal and residue field. Products of power-multiplicative seminorms give power-multiplicative seminorms on the bounded part.
items.note: Mathlib has the valuation ring and residue field of a valued field, but not the unit-ball subring of a seminormed ring or the bounded part of a product.

items.name: The spectral seminorm
items.statement: For a submultiplicative α on A, α_sp(a) = lim_{s→∞} α(a^s)^{1/s} exists (Fekete) and is power-multiplicative; equivalent seminorms give the same α_sp.
items.note: Mathlib’s smoothing seminorm is KL’s α_sp; equality for equivalent seminorms follows from eq_seminorms. Mathlib’s smoothing seminorm is KL’s α_sp when α(1) ≤ 1: tendsto_smoothingFun_of_map_one_le_one and smoothingSeminorm assume μ 1 ≤ 1, while KL allow α(1) > 1 (Remark 2.1.11) and reduce to α(1) ≤ 1 via the operator seminorm, which Mathlib lacks. Equality for equivalent seminorms: apply eq_seminorms to the two smoothings (both power-multiplicative and mutually bounded).

items.name: Product seminorm and completed tensor product
items.statement: For bounded A → B, A → C, the product seminorm on B ⊗_A C sends f to the infimum over presentations f = Σ b_i ⊗ c_i of max β(b_i)γ(c_i); B ⊗̂_A C is the separated completion. Any submultiplicative α is equivalent to its operator seminorm α′(a) = inf{c : α(ab) ≤ cα(b)}, which satisfies α′(1) ≤ 1.
items.note: A0/R0 plan completed tensor products of Huber pairs.

items.name: Analytic fields, Banach rings and Banach algebras
items.statement: An analytic field is a field complete for a nontrivial multiplicative nonarchimedean norm; finite extensions carry a unique extension. A Banach ring is a commutative ring complete for a submultiplicative norm (the zero ring allowed); a Banach algebra over R is a Banach ring S with a bounded R → S. From §2.4 on every Banach ring is assumed to contain a topologically nilpotent unit.
items.note: There is no bundled Banach ring: it is written [NormedRing A] [CompleteSpace A] [IsUltrametricDist A]. The standing assumption of a topologically nilpotent unit from §2.4 on is a convention. Review: NormedAlgebra 𝕜 𝕜' requires 𝕜 to be a NormedField and ‖c • x‖ ≤ ‖c‖‖x‖. That is a stronger hypothesis than KL's 'Banach algebra over a Banach ring R' (R need not be a field, and the structure map need only be bounded). The right library notion is boundedness of algebraMap: RingHom.IsBounded (Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Basic.lean:504, ∃ C > 0, ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C‖x‖).

items.name: Closures of proper ideals in Banach rings
items.statement: In a Banach ring the closure of a proper ideal is proper; maximal ideals are closed.

items.name: Henselian pairs from direct limits of Banach rings
items.statement: For a direct system of Banach rings and submetric maps with limit A and infimum seminorm α: (a) (A, ker α) is henselian; (b) (o_A, m_A) is henselian. In particular (o_A, m_A) is henselian for every Banach ring A.
items.locator: §2.2, Lemma 2.2.3 and the sentence before it, p. 28
items.note: The printed proof of (a) does not show that the Newton limit lies in ker(α), which the criterion of Remark 1.2.7 requires, nor that the iterates live in one A_i; both are repaired by running Newton in a single A_j with |f_0|_j small and using uniqueness of small roots in later A_k (finding E98). Partly planned (independent review): Partial. The packet node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions proves (b) that filtered colimits of henselian pairs are henselian and (c) that (A°, A°°) and (A₀, ϖA₀) are henselian for complete (or colimits of) Tate rings; for a Tate norm α_d these are KL's (o_A, m_A). AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/henselian-pairs-filtered-colimit repeats (b). KL's general Banach-ring statement (no topologically nilpotent unit, infimum seminorm) is not covered. The item stays missing because the rest is not planned.

items.name: Finite étale algebras over a completion
items.statement: With notation as in Lemma 2.2.3: (a) FÉt(A) → FÉt(Â) is rank-preserving and fully faithful; (b) if α is multiplicative and K = A/ker α is a field, FÉt(A) → FÉt(K̂) is an equivalence.
items.note: The idempotent-lifting iteration x ↦ 3x² − 2x³ was checked: the identities x_{l+1}² − x_{l+1} = 4(x_l² − x_l)³ − 3(x_l² − x_l)² and x_{l+1} − x_l = (x_l² − x_l)(1 − 2x_l) hold and β_j(x_l² − x_l) ≤ c^{−1}ε^{l+1} follows. But the printed bound β(y − x) ≤ c^{−1}ε max{β(x), 1} does not follow (one gets ε max{β(x), 1}); choosing ε with cε max{β(e), 1} < 1 repairs it (finding E99). Partly planned (independent review): Partial. (a) For topologically henselian Tate rings, FÉt(A) ≃ FÉt(Â) is PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation (b). AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-approximation's proof steps use KL Lemma 2.2.4(a) and Prop 1.2.5 explicitly. (b), the field case K̂, is not stated by any node. The item stays missing because the rest is not planned.

items.name: Uniqueness of power-multiplicative extensions to finite extensions
items.statement: For K an analytic field and L/K finite, the unique multiplicative extension of the norm of K is also the unique power-multiplicative extension.

items.name: Canonical norms on finite modules over a Banach ring
items.statement: (a) For a finite R-module M, the quotient seminorms from surjections R^n → M are all equivalent. (b) An additive R-linear map from a finite R-module to a finite S-module (R → S bounded) is bounded for these seminorms.
items.note: Neither library has norms on finite modules over a normed ring; Tau Ceti’s TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isModuleTopology is the topological analogue over Tate rings. Partly planned (independent review): The topological form over complete Tate rings is planned by AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/natural-topology-strict-exactness (a), whose proof cites 'the argument of KL15 Lemma 2.2.6'. Much is already library: Mathlib moduleTopology plus IsModuleTopology.continuous_of_linearMap, and tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isModuleTopology. The norm-level statement over an arbitrary Banach ring (§2.2, before the standing Tate convention) is not planned. The item stays missing because the rest is not planned.

items.name: Banach modules and finite Banach modules
items.statement: A Banach module over R is an R-module complete for a norm with |rv| ≤ c|r||v|; it is finite if it admits a strict surjection R^n → M (so its norm class is determined by the module). A finite R-module is a finite Banach module iff it is separated and complete for its canonical seminorm.
items.note: Review: Layer 0 never defines Banach modules. The packet node AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-banach-module does ('A Banach A-module is … (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.2.7)'). Also partly library: tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isModuleTopology (a finite complete metrisable module over a Tate ring carries the module topology) and tauceti:TauCeti.completeSpace_moduleTopology.

items.name: The open mapping theorem for Banach modules
items.statement: If R is a Banach ring with a topologically nilpotent unit, every bounded surjective homomorphism of Banach R-modules is open and strict.
items.note: Henkel; Layer 0 §0.6 plans it with Henkel’s hypotheses. Review (status changed from planned to library): Henkel's open mapping theorem is in Tau Ceti at the pin. KL's hypothesis (R has a topologically nilpotent unit z) gives HasZeroSequenceOfUnits R (u_n = z^n). Banach R-modules are complete, metrisable (countably generated nhds of 0) and nonarchimedean, the target is Baire, and |rv| <= c|r||v| gives continuity of a -> a•x at 0. The conclusion is openness plus the quotient topology, which for normed groups is KL's strictness. Keep Layer 0 §0.6 as the owning stage in the note.

items.name: Completed tensor products over an analytic field
items.statement: For Banach modules V, W, X over an analytic field K: (a) V ⊗_K W → V ⊗̂_K W is injective; (b) ker(f) ⊗̂_K X ≅ ker(f ⊗̂ X) for bounded f : V → W; (c) if f is strict, so is f ⊗̂ X.
items.note: Proved by reduction to separable modules with Schauder bases. Review (status changed from missing to planned): The packet node AdicSpacesPartII:R0/banach-completed-tensor-field-exactness is titled '(Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.2.9)'. It proves (b) and (c) for X of countable type and records that deviation; PerfectoidSpaces:P4/completed-tensor-over-analytic-field-kernel cites KL I Lemma 2.2.9. Route 5 should not re-plan it.

items.name: Noetherian Banach rings
items.statement: For a Banach ring R with a topologically nilpotent unit the following are equivalent: R is noetherian; every ideal of R is closed; finite Banach R-modules are the same as finite R-modules.

items.name: Banach structures on finite projective modules
items.statement: For a finite projective R-module P with P ⊕ Q ≅ R^n, the subspace and quotient norms from R^n are equivalent, make P a finite Banach module, and are independent of Q and the presentation; this defines a fully faithful section of the forgetful functor on finite projective modules. Generators e_1, …, e_n of P can be perturbed: e′_i with |e′_i − e_i| < c still generate.
items.note: Partly planned (independent review): Topological form over complete Tate rings. Lemma 2.2.12: R0/completed-tensor-banach-module (e) makes a finite projective module 'a finite Banach module, Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.2.12', and A3/natural-topology-strict-exactness (e) proves it complete; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra (i) proves that the subspace and quotient topologies agree for B ⊕ Q ≅ Aⁿ. Lemma 2.2.13 (perturbing generators) is R3/surjection-small-perturbation. The item stays missing because the rest is not planned.

items.name: Finite étale algebras as finite Banach algebras
items.statement: For B ∈ FÉt(A), the norm of Lemma 2.2.12 makes multiplication bounded, so an equivalent submultiplicative norm makes B a finite Banach A-algebra; for an adic Banach ring, B^+ is the integral closure of A^+ in B.
items.note: A1 plans the topology and plus ring on a finite étale algebra.

items.name: Tate algebras, affinoid homomorphisms and strongly noetherian Banach rings
items.statement: A{T_1/r_1, …, T_n/r_n} = {Σ a_I T^I : |a_I|r^I → 0} with the Gauss norm (submultiplicative, power-multiplicative or multiplicative with that of A); A → B is affinoid if it factors through a strict surjection A{T_1, …, T_n} → B; A is strongly noetherian if all A{T_1, …, T_n} are noetherian.

items.name: The Gel’fand spectrum M(A)
items.statement: M(A) is the set of multiplicative seminorms on A bounded by the norm, topologized as a closed subspace of ∏_a [0, |a|], hence compact; bounded maps induce continuous maps; M(Â) ≅ M(A).

items.name: Berkovich: the spectrum of a nonzero Banach ring is nonempty
items.statement: For A ≠ 0, M(A) ≠ ∅.

items.name: Ideals, the unit ideal and units via the spectrum
items.statement: Every proper ideal I has some α ∈ M(A) vanishing on I; f_1, …, f_n generate the unit ideal iff for every α some α(f_i) > 0; f is a unit iff α(f) > 0 for all α ∈ M(A).

items.name: Residue fields H(α) and the Gel’fand transform
items.statement: For α ∈ M(A), p_α = α^{−1}(0) is prime and H(α) is the completion of Frac(A/p_α); the Gel’fand transform A → ∏_α H(α) is bounded, and every maximal ideal is some p_α.

items.name: Uniform units, topologically nilpotent units and trivial spectra
items.statement: For a Banach ring A consider: (a) A is a Banach algebra over an analytic field; (b) A has a uniform unit z (topologically nilpotent with |z|_sp|z^{−1}|_sp = 1, so α(z) = |z|_sp for all α); (c) A has a topologically nilpotent unit; (d) A is free of trivial spectrum. Then (a) ⇒ (b) ⇒ (c) ⇒ (d). In characteristic p, (b) ⇒ (a) when A is uniform (its norm is equivalent to the spectral seminorm): a uniform unit z then makes A a Banach algebra over F_p((z)) with |z| = |z|_sp. (The paper asserts (a) ⇔ (b) for every A of characteristic p; that is false without uniformity, see finding E101.) (b) ⇏ (a) outside characteristic p, and (c) ⇏ (b) (k((z_1)) ⊕ k((z_2)) with the supremum norm, |z_i| = e^{−c_i}, c_1, c_2 linearly independent over Q). Condition (d) holds iff m_A generates the unit ideal.

items.name: Berkovich: the spectral seminorm is the supremum over the spectrum
items.statement: The restriction of the supremum norm on ∏_{α∈M(A)} H(α) along the Gel’fand transform is the spectral seminorm of A; the supremum is attained (maximum modulus principle).

items.name: Surjectivity and fibre products via the spectrum
items.statement: A map M → N of A-modules with N finite is surjective iff it is surjective after ⊗ H(α) for all α ∈ M(A); M(B ⊗̂_A C) → M(B) ×_{M(A)} M(C) is surjective; for B faithfully finite étale over A, M(B) → M(A) is surjective (and open, Lemma 2.4.17(c)).

items.name: Closed and quotient maps from quasicompact to Hausdorff spaces
items.statement: A continuous map from a quasicompact space to a Hausdorff space is closed, so a continuous surjection (resp. bijection) between such spaces is a quotient map (resp. a homeomorphism).

items.name: Inverse limits of compact Hausdorff spaces: nonemptiness, covers and disconnections
items.statement: An inverse limit X of nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces X_i is nonempty and compact; a closed subset of X_i has empty preimage in X iff it has empty preimage in some X_j; a finite open covering of X is refined by the pullback of one of some X_i; and every disconnection of X is pulled back from a disconnection of some X_j.
items.note: Mathlib has the nonemptiness (TopCat.nonempty_limitCone_of_compact_t2_cofiltered_system), the basis of the limit topology (TopCat.isTopologicalBasis_cofiltered_limit) and the clopen statement for profinite limits only (Profinite.exists_isClopen_of_cofiltered). The argument for (e) needs the stage chosen large enough (finding E5).

items.name: Adic Banach rings
items.statement: An adic Banach ring (A, A^+) is a Banach ring A with a topologically nilpotent unit and an open, integrally closed subring A^+ ⊆ A°; morphisms are bounded maps with ϕ(A^+) ⊆ B^+; coproducts are (B ⊗̂_A C, completion of the integral closure of the image of B^+ ⊗ C^+).

items.name: Semivaluations, continuity and the adic spectrum
items.statement: A semivaluation v : A → Γ ∪ {0} satisfies v(a − b) ≤ max, v(ab) = v(a)v(b), v(0) = 0, v(1) = 1; Spv(A) is the set of equivalence classes; v is continuous if every nonzero γ in its value group bounds v near 0. Spa(A, A^+) is the set of continuous semivaluations bounded by 1 on A^+, with A^+ = {x : v(x) ≤ 1 for all v}, topologized by the sets {v(a) ≤ v(b) ≠ 0}; rational subspaces are {v(f_i) ≤ v(g) ≠ 0} with the f_i generating the unit ideal.
items.note: A misprint in the subbasic sets (finding E6). Review (status changed from planned to library): Spv (valuative relations, i.e. equivalence classes of valuations) with basic opens {v(f) <= v(s) != 0}, continuity, Spa as continuous points sub-unit on A+, A+ = {x : v(x) <= 1 for all v in Spa} (Wedhorn 7.52(1), for open integrally closed A+ in a Huber ring) and rational subsets are all at the pin. Tau Ceti's rational subsets ask T·A open; over a Tate ring this is T generating the unit ideal (isOpen_iff_eq_top), which is KL's condition. The misprint E6 is in KL's subbasis, not in the library.

items.name: Tate f-adic rings versus Banach rings
items.statement: For a Tate f-adic ring A (Huber) with ring of definition A_0 and topologically nilpotent unit z, and any c ∈ (0,1), α(x) = inf{c^n : n ∈ ℤ, z^{−n}x ∈ A_0} makes A a Banach ring; Banach rings containing a topologically nilpotent unit and Tate f-adic rings form equivalent categories once continuous (not necessarily bounded) morphisms of Banach rings are allowed. For z a topologically nilpotent unit of A, a semivaluation v on A bounded by 1 on A^+ is continuous iff for every x ∈ A with v(x) ≠ 0 there is n ∈ ℤ with v(z^n) < v(x). (The remark's further claim, that over an analytic field K continuity is equivalent to the restriction to K being equivalent to the norm, is false as stated — only 'continuous ⇒ restriction equivalent to the norm' holds; see finding E104. The consequence drawn from it, that continuous morphisms of Banach algebras over K are bounded, is true.)
items.note: Review: The packet node AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm constructs α_d(x) = inf{rⁿ : ϖ⁻ⁿx ∈ A₀} '(Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.4.4)'. The Layer 0/1 texts do not mention norms.

items.name: Huber: adic spectra are quasicompact with a basis of rational subspaces
items.statement: Spa(A, A^+) is quasicompact, and the rational subspaces form a basis of quasicompact open subsets.
items.note: Review (status changed from planned to library): Wedhorn 7.35 is proved: Spa(A, A+) is spectral (hence quasicompact) for every Huber ring and every subring A+, with a global instance. The rational subsets form a basis of quasicompact opens. The hypotheses are weaker than KL's (Huber ring rather than adic Banach ring, any A+).

items.name: Comparison maps between the Gel’fand and adic spectra
items.statement: There is a natural map M(A) → Spa(A, A^+) sending α to its class as a semivaluation; it is not continuous. If A contains a uniform unit z, then v ↦ α(v), α(v)(x) = inf{|z|_sp^{r/s} : r ∈ ℤ, s ∈ ℤ_{>0}, v(z^r) > v(x^s)}, is a map Spa(A, A^+) → M(A) with M(A) → Spa(A, A^+) → M(A) the identity; hence (with a uniform unit) M(A) → Spa(A, A^+) is injective, Spa(A, A^+) ≠ ∅ when A ≠ 0, the retraction is continuous and a quotient map exhibiting M(A) as the maximal Hausdorff quotient of Spa(A, A^+), disconnections of the two spaces correspond, the image of a rational subspace U in M(A) is U ∩ M(A), and M(A) is dense in Spa(A, A^+). Spa(A, A^+) → M(A), a quotient map exhibiting M(A) as the maximal Hausdorff quotient; disconnections of the two spaces correspond, and M(A) is dense in Spa(A, A^+).
items.note: Partly planned (independent review): TB.0 plans the comparison with the quotient topology for strictly affinoid algebras. The TB packet lists the adic comparison as remaining TB.0 work: gap TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic/adic-comparison, 'prove the actual normalized rank-one map, maximal-generization uniqueness, continuity and quotient topology under precise plus-ring hypotheses', neededBy TB.0. D5 plans the maximal-Hausdorff quotient functor. KL's generality (any Banach ring with a uniform unit) goes beyond TB.0's strictly affinoid scope, so route 4 remains useful as a source for the general case. The item stays missing because the rest is not planned. Remark 2.4.4 has two further problems: its norm needs z ∈ A0 (finding E144), and its continuity criterion over an analytic field holds only in one direction (finding E104).

items.name: Perturbing the parameters of a rational subspace
items.statement: Assume A contains a uniform unit (so that the projection Spa(A, A^+) → M(A) of Definition 2.4.6 exists). For a rational subspace U = {v : v(f_i) ≤ v(g) ≠ 0} with f_1, …, f_n, g generating the unit ideal, c = inf{α(g) : α ∈ Ū} > 0, where Ū is the (compact) image of U in M(A), and d = inf{max(α(f_1), …, α(f_n), α(g)) : α ∈ M(A)} > 0. For 0 < ε < min(c, d), any f′_1, …, f′_n, g′ ∈ A with |f′_i − f_i| < ε and |g′ − g| < ε generate the unit ideal and U = {v ∈ Spa(A, A^+) : v(f′_i) ≤ v(g′) (i = 1, …, n)}. (The paper requires only ε < c, which is not enough: see finding E103.)
items.note: The qualitative version (some neighbourhood of 0) is library: tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_mem_nhds_forall_rationalSubset_eq_of_sub_mem (over any Huber ring). KL's explicit bound c = inf over the image in M(A) is not planned. AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/affinoid-system-approximation uses Remark 2.4.7 as input.

items.name: Rational subspaces of M(A) and encircling
items.statement: A rational subspace of M(A) is its intersection with a rational subspace of Spa(A, A^+), {α(f_i) ≤ α(g)}; these are closed, and those that are neighbourhoods of α (encircle α) form a neighbourhood basis. Rational subspaces of Spa are not determined by their trace on M(A) in general, and Berkovich also allows radii p_i.

items.name: Adic fields and residue fields of points of Spa
items.statement: An adic field is (K, K^+) with K analytic and K^+ a valuation ring; for v ∈ Spa(A, A^+), (H(v), H(v)^+) is the adic field of the completed residue field with the valuation ring of v, and (A, A^+) → (H(v), H(v)^+) sends the unique closed point of Spa(H(v), H(v)^+) (the point given by H(v)^+) to v.
items.note: Corrected: the paper says “generic point” (finding E7, corrected in part II). Weak citation: Layer 1 and Layer 3 plan residue fields of stalks (Layer 3.3 'the valuation therefore factors through the residue field'), not completed residue fields H(v) or adic fields. Tau Ceti has only the uncompleted residue-field valuation (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.residueFieldValuation). PerfectoidSpaces:P2 plans 'completed residue fields and their plus rings' only for perfectoid spaces.

items.name: Affinoid subdomains and localizations
items.statement: A quasicompact open U ⊆ Spa(A, A^+) is an affinoid subdomain if some affinoid (A, A^+) → (B, B^+) is initial among maps whose spectrum lands in U; rational subspaces are affinoid subdomains (rational localizations), and completed tensor products of localizations correspond to intersections.
items.note: Only the rational case is planned: Layer 3.1's universal property, already library as tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset. 'Affinoid subdomain' of Spa does not occur in any stage text. Completed tensor products versus intersections: AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation.

items.name: Rational localizations are explicit and homeomorphic onto their image
items.statement: The rational subspace U = {v(f_i) ≤ v(g)} is represented by B = A{T_1, …, T_n}/(closure of (gT_i − f_i)) with B^+ the completed integral closure of A^+[T]; Spa(B, B^+) → U is a homeomorphism under which rational subspaces correspond.
items.note: Partly library: tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaLocalizationHomeomorph (Spa of the uncompleted topological localization ≃ R(T/s), with rational subsets matching by exists_spaLocalizationHomeomorph_preimage_rationalSubset_eq). The completed A⟨T/s⟩ is not yet identified. The Laurent presentation A⟨T/s⟩⟨X⟩/(t/s − X) is in RingTheory/Huber/LocalizationTopology/Laurent/Identification.lean.

items.name: Rational, affinoid and strong rational coverings; the structure presheaf; sheafiness
items.statement: Rational (affinoid) coverings are finite coverings by rational (affinoid) subdomains; a strong rational covering is one whose relative interiors cover M(A). The structure presheaf O takes U to the inverse limit of the rational localizations inside U, with O(Spa(B, B^+)) = B; (A, A^+) is sheafy if O is a sheaf, equivalently B → H^0(Spa(B, B^+), O) is an isomorphism for every rational localization.

items.name: Huber: strongly noetherian adic Banach rings are sheafy
items.statement: If A is strongly noetherian then (A, A^+) is sheafy.
items.note: Partial library toward it: flatness and faithful flatness for rational covers (Wedhorn 8.30, 8.32) are proved (Laurent/Flat.lean, Localization/FaithfullyFlat.lean). Sheafiness itself is not: there is no IsSheafy* declaration at the pin.

items.name: Stalks and Hausdorff localizations are henselian
items.statement: (a) Each stalk O_v is a henselian local ring whose residue field is dense in H(v). (b) The Hausdorff localization A_α (direct limit over rational localizations encircling α) is a henselian local ring with residue field dense in H(α). (c) For B faithfully finite étale over A, M(B) → M(A) is open.
items.note: Locality of stalks is planned in Layer 3; the henselian property and Hausdorff localizations are not.

items.name: Standard rational and standard Laurent coverings
items.statement: For f_1, …, f_n generating the unit ideal, U_i = {v(f_j) ≤ v(f_i) for all j}; for arbitrary f_i, the Laurent covering by the S_e = ∩ S_{i,e_i} with S_{i,−} = {v(f_i) ≤ 1}, S_{i,+} = {v(f_i) ≥ 1}; n = 1 gives simple Laurent coverings.

items.name: Refinement of rational coverings
items.statement: (a) Every rational covering is refined by a standard rational covering. (b) For a standard rational covering there is a standard Laurent covering on each piece of which it restricts to a standard rational covering generated by units. (c) A standard rational covering generated by units is refined by a standard Laurent covering generated by units.
items.note: (a) is library: tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_span_eq_top_forall_rationalSubset_subset (Wedhorn Lemma 7.54 / Huber Lemma 2.6; any Huber ring, covers by R(T_i/s_i) with T_i generating the unit ideal) and …_of_isTateRing for arbitrary open covers. (b) and (c) remain planned.

items.name: Reduction of covering properties to simple Laurent coverings
items.statement: A property of rational coverings of rational subdomains that is local (passes from refinements), transitive (passes to composite coverings) and holds for simple Laurent coverings holds for all rational coverings of all rational subdomains.
items.note: Wrong cross-references in step (iv) of the proof (finding E8). Review: Add the packet node AdicSpacesPartII:R3/rational-covering-reduction, which states Prop 2.4.20 verbatim for complete Tate pairs. Layer 4 has only the strongly noetherian Lemma 8.34 route.

items.name: Čech acyclicity criterion
items.statement: Let F be a presheaf of abelian groups on Spa(A, A^+). (a) If Ȟ^0(U, F; {V_1, V_2}) = F(U) for every rational subdomain U and every simple Laurent covering {V_1, V_2} of U, then H^0(U, F) = Ȟ^0(U, F; 𝔙) = F(U) for every rational subdomain U and every rational covering 𝔙 of U. (b) If moreover Ȟ^1(U, F; {V_1, V_2}) = 0 for all such U and {V_1, V_2}, then also H^i(U, F) = Ȟ^i(U, F; 𝔙) = 0 for all i > 0.
items.note: Review: Add AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-acyclicity-simple-laurent-reduction, titled '(Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.4.21)', which covers an arbitrary presheaf. Layer 4 plans only the structure sheaf of strongly noetherian rings.

items.name: Surjectivity for simple Laurent coverings
items.statement: For the simple Laurent covering defined by f ∈ A, with localizations B_1, B_2, B_12, the map B_1 ⊕ B_2 → B_12, (b_1, b_2) ↦ b_1 − b_2, is surjective.
items.note: Review: Add AdicSpacesPartII:R3/simple-laurent-difference-surjective, titled '(Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.4.22)'. It needs no sheafiness, noetherian or Tate hypothesis.

items.name: Tate acyclicity for sheafy adic Banach rings
items.statement: If (A, A^+) is sheafy, then for every rational covering U, H^i(Spa(A, A^+), O) = Ȟ^i(Spa(A, A^+), O; U) = A for i = 0 and 0 for i > 0.
items.note: Review: Layer 4 concludes all-degree Čech exactness only for strongly noetherian A ('First let A be a complete Hausdorff strongly noetherian Tate ring …'). KL 2.4.23 is for every sheafy pair. The packet node AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity plans exactly that: 'No noetherian or uniformity hypothesis is made: the anchor's Layer 4.1 gives (1) for strongly noetherian A, and this theorem extends it to every sheafy Tate pair'.

items.name: Reduction of properties of inclusions to simple Laurent coverings
items.statement: A property of inclusions V ⊆ U of rational subdomains that is transitive and holds for each inclusion that is part of a simple Laurent covering of U holds for all inclusions of rational subdomains.
items.note: An inclusion is stated backwards in the proof (finding E9). Review (status changed from missing to planned): Planned by the packet node AdicEtaleGeometry:A3/rational-inclusion-reduction, whose title cites KL I Prop 2.4.24 exactly. Remove it from route 5.

items.name: Affinoid algebras over an analytic field: noetherian, excellent, Noether normalization
items.statement: For an affinoid algebra A over an analytic field K: A is noetherian and excellent, every ideal is closed, finite A-modules are canonically finite Banach modules with all A-linear maps strict; for A ≠ 0 there is a finite strict monomorphism K{T_1, …, T_n} → A; maximal ideals have residue fields finite over K and correspond bijectively to the points of M(A) with residue field finite over K.
items.note: Layer 0 plans noetherianity of K⟨X⟩ and Weierstrass division. The excellence reference is misprinted (finding E10, corrected in part II).

items.name: Spectral norm of reduced affinoid algebras and finiteness of reductions
items.statement: For A reduced the spectral seminorm is a norm equivalent to the given one; for a finite morphism A → B the induced map κ_A → κ_B (for the spectral seminorms) is finite.
items.note: BGR 6.2.4/1 and 6.3.4/2. Review (status changed from missing to planned): Planned by the packet nodes AdicSpacesPartII:R0/reduced-affinoid-supremum-norm (Cor 2.5.6) and R0/affinoid-reduction-finite (Cor 2.5.7), both citing KL.

items.name: Rational subdomains of adic affinoids and of Maxspec
items.statement: For an adic affinoid algebra and rational U: (a) B ≅ A{T}/(gT_i − f_i) (no closure needed); (b) U ∩ Maxspec(A) is the rational subdomain of Maxspec(A) represented by A → B; (c) A reduced ⇒ B reduced; (d) A^+ = A° ⇒ B^+ = B°; coverings of Maxspec(A) by rational subdomains are refined by rational coverings of Spa.
items.note: Review: The R3 stage text (coherent sheaves and traces) does not plan 2.5.8–2.5.10. The packet node R1/affinoid-subdomain gives the rational-subdomain coordinate ring 'A⟨T₁,…,T_n⟩/(f₀T_j − f_j)' (no closure), and R1/classical-points-constructible-density (iv) gives U ↦ U ∩ Max A. Clauses (c) and (d) (reduced, B⁺ = B°) are not found.

items.name: Gerritzen–Grauert for adic affinoids
items.statement: For an affinoid subdomain U of Maxspec(A) there is a rational covering V_1, …, V_n of Spa(A, A^+) with each U ∩ V_i a rational subdomain of V_i ∩ Maxspec(A); U is a finite union of rational subdomains.
items.note: The atlas mentions Gerritzen–Grauert only for complex comparison and modular curves. Review (status changed from missing to planned): Planned by the packet node AdicSpacesPartII:R1/gerritzen-grauert, which cites KL Theorem 2.5.11. The item's note ('the atlas mentions Gerritzen–Grauert only for complex comparison and modular curves') is wrong.

items.name: Rational coverings detected on classical points
items.statement: If A^+ = A°, a finite collection of rational subdomains of a rational subdomain Spa(B, B^+) is a rational covering iff it covers Maxspec(B).
items.note: The paper's parenthesis 'and hence A is reduced; see Definition 2.8.1' is false, and nothing uses it (finding E108). Review (status changed from missing to planned): Planned by the packet nodes AdicSpacesPartII:R1/classical-points-constructible-density (iv) and R1/max-rational-covering-refinement, which cites KL Lemma 2.5.12.

items.name: Rational subspaces are determined by their classical points when A^+ = A°
items.statement: If A^+ = A°, no two distinct rational subspaces of Spa(A, A^+) have the same intersection with Maxspec(A).
items.note: Corrected: the printed hypothesis “A reduced” is not enough (finding E11). Review (status changed from missing to planned): Planned by the packet node AdicSpacesPartII:R1/classical-points-constructible-density (iv). The bijectivity of U ↦ U ∩ Max A on rational subsets of Spa(A, A°) is Cor 2.5.13 with the corrected hypothesis A⁺ = A° (finding E11).

items.name: Affinoid subdomains of adic affinoids and of Maxspec
items.statement: (a) For an affinoid subdomain U of Spa(A, A^+) represented by A → B, U ∩ Maxspec(A) is the affinoid subdomain of Maxspec(A) represented by A → B; (b) A reduced ⇒ B reduced; (c) A^+ = A° ⇒ B^+ = B°; if A^+ = A°, affinoid coverings are detected on Maxspec.

items.name: Flatness of affinoid localizations and faithful flatness of coverings
items.statement: Affinoid localizations of adic affinoids are flat; for an affinoid covering, A → ⊕B_i is faithfully flat, so local freeness of finite modules and étaleness of finite algebras are local on affinoid coverings.
items.note: Layer 4 plans flatness of rational localizations (Wedhorn 8.30). Rational case already library for complete Hausdorff strongly noetherian Tate rings, which include adic affinoid algebras: tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.flat_toCompletionLoc (A → A⟨T/s⟩ flat), tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.faithfullyFlat_pi_toCompletionLoc (finite rational cover ⇒ faithfully flat; Wedhorn 8.32). Affinoid (non-rational) subdomains are planned by AdicSpacesPartII:R1/affinoid-subdomain-flat (cites KL 2.5.17–2.5.18) in the classical Max A setting.

items.name: Theorems of Tate and Kiehl for adic affinoids
items.statement: (a) For an affinoid covering and a finite A-module M, the Čech complex of M̃ is acyclic with H^0 = M; in particular (A, A^+) is sheafy. (b) M ↦ M̃ is a tensor equivalence between finite A-modules and coherent O-modules; A → ⊕B_i is an effective descent morphism for finite Banach modules.
items.note: Review: The packet node R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid cites KL Theorem 2.5.20 ('Kiehl's theorem: coherent sheaves on a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid are the M̃').

items.name: Clopen subsets of an adic affinoid come from idempotents
items.statement: For U closed-open in Spa(A, A^+) there is a unique idempotent e ∈ A equal to 1 on U and 0 off U, and Spa(eA, eA^+) ≅ U; likewise for M(A).
items.note: Partly planned (independent review): The packet node AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-locally-finitely-many-components proves clopen ↔ idempotent for complete strongly noetherian Tate affinoids, which include KL's adic affinoid algebras. The 'likewise for M(A)' clause is not planned. The general Prop 2.6.4 (item 95) is only used, as input to A1/etale-diagonal, so keep 95 missing. The item stays missing because the rest is not planned.

items.name: Extension to Berkovich affinoids and to affinoid algebras over Z((z))
items.statement: The results of §2.5 other than Noether normalization (Lemma 2.5.4) and Corollary 2.5.5 extend to Berkovich affinoid algebras (the base field may be trivially normed, affinoid algebras as in Remark 2.2.16, rational subspaces as in Remark 2.4.10; proved by base change to a nontrivially normed analytic field L with prescribed transcendentals, using that A → A_L is strict and faithfully flat and M(A_L) → M(A) is surjective). They also extend to affinoid algebras over Z((z)) with the norm of Remark 2.5.23 (r ∈ (0,1), s > 1, rs ≥ 1; strongly noetherian): Lemma 2.5.17, Proposition 2.5.18, Corollary 2.5.19, Theorem 2.5.20(a) and Corollary 2.5.21. Theorem 2.5.20(b) extends too, but the paper gives no reference for it. to Berkovich affinoid algebras (by base change to an analytic field with prescribed transcendentals), and to affinoid algebras over Z((z)) with the norm of Remark 2.5.23 (strongly noetherian), including flatness, faithful flatness, Tate’s theorem and idempotents.

items.name: Affinoid systems and completed direct limits
items.statement: An affinoid system is a directed system of adic affinoid algebras over Z((z)) with submetric maps; its completed direct limit is the completion of the colimit ring for the infimum seminorm, with plus ring the colimit of the A_i^+. Every adic Banach algebra is the completed direct limit of an affinoid system.
items.note: The plus rings in the proof must be integrally closed (finding E12). Review (status changed from missing to planned): Planned by the packet node AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/affinoid-system-approximation (KL Definition 2.6.1, Lemma 2.6.2). It notes one deviation: its plus rings are integral closures, which fixes finding E12.

items.name: Adic spectra of completed direct limits
items.statement: Spa(R, R^+) is homeomorphic to lim Spa(A_i, A_i^+), every rational subspace, rational localization and rational covering is defined at a finite stage (and encircling can be tested there), and colimits of stalks and of Hausdorff localizations are local rings with dense residue fields.
items.note: Partly planned (independent review): The Spa-limit, rational-subset, rational-localization and covering parts are AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/affinoid-system-approximation (a), and also PerfectoidSpaces:P5/spa-of-filtered-colimit-of-tate-pairs (KL Remark 2.6.3), P5/descent-of-quasicompact-opens (2.6.7) and P5/limit-restriction-to-rational-subsets (Lemma 2.6.5). The stalk and Hausdorff-localization clause is not planned. The item stays missing because the rest is not planned.

items.name: Clopen subsets of adic spectra come from idempotents
items.statement: For any adic Banach algebra (R, R^+) and U closed-open in Spa(R, R^+), there is a unique idempotent e ∈ R equal to 1 on U and 0 off U, and Spa(eR, eR^+) ≅ U.

items.name: Finite étale algebras over completed direct limits
items.statement: For an affinoid system with direct limit (A, α), I = ker α and R the completion, FÉt(A) → FÉt(A/I) → FÉt(R) are tensor equivalences.
items.note: Review (status changed from missing to planned): Planned by the packet node AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-approximation (KL Remark 1.2.9, Prop 2.6.8). On the reviewer's lead: this is A1, not A4. A4/finite-etale-algebras-filtered-colimit is only the ring-theoretic Remark 1.2.9.

items.name: Descent of finite étale algebras along rational coverings
items.statement: For an adic Banach algebra (R, R^+) and a rational covering {(R, R^+) → (R_i, R_i^+)}, R → R_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ R_n is an effective descent morphism for finite étale algebras over Banach rings, and hence (Remark 1.4.3) for étale Z_p-local systems.
items.note: Review (status changed from missing to planned): Planned by the packet node AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent (KL Theorem 2.6.9). Cor 2.6.10 (Z_p-local systems) is not stated there.

items.name: Factorization of matrices near the identity
items.statement: If R_1 → S, R_2 → S are bounded and R_1 ⊕ R_2 → S is strict surjective, If R_1 → S and R_2 → S are bounded homomorphisms of Banach rings (topologically nilpotent units not required) and the sum ψ: R_1 ⊕ R_2 → S is strict surjective, there is c > 0 such that for every n ≥ 1, every U ∈ GL_n(S) with |U − 1| < c can be written as ψ(U_1)ψ(U_2) with U_i ∈ GL_n(R_i). If ψ is almost optimal, c = 1 works. with |U − 1| < c is ψ(U_1)ψ(U_2) with U_i ∈ GL_n(R_i); if the sum map is almost optimal, c = 1.
items.note: A constant is off in the proof (finding E13). Review (status changed from missing to planned): Planned by the packet node AdicSpacesPartII:R3/matrix-factorisation-strict-surjection. Its constant is c = d⁻², which may already contain the correction of finding E13.

items.name: Glueing squares of Banach rings
items.statement: A commutative square R → R_1, R_2 → R_12 of Banach rings is a glueing square if 0 → R → R_1 ⊕ R_2 → R_12 → 0 is strict exact, R_2 → R_12 has dense image and M(R_1 ⊕ R_2) → M(R) is surjective.
items.note: Review (status changed from missing to planned): Planned by the packet node AdicSpacesPartII:R3/glueing-square. Its condition (c) replaces KL's surjectivity M(R₁ ⊕ R₂) → M(R) by 'every maximal ideal of R is the contraction of a prime of R₁ × R₂', a documented deviation.

items.name: Glueing finite projective modules over a glueing square
items.statement: For a finite glueing datum over a glueing square, M ⊗_R R_i → M_i and M_1 ⊕ M_2 → M_12 are surjective; for a finite projective glueing datum, M = ker(M_1 ⊕ M_2 → M_12) is finite projective and M ⊗_R R_i ≅ M_i.
items.note: The matrix identity in the proof of Lemma 2.7.4 was checked. Review (status changed from missing to planned): Planned by the packet nodes R3/glueing-square-finite-surjectivity (Lemma 2.7.4) and R3/glueing-square-finite-projective-descent (Prop 2.7.5).

items.name: Tate sheaf property and Kiehl glueing property
items.statement: A presheaf of topological rings R on Spa(A, A^+) has the Tate sheaf property if every rational covering of every rational subdomain is acyclic with H^0 = R(U) (enough for simple Laurent coverings), and the Kiehl glueing property if on every rational subdomain finite projective R(U)-modules are equivalent to locally free R-modules of finite rank.
items.note: Review (status changed from missing to planned): The content of both properties is planned: the Tate sheaf property by R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity and the Kiehl glueing property by R3/sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing. The names are only definitional sugar.

items.name: Kiehl glueing for vector bundles on sheafy adic Banach rings
items.statement: For a sheafy adic Banach ring (A, A^+), the structure sheaf satisfies the Tate sheaf property and the Kiehl glueing property: vector bundles on Spa(A, A^+) are the same as finite projective A-modules.
items.note: AdicSpacesPartII R3 plans coherent sheaves on noetherian adic spaces only. Review (status changed from missing to planned): Planned by the packet nodes R3/sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing and R3/simple-laurent-glueing-square, and R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity cites KL Theorem 2.7.7. The item's note ('R3 plans coherent sheaves on noetherian adic spaces only') is wrong.

items.name: Uniform Banach rings
items.statement: A Banach ring A is uniform if its norm is equivalent to a power-multiplicative norm, equivalently to its spectral seminorm, equivalently |x²| ≥ c|x|² for some c > 0. Uniform rings are reduced, A° is bounded in them, reduced affinoid algebras are uniform, and Tate algebras over uniform rings are uniform. Boundedness of A° alone does not imply uniformity, unless A has a topologically nilpotent unit z with |z||z^{−1}| = 1.
items.note: Corrected (finding E14, corrected in part II). Layer 4 §4.2 uses Hansen–Kedlaya’s topological definition (A° bounded), which the norm-level definition refines. Review: The packet node R3/uniform-iff-power-bound plans Definition 2.8.1 as corrected in KL II Appendix A (E14), with the counterexample.

items.name: Spectral norms and injectivity for uniform rings
items.statement: For A uniform: bounded maps of uniform rings are submetric for the spectral norms, isometric iff the image of M(B) → M(A) is a boundary for A (in particular if M(B) → M(A) is surjective; Remark 2.8.3(a) says "if and only if surjective", which is false, finding E143); for a uniform adic Banach ring, A → H^0(Spa(A, A^+), O) is injective.
items.note: Partly planned (independent review): The first sentence (submetric for the spectral norms; isometric iff the image of M(B) → M(A) is a boundary) is the packet node R3/uniform-spectral-seminorm, which corrects KL's 'iff surjective' by a counterexample. Injectivity of A → H⁰(Spa(A, A⁺), O) for uniform A is not stated by any node found. The item stays missing because the rest is not planned. Remark 2.8.3(a)'s 'only if' is false (finding E143); the item's clause 'isometric iff surjective on M' is corrected to 'iff the image of M(B) → M(A) is a boundary'.

items.name: Projectivity of modules over uniform Banach rings by continuity of rank
items.statement: For A uniform and M finitely generated, the following are equivalent: M is projective; the rank function β ↦ dim_{H(β)} M ⊗ H(β) is continuous on M(A); M ⊗_A B is projective for some bounded A → B of uniform rings with M(B) → M(A) surjective.

items.name: Stable uniformity and its failures
items.statement: Completed tensor products and rational localizations of uniform rings need not be uniform (Q_p → C_p ⊗̂ C_p; Mihara’s example); (A, A^+) is stably uniform if all rational localizations are uniform. Scalar extension by a W(ℓ)[1/p] over W(k)[1/p] preserves uniformity, and (stable) uniformity descends along A → A ⊗̂_K L and along bounded maps that split as Banach modules; sheafy rings covered by stably uniform ones are stably uniform.
items.note: Layer 4 §4.2 plans stable uniformity; the descent and extension statements are part of the route. A misprint ends the proof of Lemma 2.8.6 (finding E15). The proof of Lemma 2.8.6 treats only finite extensions ℓ/k, but the infinite case follows by density (finding E110). Example 2.8.7 as printed is wrong: X ∉ A, and r > 1 is needed (finding E111; Mihara v1 has X among the generators and r ∈ (1, ∞)). Review: The packet nodes R3/stably-uniform-sheafy (Remark 2.8.12) and R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product (Remark 2.8.5, the ℂ_p ⊗̂ ℂ_p example) plan these parts.

items.name: Mihara: closedness of principal ideals over a uniform ring
items.statement: For A uniform and f ∈ A, the ideals (T − f), (1 − fT) of A{T} and A{T, T^{−1}} are closed For A uniform and f ∈ A, the ideals (T − f), (1 − fT) of A{T} and A{T, T^{−1}} are closed: for the spectral norm, |g| ≤ |(T − f)g| for all g ∈ A{T}, so multiplication by T − f is injective and strict, and similarly for the other cases..

items.name: Laurent exactness and the Buzzard–Verberkmoes theorem
items.statement: For a uniform adic Banach ring and the simple Laurent covering by f, 0 → A → B_1 ⊕ B_2 → B_12 → 0 is exact; hence a stably uniform adic Banach ring is sheafy.
items.note: A self-citation in the proof of 2.8.9 (finding E16).

items.name: Uniformization
items.statement: The separated completion A^u of A for the spectral seminorm is uniform, M(A^u) ≅ M(A), and A ↦ A^u (with A^{u+} the completed image of A^+) is left adjoint to the inclusion of uniform (adic) Banach rings; Spa(A^u, A^{u+}) ≅ Spa(A, A^+) matching rational subspaces.
items.note: A0 plans the uniformization and its universal property. Review: The packet node AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization cites KL Definition 2.8.13 and has (a)–(e) matching the item. A4's stage text 'Construct uniform completion of a Tate pair and prove invariance of its valuation spectrum'. A0 says only that uniformization is to be 'construct[ed] … separately'.

items.name: Finite étale algebras over a Banach ring and over its uniformization
items.statement: For A uniform and B ∈ FÉt(A) there is a maximal power-multiplicative seminorm on B bounding A → B; For A uniform and B ∈ FÉt(A) there is a maximal power-multiplicative seminorm on B for which A → B is bounded. For any Banach ring A and B ∈ FÉt(A), there is a strong rational covering {(A, A°) → (A_i, A_i^+)} such that each B ⊗_A A_i splits as a direct sum of monogenic A_i-algebras A_i[T]/(P), with P monic. FÉt(A) → FÉt(A^u) is a tensor equivalence, and the maximal seminorm makes each B ∈ FÉt(A^u) a uniform Banach algebra whose norm is equivalent to that of Definition 2.2.14. If A^+ = A°, then B^+ = B°.; FÉt(A) → FÉt(A^u) is a tensor equivalence, and the maximal seminorm makes each B ∈ FÉt(A^u) a uniform Banach algebra with norm equivalent to that of Definition 2.2.14. If A^+ = A°, then B^+ = B°.
items.note: Misprints in Lemmas 2.8.14–2.8.15 and the proof of Proposition 2.8.16 (findings E17–E19). Review (status changed from missing to planned): The reviewer's lead is confirmed: AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/uniform-completion-etale-comparison (ii) gives FÉt(A) ≃ FÉt(A^u), citing KL Prop 2.8.16, for complete Tate A. PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-over-uniform-is-uniform (citing 2.8.16) gives uniformity of B ∈ FÉt(A) and B° as the integral closure (the B⁺ = B° clause). The A4 stage text: 'Construct uniform completion of a Tate pair and prove invariance of its valuation spectrum and the étale-category comparison needed in ECD 15.3–15.4'; A1 adds 'Quotient/uniformization comparison of finite étale algebras belongs to A4.' Route 6 (A1) is the wrong home. The proofs of Lemma 2.8.15 and Proposition 2.8.16(b) have the gaps E113 and E112.

items.name: Perfect F_p-algebras and the perfect closure
items.statement: An F_p-algebra R is perfect if Frobenius x ↦ x^p is bijective (so R is reduced; localizations of perfect rings are perfect). The perfect closure R^perf is the direct limit of R → R → ⋯ along Frobenius; R → R^perf identifies the reduced quotient of R with a subring. For any set X, R[X]^perf ≅ R^perf[X^{p^{−∞}}] naturally in R.
items.note: Perfect implies reduced is stated as the vanishing of the p-nilradical; Example 3.1.14 is the universal property PerfectClosure.lift applied to R[X].

items.name: Perfect uniform (adic) Banach F_p-algebras
