items.statement: A perfect uniform Banach F_p-algebra is a uniform Banach ring of characteristic p whose underlying ring is perfect; in the adic case R^+ is then perfect because it is integrally closed. A power-multiplicative seminorm on R extends uniquely to R^perf, giving homeomorphisms M(R^perf) ≅ M(R) and Spa(R^perf, R^{+,perf}) ≅ Spa(R, R^+).
items.note: PerfectoidSpaces P1 plans the characteristic-p case of perfectoid Tate rings (perfect complete uniform Tate rings).

items.name: Frobenius-fixed elements of a perfect ring are F_p-combinations of idempotents
items.statement: If R is perfect and e^p = e, then e_i = ∏_{j ≠ i}(e − j)/(i − j) (i ∈ F_p) are idempotents with e = Σ i e_i. Hence R^{ϕ=1} is the F_p-algebra generated by the idempotents of R, and equals F_p iff R is connected.

items.name: Finite étale algebras over a perfect ring are perfect
items.statement: If R is a perfect F_p-algebra, every S ∈ FÉt(R) is perfect.
items.note: Review (status changed from missing to planned): Planned by the packet node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-over-perfect-is-perfect.

items.name: Strict maps, tensor products and quotients of perfect uniform Banach algebras
items.statement: For perfect uniform Banach F_p-algebras: (a) a strict homomorphism is almost optimal (not necessarily optimal); (b) if f_1 − f_2 is strict it is almost optimal; (c) completed tensor products R ⊗̂_T S are again perfect uniform (unlike general uniform rings); (d) the quotient by a closed perfect ideal is perfect uniform.

items.name: Rational localizations of perfect uniform adic Banach F_p-algebras
items.statement: Every rational localization of a perfect uniform adic Banach F_p-algebra (R, R^+) is again perfect uniform, so (R, R^+) is stably uniform. Explicitly, the localization is the quotient of the completed perfection of R{T_1, …, T_n} by the closed ideal generated by the (gT_i − f_i)^{p^{−h}}, and for any c > 1 the quotient norm from R{T} can be taken within a factor c of the spectral norm.
items.note: PerfectoidSpaces P2 plans perfectoid rational localizations; in characteristic p these are the perfect uniform ones. Review: The node cites KL I Prop 3.1.7 and includes the explicit presentation and stable uniformity.

items.name: Finite perfect algebras over a perfect uniform Banach algebra are uniform
items.statement: If R is perfect uniform and S is a finite perfect R-algebra that is a finite Banach R-module (e.g. S ∈ FÉt(R)), then S is a perfect uniform Banach algebra. An isometric automorphism of R that extends to S ∈ FÉt(R) is isometric on S.
items.note: PerfectoidSpaces P3 plans that finite étale algebras over a perfectoid ring are perfectoid; Lemma 3.1.9 is the characteristic-p case. The isometry statement of Lemma 3.1.10 is a small addition.

items.name: Integral elements of finite étale algebras over perfect uniform algebras are almost finite étale
items.statement: For R perfect uniform over a perfect analytic field L and S ∈ FÉt(R), o_S is perfect with Ω_{o_S/o_R} = 0, and the quotient of o_S by the sum of its finitely generated projective o_R-submodules is killed by m_L; o_S need not be finite over o_R.

items.name: Tate acyclicity and Kiehl glueing for perfect uniform adic Banach algebras
items.statement: For f ∈ R and the rational subdomains {v(f) ≤ 1}, {v(f) ≥ 1}, {v(f) = 1}, the sequence 0 → R → R_1 ⊕ R_2 → R_12 → 0 is almost optimal exact (Lemma 3.1.12). Hence every perfect uniform adic Banach F_p-algebra is sheafy and satisfies the Tate sheaf and Kiehl glueing properties (Theorem 3.1.13).

items.name: Finite étale algebras are unchanged by perfection
items.statement: (a) For any F_p-algebra R, base change FÉt(R) → FÉt(R^perf) is a tensor equivalence. (b) If R is a uniform Banach F_p-algebra and S is the completion of R^perf, then FÉt(R) → FÉt(S) is a tensor equivalence.
items.note: Mathlib has the topological half (PrimeSpectrum.isHomeomorph_comap applies to R → R^perf) and the category CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale, but not the equivalence. Partly planned (independent review): (b), the completed perfection of a complete Tate ring of characteristic p, is the packet node P3/finite-etale-under-completed-perfection. (a), the uncompleted perfection of an arbitrary F_p-algebra, is not a node; P3/fontaine-wintenberger uses it as 'Frobenius twists do not change finite étale algebras'. The item stays missing because the rest is not planned.

items.name: Sheafy adic Banach F_p-algebras that are locally perfect uniform are perfect
items.statement: If (A, A^+) is a sheafy adic Banach F_p-algebra admitting a rational covering by perfect uniform algebras, then A is perfect. This is essentially Buzzard–Verberkmoes, Corollary 10, with sheafy in place of stably uniform; without uniformity the covering conjecture fails (Buzzard–Verberkmoes, Proposition 13).
items.note: Remarks 3.1.17 and 3.6.27 cite the covering conjecture from the wrong paper (findings E20, E36).

items.name: Strict p-rings and the universal property of W(R)
items.statement: A strict p-ring is a p-torsion-free p-adically complete ring S with S/(p) perfect. For p-adically complete U, every ring map S/(p) → U/(p) lifts uniquely to a multiplicative map t: S/(p) → U (t(x) ≡ y^{p^n} mod p^{n+1} for y lifting the image of x^{p^{−n}}); in particular S has a Teichmüller section [·], every x ∈ S is uniquely Σ p^n [x_n], and Σ p^n [x_n] ↦ Σ p^n t(x_n) is a ring homomorphism S → U (Lemma 3.2.2). The addition law is given by universal homogeneous polynomials P_n in p-power roots (Remark 3.2.3). S ↦ S/(p) is an equivalence from strict p-rings to perfect F_p-algebras (Theorem 3.2.4).
items.locator: §3.2, Definition 3.2.1, Lemma 3.2.2, Remark 3.2.3 and Theorem 3.2.4, pp. 71–73
items.note: RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0 plans W(R) for perfect R with its Teichmüller representatives and p-adically complete universal property. Mathlib has pieces: the multiplicative lift Perfection.teichmuller, uniqueness of maps agreeing on Teichmüller lifts (WittVector.eq_of_apply_teichmuller_eq) and θ as a special case, but no notion of strict p-ring and no general lifting theorem.

items.name: Witt vectors of a perfect ring
items.statement: For R perfect, W(R), the p-typical Witt vectors, is p-torsion-free and p-adically complete with W(R)/(p) ≅ R, every element is Σ p^n [x_n] with x_n ∈ R, and Frobenius lifts to an automorphism ϕ of W(R); W_n(R) = W(R)/(p^n) is the ring of truncated Witt vectors.
items.note: Mathlib proves existence of the Teichmüller expansion; its uniqueness follows from p-torsion-freeness and W(R)/(p) ≅ R. W_n(R) ≅ W(R)/(p^n) follows from WittVector.mem_ker_truncate and WittVector.mem_span_p_pow_iff_le_coeff_eq_zero.

items.name: ϕ-modules over W_n(R) acquire invariant bases over a faithfully finite étale cover
items.statement: Let R be perfect, n ≥ 1, and M a finite projective W_n(R)-module of everywhere positive rank with a semilinear ϕ^a-action. Some faithfully finite étale R-algebra S makes M ⊗ W_n(S) admit a ϕ^a-fixed basis; a fixed basis modulo p^m (m < n) can be lifted. The proof represents invariant bases by the closed-open part of the scheme of invariant n-tuples.
items.note: The representing ring is corrected in the authors’ errata (finding E21).

items.name: Lisse Z/p^n-sheaves on a perfect ring and ϕ-modules over W_n(R)
items.statement: For R perfect and n ≥ 1 there is a tensor equivalence, natural in R and n, between lisse sheaves of Z/p^nZ-modules on Spec R and finite projective W_n(R)-modules with a semilinear ϕ-action.
items.note: The inverse functor’s formula is corrected in the authors’ errata (finding E22).

items.name: Lang torsors for unipotent Witt group schemes
items.statement: For d, m ≥ 1, n ≥ 2 (n = 1 allowed if p > 2), an algebraic Lie subalgebra g of gl_d(Q_p), g_n = g ∩ gl_d(p^n Z_p), and G_{n,m} the unipotent group scheme of g_n ⊗ Z/p^m (Greenberg realization over F_p): for perfect R, ϕ-conjugacy classes G_{n,m}(R)/∼ (g_1 ∼ h^{−1}g_1ϕ(h)) are in natural bijection with H^1_et(R, G_{n,m}(F_p)). For general group schemes Hilbert 90 can fail (Serre, Grothendieck on special groups).

items.name: Direct perfection of a ring with a Frobenius lift
items.statement: For A p-torsion-free with A/pA reduced, an endomorphism ϕ_A lifting the p^r-power Frobenius, and (A/pA)^perf ≅ R, there is a map s_ϕ: A → W(R) with ϕ^r ∘ s_ϕ = s_ϕ ∘ ϕ_A, identifying W(R) with the p-adic completion of the direct limit of A along ϕ_A. For A = Z[T], ϕ(T) = T^p it sends T to [T̄] but s_ϕ(T + 1) ≠ [T̄ + 1].
items.note: PrismaticCohomology PR.0 plans Frobenius lifts on p-torsion-free rings and completed perfection.

items.name: Frobenius-stable finitely generated ideals of a perfect ring are idempotent
items.statement: If R is perfect and J is a finitely generated ideal with ϕ(J) = J, then J is generated by an idempotent; in particular R/J is finite projective over R.

items.name: ϕ-modules over W_n(R) flat over Z/p^n are projective
items.statement: For R perfect, a finitely presented W_n(R)-module that is flat over Z/p^nZ and carries a semilinear ϕ-action is finite projective over W_n(R).

items.name: The Gauss seminorms λ(α) on W(R) and the restriction μ(β)
items.statement: For R perfect and α a submultiplicative (power-multiplicative, multiplicative) seminorm on R bounded by the trivial norm, λ(α)(Σ p^i [x_i]) = sup_i p^{−i} α(x_i) is a seminorm of the same kind on W(R) bounded by the p-adic norm; conversely μ(β)(x) = β([x]). (Kedlaya, Nonarchimedean geometry of Witt vectors, Lemmas 4.1–4.2.) Equipping R with the trivial norm and W(R) with the p-adic norm, the maps λ: M(R) → M(W(R)) and μ: M(W(R)) → M(R) are continuous, μ ∘ λ = id and λ ∘ μ ≥ id (Lemma 3.3.3, citing loc. cit. Theorem 4.5).

items.name: Primitive elements of degree 1
items.statement: For R complete for a power-multiplicative norm α bounded by the trivial norm, z = Σ p^i [z_i] ∈ W(R) is primitive of degree 1 if α(x z_0) = p^{−1} α(x) for all x ∈ R and z_1 ∈ R^× (equivalently z − [z_0] ∈ pW(R)^×); then (z) is closed, and R[z_0^{−1}] is a Banach algebra over F_p((z_0)). The condition is stronger than Fargues–Fontaine’s α(z_0) < 1. From §3.6 on the reduction z_0 must also be a unit of R (authors’ errata).
items.note: PerfectoidSpaces P1 plans primitive degree-one ideals and the classification of marked untilts (finding E23).

items.name: A primitive element of degree 1 from p-power roots of unity
items.statement: If R is uniform with spectral norm α and π ∈ R^× has α(π) = p^{−p/(p−1)} and α(π^{−1}) = p^{p/(p−1)}, then z = Σ_{i=0}^{p−1} [π + 1]^{i/p} has z_0 = π^{(p−1)/p}, α(z_0) = p^{−1}, and z_1 a unit; so z is primitive of degree 1.
items.note: The cyclotomic test case of PerfectoidSpaces P1.

items.name: Reduced representatives modulo a primitive element
items.statement: If R is complete for a power-multiplicative norm α and z ∈ W(o_R) is primitive of degree 1, every x ∈ W(o_R) is congruent modulo z to some y = Σ p^i [y_i] with α(y_0) ≥ α(y_i) for all i > 0.

items.name: Quotient norms modulo a primitive element and the spectrum of W(o_R)/(z)
items.statement: (a) For γ a submultiplicative (power-multiplicative, multiplicative) seminorm on o_R bounded by the trivial norm, the quotient seminorm σ(γ) on W(o_R)/(z) induced by λ(γ) is of the same kind and μ(σ(γ)) = γ. (b) σ is a continuous section of μ inducing a homeomorphism M(o_R) ≅ M(W(o_R)/(z)) that matches rational subspaces. (c) If moreover z_0 ∈ R^× (the unit condition the authors' errata add from §3.6 on; without it (c) fails, see finding E114), it induces a homeomorphism M(R) ≅ M(W(o_R)[[z_0]^{−1}]/(z)) matching rational subspaces.
items.note: P1 plans the untilt construction with its topology; P2 plans the tilting homeomorphism of spectra, including the rank-one case.

items.name: Untilts of a perfect analytic field
items.statement: For L a perfect analytic field of characteristic p and z ∈ W(o_L) primitive of degree 1, F = W(o_L)[[z_0]^{−1}]/(z) is an analytic field with valuation ring W(o_L)/(z) and the same residue field, and o_L/(z_0) ≅ o_F/(p), so Frobenius is surjective on o_F/(p) and F is not discretely valued. Examples: the completions of Q_p(μ_{p^∞}) and of Q_p(p^{p^{−∞}}).

items.name: Approximation modulo a primitive element with small higher Witt components
items.statement: For R, z as above with z_0 ∈ R^× (needed for α ∈ M(R) to be evaluated on the Witt components of y ∈ W(o_R)[[z_0]^{−1}] and for the proof's α(z̄) = p^{−1}), ε > 0 and m ≥ 0, every x ∈ W(o_R)[[z_0]^{−1}] is congruent modulo z to some y = Σ p^n [y_n] with α(y_1) ≤ max{p^{−p^{−1}−⋯−p^{−m}} α(y_0), ε} and α(y_n) ≤ max{α(y_0), ε} (n > 1) for every α ∈ M(R).

items.name: Inverse perfection
items.statement: For a ring A, A^♭ = lim(⋯ → A/pA → A/pA) along Frobenius is a perfect F_p-algebra, and A^♭ → A/pA is surjective when Frobenius is surjective on A/pA. For A p-adically complete, reduction gives a multiplicative isomorphism lim_{x ↦ x^p} A ≅ A^♭ (Remark 3.4.10).

items.name: Inverse perfection only depends on A modulo a nilpotent thickening of (p)
items.statement: If I is an ideal of A with I^m ⊆ (p) ⊆ I for some m, then A^♭ → (A/I)^♭ is an isomorphism.
items.note: P1 plans the tilt and its integral descriptions, where R^♭ is computed modulo any pseudouniformizer dividing p.

items.name: Fontaine’s map θ
items.statement: From A^♭ → A/pA one gets a multiplicative map x ↦ x^♯, A^♭ → Â (the p-adic completion), and a homomorphism θ: W(A^♭) → Â with θ([x]) = x^♯ whose reduction modulo p is the projection A^♭ → A/pA; so θ is surjective iff Frobenius is surjective on A/pA.
items.note: Mathlib builds θ for a p-adically complete ring in which p is not a unit; Â is one, with Â/p = A/p. surjective_fontaineTheta is the direction used; the converse is read off mk_fontaineTheta.

items.name: Norms on the inverse perfection
items.statement: For A p-adically separated and β a submultiplicative (power-multiplicative, multiplicative) seminorm bounded by the p-adic norm, α = μ(θ^*(β)) is such a seminorm on A^♭ bounded by the trivial norm, and θ is bounded for λ(α) and β. If β is a power-multiplicative (multiplicative) norm and A is complete, α is a norm of the same kind and A^♭ is complete.
items.note: P1 plans the tilt’s completeness, uniformity and integral subrings.

items.name: Density passes to inverse perfections
items.statement: Let A_1 = ∪ A_{1,i} be p-adically separated with Frobenius surjective on each A_{1,i}/p, A_2 p-adically separated with a norm β_2 bounded by the p-adic norm, ψ: A_1 → A_2 a homomorphism and α_2 = μ(θ^*(β_2)). (a) If ψ has dense image, so does ∪ A_{1,i}^♭ → A_2^♭. (b) If the image of ψ has dense intersection with m_{A_2}, then the image of ψ^♭ has dense intersection with m_{A_2^♭}. (Density in A_2 is for β_2, in A_2^♭ for α_2.)

items.name: The kernel of θ is generated by a primitive element
items.statement: Let A be p-adically separated, p-torsion-free and complete for a power-multiplicative norm bounded by the p-adic norm, and suppose z ∈ W(A^♭) is primitive of degree 1 with θ(z) = 0. For θ extended to W(A^♭)[[z_0]^{−1}] → A[θ([z_0])^{−1}]: (a) ker θ = (z); (b) θ is optimal; (c) Frobenius is surjective on A/(p) iff θ has dense image. For R perfect, W(R)^♭ ≅ R and θ: W(W(R)^♭) → W(R) is an isomorphism (Remark 3.4.6). Surjectivity of Frobenius on A/pA passes to A/I when I^m ⊆ (p) ⊆ I, but not conversely (Z_p[√p]); a partial converse holds.
items.note: P1 plans θ, its surjectivity and the principal description of its kernel.

items.name: Perfectoid analytic fields
items.statement: An analytic field F is perfectoid if it has characteristic 0, residue characteristic p, is not discretely valued, and Frobenius is surjective on o_F/(p).

items.name: The tilt of a perfectoid field
items.statement: For F perfectoid with norm β, R = (o_F/(p))^♭ and α = μ(θ^*(β)): (a) K = Frac(R) is a perfect analytic field of characteristic p with o_K = R; (b) β(F^×) = α(K^×); (c) for z_0 ∈ K with α(z_0) = p^{−1}, o_F/(p) ≅ o_K/(z_0) naturally, so κ_F ≅ κ_K; (d) ker θ contains a primitive element of degree 1, which generates the kernel of θ: W(o_K)[[z_0]^{−1}] → F.
items.note: Mathlib has the field Tilt = Frac(PreTilt O p) with the valuation PreTilt.val, but not its completeness, value group or residue field.

items.name: The perfectoid correspondence for fields
items.statement: F ↦ (Frac((o_F/(p))^♭), ker θ) and (L, I) ↦ Frac(W(o_L)/I) are inverse equivalences between perfectoid analytic fields and pairs (L, I) with L a perfect analytic field of characteristic p and I a principal ideal of W(o_L) generated by a primitive element of degree 1.

items.name: Finite extensions correspond with the same degree
items.statement: If F and (L, I) correspond and M/L is finite, then (M, I W(o_M)) corresponds to a finite extension E/F with [E : F] = [M : L]. The proof uses Artin’s lemma, which needs the Galois group to act faithfully on E.
items.note: The faithfulness check is added in the authors’ errata (finding E24).

items.name: Untilts of algebraically closed fields are algebraically closed
items.statement: If F and (L, I) correspond and L is algebraically closed, then so is F; the proof builds a root of any monic P ∈ o_F[T] by successive approximation, solving the reduced equation in o_L/(z) ≅ o_F/(p).

items.name: Tilting of finite étale algebras over perfectoid fields
items.statement: For corresponding F and (L, I), the correspondence of Lemma 3.5.4 gives a tensor equivalence FÉt(F) ≅ FÉt(L); every finite extension of F is perfectoid and the absolute Galois groups of F and L are homeomorphic. Forgetting I, the functor F ↦ L is not fully faithful.

items.name: Vanishing of H^1(G, 1 + m_K) for finite isometric actions
items.statement: If K is a perfect analytic field of characteristic p and a finite group G acts faithfully on K by isometries, then H^1(G, 1 + m_K) = 0. The additive cochain complex of K is almost optimal exact (normal basis theorem and Frobenius), and a multiplicative cocycle is trivialized by successive approximation.

items.name: Perfectoid fields descend along finite extensions
items.statement: If E/F is a finite extension of analytic fields with E perfectoid, then F is perfectoid. After enlarging E to be Galois with group G, one finds a G-invariant primitive generator of the ideal I of the tilt L, and the fixed field of L gives F.
items.note: Findings E25–E26 concern the proof.

items.name: Perfectoid fields are deeply ramified
items.statement: An analytic field K is deeply ramified if Ω_{o_L/o_K} = 0 for every finite extension L/K. Every perfectoid field is deeply ramified (the converse is Gabber–Ramero, Proposition 6.6.6).

items.name: Perfectoid uniform adic Banach Q_p-algebras
items.statement: A uniform adic Banach Q_p-algebra (A, A^+) is perfectoid if Frobenius is surjective on A^+/(p) and some x ∈ A^+ has x^p ≡ p mod p^2A^+; a uniform Banach algebra A is perfectoid if (A, A°) is. This agrees with Fontaine’s definition for uniform Banach Q_p-algebras; Fontaine’s notion also covers perfect uniform F_p-algebras and rings over neither.

items.name: Equivalent formulations of the perfectoid condition
items.statement: For (A, A^+) uniform over an analytic field F ⊇ Q_p: (a) if |F^×| ≠ |Q_p^×|, perfectoid iff Frobenius is surjective on A^+/(p); (b) F is perfectoid as an algebra iff as a field; (c) with the spectral norm, A is perfectoid iff for some (equivalently every) c ∈ (p^{−1}, 1) every x has y with |x − y^p| ≤ c|x|; (d) A is perfectoid iff (A, A^+) is; (e) A is perfectoid iff some topologically nilpotent unit ϖ has ϖ^p | p in A^+ and Frobenius A^+/(ϖ) → A^+/(ϖ^p) surjective.

items.name: θ is surjective for perfectoid algebras, with primitive kernel
items.statement: For (A, A^+) perfectoid, θ: W(A^{+,♭}) → A^+ is surjective and its kernel is generated by an element primitive of degree 1.

items.name: The tilt and untilt functors
items.statement: For (A, A^+) perfectoid with ker θ = (z): R(A) = A^{+,♭}[z_0^{−1}], R^+(A^+) = A^{+,♭}, I(A, A^+) = ker θ. For (A, A^+) perfectoid with ker θ = (z): R(A) = A^{+,♭}[z̄^{−1}] (z̄ = z̄_0 the reduction of z), R^+(A^+) = A^{+,♭}, I(A, A^+) = ker θ = zW(A^{+,♭}). For ((R, R^+), I) with I ⊂ W(R^+) generated by an element z primitive of degree 1 whose reduction z̄_0 is a unit of R (the authors' errata: from §3.6 on this unit condition is part of 'primitive of degree 1'): A(R, I) = (W(R^+)/I)[p^{−1}], A^+(R^+, I) = W(R^+)/I; the surjection W(R^+)[[z̄_0]^{−1}] → A(R, I) is optimal. Both constructions preserve idempotents, so Spec R and Spec A have the same clopen subsets (not the same irreducible components). (That (R(A), R^+(A^+)) is an adic Banach algebra, i.e. R^+(A^+) is open and integrally closed in R(A), needs the argument of the errata; see E27.), A^+(R^+, I) = W(R^+)/I; W(R^+)[[z_0]^{−1}] → A(R, I) is optimal. Both constructions preserve idempotents, so Spec R and Spec A have the same clopen subsets (not the same irreducible components).
items.note: The authors’ errata add the argument that R^+(A^+) is a ring of integral elements of R(A) (finding E27).

items.name: The perfectoid correspondence for Banach algebras
items.statement: A ↦ (R(A), I(A)) and (R, I) ↦ A(R, I) are inverse equivalences between perfectoid uniform Banach Q_p-algebras and A ↦ (R(A), I(A)) and (R, I) ↦ A(R, I) are inverse equivalences between perfectoid uniform Banach Q_p-algebras and pairs (R, I) with R a perfect uniform Banach F_p-algebra and I ⊂ W(o_R) a principal ideal generated by an element z primitive of degree 1 whose reduction z̄_0 is a unit of R (authors' errata); likewise for adic Banach algebras with pairs ((R, R^+), I), I ⊂ W(R^+) generated by such a z. The algebras need not lie over a perfectoid field.; likewise for adic Banach algebras with pairs ((R, R^+), I), I ⊂ W(R^+). The algebras need not lie over a perfectoid field.

items.name: Perfectoid Tate algebras
items.statement: For corresponding A and (R, I) and r_1, …, r_n > 0, the completions B, S of A{T/r}[T^{p^{−∞}}] and R{T/r}[T^{p^{−∞}}] for the weighted Gauss norm are perfectoid and perfect, and B corresponds to (S, I W(o_S)) with (T_i, T_i^{1/p}, …) ↦ T_i.
items.note: A test case of PerfectoidSpaces P1 (perfected Tate balls).

items.name: Approximation by p-th powers in perfectoid algebras
items.statement: For A perfectoid with spectral norm, ε > 0, m ≥ 0 and x ∈ A, there is y = θ([y_0]) with β(x − y^p) ≤ max{p^{−1−p^{−1}−⋯−p^{−m}} β(x), ε} for all β ∈ M(A); in particular |x − y^p| ≤ p^{−1−p^{−1}−⋯−p^{−m}}|x|. The constant cannot be improved to p^{−p/(p−1)} (Davis–Kedlaya, On the Witt vector Frobenius, Example 5.9).

items.name: Strict morphisms under tilting
items.statement: With spectral norms: (a) if ψ̄: R → S is strict, the untilted ψ: A → B is almost optimal, and surjective if ψ̄ is; (b) if ψ̄_1 − ψ̄_2 is strict surjective, ψ_1 − ψ_2 is almost optimal and surjective; (c) a strict homomorphism ψ of perfectoid algebras is almost optimal and ψ(A) is perfectoid; (d) then the tilt ψ̄ is almost optimal, and surjective if ψ is. Strict surjectivity does not imply surjectivity on integral elements.
items.note: Findings E28–E29 correct the statement of (a) and a bound in the proof of (d). Partly planned (independent review): Partial. PerfectoidSpaces:P1/strict-inclusions-under-tilting proves that f is a strict inclusion iff f♭ is, and identifies strict inclusions with isometries for the spectral gauges. KL's almost-optimal and strict-surjective statements (a)–(d) are not covered. Keep it missing if 'planned' requires the whole item. The item stays missing because the rest is not planned.

items.name: Completed tensor products of perfectoid algebras
items.statement: For morphisms A → B, A → C of perfectoid uniform Banach Q_p-algebras with tilts R, S, T, the completed tensor product B ⊗̂_A C (tensor product norm) is the perfectoid algebra corresponding to S ⊗̂_R T; likewise for adic Banach algebras.
items.note: The v5 proof shows only that B ⊗̂_A C → D is surjective with the norm bound; injectivity is not shown (E30, authors' errata). The statement is proved in part II, Theorem 3.3.13.

items.name: Tilting identifies adic spectra and rational localizations
items.statement: For corresponding (A, A^+) and ((R, R^+), I): (a) the homeomorphism M(A) ≅ M(R) lifts to a functorial homeomorphism Spa(A, A^+) ≅ Spa(R, R^+); (b) the rational subspace defined by f_1, …, f_n, g ∈ R corresponds to the one defined by θ([f_i]), θ([g]), and every rational subspace of Spa(A, A^+) has this form; (c) corresponding rational localizations are perfectoid and correspond. The proof uses the explicit presentations A{T}/(T − g), A{U}/(Ug − 1) (Lemma 3.6.13) and strict presentations with quotient norm within any c > 1 of the spectral norm (Remark 3.6.16).
items.note: Finding E31 corrects a display in the proof.

items.name: Perfectoid adic Banach algebras are stably uniform and sheafy
items.statement: Every perfectoid adic Banach algebra is stably uniform and sheafy, and so satisfies the Tate sheaf and Kiehl glueing properties.
items.note: Finding E32 is a typo in the proof.

items.name: Dense-image morphisms under tilting
items.statement: (a) If ψ̄: R → S is a bounded homomorphism of uniform Banach F_p-algebras with dense image and R is perfect, then S is perfect and the untilt ψ: A → B has dense image. (b) If A is perfectoid and ψ: A → B is a bounded homomorphism with dense image to a uniform Banach Q_p-algebra, then B is perfectoid and the tilt has dense image. (c) In both cases ψ̄ is surjective iff ψ is.
items.note: Finding E33 corrects a symbol in the proof. Review (status changed from missing to planned): Planned by the packet node PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion, which cites 'Kedlaya–Liu I Theorem 3.6.17(b)'. (c), surjectivity iff, is not stated.

items.name: Uniform completed tensor products over any base are perfectoid
items.statement: If C → A and C → B are bounded homomorphisms of uniform Banach Q_p-algebras with A and B perfectoid, the uniform completion (A ⊗̂_C B)^u is perfectoid.

items.name: Completion of a perfectoid algebra along an ideal containing p
items.statement: For A perfectoid with its spectral norm and J a finitely generated ideal of o_A containing p, the inverse limit R of the o_A/J^n (quotient norms, supremum norm) gives B = R[p^{−1}], which is again a perfectoid uniform Banach Q_p-algebra.
items.note: The v5 proof does not show that B is uniform (E34, authors' errata); the statement is proved in part II, Theorem 3.3.18(v). The printed series in the proof also has a misprint (finding E123).

items.name: Finite étale algebras over perfectoid algebras correspond (almost purity)
items.statement: For corresponding A and (R, I): the untilt of S ∈ FÉt(R) lies in FÉt(A) with norm equivalent to any Banach norm on it (Lemma 3.6.20); every B ∈ FÉt(A), with a Banach norm from Proposition 2.8.16, is perfectoid, and FÉt(A) ≅ FÉt(R) as tensor categories, so Ω_{o_B/o_A} = 0 (Theorem 3.6.21). Consequently the small étale sites of the associated adic spaces agree (Scholze).

items.name: Perfectoid algebras descend along faithfully finite étale maps
items.statement: Let A → B be a morphism of uniform Banach Q_p-algebras with B perfectoid. (a) If A → B is faithfully finite étale, A is perfectoid. (b) If k ⊆ ℓ are perfect fields, K = W(k)[p^{−1}], L = W(ℓ)[p^{−1}], A is a Banach K-algebra and B = (A ⊗̂_K L)^u, then A ⊗̂_K L = B and A is perfectoid.
items.note: Finding E35 updates a citation in the proof.

items.name: The multiplicative inverse limit of a perfectoid algebra
items.statement: (a) For corresponding A and (R, I), (a) For corresponding A and (R, I), x ↦ (θ([x]), θ([x^{1/p}]), …) is a bijection (an isomorphism of multiplicative monoids, via Remark 3.4.10) R ≅ lim_{x ↦ x^p} A. (b) For A perfectoid, lim_{x ↦ x^p} A generates a dense Z-subalgebra of A. (c) If A is uniform over a perfectoid B and lim_{x ↦ x^p} A generates a dense B-subalgebra, A is perfectoid.. (b) For A perfectoid, lim_{x ↦ x^p} A generates a dense Z-subalgebra of A. (c) If A is uniform over a perfectoid B and lim_{x ↦ x^p} A generates a dense B-subalgebra, A is perfectoid.
items.note: P1 plans the multiplicative inverse limit defining the tilt.

items.name: Perfectoid Kummer covers of uniform Banach Q_p-algebras
items.statement: Let A be uniform over Q_p and U ⊆ m_A generate a dense Q_p-subalgebra. The completed direct limit B of the finite étale algebras B_{T,n} = A[x_{t,n}]/(x_{t,n}^{p^n} − 1 − t : t ∈ T) ⊗ Q_p(μ_{p^n}) (spectral seminorms) is a perfectoid uniform Banach Q_p-algebra, M(B) → M(A) is surjective, and A → B is isometric.

items.name: Preperfectoid, strongly preperfectoid and relatively perfectoid algebras
items.statement: A uniform Banach Q_p-algebra A is preperfectoid if A ⊗̂_{Q_p} K is uniform and perfectoid for some perfectoid field K (Scholze–Weinstein), strongly preperfectoid if for every perfectoid field K, and relatively perfectoid if A ⊗̂_{Q_p} B is uniform and perfectoid for every perfectoid algebra B; likewise for adic Banach algebras. The completed perfected Tate algebra Q_p{T/r}[T^{p^{−∞}}]^∧ is relatively perfectoid; perfectoid algebras are generally not preperfectoid.
items.note: Finding E37 corrects a letter in the definition.

items.name: Uniformity, rational localizations and sheafiness of preperfectoid algebras
items.statement: If A is preperfectoid then A ⊗̂_{Q_p} B is uniform for every uniform Banach Q_p-algebra B (Proposition 3.7.3). Every rational localization of a preperfectoid (A, A^+) is preperfectoid, so (A, A^+) is stably uniform, sheafy, and satisfies the Tate sheaf and Kiehl glueing properties (Theorem 3.7.4).
items.note: The v5 proof of Theorem 3.7.4 addresses only stable uniformity; that rational localizations are preperfectoid needs the identification of B ⊗̂_{Q_p} K with the corresponding rational localization of A ⊗̂_{Q_p} K (E38).

items.name: Finite étale algebras and tensor products of preperfectoid algebras
items.statement: If A is preperfectoid, every B ∈ FÉt(A) (with its Banach norm) is preperfectoid (Proposition 3.7.5). Completed tensor products of strongly preperfectoid (resp. relatively perfectoid) adic Banach algebras over Q_p are strongly preperfectoid (resp. relatively perfectoid) (Proposition 3.7.6); the argument fails for preperfectoid algebras.

items.name: Robba rings, bounded and integral Robba rings, the Amice field and their topologies
items.statement: Let K = Frac(W(k)) for a perfect field k of characteristic p, with the p-adic norm and the Witt Frobenius φ_K, and fix ω ∈ (0, 1). For r > 0, ℛ_K^r is the ring of Laurent series Σ_{i∈ℤ} c_i T^i (c_i ∈ K) with |c_i|ρ^i → 0 as i → ±∞ for every ρ ∈ [ω^r, 1), i.e. convergent on ω^r ≤ |T| < 1; ℛ_K^{int,r} ⊂ ℛ_K^r is the subring of series with all |c_i| ≤ 1, ℛ_K^{bd,r} = ℛ_K^{int,r}[p^{−1}], and ℛ_K^int, ℛ_K^bd, ℛ_K are the unions over r > 0. ℛ_K^int is a henselian but not complete local ring with residue field k((T̄)); the completion of the field ℛ_K^bd is the Amice field ℰ_K of series with sup_i |c_i| < ∞ and |c_i| → 0 as i → −∞; and the units of ℛ_K are exactly the nonzero elements of ℛ_K^bd (Newton polygons). Rings inside ℰ_K carry the p-adic topology of the Gauss norm and the weak topology (bounded sequences converging T-adically modulo each p^n), for both of which ℰ_K is complete; rings inside ℛ_K^r carry the Fréchet topology of the ω^s-Gauss norms, s ∈ (0, r], for which ℛ_K^r is complete; ℛ_K carries the LF topology, the locally convex direct limit of the ℛ_K^r. A formal series Σ c_i T^i converges in ℰ_K for the weak (not the p-adic) topology, in ℛ_K^r for the Fréchet topology and in ℛ_K for the LF topology, and a p-adically bounded sequence in ℛ_K^{bd,r} converging for the ω^r-Gauss norm converges weakly.
items.note: RD.0 nodes robba-ring, bounded-robba-ring and units-of-robba-ring; PadicHodgeTheory P7:annulus-foundations nodes robba-ring, amice-ring, bounded-robba-ring and frechet-topology (the annulus rings, Gauss norms and Fréchet and LF topologies).

items.name: Frobenius lifts, φ-modules, degree, slope and purity over the Robba rings
items.statement: A Frobenius lift on ℛ_K is an endomorphism φ(Σ c_i T^i) = Σ φ_K(c_i) u^i for some u ∈ ℛ_K^int with |u − T^p| < 1; it acts on ℛ_K^int, ℛ_K^bd and ℰ_K, carries ℛ_K^r into ℛ_K^{r/p} for small r (not ℛ_K^r into itself), and is continuous for all the topologies above. For R ∈ {ℛ_K^int, ℛ_K^bd, ℛ_K, 𝔬_{ℰ_K}, ℰ_K}, a φ-module over R is a finite free R-module M with an R-linear isomorphism φ^*M ≅ M. Its degree deg(M) is minus the p-adic valuation of the determinant of the matrix of φ on a basis (independent of the basis), its slope is μ(M) = deg(M)/rank(M) for M ≠ 0, and for s = c/d ∈ ℚ (d > 0) M is pure of slope s if p^c φ^d acts on some basis via a matrix U with U and U^{−1} of Gauss norm at most 1; this forces μ(M) = s, and étale means pure of slope 0 (every nonzero φ-module over ℛ_K^int or 𝔬_{ℰ_K} is étale). If M is pure of slope s, its dual is pure of slope −s. For a φ^d-module the degree is minus the p-adic valuation of the determinant of the matrix of φ^d, divided by d, so it is unchanged on restriction to φ^{de} (Convention 4.1.13 as printed omits the minus sign; see finding E130). This sign convention for degrees is opposite to the first author's earlier papers and agrees with geometric invariant theory (𝒪(1) has degree +1), Hartl–Pink and Fargues–Fontaine.
items.note: RD.0/frobenius-lift-on-robba-ring; RD.1 nodes frobenius-module, degree-and-slope and isoclinic-frobenius-module. The RD packet follows Kedlaya's earlier convention (degree = the valuation of the determinant, semistability with reversed inequalities), so its degrees are the negatives of these; the blueprint must fix one convention.

items.name: Pure φ-modules descend from ℛ_K to ℛ_K^bd
items.statement: For each s ∈ ℚ: (a) M ↦ M ⊗_{ℛ_K^bd} ℰ_K is a fully faithful functor from φ-modules over ℛ_K^bd pure of slope s to φ-modules over ℰ_K pure of slope s; (b) M ↦ M ⊗_{ℛ_K^bd} ℛ_K is an equivalence between φ-modules over ℛ_K^bd pure of slope s and φ-modules over ℛ_K pure of slope s. Nothing is claimed for maps between pure modules of different slopes: an exact sequence 0 → M_1 → M → M_2 → 0 over ℛ_K with M_1, M_2 of rank 1 and slopes −m, m and M étale (as for trianguline representations) cannot descend to ℛ_K^bd, since there are no nonzero maps between pure φ-modules over ℛ_K^bd of different slopes.
items.note: RD.2/isoclinic-descent-to-bounded-robba-ring (b)–(c). The proof is by reference to Kedlaya, Slope filtrations for relative Frobenius, Proposition 1.2.7 and Theorem 1.6.5, or to the reduction of Remark 4.3.4.

items.name: Slope filtration theorem over the Robba ring (Kedlaya)
items.statement: Let M be a nonzero φ-module over ℛ_K with μ(M) = s. Then M is pure of slope s if and only if M has no nonzero proper φ-submodule of slope greater than s. Every nonzero φ-module M over ℛ_K has a unique filtration 0 = M_0 ⊂ M_1 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ M_l = M by saturated φ-submodules with each M_i/M_{i−1} pure and μ(M_1/M_0) > ⋯ > μ(M_l/M_{l−1}).
items.note: RD.2/slope-filtration-for-frobenius-modules-statement and RD.1/semistability-and-harder-narasimhan-filtration. Proved by reference to Kedlaya, Slope filtrations for relative Frobenius, Theorem 1.7.1. With this paper's sign convention the slopes decrease along the filtration; with RD's they increase.

items.name: Extended Robba rings of a perfect analytic field
items.statement: Let L be a perfect analytic field of characteristic p with norm α. For r > 0, ℛ̃_L^{int,r} is the set of x = Σ_{i≥0} p^i [x̄_i] ∈ W(L) with p^{−i} α(x̄_i)^r → 0; it is a ring (by homogeneity of Witt vector addition) on which λ(α^s)(x) = max_i p^{−i} α(x̄_i)^s is a multiplicative norm for each s ∈ [0, r]. Put ℛ̃_L^{bd,r} = ℛ̃_L^{int,r}[p^{−1}], let ℛ̃_L^r be the Fréchet completion of ℛ̃_L^{bd,r} for the norms λ(α^s), s ∈ (0, r], and let ℛ̃_L^int, ℛ̃_L^bd, ℛ̃_L be the unions over r > 0. Then ℛ̃_L^int is a henselian, not complete, local ring with residue field L, the completion of the field ℛ̃_L^bd is ℰ̃_L = W(L)[p^{−1}] (also ℰ̃_L^int = W(L)), and ℛ̃_L is the extended Robba ring with residue field L.
items.note: RD.0 nodes analytic-ring, witt-partial-valuations and overconvergent-witt-vectors-henselian: Kedlaya's rings Γ^ℓ_an,r and Γ^ℓ_an,con of Slope filtrations revisited, for ℓ = L perfect with O = ℤ_p, are these rings. Review: Optional additional citation: Tau Ceti AdicSpaces Layer 6.3 plans, for 'F a complete rank-one nonarchimedean perfect field of characteristic p', 'Kedlaya's interval ring B^I and the norm λ_I = max(λ_s,λ_r)' — the ring ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_L of this item (and the field case of items 179, 188, 202).

items.name: Convexity, boundedness and units of the extended Robba ring
items.statement: For x ∈ ℛ̃_L^r, the function s ↦ log λ(α^s)(x) is continuous and convex on (0, r]. An element x ∈ ℛ̃_L lies in ℛ̃_L^bd if and only if λ(α^s)(x) is bounded for s ∈ (0, r] for some r > 0. Consequently the units of ℛ̃_L are exactly the nonzero elements of ℛ̃_L^bd.
items.note: RD.0/units-of-analytic-ring (units are the elements without slopes, lying in Γ_con[π^{−1}]); Lemma 4.2.4 is Kedlaya, Slope filtrations revisited, Corollary 2.5.6, whose erratum the RD packet records (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology/E25). The convexity is the Hadamard three-circles property.

items.name: The extended Robba rings are Bézout domains
items.statement: ℛ̃_L^r and ℛ̃_L are Bézout domains (integral domains in which every finitely generated ideal is principal). For 0 < s ≤ r, the completion ℛ̃_L^{[s,r]} of ℛ̃_L^r for max{λ(α^r), λ(α^s)} is a principal ideal domain, even a Euclidean domain.
items.note: RD.0 nodes analytic-ring-bezout and closed-interval-analytic-ring-pid (Kedlaya, Slope filtrations revisited, Theorem 2.9.6 and Proposition 2.6.8; the RD packet records that proposition's erratum, PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology/E2).

items.name: Newton polygons and slopes of elements of ℛ̃_L^r
items.statement: For nonzero x ∈ ℛ̃_L^r, its Newton polygon is the convex dual of f_x(t) = log λ(α^t)(x); the slopes of x are the t at which f_x changes slope, with multiplicity the width of the corresponding segment (the multiplicity of r is its multiplicity as a slope of any y ∈ ℛ̃_L^s, s > r, with λ(α^r)(x − y) < λ(α^r)(x), independent of y). (a) For x = yz, the multiplicity of each s ∈ (0, r] as a slope of x is the sum of its multiplicities for y and z. (b) x ∈ ℛ̃_L^r is a unit of ℛ̃_L^r if and only if it has no slopes.
items.note: RD.0 nodes analytic-ring-slope-additivity and units-of-analytic-ring.

items.name: Frobenius on the extended Robba rings and its invariants
items.statement: The Witt vector Frobenius φ acts on ℛ̃_L^int and extends by continuity to ℛ̃_L^bd, ℛ̃_L and ℰ̃_L, with λ(α^s)(φ(x)) = λ(α^{ps})(x) for x ∈ ℛ̃_L and s > 0; φ-modules (and φ^d-modules), degrees, slopes, purity and étaleness over these rings are defined as over ℛ_K. Moreover ℰ̃_L^φ = ℛ̃_L^φ = ℚ_p, and for a ≥ 1 the φ^a-invariants of ℰ̃_L and of ℛ̃_L are both W(L^{φ^a})[p^{−1}] (corrected, finding E39: this is the unramified extension of ℚ_p with residue field 𝔽_{p^a} when 𝔽_{p^a} ⊆ L, for instance when L is algebraically closed).
items.note: Finding E39 corrects the lemma's last sentence. Hypothesis 4.2.1 assumes only that L is a perfect analytic field of characteristic p (not algebraically closed, and not containing F_{p^a}), so the correction is needed as stated.

items.name: Pure φ-modules descend from ℛ̃_L to ℛ̃_L^bd, and the slope filtration over ℛ̃_L
items.statement: For each s ∈ ℚ: (a) M ↦ M ⊗_{ℛ̃_L^bd} ℰ̃_L is fully faithful from φ-modules over ℛ̃_L^bd pure of slope s to φ-modules over ℰ̃_L pure of slope s (it is also essentially surjective, Theorem 8.5.3); (b) M ↦ M ⊗_{ℛ̃_L^bd} ℛ̃_L is an equivalence between φ-modules over ℛ̃_L^bd pure of slope s and φ-modules over ℛ̃_L pure of slope s. A nonzero φ-module M over ℛ̃_L with μ(M) = s is pure of slope s iff it has no nonzero proper φ-submodule of slope greater than s; every nonzero M has a unique filtration by saturated φ-submodules with pure quotients of strictly decreasing slopes, which is the Harder–Narasimhan filtration for the degree μ(∧^{rank M} M) and is multiplicative under tensor products. For an extension L′ of perfect analytic fields with compatible norms, M is pure of slope s iff M ⊗_{ℛ̃_L} ℛ̃_{L′} is.
items.locator: §4.2, Proposition 4.2.11, Theorems 4.2.12–4.2.13, Corollary 4.2.14 and Remark 4.2.18, pp. 108–110
items.note: RD.2 nodes isoclinic-descent-to-bounded-robba-ring and slope-filtration-for-frobenius-modules-statement (stated for Γ^E_an,con with enough units, with base change (c)); RD.1/semistability-and-harder-narasimhan-filtration. Proofs by reference to Kedlaya, Slope filtrations revisited, Theorem 6.3.3, Proposition 6.3.5, Corollary 6.4.3 and Theorem 6.4.1.

items.name: Dieudonné–Manin classification over ℛ̃_L for L algebraically closed
items.statement: Suppose L is algebraically closed. If M is a φ-module over ℰ̃_L (resp. ℛ̃_L^bd) pure of slope s = c/d (d > 0), then for any basis on which p^c φ^d acts via an invertible matrix over W(L) (resp. ℛ̃_L^int), the W(L)-span (resp. ℛ̃_L^int-span) of that basis has another basis fixed by p^c φ^d. For any φ-module M over ℛ̃_L there are d > 0 and a basis on which φ^d acts via a diagonal matrix with entries in p^ℤ (using the surjectivity of x ↦ φ^d(x) − p^c x on ℛ̃_L for c, d > 0).
items.note: RD.1 nodes dieudonne-manin-over-extended-robba-ring and rank-one-frobenius-modules; RD.2/isoclinic-descent-to-bounded-robba-ring (a) (bases of eigenvectors over an algebraically closed field). Proofs by reference to Fontaine (A1.2.6) and Kedlaya, Slope filtrations revisited, Propositions 3.3.7(c) and 4.5.3, and Slope filtrations for relative Frobenius, Proposition 2.5.8.

items.name: Corrections to Kedlaya, Slope filtrations revisited, §§2.5–2.6
items.statement: The paper records corrections not in the printed erratum of Kedlaya, Slope filtrations revisited (Doc. Math. 10 (2005)): in Lemma 2.5.3(a) i ∈ ℤ should be i ≥ 0, with n replaced by i in the proofs of (a) and (c); Lemma 2.5.4 needs r > 0; in Corollary 2.5.6 v_{j,n} should be v_{j,r}; Lemma 2.5.11 needs r ∈ I; the displayed inequalities in the proof of Lemma 2.6.3 are replaced by bounds of the form v_{n,r}(·) ≥ min{w_r(y_l) + (1 − r/r_0), min_{n′>n} v_{n′,r}(y_l)} (n ≥ m), with the last paragraph rewritten accordingly; in Remark 2.6.4 'on K' should be 'on 𝒪'; a sentence of the proof of Lemma 2.6.7 is completed; and the proof of Proposition 2.6.8 should cite Proposition 2.6.5.
items.note: Corrections of another paper, in print here. The RD packet already records them from Kedlaya's 'Additional errata for Slope filtrations revisited' (12 February 2013): PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology/E2 and E23–E29. The RD.0 nodes built on §§2.5–2.6 of that paper (witt-partial-valuations, analytic-ring, closed-interval-analytic-ring-pid) must use the corrected statements.

items.name: The embedding of the Robba ring into the extended Robba ring
items.statement: Equip k((T̄)) with the T̄-adic norm α, α(T̄) = ω, and let L be its completed perfection. Proceeding as for the perfection of a Frobenius lift, one obtains s_φ : ℰ_K → ℰ̃_L, which identifies ℰ̃_L with the completion of the direct perfection of ℰ_K for the weak topology. For r > 0 so small that the ω^{r/p}-Gauss norm of φ(T)/T^p − 1 is less than 1, s_φ maps ℛ_K^{int,r} into ℛ̃_L^{int,r} isometrically for the ω^r-Gauss norm and λ(α^r), giving a φ-equivariant homomorphism ℛ_K → ℛ̃_L. For φ(T) = (T + 1)^p − 1 and ω = p^{−p/(p−1)}, s_φ is isometric for the ω^r-Gauss norm for all r ∈ (0, 1).
items.note: RD.0/frobenius-equivariant-embedding (the σ-equivariant embedding of ℛ^int, ℛ^bd, ℰ and ℛ into the Witt-vector rings over the perfection); isometry is Kedlaya, Slope filtrations revisited, Lemma 2.3.5.

items.name: Étale φ-modules over 𝔬_ℰ and ℛ^int are trivialized over the extended rings
items.statement: Let L′ be the completed direct perfection of 𝔬_{ℰ̂_K^unr}/(p), which is algebraically closed, and view ℰ̂_K^unr inside ℰ̃_{L′}. (a) For an étale φ-module M over 𝔬_{ℰ_K}, V = (M ⊗ 𝔬_{ℰ̂_K^unr})^φ satisfies V ⊗_{ℤ_p} 𝔬_{ℰ̂_K^unr} ≅ M ⊗ 𝔬_{ℰ̂_K^unr}. (b) For an étale φ-module M over ℛ_K^int, V = (M ⊗ (𝔬_{ℰ̂_K^unr} ∩ ℛ̃_{L′}^int))^φ satisfies V ⊗_{ℤ_p} (𝔬_{ℰ̂_K^unr} ∩ ℛ̃_{L′}^int) ≅ M ⊗ (𝔬_{ℰ̂_K^unr} ∩ ℛ̃_{L′}^int), and V ⊗_{ℤ_p} ℚ_p = (M ⊗ ℛ̃_{L′})^φ = (M ⊗ ℰ̃_{L′})^φ. Since Hom(M_1, M_2) = M_1^∨ ⊗ M_2 is étale when M_1, M_2 are pure of the same slope, Propositions 4.1.8 and 4.2.11 reduce to these trivializations.
items.note: RD.2 nodes isoclinic-descent-to-bounded-robba-ring (a) and slope-zero-eigenvectors-descend-to-overconvergent (de Jong) for (b); PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology PG.1 (Fontaine's equivalence for étale φ-modules) for (a). PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology PG.1 (Fontaine's equivalence for étale φ-modules) plans (a) only in the cyclotomic case (A_K for K finite over ℚ_p, residue field k finite, the cyclotomic Frobenius lift); part (a) for K = Frac W(k) with k an arbitrary perfect field and an arbitrary Frobenius lift (Katz's trivialization of unit-root φ-modules over 𝔬_{ℰ̂^unr}) is not stated in any RD or PG node.

items.name: Purity and semistability are unchanged by base extension from ℛ_K to ℛ̃_L
items.statement: A pure φ-module over ℛ_K stays pure over ℛ̃_L, and a φ-module over ℛ_K whose base extension to ℛ̃_L is semistable (has no nonzero proper φ-submodule of larger slope) is itself semistable. The reverse implications also hold; they are part of the proof of Theorem 4.1.9, which is reduced to Theorem 4.2.12, either by explicit calculation (Slope filtrations revisited) or by faithfully flat descent (Slope filtrations for relative Frobenius, §3).
items.note: RD.2/slope-filtration-for-frobenius-modules-statement (c) (compatibility with base change). Remark 4.3.6 corrects the statement and proof of Kedlaya, Slope filtrations for relative Frobenius (Astérisque 319), Proposition 3.3.2: M should only be an R-module with φ^*M ≅ M, not a φ-module; the conclusion gives N finite locally free (not free) with φ^*N ≅ N, by SGA 1 XIII 1.1 and VIII 1.10 in place of VIII 1.3; this suffices there because the rings are Bézout. That paper is not otherwise used in the atlas.

items.name: Relative extended Robba rings of a perfect uniform adic Banach 𝔽_p-algebra
items.statement: From here on (R, R⁺) is a perfect uniform adic Banach 𝔽_p-algebra with spectral norm α, and R is a Banach algebra over some analytic field (no restriction up to changing the norm within its topology). For ∗ ∈ {R, R⁺} put ℰ̃^int_∗ = W(∗), ℰ̃_∗ = W(∗)[p^{−1}]; for r > 0 let ℛ̃^{int,r}_∗ be the ring of x = Σ_{i≥0} p^i [x̄_i] ∈ W(∗) with p^{−i}α(x̄_i)^r → 0, with the power-multiplicative norms λ(α^s)(x) = max_i p^{−i}α(x̄_i)^s (s ∈ (0, r]); ℛ̃^{bd,r}_∗ = ℛ̃^{int,r}_∗[p^{−1}]; ℛ̃^r_∗ the Fréchet completion of ℛ̃^{bd,r}_∗ for the λ(α^s), s ∈ (0, r]; ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_∗ (0 < s ≤ r) the completion for the λ(α^t), t ∈ [s, r], a Banach ring for max{λ(α^r), λ(α^s)}; and ℛ̃^int_∗, ℛ̃^bd_∗, ℛ̃_∗ the unions over r. The rings ℰ̃^int_{R⁺}, ℛ̃^{int,r}_{R⁺}, ℛ̃^int_{R⁺} all equal W(R⁺) =: ℛ̃^{int,+}_R (and similarly ℛ̃^{bd,+}_R = W(R⁺)[p^{−1}]), and ℛ̃^+_R is the Fréchet completion of ℛ̃^{bd,+}_R for all λ(α^s), s > 0, in general strictly smaller than ℛ̃^∞_R = ∩_r ℛ̃^r_R. ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R is a Banach ℚ_p-algebra; ℛ̃^{int,r}_R is a Banach ring (not over a field) in which [z̄] is a topologically nilpotent (uniform) unit for any such z̄ ∈ R; ℛ̃^r_R = lim_s ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R behaves like a Fréchet–Stein algebra. For x ∈ W(R)[p^{−1}], the p-adic absolute value of its image in W(ℋ(β))[p^{−1}] is lower semicontinuous in β ∈ ℳ(R), and continuous when x is a unit.
items.locator: §5.0–5.1, Hypothesis 5.0.1, Remark 5.0.2, Definition 5.1.1 and Remarks 5.1.8–5.1.9, pp. 113–116
items.note: RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0:annuli constructs the annulus rings as rational localizations of Spa W(R⁺) for perfectoid S (node radius-function-and-rational-annuli, following Fargues–Scholze II.1.16); these Witt-vector norm descriptions, for any perfect uniform R, are not stated there. The field case R = L (a perfect analytic field) of the annulus rings and norms is planned upstream: tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-6-the-adic-farguesfontaine-curve, §6.3 'For a closed interval I=[s,r] ⊂ (0,∞), define Kedlaya's interval ring B^I and the norm λ_I = max(λ_s,λ_r)' with 'F a complete rank-one nonarchimedean perfect field of characteristic p'. RF0 plans W_OE(R) and the annulus rings (as rational localizations) for perfectoid S — which, by Hypothesis 5.0.1, is KL's generality — but not the Robba rings ℛ̃^r, ℛ̃^bd, ℛ̃, ℛ̃⁺ with their Witt-vector norms; status stays missing.

items.name: The norms λ(β) and the seminorms μ(γ) on relative Witt rings
items.statement: Let 0 < s ≤ r. (a) ℛ̃^{int,r}_R is a ring on which λ(α^s) is a power-multiplicative norm, multiplicative if α is. (b) For β a submultiplicative (resp. power-multiplicative, multiplicative) (semi)norm on R dominated by max{α^s, α^r}, λ(β)(Σ p^i[x̄_i]) = max_i p^{−i}β(x̄_i) is a submultiplicative (resp. power-multiplicative, multiplicative) (semi)norm on ℛ̃^{int,r}_R dominated by max{λ(α^s), λ(α^r)}. (c) If β is power-multiplicative (resp. multiplicative), λ(β) extends to such a (semi)norm on ℛ̃^{bd,r}_R and by continuity to ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R. (d) For γ a power-multiplicative (resp. multiplicative) (semi)norm on ℛ̃^{int,r}_R dominated by max{λ(α^s), λ(α^r)}, μ(γ)(x̄) = γ([x̄]) is such a (semi)norm on R dominated by max{α^s, α^r}, and γ is dominated by λ(μ(γ)).
items.note: Extends Kedlaya, Nonarchimedean geometry of Witt vectors, Lemmas 4.1 and 4.4 and Theorem 4.5; the absolute case is checkpoint 1's route to RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0.

items.name: Topologies on the relative Robba rings and functoriality
items.statement: Rings inside ℰ̃_R carry the p-adic topology (Gauss norm) and the weak topology (bounded and convergent under λ(α) modulo each p^n), for both of which ℰ̃_R is complete; rings inside ℛ̃^r_R carry the Fréchet topology of the λ(α^s), s ∈ (0, r], for which ℛ̃^r_R is complete; rings inside ℛ̃_R carry the LF topology. A p-adically bounded sequence in ℛ̃^{bd,r}_R convergent under λ(α^r) converges weakly. If α is trivial (for instance if R is generated by idempotents, equivalently φ̄ = id on R) the rings ℰ̃_R, ℛ̃^bd_R, ℛ̃_R coincide and all these topologies are the p-adic one. The constructions are functorial for bounded homomorphisms R → S of perfect uniform Banach 𝔽_p-algebras; a strict injection (hence isometry) induces strict injections, and a strict surjection induces strict surjections, for all these topologies: lifting Teichmüller coordinates, each y ∈ ℛ̃^{int,r}_S lifts to x ∈ ℛ̃^{int,r}_R with λ(α^s)(x) ≤ c^r λ(β^s)(y) for s ∈ (0, r] (corrected, finding E40).
items.note: Finding E40 corrects the ring into which y is lifted.

items.name: Generators extend to a rational neighbourhood
items.statement: Let 0 < s ≤ r and M a finite projective ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R-module. If e_1, …, e_n ∈ M generate M ⊗ ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_{ℋ(β)} for some β ∈ ℳ(R), then they generate M ⊗ ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_{R′} for some rational localization (R, R⁺) → (R′, R′⁺) encircling β.

items.name: Convexity, bounded elements, units and φ-invariants of the relative Robba rings
items.statement: For x ∈ ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R, t ↦ log λ(α^t)(x) is continuous and convex, so max{λ(α^r), λ(α^s)} = sup_{t∈[s,r]} λ(α^t). An x ∈ ℛ̃_R lies in ℛ̃^bd_R iff λ(α^s)(x) is bounded for s ∈ (0, r] for some r > 0; hence every unit of ℛ̃_R is a unit of ℛ̃^bd_R. Moreover ℰ̃^φ_R = ℛ̃^φ_R = W(R^{φ̄})[p^{−1}], which is ℚ_p iff R is connected.

items.name: Restriction maps, intersections and splittings of the relative Robba rings
items.statement: (a) For 0 < s_1 ≤ s_2 ≤ r_2 ≤ r_1, restriction ℛ̃^{[s_1,r_1]}_R → ℛ̃^{[s_2,r_2]}_R is injective (R embeds in ∏_{β∈ℳ(R)} ℋ(β) and one reduces to fields). (b) For 0 < r ≤ r′, ℛ̃^{int,r}_R ∩ ℛ̃^{[r,r′]}_R = ℛ̃^{int,r′}_R inside ℛ̃^{[r,r]}_R. (c) For 0 < s ≤ r and n ∈ ℤ, every x ∈ ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R is y + z with y ∈ p^n ℛ̃^{int,r}_R, z ∈ ∩_{r′≥r} ℛ̃^{[s,r′]}_R and λ(α^t)(z) ≤ p^{(1−n)(1−t/r)} λ(α^r)(x)^{t/r} for t ≥ r. (d) For c < 1 and 0 < s ≤ r, every x ∈ ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R is y + z with y ∈ ℛ̃^{bd,r}_R ∩ p^n ℛ̃^{int,r}_R for n = ⌈−log_p(λ(α^s)(x) c^{−s})⌉, z ∈ ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_{R⁺}, λ(α^t)(y), λ(α^t)(z) ≤ λ(α^t)(x) for t ∈ [s, r] and λ(α^t)(z) ≤ c^{t−r} λ(α^r)(z) for t > r (the printed ᾱ is undefined notation for the spectral norm α; see finding E132); so for q = p^a, λ(α^t)(φ^{−a}(y)) ≤ c^{−(q−1)t/q} λ(α^t)(x) and λ(α^t)(φ^a(z)) ≤ c^{(q−1)t} λ(α^t)(x). (e) For 0 < s ≤ s′ ≤ r ≤ r′, ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R ∩ ℛ̃^{[s′,r′]}_R = ℛ̃^{[s,r′]}_R inside ℛ̃^{[s′,r]}_R. (f) For strict inclusions R ⊆ S′, S″ ⊆ S with S′ ∩ S″ = R, the corresponding intersections of Witt-type rings recover those of R, and also of ℛ̃^{[s,r]}, ℛ̃^r, ℛ̃^+, ℛ̃ when S′ ⊕ S″ → S is strict.
items.note: Findings E41 and E42 correct signs in the proofs of Lemmas 5.2.8 and 5.2.10. Remark 5.2.14 leaves open whether boundedness can be tested at the points of ℳ(R).

items.name: The plus ring ℛ̃⁺_R and the eigenvectors of φ^d
items.statement: Suppose R⁺ = 𝔬_R. (a) x ∈ ℛ̃^∞_R lies in ℛ̃⁺_R iff limsup_{r→∞} λ(α^r)(x)^{1/r} ≤ 1. (b) Every x ∈ ℛ̃^r_R is y + z with y ∈ ℛ̃^{bd,r}_R and z ∈ ℛ̃⁺_R. (c) ℛ̃^{int,r}_R ∩ ℛ̃⁺_R = ℛ̃^{int,+}_R. For general R⁺ and n ≥ 0, d > 0, q = p^d, r > 0: the elements x with φ^d(x) = p^n x are the same in ℛ̃⁺_R, in ℛ̃_R and in ℛ̃^{[r/q,r]}_R.
items.note: Finding E43 (corrected in the authors' errata) fixes a display in the proof of Corollary 5.2.12. These eigenspaces are the global sections of 𝒪(n) on the relative Fargues–Fontaine curve (§§6.3 and 8.7), which RelativeFarguesFontaine RF3 and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB1 consume.

items.name: The relative Robba rings form sheaves on Spa(R, R⁺)
items.statement: For ∗ among ℰ̃^int, ℰ̃, ℛ̃^{int,r}, ℛ̃^{int,+}, ℛ̃^int, ℛ̃^{bd,r}, ℛ̃^{bd,+}, ℛ̃^bd, ℛ̃^{[s,r]}, ℛ̃^r, ℛ̃^+, ℛ̃, the presheaf on Spa(R, R⁺) sending an open U to lim ∗_S over rational localizations (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) with Spa(S, S⁺) ⊆ U is a sheaf; for ∗ = ℰ̃^int, ℰ̃, ℛ̃^{int,r}, ℛ̃^int, ℛ̃^{bd,r}, ℛ̃^bd, ℛ̃^{[s,r]}, ℛ̃^r, ℛ̃ it is acyclic (Tate sheaf property). The key input: for a simple Laurent covering of Spa(R, R⁺) the sequence 0 → R → R_1 ⊕ R_2 → R_{12} → 0 stays exact, with almost optimal maps, after applying ℰ̃^int, ℰ̃, ℛ̃^{int,r}, ℛ̃^{bd,r}, ℛ̃^{[s,r]} (for the indicated norms) or ℛ̃^r.
items.note: Sheaf property in the base variable, as RelativeFarguesFontaine RF1 needs to glue Y_S over covers of S.

items.name: Seminorms on ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R and their radius
items.statement: Let 0 < s ≤ r. (a) A multiplicative seminorm β on ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R is dominated by max{λ(α^s), λ(α^r)} iff it is dominated by λ(α^t) for a unique t ∈ [s, r]. (b) For such β and t, with γ = μ(β)^{1/t} ∈ ℳ(R), β extends uniquely to a multiplicative seminorm on ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_{ℋ(γ)}.
items.note: The Gel'fand-spectrum form of the radius function of RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0:annuli/radius-function-and-rational-annuli.

items.name: Kiehl glueing for ℰ̃^int and ℛ̃^{int,r}
items.statement: For a simple Laurent covering of Spa(R, R⁺), the squares formed by R, R_1, R_2, R_{12} and by ℛ̃^{int,r}_R, ℛ̃^{int,r}_{R_1}, ℛ̃^{int,r}_{R_2}, ℛ̃^{int,r}_{R_{12}} are glueing squares; the sheaves ℰ̃^int and ℛ̃^{int,r} satisfy the Kiehl glueing property for finite projective modules. The argument for ℛ̃^{int,r} does not apply to ℰ̃^int (ℰ̃^int_{R_2} is dense in ℰ̃^int_{R_{12}} only weakly), which is handled by lifting modulo p; the Kiehl property fails for ℰ̃ and ℛ̃^{bd,r} (Example 8.5.17), although these rings are themselves sheafy.

items.name: The relative Robba rings are relatively perfectoid (Rodriguez)
items.statement: Let K be the completion of ℚ_p(p^{p^{−∞}}); every x ∈ A ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} K (A a Banach ℚ_p-algebra) is uniquely a convergent sum Σ x_i ⊗ p^i over i ∈ ℤ[p^{−1}] ∩ [0, 1), with tensor norm max_i |x_i| p^{−i}. For 0 < s ≤ r, the Banach rings ℰ̃_R, ℛ̃^{bd,r}_R and ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R are relatively perfectoid: their completed tensor products with any perfectoid algebra are uniform and perfectoid. Hence any adic Banach ring extending one of them is stably uniform and sheafy and satisfies the Tate sheaf and Kiehl glueing properties.
items.note: RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0:integral-Y (node chart-cover-perfectoidness-and-sheafiness, Fargues–Scholze II.1.1) plans the case of the single field K = E_∞, which gives sheafiness for perfectoid S; relative perfectoidness for every perfectoid algebra and every perfect uniform R is this paper's (from R. Rodriguez's thesis).

items.name: Rational localizations of the base lift to the relative Robba rings
items.statement: For 0 < s ≤ r, a semivaluation v on ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R defines (via Lemma 5.3.4) a valuation on R, giving μ : Spa(ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R, ℛ̃^{[s,r],+}_R) → Spa(R, R⁺), where ℛ̃^{[s,r],+}_R is the completion of the subring generated by the x with max{λ(α^s), λ(α^r)}(x) < 1 and the [ȳ], ȳ ∈ R⁺. For a rational localization (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺), the map (ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R, ℛ̃^{[s,r],+}_R) → (ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_S, ℛ̃^{[s,r],+}_S) is the rational localization representing μ^{−1}(Spa(S, S⁺)); so rational coverings of the base lift to rational coverings.
items.note: RF0:integral-Y/gluing-for-general-base (Fargues–Scholze II.1.3: open immersion and cartesian square for affinoid subsets of the base).

items.name: Kiehl glueing for ℛ̃^{[s,r]} and descent along covers of the interval
items.statement: The sheaf ℛ̃^{[s,r]} on Spa(R, R⁺) satisfies the Kiehl glueing property. For K a perfectoid field containing ℚ_p(p^{p^{−∞}}) with |K^×| = ℝ^+: the tensor norm on ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} K is power-multiplicative and this ring is perfectoid; for 0 < s ≤ s′ ≤ r′ ≤ r and z̄ ∈ R with α(z̄) < 1 and α(z̄)α(z̄^{−1}) = 1, the map to ℛ̃^{[s′,r′]}_R ⊗̂ K (with plus rings) is the rational localization {v([z̄]) ∈ [α(z̄)^{r′}, α(z̄)^{s′}]}; so for closed intervals with I = I_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ I_n these form a rational covering, and ℛ̃^I_R → ⊕_i ℛ̃^{I_i}_R is an effective descent morphism for finite projective modules over uniform Banach rings.
items.locator: §5.3, Theorem 5.3.13, Lemma 5.3.14, Corollary 5.3.15 and Theorem 5.3.16, p. 125
items.note: Used to glue φ-bundles over overlapping annuli in §6. RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0:annuli plans the annuli Y_{S,I} as rational subsets and RF4:vector-bundles the patching of bundles; the descent statement for these Banach rings is not stated there. Review (status changed from missing to planned): Under Hypothesis 5.0.1, R is a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p (kl.tex 6644ff with the analytic-field convention at 1497), so ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R is the ring of the affinoid annulus Y_{S,I} of RF0:annuli. VB1 plans the comparison of bundles on the annuli with finite projective modules and effective gluing for rational covers. That is Kiehl glueing on the affinoid Y_{S,I}, which covers both the interval coverings I = ∪ I_i (rational coverings of Y_{S,I}) and the rational coverings of the base S, which pull back to rational coverings of Y_{S,I} by RF0:annuli 'restriction' and RF0:integral-Y/gluing-for-general-base (open immersion, cartesian square). The auxiliary lemma that ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R ⊗̂ K is perfectoid for a perfectoid K with |K^×| = ℝ^+ is route detail, done by RF0's sousperfectoid argument (base change to E_∞).

items.name: The maps λ and μ between Gel'fand spectra, and the homotopy H
items.statement: Let λ : ℳ(R) → ℳ(ℛ̃^{int,1}_R) and μ : ℳ(ℛ̃^{int,1}_R) → ℳ(R) be as in Proposition 5.1.2. (a) λ and μ are continuous, and inverse images of finite unions of Weierstrass (resp. Laurent, rational) subdomains are of the same form. (b) μ∘λ = id. (c) (λ∘μ)(γ) ≥ γ. If ℳ(S) → ℳ(R) is surjective for a bounded map R → S of perfect uniform Banach 𝔽_p-algebras, so is ℳ(ℛ̃^{int,r}_S) → ℳ(ℛ̃^{int,r}_R). There is a family of multiplicative seminorms H(γ, t) (t ∈ [0, 1]) on ℛ̃^{int,r}_R with H(γ, 0) = γ, H(γ, 1) = (λ∘μ)(γ), μ(H(γ, t)) = μ(γ) and H(H(γ, t), u) = H(γ, max{t, u}), and H : ℳ(ℛ̃^{int,r}_R) × [0, 1] → ℳ(ℛ̃^{int,r}_R) is continuous.
items.locator: §5.4, Theorem 5.4.1, Lemma 5.4.2, Definition 5.4.3, Theorem 5.4.4 and Remark 5.4.5, pp. 126–127
items.note: Carries over Kedlaya, Nonarchimedean geometry of Witt vectors, Theorems 4.5 and 7.8, to the relative setting.

items.name: The radius fibration of the relative annuli and the quotient X_R
items.statement: Let T_R = ∪_{0<s<r} ℳ(ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R). (a) For each β ∈ T_R there is a unique t(β) ∈ (0, ∞) with α^{t(β)} dominating μ(β) (equivalently λ(α^{t(β)}) dominating β). (b) β ↦ (μ(β)^{1/t(β)}, t(β)) is a continuous map T_R → ℳ(R) × (0, ∞); in particular t is continuous. (c) (φ^*)^ℤ acts properly discontinuously on T_R with compact (Hausdorff) quotient X_R, mapping to ℳ(R) × S^1. (d) T_R → ℳ(R) × (0, ∞) and X_R → ℳ(R) × S^1 are strong deformation retracts. So when ℳ(R) is contractible (e.g. R = L an analytic field), X_R has the homotopy type of a circle with universal cover T_R and φ^* generating its deck group.
items.note: In §8.7, X_R is the maximal Hausdorff quotient of the relative Fargues–Fontaine curve. RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0:annuli (radius function) and RF1 (free, totally discontinuous φ-action and the quotient X_S) plan the adic analogues, not these Gel'fand-spectrum statements. Adic analogues of (a)–(c) are planned: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:annuli/radius-function-and-rational-annuli ('rad : |Y_S| -> (0,infty) ... factors through the Berkovich quotient of |Y_S| and satisfies rad(phi(x)) = q rad(x)'), RF1/frobenius-quotient-and-presentation, RF1/diamond-formula-and-map-to-base; the field case of the quotient is Tau Ceti AdicSpaces Layer 6.2 (𝒳 = 𝒴/φ^ℤ). The compact Hausdorff quotient X_R, the deformation retractions and the homotopy type are not planned; status stays missing.

items.name: Finite étale algebras over R, W(R) and the integral Robba rings correspond
items.statement: Every S ∈ FÉt(R) is a finite Banach R-algebra and a perfect uniform Banach 𝔽_p-algebra. If x_1, …, x_n ∈ ℛ̃^int_S reduce modulo p to generators of S over R, they generate ℛ̃^{int,r}_S over ℛ̃^{int,r}_R for small r. For r > 0 the base extensions φ^{−1}-FÉt(ℛ̃^{int,r}_R) → FÉt(ℛ̃^int_R) → FÉt(W(R)) → FÉt(R) are tensor equivalences ((ℛ̃^int_R, (p)) is henselian), where φ^{−1}-FÉt denotes finite étale algebras with an isomorphism to their φ^{−1}-pullback, and S ↦ ℛ̃^{int,r}_S is a quasi-inverse. For z ∈ W(𝔬_R) primitive of degree 1, r ≥ 1 and A = W(𝔬_R)[[z̄]^{−1}]/(z) = ℛ̃^{int,r}_R/(z), the base extensions φ^{−1}-FÉt(ℛ̃^{int,r}_R) → FÉt(A) and FÉt(R), and the equivalence FÉt(R) ≅ FÉt(A) of Theorem 3.6.21, 2-commute; all are tensor equivalences.
items.locator: §5.5, Convention 5.5.1, Lemma 5.5.2, Proposition 5.5.3, Corollary 5.5.6 and Remark 5.5.7, pp. 128–132
items.note: Finding E44 corrects a phrase in the proof of Proposition 5.5.3. PerfectoidSpaces P3 plans the tilting equivalence on finite étale algebras (item 166); the passage through φ^{−1}-equivariant finite étale algebras over the Robba rings is not stated there.

items.name: Finite étale maps of the base give finite étale maps of the relative Robba rings
items.statement: For S a (faithfully) finite étale R-algebra and ∗ ∈ {ℰ̃, ℛ̃^{int,r}, ℛ̃^int, ℛ̃^{bd,r}, ℛ̃^bd, ℛ̃^{[s,r]}, ℛ̃^r, ℛ̃}, the map ∗_R → ∗_S is (faithfully) finite étale; in particular ℛ̃^r_R ⊗_{ℛ̃^{bd,r}_R} ℛ̃^{bd,r}_S → ℛ̃^r_S is an isometric isomorphism for λ(α^r).
items.note: Finding E45 corrects the list of cases in the proof.

items.name: Reduction of the period rings modulo a primitive element
items.statement: Let z ∈ W(R⁺) be primitive of degree 1 with z − [z̄] ∈ pW(R⁺)^×, and r ≥ 1. (a) Every x ∈ ℛ̃^{int,r}_R/(z) lifts to y = Σ p^i [ȳ_i] ∈ W(R) with α(ȳ_0) ≥ α(ȳ_i) for all i. (b) For any closed interval I ⊂ (0, ∞) containing 1 and any m ≥ 1, all the maps among W(R⁺)[[z̄]^{−1}] = W(𝔬_R)[[z̄]^{−1}], their p-localizations, W(R⁺)[p^{−1}], W(𝔬_R)[p^{−1}], ℛ̃^{int,r}_R, ℛ̃^{bd,r}_{R⁺} → ℛ̃^{bd,r}_{𝔬_R} → ℛ̃^{bd,r}_R and ℛ̃^I_{R⁺} → ℛ̃^I_{𝔬_R} → ℛ̃^I_R (and ℛ̃^{bd,r}_R → ℛ̃^I_R when I ⊆ (0, r]) become isomorphisms modulo z^m.
items.note: Findings E46 (corrected in the authors' errata) and E47 concern the proof of (b). The quotient by z is the untilt; RelativeFarguesFontaine RF2:untilts plans the untilt divisor and its completions (nodes closed-cartier-divisor-norm-estimate and BdR-completion-and-filtration), not this comparison.

items.name: Almost modules, almost finite projective and almost finite étale algebras
items.statement: Let A be a uniform Banach algebra with its spectral norm such that for each ε > 1 there is λ ∈ A with 1 < |λ| < ε and |λ||λ^{−1}| = 1 (e.g. A over a nondiscretely normed analytic field). An 𝔬_A-module is almost zero if killed by 𝔪_A, and almost 𝔬_A-modules form the localization at morphisms with almost zero kernel and cokernel. An A-module B is almost finite projective if for each t ∈ 𝔪_A there are a finite free F and maps B → F → B composing to t, uniformly almost finite projective if F can always be taken of a fixed rank m; for B almost finite projective there is an almost trace B → A, and B is almost finite étale if the trace pairing gives an almost isomorphism B → Hom_A(B, A) (equivalent to Gabber–Ramero's definition by their Theorem 4.1.14).
items.note: PerfectoidSpaces P0 (almost mathematics: almost finite projective, uniformly almost finite projective and almost finite étale algebras, and the trace).

items.name: Almost purity (Kedlaya–Liu, Scholze)
items.statement: Let A be a perfectoid algebra. For every B ∈ FÉt(A), 𝔬_B is uniformly almost finite projective and almost étale over 𝔬_A. The proof applies φ^{−n} to a splitting and to the trace pairing of ℛ̃^{int,1}_S over ℛ̃^{int,1}_R and reduces modulo y_n = [z̄^{−p^{−n}}]z, using Lemma 5.5.5; unlike Faltings's original theorem it does not refer to toric coordinates.
items.note: PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-purity-theorem.

items.name: φ^a-modules, models, φ^a-modules over annuli and φ^a-bundles
items.statement: Fix a > 0 and q = p^a. A φ^a-module over W(R), ℰ̃_R, ℛ̃^int_R, ℛ̃^bd_R, ℛ̃_R, ℛ̃⁺_R or ℛ̃^∞_R is a finite locally free module with a semilinear φ^a-action (trivial if it is a sum of copies of the ring); for ∗ ∈ {ℛ̃^int, ℛ̃^bd, ℛ̃} such a module over ∗_R descends uniquely to its model M_r over ∗^r_R with (φ^a)^*M_r ≅ M_r ⊗ ∗^{r/q}_R. For 0 < s ≤ r/q, a φ^a-module over ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R is a finite locally free M with (φ^a)^*M ⊗ ℛ̃^{[s,r/q]}_R ≅ M ⊗ ℛ̃^{[s,r/q]}_R. A φ^a-bundle over ℛ̃_R is a compatible family of φ^a-modules M_I over ℛ̃^I_R for all I = [s, r] with 0 < s ≤ r/q, with isomorphisms ψ_{I,I′} for I′ ⊆ I satisfying the cocycle condition; it extends to all closed I ⊂ (0, ∞), and its global sections form a φ^a-stable module. Kernels of surjections of φ^a-modules (resp. bundles) are again φ^a-modules (resp. bundles). For 0 < s ≤ r/q, restriction is a tensor equivalence from φ^a-bundles over ℛ̃_R to φ^a-modules over ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R (glueing by Theorem 5.3.16), and φ^a-modules over ℛ̃_R embed fully faithfully into φ^a-bundles (the model M_r is the module of (0, r]-sections).
items.locator: §6.0–6.1, Hypothesis 6.0.1, Definitions 6.1.1–6.1.2, Remarks 6.1.3 and 6.1.6, Lemma 6.1.5, pp. 134–135
items.note: VB1 ('compare [bundles] with finite projective modules on annuli and Frobenius descent') and RF1 (the Frobenius quotient X_S = Y_S/φ^ℤ): a φ^a-module over ℛ̃_R, over an annulus ring ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R, or a φ^a-bundle, is a vector bundle on the relative curve. Not planned: φ^a-modules over W(R), ℰ̃_R, ℛ̃^int_R, ℛ̃^bd_R, ℛ̃⁺_R, ℛ̃^∞_R, their unique models over ∗^r_R, and the kernel statement (Lemma 6.1.5).

items.name: Generators of a φ^a-bundle generate its global sections
items.statement: If global sections v_1, …, v_n of a φ^a-bundle M over ℛ̃_R generate M_I over ℛ̃^I_R for every closed interval I ⊂ (0, ∞), they generate the module of global sections of M over ℛ̃^∞_R (after Kiehl, Satz 2.4).

items.name: Twists, surjectivity of φ^a − 1 and global generation (ampleness of 𝒪(1))
items.statement: For a φ^a-module or bundle M and n ∈ ℤ, M(n) is M with φ^a multiplied by p^{−n}. For a φ^a-bundle M there is N such that for n ≥ N and 0 < s ≤ r, φ^a − 1 : M_{[s,rq]}(n) → M_{[s,r]}(n) is surjective (N = 1 if M comes from a φ^a-module over ℛ̃^int_R); hence twisting a short exact sequence of φ^a-bundles by n ≥ N keeps it exact on φ^a-invariants. For n ≥ N, finitely many φ^a-invariant global sections of M(n) generate M (2m of them, N = 1, if M comes from an m-generated φ^a-module over ℛ̃^int_R). One cannot produce the generators on a single interval [r/q, r] (that would give isomorphic φ-modules of different degrees); the argument uses that R is Banach over an analytic field, and extends to R free of trivial spectrum by compactness.
items.locator: §6.2, Definition 6.2.1, Propositions 6.2.2 and 6.2.4, Corollary 6.2.3 and Remarks 6.2.5–6.2.6, pp. 135–138
items.note: VB2:ampleness ('sufficiently positive twists of a bundle are globally generated with higher cohomology zero', for affinoid perfectoid S). Findings E48 (corrected in the authors' errata) and E49 concern the proof of Proposition 6.2.4.

items.name: The graded ring P = ⊕ P_n and the scheme Proj(P)
items.statement: P_n = {x ∈ ℛ̃⁺_R : φ^a(x) = p^n x} = {x ∈ ℛ̃_R : φ^a(x) = p^n x} (n ≥ 0), a reduced graded ring; Proj(P), glued from D_+(f) = Spec P[f^{−1}]_0 for homogeneous f of positive degree, is a reduced separated scheme. For any d > 0, P_d generates the unit ideal of ℛ̃^∞_R, so some f_1, …, f_m ∈ P_d generate it; the ideal they generate in P is saturated, so the D_+(f_i) cover Proj(P) and Proj(P) is quasicompact. For a maximal ideal 𝔭 of P[f^{−1}]_0 with homogeneous prime 𝔮, 𝔮 and f generate the unit ideal of ℛ̃^{[r/q,r]}_R but 𝔮 alone does not. For V a sheaf on Proj(P) and 𝒪(n) the invertible sheaf of the rank-one φ^a-module with φ^a(v) = p^{−n}v, M(V(n)) = M(V)(n), and V(n) is globally generated for n large.
items.note: RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map (the graded ring P and the map to the schematic curve; 𝒪(n) and the sign conversion) and VB2:ampleness.

items.name: φ^a-bundles over ℛ̃_R are vector bundles on Proj(P)
items.statement: For f ∈ P_d (d > 0) and a φ^a-bundle M, M_f = ∪_n f^{−n} M(dn)^{φ^a} = M[f^{−1}]^{φ^a} is a finite projective P[f^{−1}]_0-module, and M_f ⊗_{P[f^{−1}]_0} ℛ̃^I_R[f^{−1}] → M_I ⊗ ℛ̃^I_R[f^{−1}] is bijective for every closed interval I; M ↦ M_f is exact and compatible with sums of subbundles. Consequently the following tensor categories are equivalent: (a) finite locally free quasicoherent sheaves on Proj(P); (b) φ^a-modules over ℛ̃^∞_R; (c) φ^a-modules over ℛ̃_R; (d) φ^a-bundles over ℛ̃_R, via V ↦ M(V) (glueing Γ(D_+(f), V) ⊗ ℛ̃^∞_R[f^{−1}]), base extension, Remark 6.1.6, and M ↦ V(M). Hence φ^a-modules over ℛ̃_∗ satisfy effective descent along rational coverings of Spa(R, R⁺).
items.locator: §6.3, Definitions 6.3.2, 6.3.10–6.3.11, Lemma 6.3.3, Corollaries 6.3.4 and 6.3.13, Theorems 6.3.9 and 6.3.12, pp. 138–142
items.note: VB2:ampleness ('Compare bundles and cohomology on X_S and the Proj curve built in RF3'; node gaga-equivalence, Fargues–Scholze II.2.7) with RF3; descent is VB1. This paper proves the equivalence for every perfect uniform R, not only perfectoid S. The generality agrees: under Hypothesis 5.0.1 R is a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p, so Spa(R,R⁺) is an affinoid perfectoid S.

items.name: For an analytic field, the rings P[f^{−1}]_0 are Prüfer and coherent sheaves correspond to finitely presented φ^a-modules
items.statement: A domain is Prüfer if every finitely generated ideal is projective, equivalently every finitely generated torsion-free module is projective, equivalently I_1 ∩ I_2 + I_1 ∩ I_3 = I_1 ∩ (I_2 + I_3) for all ideals (Bézout ⇒ Prüfer; noetherian Prüfer = Dedekind). If R = L is an analytic field, P[f^{−1}]_0 = (ℛ̃_L[f^{−1}])^{φ^a} is a Prüfer domain, and Definition 6.3.10 gives an equivalence between coherent sheaves on Proj(P) and finitely presented ℛ̃_L-modules with semilinear φ^a-action. For general R it is unclear whether the P[f^{−1}]_0 are coherent. (Fargues–Fontaine show Proj(P_L) is a complete absolute curve: noetherian, connected, separated, regular of dimension 1, so these rings are Dedekind.)
items.locator: §6.3, Definition 6.3.5, Lemma 6.3.6, Theorem 6.3.14 and Remarks 6.3.15, 6.3.20, pp. 139–144
items.note: VB2:ampleness plans the regular noetherian dimension-one structure of the schematic curve at a geometric point (from Fargues–Fontaine); the Prüfer property for any analytic field and the coherent-sheaf equivalence are not planned. Also VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/classical-points-and-principal-ideal-domains ('for U = Spa(B,B^+) an affinoid open of X_C with U connected, B is a Dedekind domain (in fact a PID)'), only at an algebraically closed C. Mathlib has no Prüfer domains (Mathlib/RingTheory/Flat/TorsionFree.lean:32: '-- TODO: Add definition and properties of Prüfer domains.').

items.name: Norms on the spaces of twisted invariants and continuous group actions
items.statement: For a φ^a-bundle M, r > 0 and a norm on M_{[r/q,r]} induced from λ(α^r), the equivalence class of its restriction to M(n)^{φ^a} = {v : φ^a(v) = p^{−n}v} is independent of r and of the norm (not uniformly in n). If a profinite group G acts continuously on each ℛ̃^r_R commuting with φ^a, an action of G on a φ^a-module M over ℛ̃_R (equivalently on the corresponding sheaf V on Proj(P)) is continuous for the LF topology iff it is continuous on each M(n)^{φ^a} = Γ(Proj(P), V(n)) for these norms; such actions are called continuous.
items.note: Used for the relative (φ, Γ)-modules of §9.

items.name: φ^a-cohomology is computed on an annulus and is Banach
items.statement: Let M be a φ^a-module over ℛ̃^∞_R. (a) For r > 0 the complex M_r →^{φ^a−1} M_{r/q} (M_r = M ⊗ ℛ̃^r_R) computes H^i_{φ^a}(M); (b) so does M ⊗ ℛ̃_R; (c) for 0 < s ≤ r/q so does M_{[s,r]} →^{φ^a−1} M_{[s,r/q]}; (d) in (c), φ^a − 1 is strict, so H^0_{φ^a}(M) and H^1_{φ^a}(M) are Banach spaces over ℚ_p.
items.note: VB1 ('Construct H^0 and H^1 … from annular descent'). The Banach structure in (d) is not stated there; the note records it for the design.

items.name: Frobenius-stable bases on an annulus extend over the model, and the approximation lemma
items.statement: Let M be a φ^a-module over ℛ̃_R with models M_r. (7.1.1) If v_1, …, v_n is a basis of M_{[r/q,r]} on which φ^a acts via an invertible matrix over ℛ̃^{r/q}_R, then it is a basis of M_r. (7.1.2) Let h ≥ 0, let D be diagonal with entries p^{d_1}, …, p^{d_n} (d_i ∈ ℤ, no two differing by more than h), and let e_1, …, e_n be a basis of M_{[r/q,r]} on which φ^a acts via F over ℛ̃^{[r/q,r/q]}_R with λ(α^{r/q})(FD − 1) < p^{−h}. Then M_r has a basis v_j = Σ_i U_{ij} e_i on which φ^a acts via F′ with F′D − 1 having entries in pℛ̃^{int,r/q}_R, where λ(α^{r/q})(U − 1), λ(α^r)(D^{−1}UD − 1) < p^{−h}.
items.note: RD.2/good-models-of-sigma-modules (a) plans the matrix lemma over a field (Kedlaya, Slope filtrations revisited, Lemma 6.1.1); the version over a perfect uniform Banach ring R, which spreads a good basis from ℋ(β) to a neighbourhood in Theorems 7.3.7 and 7.4.5, is not planned. Findings E50 and E51 concern these lemmas.

items.name: Rank, degree and slope as functions on ℳ(R); pure and étale loci
items.statement: For a φ^a-module M over W(R), ℰ̃_R, ℛ̃^int_R, ℛ̃^bd_R or ℛ̃_R, rank(M, β) ∈ ℤ and deg(M, β) ∈ a^{−1}ℤ are the rank and degree of the base extension of M from R to ℋ(β), for β ∈ ℳ(R) (Convention 4.1.13 when a > 1); the degree is identically zero over W(R) and ℛ̃^int_R. Both functions are continuous, i.e. locally constant, on ℳ(R) (Lemma 7.2.2), hence so is the slope μ(M, β) = deg(M, β)/rank(M, β) when the rank is nowhere zero. The pure (resp. étale) locus of M is the set of β at which the base extension to ℋ(β) is pure (resp. étale); M is pointwise pure (resp. étale) if the locus is ℳ(R). At a point of rank 0 a module counts as pure of every slope, so that pure and étale φ-modules admit kernels of surjections.
items.locator: §7.2, Definitions 7.2.1 and 7.2.3, Lemma 7.2.2 and Convention 7.2.4, p. 147
items.note: VB1/degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism defines rank, degree and slope at a geometric point of X_S, and VB4/semicontinuity-of-HN-polygon states that the endpoint of the HN polygon (the degree) is locally constant in a family of constant rank over a perfectoid S. Here the functions live on the Gel’fand spectrum ℳ(R) of any perfect uniform Banach F_p-algebra. Here the functions live on the Gel’fand spectrum ℳ(R) (the rank-one points of S = Spa(R,R⁺); R is a perfectoid Tate ring by Hypothesis 5.0.1, so the generality matches). Not planned: rank and degree for φ^a-modules over W(R), ℰ̃_R, ℛ̃^int_R, ℛ̃^bd_R, and the pure and étale loci for those rings.

items.name: Pure models, local pure models and the hierarchy of purity conditions
items.statement: Let c, d ∈ ℤ with d a positive multiple of a. A (c,d)-pure model of a φ^a-module M over ℰ̃_R (resp. ℛ̃^bd_R, ℛ̃_R) Let c, d ∈ ℤ with d a positive multiple of a. A (c,d)-pure model of a φ^a-module M over ℰ̃_R (resp. ℛ̃^bd_R, ℛ̃_R) is a W(R)-submodule (resp. ℛ̃^int_R-submodule) M_0 of M which is bounded (there is a finitely generated submodule N_0 over the same subring with p^n M_0 ⊆ N_0 and p^n N_0 ⊆ M_0 for some n ≥ 0) such that the natural map M_0 ⊗_{W(R)} ℰ̃_R → M (resp. M_0 ⊗_{ℛ̃^int_R} ℛ̃^bd_R → M, M_0 ⊗_{ℛ̃^int_R} ℛ̃_R → M) is an isomorphism and the φ^a-action on M induces an isomorphism (p^cφ^d)^*M_0 ≅ M_0 (only stability of M_0[p^{−1}] under φ^d, not φ^a, is assumed; Remark 7.3.2). Its existence makes M pointwise pure of constant slope c/d; a (0,d)-pure model is an étale model; a pure model is (locally) free if its underlying module is finite (locally) free, and a finitely presented pure model is locally free. A (locally free, free) local (c,d)-pure model at β ∈ ℳ(R) is a rational localization R → R′ encircling β together with a (locally free, free) (c,d)-pure model of the base extension of M to R′. M has a locally free local pure model at β iff it has a free one, and over ℛ̃^bd_R this can be tested over ℰ̃_R (Lemma 7.3.3). M is pure of slope s at β if it has a locally free local (c,d)-pure model at β with c/d = s (forcing s = μ(M, β) when rank(M, β) > 0; every slope when the rank is 0), pure if it is pure at every β (finitely many local models then cover ℳ(R)), étale = pure of slope 0, and globally pure if it has a locally free pure model. For the conditions (a) globally pure, (b) admits a pure model, (c) pure, (d) admits local pure models, (e) pointwise pure: over ℰ̃_R and ℛ̃^bd_R, (a) strictly implies (b) and (b)–(e) are equivalent; over ℛ̃_R, (a) strictly implies (b), (b) strictly implies (c), and (c)–(e) are equivalent (by Corollaries 7.3.9 and 8.5.14 and Examples 8.5.17 (Tate curve) and 8.5.18 (banana)). Purity of a φ^a-module over ℛ̃^bd_R cannot be read off from its base extension to ℛ̃_R.; its existence makes M pointwise pure of slope c/d, and a (0,d)-pure model is an étale model. A local model at β ∈ ℳ(R) is a model after a rational localization R → R′ encircling β. M has a locally free local pure model at β iff it has a free one, and over ℛ̃^bd_R this can be tested over ℰ̃_R (Lemma 7.3.3). M is pure of slope s at β if it has a locally free local (c,d)-pure model at β with c/d = s, pure if it is pure at every β (finitely many local models then cover ℳ(R)), and globally pure if it has a locally free pure model. For the conditions (a) globally pure, (b) admits a pure model, (c) pure, (d) admits local pure models, (e) pointwise pure: over ℰ̃_R and ℛ̃^bd_R, (a) strictly implies (b) and (b)–(e) are equivalent; over ℛ̃_R, (a) strictly implies (b), (b) strictly implies (c), and (c)–(e) are equivalent (by Corollaries 7.3.9 and 8.5.14 and Examples 8.5.17–8.5.18). Purity of a φ^a-module over ℛ̃^bd_R cannot be read off from its base extension to ℛ̃_R.

items.name: Relative Dieudonné–Manin for free pure models
