items.statement: If a φ^a-module M over ℰ̃_R (resp. ℛ̃^bd_R, ℛ̃_R) has a free (c,d)-pure model M_0, there is an R-algebra S, the completed direct limit of faithfully finite étale R-subalgebras, such that M_0 ⊗ W(S) (resp. M_0 ⊗ ℛ̃^int_S) has a basis fixed by p^cφ^d.
items.note: VB4/relative-HN-filtration-and-proetale-splitting plans the rational analogue for bundles on X_S over a perfectoid S (pro-étale locally E^λ ≅ O(λ)^{n_λ}); the integral statement for pure models over W(S) and ℛ̃^int_S is not planned.

items.name: Pure models spread out from a point; pure and étale loci are open; pointwise pure is pure
items.statement: Let M be a φ^a-module over ℛ̃_R of nowhere zero rank, β a point of its pure locus, and c, d ∈ ℤ with d a positive multiple of a and c/d = μ(M, β). Every (c,d)-pure model of M ⊗ ℛ̃_{ℋ(β)} extends to a free local (c,d)-pure model of M at β (Theorem 7.3.7). Consequently, for any φ^a-module M over ℛ̃_R: the pure and étale loci are open; M is étale (resp. pure) iff it is pointwise étale (resp. pointwise pure); and M is pure at β iff it has a (not necessarily locally free) local pure model at β.
items.note: VB4/slope-zero-local-systems plans, for perfectoid S, the equivalence between bundles with constant zero HN polygon and pro-étale ℚ_p-local systems (Fargues–Scholze II.2.20), which the packet proves from the relative HN filtration instead of from local étale models; the spreading of pure models and the openness of the pure locus are not planned.

items.name: Slope polygons over an analytic field; the special and generic polygons over ℛ̃^bd_L
items.statement: For R = L an analytic field and M a φ^a-module over ℛ̃_L with slope filtration 0 = M_0 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ M_l = M (Theorem 4.2.13; pure quotients with μ(M_1/M_0) > ⋯ > μ(M_l/M_{l−1})), For R = L an analytic field and M a φ^a-module over ℛ̃_L with slope filtration 0 = M_0 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ M_l = M (Theorem 4.2.13; pure quotients with μ(M_1/M_0) > ⋯ > μ(M_l/M_{l−1})), the slope polygon starts at (0,0) and consists, for i = l, …, 1 in order, of a segment of width rank(M_i/M_{i−1}) and slope μ(M_i/M_{i−1}); so the slopes increase from left to right and the polygon is convex (the paper reverses the slope sign of Kedlaya's 'Slope filtrations revisited' and swaps the order of the segments to keep the convex shape). It ends at (rank M, deg M) and is unchanged by passing to a complete extension of L. For M over ℛ̃^bd_L, the special polygon is that of M ⊗ ℛ̃_L and the generic polygon is that of M ⊗ ℰ̃_L, viewing ℰ̃_L as ℛ̃_L for the trivial norm on L (equivalently, the Dieudonné–Manin slopes). and is unchanged by passing to a complete extension of L. For M over ℛ̃^bd_L, the special polygon is that of M ⊗ ℛ̃_L and the generic polygon is that of M ⊗ ℰ̃_L, viewing ℰ̃_L as ℛ̃_L for the trivial norm on L (equivalently, the Dieudonné–Manin slopes).
items.note: RD.1/frobenius-slopes (HN polygons and generic slopes) and RD.2/special-polygon-above-generic (the special polygon as the HN polygon over the extended Robba ring).

items.name: The special slope polygon lies above the generic one
items.statement: For L an analytic field and M a φ^a-module over ℛ̃^bd_L: (a) the special slope polygon lies on or above the generic one, with the same endpoints; (b) if the two coincide, the slope filtration of M ⊗ ℛ̃_L descends to M.
items.note: RD.2/special-polygon-above-generic and RD.2/coincident-polygons-common-filtration state Kedlaya, Slope filtrations revisited, Proposition 5.5.1 and Theorem 5.5.2, which the paper cites as its proof.

items.name: Reading generic slopes from a matrix AD over a relative base
items.statement: Let M be a φ^a-module over ℛ̃^bd_R with a basis on which φ^a acts via AD, D diagonal with entries in p^ℤ and A − 1 with entries in pℛ̃^int_R. Then there are an R-algebra S which is the union (not only the completed union) of faithfully finite étale R-subalgebras and an invertible U over W(S), congruent to 1 modulo p, with U^{−1}ADφ^a(U) = D. In particular, at every β ∈ ℳ(R) the generic slopes of M are the negatives of the p-adic valuations of the diagonal entries of D, divided by a.
items.note: RD.1/generic-newton-polygon-from-cyclic-vector (b) plans the case of a field (Kedlaya, monodromy paper, Proposition 5.9); the relative form over R, and the refinement that S need not be completed (used in Theorem 7.4.9), are not planned.

items.name: The slope polygon is lower semicontinuous on ℳ(R)
items.statement: For any φ^a-module M over ℛ̃_R, β ↦ the slope polygon of M ⊗ ℛ̃_{ℋ(β)} is lower semicontinuous on ℳ(R): where the rank is constant, for each x ∈ [0, rank M] the y-coordinate of the polygon at x is a lower semicontinuous function of β, and it is locally constant at x = rank M.
items.note: The slope signs agree with Fargues–Scholze (in the paper ℛ̃_R(1), φ^a(v) = p^{−1}v, corresponds to 𝒪(1) (Remark 6.3.16) and has slope +1/a; cf. Lemma 7.4.4 and the proof of Proposition 7.4.6). What differs is the drawing of the polygon: Definition 7.4.1 lays the segments out in order of increasing slope (i = l, …, 1 with μ(M_1/M_0) > ⋯ > μ(M_l/M_{l−1})), so the paper’s slope polygon is convex (concave up) and is the point reflection of the usual concave HN polygon (y_KL(x) = deg − y_HN(rank − x)). Lower semicontinuity of the y-coordinates in Theorem 7.4.5 ('the polygon at nearby points lies on or above the polygon at β') is therefore the same statement as upper semicontinuity of the concave HN polygon in Fargues–Scholze II.2.19(i). The packet’s proof goes through properness of the projectivized Banach–Colmez space instead of the approximation lemma.

items.name: The slope polygon is bounded and is locally constant on an open dense subset
items.statement: For any φ^a-module M over ℛ̃_R, the slope polygons of M at the points of ℳ(R) are bounded above and below (all slopes are at least −N/a for N as in Proposition 6.2.4, and the sum of the slopes is continuous). Hence the polygon takes finitely many values locally, and there is an open dense U ⊆ ℳ(R) on which it is locally constant.

items.name: Splitting off the first m slopes when a vertex is constant
items.statement: (7.4.8) Let A be an n × n matrix over ℛ̃^int_R invertible over ℛ̃^bd_R, x_1, …, x_n ∈ ℛ̃^bd_R, and y_1, …, y_n ∈ ℰ̃_R with y_i − x_i = Σ_j A_{ij}φ^a(y_j). Then all y_i lie in ℛ̃^bd_R iff their images lie in ℛ̃^bd_{ℋ(β)} for every β ∈ ℳ(R). (7.4.9) Let M over ℛ̃_R have constant rank n and slopes μ_1(M,β) ≥ ⋯ ≥ μ_n(M,β) at β. If for some m ∈ {1, …, n−1} and all β we have μ_m(M,β) > μ_{m+1}(M,β) and μ_1 + ⋯ + μ_m constant, there is a unique φ^a-submodule N of rank m with M/N a φ^a-module such that at every β the slopes of N are μ_1, …, μ_m and those of M/N are μ_{m+1}, …, μ_n.
items.note: VB4/relative-HN-filtration-and-proetale-splitting plans the case of a constant HN polygon over a perfectoid S (next item); the splitting at a single constant vertex, with a polygon that may vary, is not planned.

items.name: Slope filtration in families with constant slope polygon
items.statement: If the slope polygon of a φ^a-module M over ℛ̃_R is constant on ℳ(R), there is a unique filtration 0 = M_0 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ M_l = M by φ^a-submodules whose quotients are φ^a-modules pure of constant slope with μ(M_1/M_0) > ⋯ > μ(M_l/M_{l−1}).
items.note: VB4/relative-HN-filtration-and-proetale-splitting (Fargues–Scholze II.2.19(ii)) for perfectoid S; the paper proves it for any perfect uniform R by induction on the rank from Theorem 7.4.9. the paper proves it by induction on the rank from Theorem 7.4.9; under Hypothesis 5.0.1 its R is a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p, so the generality agrees with VB4's perfectoid S.

items.name: Negative slopes: H^0 vanishes and H^1 injects into the product of the pointwise H^1
items.statement: If M over ℛ̃_R has everywhere negative slopes, then H^0_{φ^a}(M) = 0, H^0_{φ^a}(M ⊗ ℛ̃_{ℋ(β)}) = 0 for all β ∈ ℳ(R), and H^1_{φ^a}(M) → ∏_β H^1_{φ^a}(M ⊗ ℛ̃_{ℋ(β)}) is injective. For any M this applies to M(n) for n small enough (by Proposition 7.4.6); the injectivity also holds for n large, since then H^1_{φ^a}(M(n)) = 0 by Proposition 6.2.2.
items.note: Findings E52 and E53 (the second corrected in the authors’ errata) concern this item.

items.name: Sober, quasiseparated and spectral spaces (Definition 8.1.1)
items.statement: A topological space X is sober if every irreducible closed subset has a unique generic point; this implies that X is T0 (no two distinct points lie in exactly the same closed subsets). X is quasiseparated if the intersection of any two quasicompact open subsets is quasicompact; qcqs abbreviates quasicompact and quasiseparated. A spectral space is a topological space which is sober and qcqs and admits a neighbourhood basis consisting of quasicompact open subsets.
items.note: Mathlib's SpectralSpace extends T0Space, CompactSpace, QuasiSober (existence of generic points of irreducible closed sets), QuasiSeparatedSpace (intersections of two compact opens are compact) and PrespectralSpace (compact opens form a basis); sober in the paper's sense is QuasiSober together with T0Space, which gives uniqueness.

items.name: Locally spectral spaces (Definition 8.1.1; Remark 8.1.7, first sentence)
items.statement: A locally spectral space is a topological space admitting a neighbourhood basis consisting of open spectral subspaces. Such a space is spectral if and only if it is qcqs. Any scheme is a locally spectral space (Remark 8.1.7).
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/locally-spectral-space (defined there by an open cover by spectral subspaces; the two definitions agree because a quasicompact open subspace of a spectral space is spectral, mathlib:Topology.IsOpenEmbedding.spectralSpace). The criterion 'spectral iff qcqs' is not stated in the node, but follows from Mathlib's local-to-global lemmas quasiSober_of_open_cover and PrespectralSpace.of_isOpenCover; for schemes Mathlib has the (unnamed) T0Space, QuasiSober and PrespectralSpace instances in Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Properties.lean, but no locally spectral predicate.

items.name: Hochster: spectral spaces are the inverse limits of finite T0 spaces (Lemma 8.1.2)
items.statement: A topological space is spectral if and only if it is an inverse limit of finite T0 spaces.
items.note: Nodes DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-category-of-finite-t0-spaces (every spectral space is an inverse limit of finite T0 spaces; spectral spaces with spectral maps ≃ Pro(finite T0 spaces)) and, for the converse, DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces (finite T0 spaces are spectral and every continuous map between finite spaces is spectral). Mathlib has Ind but no Pro at the pinned commit.

items.name: Inverse limits of spectral spaces are spectral (Corollary 8.1.3)
items.statement: Any inverse limit of spectral spaces is again a spectral space.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces, stated for cofiltered systems with spectral transition maps (with the limit maps spectral). The deduction from Lemma 8.1.2 uses such transition maps: a continuous map from a spectral space to a finite T0 space factors through a finite stage only when it is spectral. The corollary is to be read with spectral transition maps.

items.name: The patch (constructible) topology (Definition 8.1.4)
items.statement: For X a spectral space, the patch topology on X is the topology generated by the quasicompact open subsets for the original (spectral) topology and their complements. The spectral topology cannot be recovered from the patch topology alone.
items.note: Mathlib's constructible topology is generated by the compact open sets and the closed sets with compact complement, which is the patch topology. Tau Ceti adds pro-constructible sets (tauceti:TauCeti.IsProConstructible). The example showing non-recoverability is the next item.

items.name: Hochster duality: the inverse spectral topology (Definition 8.1.4)
items.statement: For a spectral space X there is another spectral topology on the same set whose quasicompact open subsets are exactly the complements of the quasicompact open subsets of X; it has the same patch topology as X.
items.note: Mathlib and Tau Ceti have the constructible topology but not the inverse (Hochster dual) topology, and DiamondsAndVStacks:D0 plans constructible and pro-constructible sets, generalization and limits but not the dual topology. The paper uses it only as an illustration; it would belong in DiamondsAndVStacks:D0.

items.name: Hochster: a spectral space is compact in the patch topology (Lemma 8.1.5)
items.statement: Let X be a spectral space. Then X is compact (quasicompact and Hausdorff) for the patch topology.
items.note: Quasicompactness is in Mathlib: mathlib:compactSpace_withConstructibleTopology (for any quasicompact, quasi-sober, prespectral, quasiseparated space). The Hausdorff property, needed for 'compact' in the paper's (Bourbaki) sense, is a Mathlib TODO and is planned in node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/constructible-topology-profinite (the patch topology is profinite).

items.name: Spectral maps between locally spectral spaces (Definition 8.1.6, as corrected)
items.statement: A map f: Y → X between locally spectral spaces is spectral if it is continuous and, for any qcqs open subsets U ⊆ X and V ⊆ Y with f(V) ⊆ U, the induced map V → U is quasicompact (the inverse image of any quasicompact open subset of U is quasicompact). In particular, a spectral map between spectral spaces is continuous for the patch topologies.
items.note: Node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/locally-spectral-space (spectrality tested on pairs of spectral opens). For spectral spaces the notion is mathlib:IsSpectralMap, and patch continuity is tauceti:TauCeti.IsSpectralMap.continuous_constructibleTopology. The printed second sentence ('Equivalently, the inverse image of any quasicompact open subset is a quasicompact open subset') is false and is deleted by the authors' errata (source issue).

items.name: Schemes: qcqs schemes are spectral and quasicompact morphisms are spectral (Remark 8.1.7, as corrected)
items.statement: Any scheme which is qcqs in the sense of algebraic geometry (its underlying topological space is quasicompact and its absolute diagonal is quasicompact) has a spectral underlying space. Any quasicompact morphism of schemes is spectral.
items.note: The printed last sentence ('Any morphism of schemes is spectral') is changed by the authors' errata (source issue). Under the local Definition 8.1.6 that remains after the erratum deletes its second sentence, every morphism of schemes is in fact spectral: for qcqs opens V ⊆ Y, U ⊆ X with f(V) ⊆ U, V → U is a morphism from a quasicompact scheme to a quasiseparated one and hence quasicompact (Stacks 03GI). The quasicompactness hypothesis is needed only for the global condition (Mathlib IsSpectralMap).

items.name: Huber: the adic spectrum is a spectral space (Theorem 8.1.8, first sentence)
items.statement: For any adic Banach ring (A, A⁺), Spa(A, A⁺) is a spectral space.
items.note: Tau Ceti proves Wedhorn's Theorem 7.35 for every Huber ring A and every subring A⁺ (with an unnamed SpectralSpace instance on spa Aplus); an adic Banach ring is a complete Tate, hence Huber, pair. This refines Theorem 2.4.5 (PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/65).

items.name: Huber: morphisms of adic Banach rings induce spectral maps (Theorem 8.1.8, second sentence)
items.statement: For any morphism (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) of adic Banach rings, the induced map Spa(B, B⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is spectral.
items.note: Layer 2.1 asks to 'state the exact hypotheses under which this map is spectral'. Tau Ceti already has the continuous map (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap, TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.continuous_spaComap) and the preimage of R(T/s) as R(φ(T)/φ(s)) (TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset); for Tate rings φ(T) still generates the unit ideal, so preimages of rational subsets are rational and hence quasicompact, but spectrality is not stated.

items.name: Patch density of classical points (Remark 8.1.9)
items.statement: For (A, A⁺) an adic Banach algebra, the image of M(A) in Spa(A, A⁺) need not be dense for the patch topology. If A is an affinoid algebra over an analytic field and A⁺ = A°, then Maxspec(A) is dense in Spa(A, A⁺) for the patch topology.
items.note: Node AdicSpacesPartII:R1/classical-points-constructible-density (ii) (Huber 1993, Corollary 4.2). The paper presents this as a reinterpretation of Remark 2.4.9 (for A = K{T}, A⁺ = o_K + m_K·K{T}°, the patch-open set {v(T) ≥ 1} ∖ {v(T) ≤ 1} is nonempty with no rank-one point) and Corollary 2.5.13, whose correct hypothesis A⁺ = A° (finding E11) is the one used here; passing from rational subspaces to arbitrary patch-open sets is Huber's Corollary 4.3, node (iii).

items.name: Taut locally spectral spaces and taut morphisms (Definition 8.1.10, Remark 8.1.11)
items.statement: A locally spectral space X is taut if X is quasiseparated and the closure of every quasicompact subset of X is quasicompact; if X is qcqs, or more generally quasiseparated with a locally finite covering by quasicompact open subsets, then X is taut. A spectral morphism of locally spectral spaces is taut if the inverse image of every taut open subspace is taut; every qcqs morphism is taut. For k a field, glueing finitely many copies of Spec k[t] along Spec k[t, t⁻¹] gives a taut locally spectral space, but glueing infinitely many copies does not; for K an analytic field, glueing two copies of Spa(K{T}, K{T}°) along the complement of the origin does not give a taut space, the complement of the origin not being quasicompact.
items.locator: §8.1, Definition 8.1.10 and Remark 8.1.11, p. 158; Huber [79, Lemma 5.1.3] (arXiv 1301.0792v5)
items.note: Node ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/taut-spaces-and-morphisms states the definition (with the equivalent 'closure of every quasicompact open'), the qcqs and locally-finite-covering examples, qcqs maps are taut, composites, and the two-disc non-example. The scheme examples of Remark 8.1.11 are not in the node.

items.name: Locally valuation-ringed (locally v-ringed) spaces (Definition 8.2.1)
items.statement: The category of locally v-ringed spaces has as objects triples X = (|X|, O_X, (v_x)_{x∈|X|}) with |X| a topological space, O_X a sheaf of complete topological rings and each v_x a semivaluation on the stalk O_{X,x}; a morphism X → Y is a pair (f, φ) with f: |X| → |Y| continuous and φ: O_Y → f_*O_X a morphism of sheaves of topological rings such that, for each x, the restriction of v_x along φ_x: O_{Y,f(x)} → O_{X,x} is equivalent to v_{f(x)}.
items.note: Layer 3.4 plans Wedhorn's categories 𝒱^pre and 𝒱 (presheaf, resp. sheaf, of complete separated topological rings, local stalks, valuations on the residue fields, local morphisms), in which the anchor's adic spaces live; the paper's category does not ask for local stalks or local homomorphisms and puts the semivaluation on the stalk, but the two agree on adic spaces. The existence of fibred products of locally v-ringed spaces (Remark 8.2.5) is not planned.

items.name: Adic affinoid spaces, adic spaces and open immersions (Definition 8.2.2)
items.statement: For (A, A⁺) a sheafy adic Banach ring, X = Spa(A, A⁺) is a locally v-ringed space with O_X the structure sheaf (Definition 2.4.15) and v_x the restriction to O_{X,x} of the canonical valuation on H(x); such spaces are adic affinoid spaces. An adic space is a locally v-ringed space admitting an open covering by adic affinoid spaces, and a morphism of adic spaces is a morphism of locally v-ringed spaces. If X is an adic space and U ⊆ X is open, U acquires an adic space structure making U → X a morphism of adic spaces, an open immersion.
items.note: Layer 5 (affinoid adic spaces are pre-adic spectra of sheafy Huber pairs, adic spaces are covered by them; open immersions and open subspaces in 5.1, gluing in 5.3), for arbitrary Huber pairs; the paper's affinoids are complete Tate pairs.

items.name: Huber: morphisms of adic spaces over Tate rings are adic (Definition 8.2.2)
items.statement: Every morphism of adic spaces in the sense of Definition 8.2.2, whose rings contain topologically nilpotent units, is an adic morphism in the sense of Huber [78, §3].
items.note: Nodes AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-morphism ('every morphism into an analytic adic space is adic') and AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/yoneda-adic-analytic-tate-local (b) ('every morphism of Huber pairs out of a Tate ring is adic').

items.name: Preadic affinoid spaces and preadic spaces (Definition 8.2.3, Remark 8.2.4)
items.statement: Let AdBan be the category of adic Banach rings, viewed as a site AdBan^op whose coverings are the rational coverings, and (AdBan^op)~ its topos of set-valued sheaves. For (A, A⁺) ∈ AdBan, the preadic affinoid space Spa~(A, A⁺) is the sheafification of (B, B⁺) ↦ Hom_AdBan((A, A⁺), (B, B⁺)); a rational subspace of it is a morphism Spa~(B, B⁺) → Spa~(A, A⁺) induced by a rational localization. A morphism F → G in (AdBan^op)~ is an open immersion if for every morphism Spa~(A, A⁺) → G there is an open U ⊆ Spa(A, A⁺) with F ×_G Spa~(A, A⁺) = colim_{V ⊆ U rational} Spa~(O(V), O⁺(V)). A preadic space (an adic space in Scholze–Weinstein) is an F ∈ (AdBan^op)~ with F = colim Spa~(A, A⁺) over the open immersions Spa~(A, A⁺) → F. There are functors from adic spaces to preadic spaces and from preadic spaces to locally v-ringed spaces whose composite is the full embedding of adic spaces, so adic spaces form a full subcategory of preadic spaces (Spa~(A, A⁺) = Spa(A, A⁺) for (A, A⁺) sheafy); every preadic space X has an underlying topological space |X| with |Spa~(A, A⁺)| = Spa(A, A⁺). A preadic affinoid space can be an adic space without being an adic affinoid space (Remark 8.2.4).
items.locator: §8.2, Definition 8.2.3 and Remark 8.2.4, pp. 159–160; Scholze–Weinstein [115, Definition 2.1.5] (arXiv 1301.0792v5)
items.note: Nodes AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/huber-pair-rational-site, A1/generalized-adic-presentation ('Yoneda-adic spaces': Scholze–Weinstein pre-adic spaces, Kedlaya–Liu preadic spaces), A1/yoneda-adic-open-immersions, A1/yoneda-adic-ind-ringed-description (the underlying space |F|), A1/adic-spaces-in-yoneda-adic-spaces (full embedding) and A1/yoneda-adic-analytic-tate-local (c) (restriction to complete Tate pairs gives exactly the paper's preadic spaces). A1 describes Yoneda-adic spaces through sheaves of ind-topological rings; the paper's functor to locally v-ringed spaces (sheaves of topological rings) is not stated there and is not fully faithful on all preadic spaces, which the paper does not claim.

items.name: Fibred products of preadic spaces (Remark 8.2.5)
items.statement: The categories of locally v-ringed spaces and of preadic spaces admit fibred products. It is unknown whether the fibred product of adic spaces over an adic space is an adic space; a counterexample would have to involve nonnoetherian Banach rings (Proposition 2.4.16), and perfectoid spaces show that failure of the noetherian property alone is not sufficient.
items.note: Node AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/yoneda-adic-fibre-products (fibre products of analytic Yoneda-adic spaces, affinoid case Spa~(B ⊗̂_A C), surjectivity on underlying spaces); A1/etale-base-change records that fibre products of adic spaces are not asserted in general. Fibre products of locally v-ringed spaces are not planned.

items.name: Quasicompact, quasiseparated and taut preadic spaces (Definition 8.2.6)
items.statement: A preadic space X is quasicompact if it admits a finite covering by open immersions of preadic affinoid spaces; quasiseparated if U_1 ×_X U_2 is quasicompact for any two open immersions U_1 → X, U_2 → X with U_1, U_2 quasicompact; taut if it is quasiseparated and, for every open immersion U → X with U quasicompact, there is a covering V_1 → X, V_2 → X by open immersions with V_1 quasicompact, U → X factoring through V_1 and U ×_X V_2 = ∅. For X an adic space, X is quasicompact, quasiseparated or taut if and only if |X| is.
items.note: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/taut-spaces-and-morphisms defines taut adic spaces through |X|; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/yoneda-adic-open-immersions (b) and A1/yoneda-adic-ind-ringed-description identify open immersions into a preadic space with open subsets of |X|, which reduces the preadic definitions to |X|. The preadic-level definitions themselves are not written out in the plan.

items.name: The sheaves O_X and O_X⁺ on preadic spaces (Definition 8.2.7, Remark 8.2.8)
items.statement: On any preadic space X, the assignments (A, A⁺) ↦ A and (A, A⁺) ↦ A⁺ give sheaves of rings O_X and O_X⁺. If X is an adic space, O_X is the structure sheaf and O_X⁺ is the subsheaf with O_X⁺(U) = {f ∈ O_X(U) : the image of f in H(x) lies in H(x)⁺ for every x ∈ U}; the stalk O⁺_{X,x} is the inverse image of H(x)⁺ in O_{X,x}. For (A, A⁺) an adic Banach ring and X = Spa~(A, A⁺), A⁺ = O_X⁺(X) by (2.4.3.1). O_X⁺ need not be acyclic on an adic affinoid space (Remark 8.2.8).
items.note: Layer 3.3 defines 𝒪_X⁺(U) = {f ∈ 𝒪_X(U) : v_x(f_x) ≤ 1 for every x}; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/huber-pair-rational-site has 𝒪 on the Huber-pair site and A1/etale-structure-sheaf has O and O⁺ on the étale site. The input (2.4.3.1) is Wedhorn Proposition 7.52(1), in the library as tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.coe_eq_setOf_forall_vle_one. The stalk description of O⁺ is not stated in the plan. The almost acyclicity of O⁺ on perfectoid affinoids is Proposition 8.3.2.

items.name: Huber: maps into an affinoid are maps of rings into global sections (Lemma 8.2.9, Remark 8.2.10)
items.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be an adic Banach ring. For each adic space X, the global sections functor induces a bijection between morphisms X → Spa~(A, A⁺) of preadic spaces and morphisms A → O_X(X) of topological rings taking A⁺ into O_X⁺(X). The same holds for X a preadic space, where it is formal; the content of the lemma is the functor from adic spaces to preadic spaces.
items.locator: §8.2, Lemma 8.2.9 and Remark 8.2.10, p. 160; Huber [78, Proposition 2.1(ii)] (arXiv 1301.0792v5)
items.note: Node AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/maps-from-adic-spaces-to-yoneda-affinoids (explicitly Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 8.2.9, for any complete Huber pair, sheafy or not).

items.name: The real quotient and partially proper open subsets (Definition 8.2.11)
items.statement: For an adic Banach ring (A, A⁺) over an analytic field, the continuous map Spa(A, A⁺) → M(A) of Definition 2.4.8 takes x to the unique point of M(A) in the intersection of all open neighbourhoods of x, and the topology of M(A) is the quotient topology (not the subspace topology for the discontinuous section M(A) → Spa(A, A⁺)). For a preadic space X over an analytic field, let X̄ be the set of x ∈ |X| for which v_x is equivalent to a real semivaluation; for each x ∈ |X| the intersection of all open neighbourhoods of x contains a unique point of X̄, giving a map |X| → X̄. With the quotient topology X̄ is the real quotient of X. An open subset of X is partially proper if it is the inverse image of a (necessarily open) subset of X̄.
items.note: The affinoid retraction is PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/66 (missing, routed to TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0). The plan has the real quotient only for adic spaces locally of finite type over a field (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/berkovich-taut-comparison (b), which names 'Kedlaya–Liu's real quotient') and for small v-sheaves (DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/berkovich-quotient, |Y|_B); AdicSpacesPartII:R0/partially-proper-morphism records that the paper's partially proper open subsets differ from Huber's partially proper morphisms. The authors' erratum for this definition is a typo absent from arXiv v5 (source issue).

items.name: The real quotient of a taut adic space is its maximal Hausdorff quotient (Lemma 8.2.12(a)–(b), Example 8.2.13)
items.statement: Let X be an adic space over an analytic field. (a) If X is quasicompact, then so is X̄. (b) If X is taut, then X̄ is Hausdorff, and thus is the maximal Hausdorff quotient of X. Part (b) fails without tautness: for K an analytic field, the adic space obtained by glueing two copies of Spa(K{T}, K{T}°) along the complement of the origin has real quotient obtained by glueing two copies of M(K{T}) along the complement of the origin, which is not Hausdorff (Example 8.2.13).
items.locator: §8.2, Lemma 8.2.12(a)–(b) and Example 8.2.13, p. 161; Huber [79, Lemma 8.1.8(ii)] (arXiv 1301.0792v5)
items.note: (b) follows the proof of Huber [79, Lemma 8.1.8(ii)]. Planned only for taut adic spaces locally of finite type over a complete field (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/berkovich-taut-comparison (a): the retraction |X^ad| → |X^Berk| is the maximal Hausdorff quotient); DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/berkovich-quotient gives the maximal Hausdorff quotient of qcqs small v-sheaves, not of taut spaces. Would belong with H3 (generalising that node beyond finite type) or with TB.0 next to PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/66.

items.name: Partially proper open subsets of a taut adic space are taut (Lemma 8.2.12(c))
items.statement: Let X be a taut adic space over an analytic field. Then every partially proper open subset of X is taut.
items.note: The proof uses without comment that in a taut space the closure of a quasicompact open V is the set of specializations of points of V, hence equals the inverse image of the (closed) image of V in X̄. Planned only in the locally finite type case (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/berkovich-taut-comparison (b): inverse images of opens of X^Berk are the partially proper opens and are taut).

items.name: Huber: taut adic spaces of finite type and Hausdorff Berkovich spaces (Proposition 8.2.14)
items.statement: Let K be an analytic field. The real quotient functor defines an equivalence of categories between taut adic spaces locally of finite type over K (covered by open subspaces Spa(A, A°) with A an affinoid algebra over K) and Hausdorff strictly K-analytic spaces in the sense of Berkovich.
items.note: Node ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/berkovich-taut-comparison (a) (Huber's functor, M(A) ↦ Spa(A, A°), with the retraction the maximal Hausdorff quotient). The statement uses A⁺ = A°; the printed parenthetical 'covered by the adic spectra of affinoid algebras over K' does not fix the plus rings (source issue). Proof: Lemma 8.2.12 and Huber [79, Proposition 8.3.1].

items.name: Surjective, finite étale and étale morphisms of preadic spaces (Definition 8.2.16)
items.statement: Let ψ: Y → X be a morphism of preadic spaces. ψ is surjective if for any morphism Z → X the map |Y ×_X Z| → |Z| is surjective; for X an adic space this is the same as |Y| → |X| being surjective. ψ is finite étale if, locally on the target, it has the form Spa~(B, B⁺) → Spa~(A, A⁺) with B a finite étale A-algebra and B⁺ the integral closure of A⁺ in B. ψ is étale if each y ∈ Y has an open neighbourhood U such that ψ|_U factors as an open immersion followed by a finite étale morphism followed by an open immersion. These properties are stable under base extension.
items.note: Nodes AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-morphism and A1/etale-morphism (both citing Definition 8.2.16), A1/etale-site-generalized (the same definitions for Yoneda-adic, i.e. preadic, spaces) and A1/etale-base-change; the surjectivity of |F ×_H G| → |F| ×_{|H|} |G| is in A1/yoneda-adic-fibre-products. The paper's justification of the parenthetical on surjectivity cites only Lemma 2.3.13 (source issue).

items.name: Finite étale covers of a preadic affinoid are finite étale algebras (Lemma 8.2.17(a), Remark 8.2.18)
items.statement: For (A, A⁺) an adic Banach ring, the global sections functor induces an equivalence of categories between finite étale morphisms to Spa~(A, A⁺) and FÉt(A). (It is not known that a finite étale extension of a sheafy adic Banach algebra is sheafy, nor that a finite étale cover of an adic affinoid space is an adic space.)
items.note: Node AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-generalized (ii) (any complete Tate pair, sheafy or not; cites Lemma 8.2.17(a)); A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (c) for strongly sheafy A. The proof rests on Theorem 2.6.9 (PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/97, planned as A1/finite-etale-rational-descent).

items.name: Quasicompact étale maps factor through their open image (Lemma 8.2.17(b))
items.statement: Any étale morphism Y → X of preadic spaces with Y quasicompact factors uniquely as Y → Z → X with Y → Z surjective, Z quasicompact and Z → X an open immersion.
items.locator: §8.2, Lemma 8.2.17(b), p. 162; de Jong–van der Put [34, Proposition 3.1.7] (arXiv 1301.0792v5)
items.note: Node AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-open-map (ii) (citing Lemma 8.2.17(b) and de Jong–van der Put 3.1.7(1)), stated for X a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space; the general preadic case is not stated. The paper reduces to classical affinoids through Lemma 2.6.2 and Proposition 2.6.8. Status changed from planned (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1) to missing by the independent review: Planned only for X a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space; Kedlaya–Liu state Lemma 8.2.17(b) for an arbitrary preadic X (and use it for the sites of §8.2 and §9.1 on preadic spaces). If the reviewer prefers to keep 'planned' for the special case, the note must say so explicitly (it already does: 'the general preadic case is not stated').

items.name: Stability of surjective, finite étale and étale morphisms (Lemma 8.2.17(c))
items.statement: The properties of Definition 8.2.16 (surjective, finite étale, étale) are stable under composition and fibred products.
items.note: Nodes AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-generalized (i) (for Yoneda-adic spaces, citing Lemma 8.2.17(c)), A1/etale-composition and A1/etale-base-change (locally strongly sheafy case). The paper reduces to classical affinoids (Lemma 2.6.2, Proposition 2.6.8) and applies Huber [79, Proposition 1.7.5].

items.name: Set-theoretic coverings and the small étale and finite étale sites (Definition 8.2.19)
items.statement: A family {Y_i → X} of morphisms of preadic spaces is a set-theoretic covering if the morphism from the disjoint union of the Y_i to X is surjective; for Y_i → X étale (and Y_i quasicompact), factoring Y_i → Z_i → X as in Lemma 8.2.17(b), this holds iff {Z_i → X} is a covering. For a preadic space X over an analytic field, the small finite étale site X_fét (resp. small étale site X_ét) has as objects the finite étale (resp. étale) morphisms Y → X and as coverings the set-theoretic coverings.
items.note: Nodes AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-generalized (the Kedlaya–Liu sites of an arbitrary analytic adic space, with Yoneda-adic objects), A1/etale-site and A1/finite-etale-site (locally strongly sheafy case), A1/etale-open-map (iii).

items.name: Stable bases and stably adic spaces (Definition 8.2.19)
items.statement: A stable basis of X_ét is a basis B of X_ét consisting of adic affinoid spaces such that for any morphism Y′ → Y in X_ét which is finite étale or a rational subdomain embedding, Y ∈ B implies Y′ ∈ B; the basis property includes stability under fibred products. X is stably adic if X_ét admits a stable basis. Rigid analytic spaces are stably adic, and so are perfectoid spaces (Definition 8.3.1).
items.note: Nodes AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison (b) (the composites of rational localizations and finite étale maps form a stable basis 'in the sense of Kedlaya–Liu Definition 8.2.19' for any locally strongly sheafy analytic space, in particular for rigid spaces) and AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-stably-adic. The fibred products are over objects of B, as in the proof of Proposition 8.2.20; over a non-quasiseparated X a fibred product over X of affinoids need not be affinoid.

items.name: De Jong–van der Put reduction for étale coverings (Proposition 8.2.20)
items.statement: Let X be a preadic space and B a basis of X_ét consisting of preadic affinoid subspaces, closed under finite étale extensions and rational subdomain embeddings (e.g. a stable basis). Let P be a property of coverings in X_ét of and by elements of B such that: (a) any covering admitting a refinement with property P has P; (b) any composition of coverings with P has P; (c) for any Y ∈ B, any rational covering of Y has P; (d) for any Y ∈ B, any faithfully finite étale morphism Y′ → Y, viewed as a covering, has P. Then every covering in X_ét of and by elements of B has property P.
items.locator: §8.2, Proposition 8.2.20, pp. 163–164; adapted from de Jong–van der Put [34, Proposition 3.2.2] (arXiv 1301.0792v5)
items.note: Nodes AdicSpacesPartII:R5/stable-basis-covering-reduction (i) (X an analytic adic space, B a class of sheafy Tate affinoids closed under fibre products, finite étale extensions and rational subdomains) and AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction (X locally strongly sheafy, B = X_ét^aff). The paper allows a preadic X and a basis of preadic affinoids; for a stable basis X is adic. The authors' erratum corrects a sentence of the proof (source issue; AdicEtaleGeometry/E21). The paper allows a preadic X and a basis of preadic affinoids (not only sheafy ones); the planned nodes require sheafy affinoids (R5) or a locally strongly sheafy X (A1), which covers the stable-basis case used in 8.2.21–8.2.22 but not the general statement.

items.name: Čech acyclicity on the étale site from Laurent and finite étale coverings (Proposition 8.2.21)
items.statement: For X and B as in Proposition 8.2.20, let F be a presheaf of abelian groups on X_ét such that for every Y = Spa~(A, A⁺) ∈ B and every covering V of Y which is a simple Laurent covering or a faithfully finite étale morphism, Ȟ⁰(Y, F; V) = F(Y) (resp. Ȟ⁰(Y, F; V) = F(Y) and Ȟⁱ(Y, F; V) = 0 for i > 0). Then for every covering V of Y ∈ B by elements of B, H⁰(Y, F) = Ȟ⁰(Y, F; V) = F(Y) (resp. also Hⁱ(Y, F) = Ȟⁱ(Y, F; V) = 0 for i > 0). In particular, on Y, F takes the same value as its sheafification.
items.note: Nodes AdicSpacesPartII:R5/stable-basis-covering-reduction (ii) and ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/cech-to-derived-comparison (b) (acyclic-basis comparison on X_ét^aff, testing on rational coverings and single faithfully finite étale maps). The étale analogue of Proposition 2.4.21 (PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/78).

items.name: Tate acyclicity of vector bundles for the adic and finite étale topologies (Theorem 8.2.22(a))
items.statement: Let X = Spa(A, A⁺) be an adic affinoid space. For any finite projective A-module M, the presheaf M̃ with M̃(U) = M ⊗_A O_X(U) is an acyclic sheaf for the adic topology and for the finite étale topology.
items.note: Adic case: Tate acyclicity of O (Theorem 2.4.23, PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/80, planned at AdicSpaces layer 4 for the Čech complexes) tensored with the flat module M; finite étale case: Lemma 8.2.17(a) and Amitsur exactness. The plan states it only for strongly sheafy A (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-acyclicity-of-vector-bundles) and for perfectoid A (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-descent-perfectoid (c)); AdicSpacesPartII:R3 is noetherian. Would belong in AdicSpacesPartII:R3 with Kiehl glueing (PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/102). AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-module-acyclicity plans the adic-topology half for every sheafy complete Tate pair. The adic-topology half of Theorem 8.2.22(a) is planned in full generality. The finite étale half (higher Čech acyclicity for faithfully flat finite étale covers, i.e. Amitsur exactness) is stated only for strongly sheafy A (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-acyclicity-of-vector-bundles); R3/finite-projective-etale-descent gives only the degree-0 (descent) statement. Recommend splitting 262 into a planned adic half (R3) and a missing fét half; the item note's 'AdicSpacesPartII:R3 is noetherian' is wrong. Evidence: AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-module-acyclicity: 'Let (A, A⁺) be a complete sheafy Tate Huber pair, X = Spa(A, A⁺) and P a finite projective A-module. Then P̃ ... is a sheaf, for every rational U and every finite rational covering 𝔘 of U the augmented Čech complex of P̃ is exact, P̃(U) = P ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U), and Hⁱ(U, P̃) = 0 for i > 0.'

items.name: Vector bundles on an adic affinoid: modules, O_X-modules and O_{X_fét}-modules (Theorem 8.2.22(b))
items.statement: Let X = Spa(A, A⁺) be an adic affinoid space. The categories of finite projective A-modules, of finite locally free O_X-modules and of finite locally free O_{X_fét}-modules are equivalent.
items.note: The first equivalence is Kiehl glueing for sheafy rings (Theorem 2.7.7, PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/102, missing); the second is faithfully flat descent of finite projective modules along finite étale covers (Theorems 1.3.4–1.3.5; PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/16 missing). Nearest plans: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-acyclicity-of-vector-bundles (strongly sheafy X), PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-descent-perfectoid (c) (perfectoid). Would belong in AdicSpacesPartII:R3. The first equivalence is planned in full generality at AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing (sheafy complete Tate pairs, 'No noetherian hypothesis is made'). The second is planned only when the finite étale covers are themselves sheafy: AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-etale-descent assumes '(A, A⁺) and (B, B⁺) sheafy', and H0/etale-acyclicity-of-vector-bundles assumes A strongly sheafy; Kedlaya–Liu's statement covers X_fét for any adic affinoid X, whose objects Spa~(B, B⁺) need not be adic (Remark 8.2.18: 'It is not known that a finite étale extension of a sheafy adic Banach algebra is sheafy'). The purely algebraic faithfully flat descent it needs is item 16 (missing).

items.name: Vector bundles are acyclic on a stable basis (Theorem 8.2.22(c))
items.statement: Let X = Spa(A, A⁺) be an adic affinoid space and suppose X_ét admits a stable basis B. Then for any finite projective A-module M, the presheaf M̃ on X_ét, M̃(Y) = M ⊗_A O(Y), is an acyclic sheaf on B: for Y ∈ B, H⁰(Y, M̃) = M̃(Y) and Hⁱ(Y, M̃) = 0 for i > 0.
items.note: Node AdicSpacesPartII:R5/stable-basis-etale-vector-bundles (c) (explicitly Kedlaya–Liu 8.2.22(c)); ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-acyclicity-of-vector-bundles covers strongly sheafy A. Deduced from (a) and Proposition 8.2.21.

items.name: Vector bundles on the étale site of a stably adic affinoid (Theorem 8.2.22(d))
items.statement: Let X = Spa(A, A⁺) be an adic affinoid space which is stably adic. Then the categories of finite projective A-modules and of finite locally free O_{X_ét}-modules are equivalent.
items.note: Node AdicSpacesPartII:R5/stable-basis-etale-vector-bundles (d); ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-acyclicity-of-vector-bundles (vector bundles on X_an and X_ét correspond, strongly sheafy case; cites 8.2.22(d)). Deduced from (b) and Proposition 8.2.20.

items.name: Perfect and perfectoid spaces (Definition 8.3.1, Remark 8.3.3)
items.statement: A perfect uniform (resp. perfectoid) affinoid space is a preadic affinoid space Spa~(A, A⁺) with (A, A⁺) a perfect uniform adic Banach F_p-algebra (resp. a perfectoid uniform adic Banach Q_p-algebra); it is an adic affinoid space (Theorem 3.1.13, resp. Theorem 3.6.15). A perfect (resp. perfectoid) space is a preadic space covered by open subspaces which are perfect uniform (resp. perfectoid) affinoid spaces; it is an adic space and even stably adic, its perfect uniform (resp. perfectoid) affinoid subspaces forming a basis for the étale topology (Theorems 3.6.14, 3.6.21). An adic affinoid space which is a perfect space is a perfect uniform affinoid space (Remark 8.3.3, by Proposition 3.1.16); the corresponding statement for perfectoid spaces is unknown.
items.locator: §8.3, Definition 8.3.1 and Remark 8.3.3, p. 166; after Scholze [112] (arXiv 1301.0792v5)
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space, P2/perfectoid-space (perfectoid spaces as a full subcategory of adic spaces; characteristic p perfectoid = perfect complete Tate, P1/characteristic-p-perfectoid-iff-perfect), P2/perfectoid-stably-uniform-and-sheafy, P2/characteristic-p-affinoid-perfectoid-criterion (iii) (Remark 8.3.3: an affinoid perfectoid space of characteristic p is affinoid perfectoid; open in characteristic 0), and P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space (i) (the affinoid perfectoid basis of X_ét, 'Kedlaya–Liu 8.3.1: perfectoid spaces are stably adic'). Remark 8.3.3 restates PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/121.

items.name: Preperfectoid, strongly preperfectoid and relatively perfectoid spaces (Definition 8.3.1)
items.statement: A preperfectoid (resp. strongly preperfectoid, relatively perfectoid) affinoid space is a preadic affinoid space Spa~(A, A⁺) with (A, A⁺) a preperfectoid (resp. strongly preperfectoid, relatively perfectoid) adic Banach algebra (Definition 3.7.1); it is an adic affinoid space (Theorem 3.7.4). A preperfectoid (resp. strongly preperfectoid, relatively perfectoid) space is a preadic space covered by open subspaces of this form; it is an adic space and even stably adic, the subspaces which are themselves preperfectoid (resp. strongly preperfectoid, relatively perfectoid) affinoid spaces forming a basis for the étale topology.
items.note: Preperfectoid algebras are PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/170–172 (missing, routed to AdicSpacesPartII:R5); the closest planned class is R5's sousperfectoid spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-adic-space, R5/sousperfectoid-stably-adic). The stable-basis claim is not supported by the cited theorems for these classes (source issue). Would belong in AdicSpacesPartII:R5 next to the sousperfectoid spaces.

items.name: Acyclicity of O on perfect and perfectoid affinoids (Proposition 8.3.2(a)–(b))
items.statement: Let X = Spa(A, A⁺) be a perfect uniform or perfectoid affinoid space, with A carrying its spectral norm. Then H⁰(X, O) = H⁰(X_ét, O) = A, and Hⁱ(X, O) = Hⁱ(X_ét, O) = 0 for i > 0.
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity (iii) and P3/etale-almost-acyclicity (b) (also P3/etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity (ii)); P2 and P3 work with perfectoid Tate pairs of any characteristic, which include the perfect uniform ones. The paper's proof: Theorems 2.8.10, 2.4.23 and 8.2.22.

items.name: Almost acyclicity of O⁺ on perfect and perfectoid affinoids (Proposition 8.3.2(c))
items.statement: Let X = Spa(A, A⁺) be a perfect uniform or perfectoid affinoid space, with A carrying its spectral norm. For i > 0 the groups Hⁱ(X, O_X⁺) and Hⁱ(X_ét, O_X⁺) are annihilated by m_A = {x ∈ A : |x| < 1}, i.e. they are almost zero.
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity (iv) (killed by the topologically nilpotent elements of R⁺, which for the spectral norm is m_A) and P3/etale-almost-acyclicity (a). The paper deduces it from (a)–(b) with Remark 3.1.6 (perfect uniform case) or Proposition 3.6.9 (perfectoid case; findings E28–E29).

items.name: Sheaves of relative period rings on a perfect adic space (Definition 8.3.4)
items.statement: For X a perfect adic space and ∗ one of Ẽ^int, Ẽ, R̃^{int,r}, R̃^{int,+}, R̃^int, R̃^{bd,r}, R̃^{bd,+}, R̃^bd, R̃^{[s,r]}, R̃^r, R̃^+, R̃, there is a sheaf of rings ∗_X on X obtained by glueing the presheaves of Definition 5.3.1 on perfect uniform affinoid subspaces, which are sheaves by Theorem 5.3.3. Viewed as presheaves on X_ét, their sheafifications do not change their values on any perfect adic affinoid space (by Proposition 8.2.21).
items.note: The affinoid sheaf property is PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/195 (missing, route to RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:annuli and RF1); the étale statement also needs the sheaf condition along faithfully finite étale covers (from Proposition 5.5.4, PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/204). The layers glue the spaces Y_S over the base (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:integral-Y/gluing-for-general-base, RF1) rather than these sheaves of rings on the base; the ring R̃^{int,+}_X is the sheaf U ↦ W(O_X⁺(U)).

items.name: The global perfectoid correspondence (Theorem 8.3.5)
items.statement: There is an equivalence of categories between perfectoid adic spaces and pairs (X, I) in which X is a perfect adic space and I is an ideal subsheaf of R̃^{int,+}_X (the sheaf U ↦ W(O_X⁺(U))) locally generated by a single element which is primitive of degree 1 — in the corrected sense, whose reduction z̄ is a unit of R (finding E23); a morphism (Y, J) → (X, I) is a morphism f: Y → X of perfect uniform adic spaces such that J is the pullback of I (printed: 'J is isomorphic to the pullback of I', to be read as J being the ideal generated by the image of I). The equivalence is compatible with rational localizations, fibred products and étale morphisms, and corresponding spaces are functorially homeomorphic.
items.note: The global form of Theorem 3.6.5 (PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/156, planned at PerfectoidSpaces:P1). Nearest plans: PerfectoidSpaces:P1/untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals and P1/marked-untilt (affinoid), P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting, P2/tilting-slice-equivalence (c) (untilts over a fixed perfectoid base), DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-of-a-tate-pair and D6/untilt-descent-along-v-covers (marked untilts glue); none states the equivalence with pairs (X, I). The printed 'J is isomorphic to the pullback of I' has to be read as J being the ideal generated by the image of I (principal ideals generated by primitive elements are always abstractly isomorphic). Compatibility with fibred products also uses Proposition 3.6.11 (finding E30; PerfectoidSpaces/E20), not cited in the proof. Would belong in PerfectoidSpaces:P2.

items.name: Scholze's tilting equivalence over a perfectoid field (Corollary 8.3.6)
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid analytic field of characteristic 0 and K′ the corresponding perfect analytic field of characteristic p (Theorem 3.5.3; the tilt of K). There is a canonical equivalence of categories between perfectoid adic spaces over K and perfect uniform adic spaces over K′, compatible with fibred products; corresponding spaces have homeomorphic underlying topological spaces and isomorphic étale topoi.
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-slice-equivalence, P2/perfectoid-spaces-over-a-perfectoid-field-comparison (iii) (Scholze's Proposition 6.17 as the slice equivalence over Spa(K, K⁺₀)), P2/tilting-commutes-with-fibre-products and P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence (equivalence of étale topoi).

items.name: A surjective étale cover acquires a faithfully finite étale factor near each point of ℳ(A) (Lemma 8.4.1)
items.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be an adic Banach ring and Spec(A′) → Spec(A) a surjective étale morphism of schemes. Then for every α ∈ ℳ(A) there is a rational localization (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) encircling α such that A′ ⊗_A B splits as a direct sum of subrings, at least one of which is faithfully finite étale over B.
items.note: A refinement of Lemma 2.4.17 (item 'Stalks and Hausdorff localizations are henselian', missing): the Hausdorff localization A_α is a henselian local ring, so an étale A_α-algebra with a prime over its maximal ideal has a finite étale local factor, which spreads out to a rational localization encircling α. Nearest planned layer: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian (affinoid henselizations after Huber §3); Mathlib has HenselianLocalRing but not the splitting of étale algebras over a henselian local ring. The last display of the proof names an undefined ring S for B (source issue on the proof of Lemma 8.4.1).

items.name: Étale ℚ_p-local systems on Spec(A) are isogeny ℤ_p-local systems near each point of ℳ(A) (Lemma 8.4.2)
items.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be an adic Banach ring and V an étale ℚ_p-local system over Spec(A) (Definition 1.4.1). Then for every α ∈ ℳ(A) there is a rational localization (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) encircling α such that V ×_{Spec(A)} Spec(B) is an isogeny ℤ_p-local system on Spec(B).
items.note: Proof: Lemma 8.4.1 plus descent of isogeny ℤ_p-local systems along faithfully finite étale maps (Lemma 1.4.8, item missing, routed with §1.4 to InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0).

items.name: Étale ℤ_p-local systems on a preadic space (Definition 8.4.3, Remark 8.4.4)
items.statement: Let X be a preadic space. For a covering of X by preadic affinoid spaces U_i = Spa~(A_i, A_i⁺), a descent datum of étale ℤ_p-local systems consists of an étale ℤ_p-local system V_i on Spec(A_i) for each i, a covering of each U_i ∩ U_j by preadic affinoid spaces Spa~(B_k, B_k⁺), and isomorphisms between the restrictions of V_i and V_j to Spec(B_k) satisfying the cocycle condition. The category of étale ℤ_p-local systems over X is the direct 2-limit (as in Remark 1.2.9) of these categories of descent data over all covering families. By the local factorization of étale morphisms (Remark 8.4.4) the same category results from coverings in the étale topology (Definitions 8.2.16, 8.2.19). For X = Spa(A, A°) with A an affinoid algebra over an analytic field it is equivalent to de Jong's category defined through étale covering spaces [33].
items.note: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/torsion-local-systems defines, on a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space, lisse ℤ_ℓ-sheaves for every prime ℓ (ℓ = p included) as inverse systems of locally constant sheaves of ℤ/ℓ^m-modules on X_ét; with H0/local-systems-and-finite-etale-covers and AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (c) (= Lemma 8.2.17(a)) this agrees with the present definition on such spaces (compare Remark 8.4.5). The paper's definition also covers preadic spaces not known to be sheafy, which is not planned. Status changed from planned (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0) to missing by the independent review: The item is Kedlaya–Liu's definition for an arbitrary preadic space (descent data of étale ℤ_p-local systems on Spec(A_i) over preadic affinoid covers, 2-colimit over coverings). H0 plans lisse ℤ_ℓ-sheaves only on locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces, and the note itself says 'The paper's definition also covers preadic spaces not known to be sheafy, which is not planned.' The Spec(A_i)-descent-data formulation and its agreement with the étale-topology version (Remark 8.4.4) are also not stated. Either downgrade to missing or keep 'planned' with an explicit special-case note; missing is consistent with items 276–282 (the ℚ_p-version and the comparisons are all missing).

items.name: Étale ℚ_p-local systems on a preadic space (Definition 8.4.3, Remark 8.4.4)
items.statement: Let X be a preadic space. The category of étale ℚ_p-local systems over X is defined as in the ℤ_p case: for a covering of X by preadic affinoid spaces Spa~(A_i, A_i⁺), a descent datum consists of étale ℚ_p-local systems V_i on Spec(A_i) (Definition 1.4.1: descent data of isogeny ℤ_p-local systems for the étale topology of Spec(A_i)) with isomorphisms of restrictions on coverings of the overlaps by preadic affinoid spaces satisfying the cocycle condition, and one takes the direct 2-limit over all covering families. Coverings in the étale topology give the same category (Remark 8.4.4). For X = Spa(A, A°), A an affinoid algebra over an analytic field, it is equivalent to de Jong's category [33].
items.note: Not planned. PadicHodgeTheory:P8/lisse-zp-sheaf (Scholze, Definition 8.1) takes L ⊗ ℚ̂_p for lisse Ẑ_p-sheaves on locally noetherian X, which gives only isogeny ℤ_p-local systems, and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB4/slope-zero-local-systems uses pro-étale E-local systems on perfectoid spaces (Fargues–Scholze); no node defines ℚ_p-local systems by étale-local isogeny descent on (pre)adic spaces or compares them with pro-étale ℚ_p-local systems (the scheme analogue is Theorem 1.4.11, item missing). By Corollary 8.4.7 they are locally isogeny ℤ_p-local systems.

items.name: ℤ_p-local systems on Spec(A) and on Spa(A, A⁺) agree (Remark 8.4.5)
items.statement: For an adic Banach ring (A, A⁺), the natural functor from étale ℤ_p-local systems over Spec(A) to étale ℤ_p-local systems over Spa~(A, A⁺) is an equivalence of categories, because ℤ_p-local systems are determined by finite étale algebras (Remark 1.4.3) and these glue over covering families of rational localizations (Theorem 2.6.9). The corresponding functor for étale ℚ_p-local systems is not an equivalence in general (Remark 8.4.8).
items.note: For strongly sheafy A this is a formal consequence of planned nodes (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent and A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (c), with ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/local-systems-and-finite-etale-covers), but no node states the comparison with the étale site of Spec(A); Theorem 2.6.9 for general adic Banach rings is the missing item 'Descent of finite étale algebras along rational coverings'. KL's input Theorem 2.6.9 is planned without any sheafiness hypothesis: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent ('Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair (no sheafiness assumed) ... A → A_1 × ⋯ × A_n is an effective descent morphism for finite étale algebras (Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 2.6.9)'). The comparison itself (with Remark 1.4.3 on ℤ_p-local systems as systems of finite étale algebras, §1.4 missing) is stated by no node.

items.name: Étale ℚ_p-local systems on Spa(A, A⁺) are locally isogeny ℤ_p-local systems (Proposition 8.4.6)
items.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be an adic Banach ring and V an étale ℚ_p-local system over Spa~(A, A⁺). Then for every α ∈ ℳ(A) there is a rational localization (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) encircling α such that the restriction of V to Spa~(B, B⁺) is an isogeny ℤ_p-local system.
items.note: Proof as for Lemma 8.4.2: the lattice functors of Remark 1.4.7 are represented by finite étale maps L_m(T) → X over a preadic space (Lemma 8.2.17(a)); with Theorem 1.2.8 and Lemma 2.4.17 one finds a faithfully finite étale (B, B⁺) → (C, C⁺) and a ℤ_p-lattice over Spa~(C, C⁺) with descent datum, and Lemma 1.4.8 descends it. All §1.4 inputs are missing items.

items.name: Étale ℚ_p-local systems as descent data of isogeny ℤ_p-local systems (Corollary 8.4.7)
items.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be an adic Banach ring. Every étale ℚ_p-local system over Spa~(A, A⁺) can be realized as a descent datum for isogeny ℤ_p-local systems for some strong covering family of rational localizations of (A, A⁺).
items.note: From Proposition 8.4.6 and the compactness of ℳ(A). Used in Remark 8.4.9 and, implicitly, in Theorem 8.5.12.

items.name: ℚ_p-local systems on Spec(A) versus Spa(A, A⁺): fully faithful, not essentially surjective (Remark 8.4.8)
items.statement: For an adic Banach ring (A, A⁺), the natural functor from étale ℚ_p-local systems over Spec(A) to étale ℚ_p-local systems over Spa~(A, A⁺) is fully faithful, but need not be essentially surjective, even when A is a reduced affinoid algebra over an analytic field (de Jong). For A a normal integral affinoid algebra over an analytic field [the text says only 'integral'], Spec(A) is normal and noetherian, so ℤ_p-ILoc(Spec(A)) = ℚ_p-Loc(Spec(A)) (Remark 1.4.9), whereas étale ℚ_p-local systems over Spa(A, A⁺) correspond to continuous representations of de Jong's étale fundamental group of ℳ(A) [33, §2.6] on finite-dimensional ℚ_p-vector spaces, which can have non-compact image: p-adic uniformization such as the Tate uniformization of an elliptic curve with split multiplicative reduction (Example 8.5.17), and Rapoport–Zink period morphisms [33, §7].
items.note: Full faithfulness is asserted without proof. The printed hypothesis 'integral' must be 'normal' (source issue on Remark 8.4.8); the Tate-curve piece of Example 8.5.17 is smooth, so the conclusion stands. Not planned (see the external item on de Jong's fundamental group).

items.name: Extensions of isogeny ℤ_p-local systems inside étale ℚ_p-local systems on Spa(A, A⁺) descend to Spec(A) (Remark 8.4.9)
items.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be an adic Banach ring and V_1, V_2 isogeny ℤ_p-local systems on Spec(A). Every extension 0 → V_1 → V → V_2 → 0 in the category of étale ℚ_p-local systems on Spa~(A, A⁺) descends to an extension of isogeny ℤ_p-local systems on Spec(A).
items.note: Proof: write V_i = T_i ⊗ ℚ_p; by Corollary 8.4.7 the extension is given by classes x_i ∈ Ext(T_2, T_1) ⊗ ℚ_p over a strong covering by rational localizations B_i; rescaling T_1 by powers of p makes each x_i integral and each x_i − x_j vanish in Ext(T_2, T_1) over B_i ⊗̂_A B_j, so the extension glues to one of étale ℤ_p-local systems on Spa~(A, A⁺), which descends to Spec(A) by Remark 8.4.5. Used for H¹ in Theorem 8.6.4.

items.name: De Jong: étale fundamental groups of non-archimedean analytic spaces and their ℚ_p-representations (external, [33])
items.statement: (A. J. de Jong, Étale fundamental groups of non-Archimedean analytic spaces, Compositio Math. 97 (1995).) For a connected affinoid algebra A over an analytic field K, de Jong defines an étale fundamental group of ℳ(A) through étale covering spaces (not only finite ones) [33, §2]; its continuous representations on finite-dimensional ℚ_p-vector spaces correspond to étale ℚ_p-local systems on Spa(A, A°) [33, Lemma 2.6], these agree with the categories of Definition 8.4.3 for X = Spa(A, A°), and such representations can have non-compact image (Tate curves; Rapoport–Zink period morphisms [33, §7]).
items.note: Not planned: InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.0 and AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-galois-category plan only the profinite fundamental group of finite étale covers, whose ℚ_p-representations give isogeny ℤ_p-local systems. Remark 8.5.19 adds, without proof, the expectation that ℳ(A) and ℳ(ℛ̃^{int,1}_R/(z)) have the same étale fundamental group (via Theorems 3.3.7(c) and 3.6.21) once the latter is defined.

items.name: Approximate solutions of x = y − y^{p^d} in a perfect Banach algebra (Lemma 8.5.2)
items.statement: Let R be a perfect Banach algebra over 𝔽_p with spectral norm α. For every c > 1, every positive integer d and every x ∈ R there is y ∈ R with α(x − y + y^{p^d}) < c. Explicitly: y = 0 if α(x) ≤ 1; otherwise y = −(x^{p^{−d}} + ⋯ + x^{p^{−md}}) with m so large that α(x)^{p^{−md}} < c, for which x − y + y^{p^d} = x^{p^{−md}}.
items.note: Elementary (Frobenius is additive and α is power-multiplicative); used entrywise in the successive approximation of Theorem 8.5.3. Not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti and not stated by any node; it belongs with Theorem 8.5.3.

items.name: Étale ℤ_{p^d}-local systems and φ^d-modules over W(R) and ℛ̃^int_R (Theorem 8.5.3)
items.statement: (Hypothesis 8.5.1: d is a positive integer, ℚ_{p^d} the unramified extension of ℚ_p of degree d, ℤ_{p^d} its valuation ring.) Let (R, R⁺) be a perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_{p^d}. The following categories are equivalent: (a) étale ℤ_{p^d}-local systems over Spec(R) (equivalently over Spa(R, R⁺)); (b) étale ℤ_{p^d}-local systems over Spec(R_0) (equivalently Spa(R_0, R_0⁺)) for any complete subring R_0 of R whose completed direct perfection is R, with R_0⁺ = R_0 ∩ R⁺; (c) étale ℤ_{p^d}-local systems over Spec(A) (equivalently Spa(A, A⁺)) for (A, A⁺) corresponding to (R, R⁺) as in Theorem 3.6.5; (d) φ^d-modules over ℰ̃^int_R = W(R); (e) φ^d-modules over ℛ̃^int_R. The functor from (e) to (d) is base extension.
items.note: (a)⇔(b) and (a)⇔(c) come from Remark 1.4.3 with Theorem 3.1.15 (missing) and Theorem 3.6.21 (planned PerfectoidSpaces:P3); (a)⇔(d) is the ℤ_p-form of Katz's correspondence, Proposition 3.2.7 (missing; routed to PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology:PG.1, which plans Fontaine's equivalence over fields only). (d)⇔(e) — descent of étale φ^d-modules from W(R) to ℛ̃^int_R: full faithfulness through Proposition 7.3.6, essential surjectivity by successive approximation with Lemma 8.5.2 — is an overconvergence theorem for perfect uniform R that no stage plans (PG.2 plans Cherbonnier–Colmez only for representations of finite extensions of ℚ_p). Remark 8.5.4 reads (a)⇔(d) as nonabelian Artin–Schreier theory via Lang torsors (Milne [100, Proposition 4.12]). (a)⇔(e) for d = 1 and affinoid perfectoid Spa(R,R⁺) is planned via SW 22.3.2 (pro-étale ℤ_p-local systems on Spa); the W(R) form (d), d > 1, (b) and the Spec(R) formulation are not. The item note's claim that 'no stage plans' (d)⇔(e) is correct for W(R) but should cite this route. Evidence: Same PAPER-SCHOLZE-WEINSTEIN-20 route 6 / item /159 as for 285 (affinoid S: 'φ-modules over the integral Robba ring R̃_R^int'); the route's reason attributes 'Theorem 12.3.4, Kedlaya–Liu 8.5.3' but SW-20/85 (Theorem 12.3.4) is stated only over C♭ ('φ-modules over R̃^int, φ-modules over W(C♭) and finite free ℤ_p-modules are equivalent').

items.name: Étale ℤ_{p^d}-local systems on a perfectoid space and φ^d-modules on its tilt (Theorem 8.5.5)
items.statement: Let X be a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_{p^d} and X′ the corresponding perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} (Theorem 8.3.5). The following categories are equivalent: (a) étale ℤ_{p^d}-local systems over X; (b) étale ℤ_{p^d}-local systems over X′; (c) étale ℤ_{p^d}-local systems over X_0′ for any adic space X_0′ whose inverse perfection (inverse limit along absolute Frobenius) is isomorphic to X′; (d) φ^d-modules over ℰ̃^int_{X′}; (e) φ^d-modules over ℛ̃^int_{X′}.
items.note: Globalization of Theorem 8.5.3 through Theorem 8.3.5. (a)⇔(b) also follows from the planned tilting equivalence of étale topoi (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence) once ℤ_p-local systems are sheaves on X_ét (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/torsion-local-systems); the φ-module descriptions (d), (e) and part (c) are not planned. With S = X′ perfectoid of char p (KL Hypothesis 5.0.1 makes R perfectoid Tate), SW 22.3.2 plans (b)⇔(e) for d = 1 with pro-étale local systems; d > 1 (ℤ_{p^d}, φ^d), the W(R)-form (d) and (c) (inverse perfections) are not planned. Cite the SW route in the note. Evidence: Accepted PAPER-SCHOLZE-WEINSTEIN-20 route 6 (source → VB3/VB4), review: 'VB4 owns the equivalence of slope-zero bundles with pro-étale local systems, and its integral forms (Theorem 12.3.4, Propositions 22.3.2 and 22.6.1) ... extend that layer.' Routed item PAPER-SCHOLZE-WEINSTEIN-20/159 (Prop. 22.3.2): 'L ↦ L ⊗_{ℤ_p} 𝒪_{𝒴_{[0,r]}(S)} is an equivalence from pro-étale ℤ_p-local systems on S to φ^{-1}-modules on 𝒴_{[0,r]}(S) (equivalently, for affinoid S, φ-modules over the integral Robba ring R̃_R^int ...)'. (a)⇔(b) by PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence.

items.name: Isogeny ℤ_{p^d}-local systems and globally étale φ^d-modules (Theorem 8.5.6)
items.statement: Let (R, R⁺) be a perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_{p^d}. The following categories are equivalent: (a) isogeny ℤ_{p^d}-local systems over Spec(R) (equivalently Spa(R, R⁺)); (b) isogeny ℤ_{p^d}-local systems over Spec(R_0) (equivalently Spa(R_0, R_0⁺)) for any complete subring R_0 of R whose completed direct perfection is R, with R_0⁺ = R_0 ∩ R⁺; (c) isogeny ℤ_{p^d}-local systems over Spec(A) (equivalently Spa(A, A⁺)) for (A, A⁺) corresponding to (R, R⁺) as in Theorem 3.6.5; (d) globally étale φ^d-modules over ℰ̃_R; (e) globally étale φ^d-modules over ℛ̃^bd_R; (f) globally étale φ^d-modules over ℛ̃_R. (Globally étale: admitting a locally free étale model, Definition 7.3.4.) The functors from (e) to (d) and from (e) to (f) are base extensions.
items.note: From Theorem 8.5.3 and Corollary 5.2.4 (ℰ̃_R^φ = ℛ̃_R^φ = W(R^φ)[p^{-1}]): V = T ⊗ ℚ_p goes to the base extension of the φ^d-module of T, and a φ^d-module goes to T ⊗ ℚ_p for the local system T of any locally free étale model. Not planned; VB4 plans only the rational slope-zero statement for bundles on X_S (see Theorem 8.5.12).

items.name: Isogeny (c, d)-ℤ_p-local systems and étale (c, d)-ℚ_p-local systems (Definition 8.5.7)
items.statement: For c, d ∈ ℤ with d > 0, an isogeny (c, d)-ℤ_p-local system on a scheme X is an isogeny ℤ_{p^d}-local system V on X equipped with a semilinear action on sections of the Frobenius automorphism τ of ℚ_{p^d}, such that p^c τ^d acts as the identity. Étale (c, d)-ℚ_p-local systems are defined in the same way from étale ℚ_{p^d}-local systems (and, through Definition 8.4.3, on preadic spaces).
items.note: Compare Berger [12, Théorème 3.2.3]. Not planned; the field-level counterpart is the isoclinic isocrystal of VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0.

items.name: (c, d)-local systems depend only on the ratio c/d (Definition 8.5.7)
items.statement: For c, d, c′, d′ ∈ ℤ with d, d′ > 0 and c′/d′ = c/d, the categories of isogeny (c, d)-ℤ_p-local systems and of isogeny (c′, d′)-ℤ_p-local systems on any scheme are naturally equivalent, and likewise for étale (c, d)-ℚ_p-local systems. The proof reduces to c′ = ce, d′ = de for a positive integer e and uses Hilbert's Theorem 90.
items.note: Stated as an easy exercise. For c′ = ce, d′ = de the operator p^cτ^d on a (c′, d′)-system is a semilinear action of Gal(ℚ_{p^{de}}/ℚ_{p^d}) ≅ ℤ/e, and Galois descent of vector spaces (Hilbert 90 for GL_n) gives the (c, d)-system of its fixed points; Mathlib has Hilbert 90 only for units (groupCohomology.isMulCoboundary₁_of_isMulCocycle₁_of_aut_to_units). Used by Corollary 8.5.13. Mathlib has Hilbert 90 only for units (groupCohomology.isMulCoboundary₁_of_isMulCocycle₁_of_aut_to_units); Tau Ceti has Galois descent for semilinear representations (tauceti:TauCeti.GaloisDescent.span_invariants_eq_top, TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/GaloisDescent/Span.lean:38, and tauceti:TauCeti.GaloisDescent.liftBaseChange_injective_of_invariant, Injective.lean:42), which together give V ≅ L ⊗_k V^G for a semilinear action of a finite Aut(L/k) — the descent step of this exercise.

items.name: Isogeny (c, d)-ℤ_p-local systems and globally (c, d)-pure φ-modules (Theorem 8.5.8)
items.statement: Let (R, R⁺) be a perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_{p^d} and c ∈ ℤ. The following categories are equivalent: (a) isogeny (c, d)-ℤ_p-local systems over Spec(R); (b) isogeny (c, d)-ℤ_p-local systems over Spec(R_0) for any complete subring R_0 of R whose completed direct perfection is R [the text says 'any subring']; (c) isogeny (c, d)-ℤ_p-local systems over Spec(A) for A = ℛ̃^{int,1}_R/(z), for any z ∈ W(R⁺) primitive of degree 1 (with the extra condition that z̄ be a unit of R, which the authors' errata impose from §3.6 on); (d) globally (c, d)-pure φ-modules over ℰ̃_R; (e) globally (c, d)-pure φ-modules over ℛ̃^bd_R; (f) globally (c, d)-pure φ-modules over ℛ̃_R. The functors from (e) to (d) and to (f) are base extensions.
items.note: 'Immediate from Theorem 8.5.6.' Part (b) needs R_0 complete, as in Theorems 8.5.3(b) and 8.5.6(b) (source issue on Theorem 8.5.8(b)); the condition on z is finding E23 of this extraction. For R = L an analytic field, (d)–(f) supply the essential surjectivity that Proposition 4.2.11(a) (item planned in RD.2) defers to this section.

items.name: Pointwise purity, slope polygons, pure and étale loci on perfect uniform adic spaces (Definition 8.5.9)
items.statement: Let X be a perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p and M a φ-module over one of ℰ̃_X, ℛ̃^bd_X, ℛ̃_X (Definition 8.3.4). For x ∈ X, M is (c, d)-pure at x if it is (c, d)-pure (Definition 7.3.4) at the rank-1 seminorm induced by x, and M is (c, d)-pure if it is so at every x ∈ X. The slope polygon of M at x is that at the induced rank-1 seminorm; this defines the pure locus and the étale locus of M in X. These sets are pulled back from subsets of the real quotient X̄ (Definition 8.2.11) when the latter is defined.
items.note: As for rank, degree, slope and the pure and étale loci on ℳ(R) (Definitions 7.2.1–7.2.3, item planned in VB1, VB4): VB1/degree-rank-slope-and-HN-formalism and VB4 ('construct the geometric HN polygon of E_s') define slopes and HN polygons of bundles on X_S at geometric points of a perfectoid S. The sheaf-level notion on perfect uniform adic spaces and its descent to the real quotient are not planned. The sheaf-level notion (φ-modules over the sheaves ℰ̃_X, ℛ̃^bd_X, ℛ̃_X of Definition 8.3.4, item 270, missing) and its descent to the real quotient (items 250–251, missing) are not planned; only the ℛ̃-case at a point is (VB1/VB4). A perfect uniform adic space over F_p is here a perfectoid space of characteristic p.

items.name: Local φ^d-modules: full faithfulness, and an equivalence over ℛ̃ only (Remark 8.5.10)
items.statement: Let (R, R⁺) be a perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p and X = Spa(R, R⁺). For ∗ ∈ {ℰ̃, ℛ̃^bd, ℛ̃}, the natural functor from φ^d-modules over ∗_R to φ^d-modules over the sheaf ∗_X (called local φ^d-modules over ∗_R) is fully faithful (Theorem 5.3.3). For ∗ = ℛ̃ it is an equivalence of categories (Corollary 6.3.13); for ∗ = ℰ̃ and ∗ = ℛ̃^bd it is not (Example 8.5.17). A φ^d-module over ∗_R is pure (resp. étale) if and only if the corresponding φ^d-module over ∗_X is.
items.note: The ℛ̃ equivalence is gluing of φ-modules over rational coverings (Corollary 6.3.13, part of the item planned in VB2:ampleness/RF3 with descent in VB1: bundles on X_S glue over analytic covers of S). Full faithfulness rests on the sheaf property of ℰ̃, ℛ̃^bd, ℛ̃ on Spa(R, R⁺) (Theorem 5.3.3, item missing); the failure of gluing over ℰ̃ and ℛ̃^bd is not planned.

items.name: The pure and étale loci are open and partially proper (Lemma 8.5.11)
items.statement: Let X be a perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} and M a φ^d-module over ℛ̃_X. Then the pure locus and the étale locus of M [printed 'of ℛ̃_X'] are open and partially proper (partial properness, Definition 8.2.11, presupposes X over an analytic field). In particular, by Lemma 8.2.12, if X is taut then so are the pure locus and the étale locus.
items.note: Immediate from Corollary 7.3.8 (openness of the pure and étale loci in ℳ(R), item missing). VB4 plans semicontinuity of the HN polygon for bundles on X_S (Fargues–Scholze II.2.19(i)), which yields openness of the semistable locus in that setting; partial properness and tautness of these loci are not planned (AdicEtaleGeometry:A2 plans partially proper morphisms, not the real quotient). Source issue on the statement.

items.name: Étale (c, d)-ℚ_p-local systems on a perfectoid space and (c, d)-pure φ-modules on its tilt (Theorem 8.5.12)
items.statement: Let X be a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_{p^d}, X′ the corresponding perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d}, and c ∈ ℤ. The following categories are equivalent: (a) étale (c, d)-ℚ_p-local systems over X; (b) étale (c, d)-ℚ_p-local systems over X′; (c) étale (c, d)-ℚ_p-local systems over X_0′ for any adic space X_0′ whose inverse perfection is isomorphic to X′; (d) (c, d)-pure φ-modules over ℰ̃_{X′}; (e) (c, d)-pure φ-modules over ℛ̃^bd_{X′}; (f) (c, d)-pure φ-modules over ℛ̃_{X′}.
items.note: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB4/slope-zero-local-systems (Fargues–Scholze II.2.20) plans, for S perfectoid, the equivalence between pro-étale E-local systems and bundles on X_S with constant HN polygon 0; with E = ℚ_p and bundles = φ-modules over ℛ̃ (Theorem 8.7.8; Theorem 6.3.12 is planned in VB2:ampleness/RF3) this is (a)⇔(f) for c = 0, though with pro-étale ℚ_p-local systems instead of étale-local isogeny descent data. PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-equivalence gives (a)⇔(b). Not planned: c ≠ 0 (local systems with Frobenius structure), the forms (d), (e) over ℰ̃ and ℛ̃^bd, and (c). The proof, 'immediate from Theorems 8.3.5 and 8.5.8', also uses Corollary 8.4.7 and Remark 8.5.10. Corollary 8.7.10 restates the case c = 0 with vector bundles on FF_X. Status changed from planned (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB4, PerfectoidSpaces:P3) to missing by the independent review: Only the special case c = 0, (a)⇔(b) and (a)⇔(f) (with pro-étale instead of étale-isogeny local systems) is planned, as the item's own note records ('Not planned: c ≠ 0 ..., the forms (d), (e) over ℰ̃ and ℛ̃^bd, and (c)'). The theorem's content is the (c,d)-version for all c and the six-way equivalence; its inputs 8.3.5, 8.4.7, 8.5.8, 8.5.10 (items 271, 279, 289, 291) are all missing. Recommend missing, with the c = 0 case cited as partial overlap (it is Corollary 8.7.10, item 312, which stays planned in VB4). Note also that the accepted SCHOLZE-WEINSTEIN-20 route 6 routes SW Theorem 12.3.4 (= KL 8.5.3) to VB4 (see fork notes).

items.name: Purity of slope s does not depend on the choice of (c, d) (Corollary 8.5.13)
items.statement: Let X be a perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d}. A φ^d-module over ℰ̃_X, ℛ̃^bd_X or ℛ̃_X is pure of slope s at a point x ∈ X if and only if it is (c′, d′)-pure at x for every (not just one) pair of integers (c′, d′) with d′ a positive multiple of d and c′/d′ = s.
items.note: From Theorem 8.5.8 and the (c, d)-independence of Definition 8.5.7; Definition 7.3.4 (item on pure models) anticipates it. Not planned.

items.name: Pointwise pure φ^d-modules over ℰ̃_R, ℛ̃^bd_R and ℛ̃_R are pure (Corollary 8.5.14)
items.statement: Let (R, R⁺) be as in Hypothesis 5.0.1 (a perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p that is a Banach algebra over an analytic field) and M a φ^d-module over ℰ̃_R, ℛ̃^bd_R or ℛ̃_R. If M is pointwise pure (M ⊗ ℋ(β) is pure for every β ∈ ℳ(R)), then M is pure (it admits a locally free local pure model at every β ∈ ℳ(R)).
items.note: Over ℛ̃_R this is Corollary 7.3.9 (item on spreading pure models, missing). Over ℰ̃_R and ℛ̃^bd_R the proof takes a cyclic vector of M ⊗ ℰ̃_{ℋ(β)} (resp. ℛ̃^bd_{ℋ(β)}) for p^{c′}φ^{d′} (perturbing a basis by powers [x]^{r_i}, x ∈ L^× small, r_i ∈ ℤ[p^{-1}]), spreads it to a rational localization S encircling β, and takes the W(S)- (resp. ℛ̃^int_S-) span of the cyclic basis as a free pure model by [83, Lemma 5.2.4] (external item). Remark 7.3.5 uses it for the equivalence of conditions (b)–(e) over ℰ̃_R and ℛ̃^bd_R.

items.name: Purity descends along maps with surjective adic spectra (Corollary 8.5.15)
items.statement: Let (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) be a bounded homomorphism of perfect uniform adic Banach algebras over 𝔽_{p^d} such that Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺) is surjective, and let M be a local φ^d-module over ℰ̃_R (resp. ℛ̃^bd_R, ℛ̃_R). Then M is pure if and only if M ⊗ ℰ̃_S (resp. M ⊗ ℛ̃^bd_S, M ⊗ ℛ̃_S) is pure.
items.note: The proof treats the nontrivial direction: purity after base change makes M pointwise pure by Corollary 4.2.14 (item planned in RD.2/RD.1; stated there over ℛ̃_L), hence pure by Corollary 8.5.14.

items.name: Purity and étaleness are detected after a surjective morphism of perfectoid spaces (Corollary 8.5.16)
items.statement: Let Y → X be a surjective morphism of perfectoid adic spaces and M a φ^d-module over ℛ̃_X (the sheaf of the tilt X′, on the same underlying space). Then M is pure (resp. étale) if and only if its pullback to ℛ̃_Y is pure (resp. étale).
items.note: Stated without proof; the global form of Corollary 8.5.15. In VB4's curve language purity is a pointwise condition on the HN polygon, but its comparison with purity in the paper's sense (local pure models, Corollary 7.3.9) is not planned.

items.name: A Tate-curve ℚ_p-local system with no φ-module over ℰ̃_R or ℛ̃^bd_R (Example 8.5.17)
items.statement: Let K = 𝔽_p((q)) with |q| = ω < 1, B = K{ω²/T, T, U/ω^{−2}}/(U(T − q) − 1) (so Spa(B, B°) is the annulus ω² ≤ |T| ≤ 1 minus the open disc |T − q| < ω²), and B_1 = K{ω²/T, T/ω²}, B_2 = K{1/T, T} (its boundary circles |T| = ω² and |T| = 1). The substitution T ↦ q²T is an isomorphism σ_q: B_1 → B_2 [printed as a map B_2 → B_1]; identifying the two circles through it gives a strictly affinoid subspace Spa(A, A°) of the Tate curve over K with parameter q², the analytification of a smooth projective genus-1 curve over K. Glueing the trivial ℚ_p-local system on Spa(B, B°) along this identification by matching the generator 1 on one circle with p on the other gives an étale ℚ_p-local system V on Spa(A, A°). Let R, S, S_1, S_2 be the completed perfections of A, B, B_1, B_2 and X = Spa(R, R°). Then V corresponds to no étale φ-module over ℰ̃_R or ℛ̃^bd_R (a nonzero v would give x ∈ ℰ̃_S with x_2 = pσ_q(x_1) ∈ ℰ̃_{S_2}, forcing x ∈ ∩_m p^m W(S) = 0).
