By Theorem 8.5.12, V does correspond to an étale φ-module over ℛ̃_R and to étale φ-modules over ℰ̃_X and ℛ̃^bd_X, which therefore do not descend to ℰ̃_R, ℛ̃^bd_R (an obstruction to glueing finite projective modules over these rings, Remark 5.3.7); and the étale φ-module over ℛ̃_R admits no étale model, locally free or not.
items.note: Remark 7.3.5 uses it for '(c) does not imply (b)' over ℛ̃_R, and Remark 8.5.10 for the failure of essential surjectivity over ℰ̃ and ℛ̃^bd. The Tate-curve input (external item) is planned in TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.7; the example itself is not planned. Source issues on the direction of σ_q and on 'the Tate curve over X'.

items.name: An étale ℚ_p-local system whose φ-modules are étale but not globally étale (Example 8.5.18)
items.statement: Let K be an algebraically closed analytic field of characteristic p ≠ 2, R the completed perfection of K{X, Y}/(Y² − (X² − 1)²), and X = Spa(R, R°). Then X has an étale cover by a doubly infinite chain of copies of the (perfected) closed unit disc Spa(K{X}, K{X}°), which, as in Example 8.5.17, gives an étale ℚ_p-local system V on X that is not an isogeny ℤ_p-local system. By Theorems 8.5.8 and 8.5.12, V corresponds to étale φ-modules over ℰ̃_X, ℛ̃^bd_X [printed Ẽ^bd_X] and ℛ̃_X that are not globally étale.
items.note: Y² = (X² − 1)² is the union of the two discs Y = ±(X² − 1), meeting at (±1, 0), so X is a cycle of two perfected discs. Remark 7.3.5 uses the example for '(c) does not imply (a)' over ℰ̃_R, ℛ̃^bd_R and ℛ̃_R; over ℰ̃_R and ℛ̃^bd_R this needs the modules to descend from ℰ̃_X, ℛ̃^bd_X to ℰ̃_R, ℛ̃^bd_R, which the example does not show and Example 8.5.17 shows can fail (source issue). Not planned.

items.name: Tate uniformization: the Tate curve as a rigid-analytic quotient (external, [120, Theorem V.3.1])
items.statement: (As used in Example 8.5.17.) For a complete nonarchimedean field K and q ∈ K^× with |q| < 1, the Tate curve E_q is the elliptic curve over K with split multiplicative reduction given by explicit Weierstrass equations in q (Silverman, Advanced Topics in the Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves, Theorem V.3.1), and the rigid-analytic quotient 𝔾_m^an/q^ℤ, obtained from the closed annulus |q| ≤ |T| ≤ 1 by identifying its boundary circles through T ↦ qT, is the analytification of E_q.
items.note: TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.7 plans 'Tate uniformization and the Schottky/Mumford-curve quotient'. tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves#layer-4-elliptic-curves-over-local-fields--reduction-tates-algorithm-the-tate-curve-aec-vii-ataec-ivv plans the Tate curve over any complete rank-1 valued field with its point-level uniformization L^×/q^ℤ ≅ E_q(L), explicitly excluding the rigid-space quotient that the example uses. In the example K = 𝔽_p((q)) has characteristic p and the parameter is q².

items.name: Kedlaya: the slope polygon of a Frobenius module is read off a cyclic vector (external, [83, Lemma 5.2.4])
items.statement: (Kedlaya, Slope filtrations revisited, Doc. Math. 10 (2005), Lemma 5.2.4.) Let M be a σ-module of rank n over Γ[π^{-1}] (for instance over ℰ̃_L = W(L)[p^{-1}], L a perfect analytic field) with a cyclic vector v, i.e. v, Fv, …, F^{n−1}v form a basis, and F^n v + a_{n−1}F^{n−1}v + ⋯ + a_0 v = 0. Then the generic HN polygon of M is the Newton polygon of x^n + a_{n−1}x^{n−1} + ⋯ + a_0. As used in Corollary 8.5.14 (with F = p^{c′}φ^{d′}, at every point of ℳ(S)): if M ⊗ ℰ̃_S has a cyclic basis and is pointwise pure of slope 0 for F, the W(S)-span (resp. ℛ̃^int_S-span over ℛ̃^bd_S) of that basis is a free pure model.
items.note: Node PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/generic-newton-polygon-from-cyclic-vector states Lemma 5.2.4 over Γ[π^{-1}] (or a complete discretely valued field with algebraically closed residue field). The relative consequence used in Corollary 8.5.14 (integrality of the coefficients a_i and invertibility of a_0 over W(S), checked pointwise on ℳ(S)) is not planned.

items.name: Étale cohomology of ℤ_{p^d}-local systems on Spec(R) is φ^d-cohomology (Theorem 8.6.2)
items.statement: (Hypothesis 8.6.1: Hypothesis 8.5.1 holds and R is a perfect uniform Banach algebra over 𝔽_{p^d}, as in Hypothesis 5.0.1.) Let T be an étale ℤ_{p^d}-local system on Spec(R) and M the φ^d-module over ℛ̃^int_R or over W(R) corresponding to T by Theorem 8.5.3. Then there are bijections H^i_ét(Spec(R), T) ≅ H^i_{φ^d}(M) for all i ≥ 0 [the text writes an undefined X for Spec(R)], natural in T and R, where H^0_{φ^d}(M) = ker(φ^d − 1), H^1_{φ^d}(M) = coker(φ^d − 1) and H^i_{φ^d}(M) = 0 for i ≥ 2 (Definition 1.5.4); in particular H^i_ét(Spec(R), T) = 0 for i ≥ 2.
items.note: Over W(R): the Artin–Schreier–Witt sequences 0 → T/p^nT → M̃_n → M̃_n → 0 (map φ^d − 1) of étale sheaves on Spec(R), exact on the right by Theorem 8.5.3 (or Proposition 7.3.6), with M̃_n acyclic as an iterated extension of quasicoherent sheaves on an affine scheme. Over ℛ̃^int_R: H^0 and H^1 are Ext groups of φ^d-modules (Definition 1.5.4), unchanged by base extension to W(R) (Theorem 8.5.3). Not planned: the atlas uses the Artin–Schreier sequence only with 𝔽_p coefficients on characteristic-p perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-almost-acyclicity, PadicHodgeTheory:P8/affinoid-k-pi-one-for-p-torsion), not with W_n(R) coefficients on Spec(R) for a perfect ring R.

items.name: Two-out-of-three for (c, d)-purity in short exact sequences over ℛ̃_R (Lemma 8.6.3)
items.statement: Assume Hypothesis 8.6.1. Let 0 → M_1 → M → M_2 → 0 be a short exact sequence of φ-modules over ℛ̃_R. If any two of M, M_1, M_2 are (c, d)-pure, then so is the third.
items.note: By Corollary 7.3.9 it reduces to R = L an analytic field, where it follows from Theorem 4.2.12 (item planned in RD.2/RD.1). VB1 plans semistability and degree additivity for bundles on X_S, but not this two-out-of-three statement.

items.name: Étale cohomology of isogeny ℤ_{p^d}-local systems on Spec(R) is φ^d-cohomology (Theorem 8.6.4, corrected)
items.statement: Assume Hypothesis 8.6.1. Let E be an isogeny ℤ_{p^d}-local system on Spec(R) and M the globally étale φ^d-module over ℛ̃^bd_R, ℰ̃_R or ℛ̃_R corresponding to E by Theorem 8.5.6. Then there are bijections H^i_ét(Spec(R), E) ≅ H^i_{φ^d}(M) for all i ≥ 0 [the text writes an undefined X for Spec(R)], natural in E and R, where H^i_ét(Spec(R), E) = H^i_ét(Spec(R), T) ⊗_{ℤ_p} ℚ_p for any T with E = T ⊗ ℚ_p; both sides vanish for i ≥ 2.
items.note: Over ℛ̃^bd_R and ℰ̃_R: Theorem 8.6.2 tensored with ℚ_p (φ-cohomology commutes with direct limits). Over ℛ̃_R: H^0 by the full faithfulness in Theorem 8.5.6; H^1 as Ext^1 in étale ℚ_{p^d}-local systems on Spa(R, R⁺) (Remark 8.4.9), identified with Ext^1 of étale φ^d-modules over ℛ̃_R (Theorem 8.5.12 with Remark 8.5.10), which is all of H^1_{φ^d}(M) since extensions of étale modules are étale (Lemma 8.6.3). The printed proof also cites a nonexistent 'Theorem 6.2.9', deleted in the authors' errata. VB1/cohomology-of-twists (Fargues–Scholze II.2.5(ii): RΓ_proét(S, E) ≅ RΓ(X_S, O)) plans the trivial-coefficient case over the curve for perfectoid S. Remark 8.6.5 mentions, without statement, the analogue for isogeny (c, d)-local systems with H^1_{p^cφ^d}.

items.name: The relative period space U_R and the relative Fargues–Fontaine curve FF_R (Definitions 8.7.3–8.7.4)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5): for 0 < s ≤ r the ring ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R is a relatively perfectoid Banach ring (Theorem 5.3.9), promoted to an adic Banach ring (ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R, ℛ̃^{[s,r],+}_R) as in Definition 5.3.10. Put U_R = ⋃_{0<s<r} Spa(ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R, ℛ̃^{[s,r],+}_R). Its maximal Hausdorff quotient is the space T_R = ⋃_{0<s<r} ℳ(ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R) of Proposition 5.4.6, and U_R is a relatively perfectoid space. The action of φ^{a*} on U_R is properly discontinuous (Proposition 5.4.6), and the orbit space FF_R = U_R/(φ^{a*})^ℤ is again a relatively perfectoid space.
items.note: Nodes RF0:annuli/radius-function-and-rational-annuli and RF0:annuli/stein-exhaustion-and-higher-acyclicity (Y_S, its rational annuli, affinoid sousperfectoid; FS II.1.16 and the II.2 preamble) and RF1/frobenius-quotient-and-presentation (X_S = Y_S/φ^ℤ). For S = Spa(R, R⁺), U_R is FS's Y_S for E = ℚ_p and FF_R = Y_S/φ^{aℤ}; this is X_{S,E} for E = ℚ_{p^a} when R is an 𝔽_{p^a}-algebra, and in general a cyclic degree-a finite étale cover of X_{S,ℚ_p} (Definition 8.7.11). KL say 'relatively perfectoid' (Rodriguez's Theorem 5.3.9, item 198) where FS say 'sousperfectoid'. Remark 8.7.2 (z ∈ W(R⁺) primitive of degree 1 generating ker θ) restates item 154; Definition 5.3.10 is item 199; Proposition 5.4.6 is item 202.

items.name: FF over a perfectoid space: FF_{X′}, FF_X, the canonical section X → FF_X and the projection |FF_X| → |X| (Definition 8.7.4, continued)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5): the spaces FF_R glue along rational localizations (Lemma 5.3.11) to a relatively perfectoid space FF_{X′} with a natural isomorphism FF_{X′} ≅ FF_R when X′ = Spa(R, R⁺), and there is a natural continuous map |FF_{X′}| → |X′| of topological spaces, which does not arise from a morphism of adic spaces. FF_A denotes FF_R together with the morphism Spa(A, A⁺) → FF_R induced by θ : ℛ̃^{[1,1]}_R → A (Lemma 5.5.5); these glue to a space FF_X, naturally isomorphic to FF_{X′}, equipped with a distinguished morphism X → FF_X. The induced map |X| → |FF_X| is a continuous section of the projection |FF_X| ≅ |FF_{X′}| → |X′| ≅ |X|, and |FF_X| → |X| is not induced by a morphism FF_X → X of adic spaces.
items.note: RF1 ('Glue Y_S over perfectoid affinoid covers … do not infer that the adic X_S has an ordinary structural morphism to S'; node RF1/diamond-formula-and-map-to-base, the qcqs map |X_S| → |S|) and RF2:untilts (node closed-cartier-divisor-norm-estimate, FS II.1.4: an untilt S^♯ → 𝒴_S is a closed Cartier divisor, then descended to X_S). KL phrase the section with the characteristic-0 space X, FS with its tilt S = X′. Lemma 5.5.5 is item 205.

items.name: The morphism FF_R → Proj(P_R) and the line bundles O(n) on FF_R (Definition 8.7.5)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), let P_R = ⊕_{n≥0} P_{R,n} with P_{R,n} = {x ∈ ℛ̃⁺_R : φ^a(x) = p^n x} (Definition 6.3.1). The natural morphisms P_R → ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R define a morphism U_R → Proj(P_R) of locally ringed spaces, which factors through a morphism FF_R → Proj(P_R). For n ∈ ℤ, the line bundle O(n) on FF_R is the pullback of the line bundle O(n) on Proj(P_R) of Remark 6.3.16 (the rank-one φ^a-module free on v with φ^a(v) = p^{−n}v).
items.note: Nodes RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map (P = ⊕ H^0(X_S, O(n)) and the formal map of locally ringed spaces X_S → X_S^alg = Proj P, from the proof of FS II.2.7) and RF3/isocrystal-line-bundles-and-sign (O(n) = ℰ(Ĕ, π^{−n}σ), the same sign as KL's φ^a(v) = p^{−n}v). The graded ring P and Proj(P) are item 211.

items.name: Proj(P_R) is covered by two affine opens and its quasicoherent cohomology vanishes above degree 1 (Remark 8.7.6, Definition 8.8.1)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), let L be a perfect analytic field of characteristic p over which R is a Banach algebra (e.g. the completed perfect closure of 𝔽_p((z̄))). By Proposition 6.2.4 there are nonzero homogeneous f_1, f_2 ∈ P_{L,+}, which may be taken in P_{L,1}, generating the unit ideal in ℛ̃_L and hence in ℛ̃_R. (a) For positive integers m, n such that f_1^m and f_2^n have the same degree d, with P_{R,(d)} = ⊕_{h≥0} P_{R,hd}, the scheme Proj(P_R/(f_1^m)) is isomorphic to Spec(P_{R,(d)}[f_2^{−n}]_0/(f_1^m f_2^{−n})), hence affine. (b) Proj(P_R) is covered by the two open affines D_+(f_1), D_+(f_2) (Lemma 6.3.7); since Proj(P_R) is separated, Čech cohomology for this covering computes the sheaf cohomology of quasicoherent sheaves, which therefore vanishes in degrees > 1. Fixing f_1, f_2 ∈ P_{L,1} (Definition 8.8.1), the zero locus Z_1 of f_1 and U_1 = Proj(P_R) ∖ Z_1 = D_+(f_1) are affine schemes.
items.note: Nearest: RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map (Proj P covered by finitely many D_+(g) of one degree, quasicompact) and VB2:ampleness/gaga-equivalence (comparison of H^i for vector bundles only); neither states the two-affine cover, the affineness of V_+(f_1^m) or vanishing above degree 1 for all quasicoherent sheaves. The existence of f_1, f_2 is Proposition 6.2.4 (item 210); the Čech step is EGA III 1.4.1 (black-box item). Part II (Definition 4.8.2) cites this remark to find an affine open on which the untilt divisor is principal.

items.name: GAGA for the relative Fargues–Fontaine curve (Theorem 8.7.7)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), pullback along the morphism FF_R → Proj(P_R) of locally ringed spaces defines an equivalence between the categories of vector bundles on Proj(P_R) and on FF_R. Consequently (Theorem 6.3.12) vector bundles on FF_R are equivalent to φ^a-modules over ℛ̃_R, a category independent of R⁺.
items.note: Node VB2:ampleness/gaga-equivalence (FS II.2.7, axiomatic GAGA from eventual global generation and vanishing, fed by VB2:ampleness/quantitative-global-generation, FS II.2.6 'after KL15 6.2.4'), with RF3's map X_S → X_S^alg; FS assume S affinoid perfectoid, as here. KL prove it from Theorem 6.3.12 (item 212: φ^a-bundles over ℛ̃_R = vector bundles on Proj(P_R)) and Theorem 8.2.22 (vector bundles on the affinoid pieces of U_R = finite projective modules); the proof writes 'ϕ-bundles' for φ^a-bundles.

items.name: Vector bundles on FF_X are φ^a-modules over ℛ̃ (Theorem 8.7.8)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), the category of vector bundles on FF_X is functorially equivalent to the category of φ^a-modules over ℛ̃_X, the sheaf ℛ̃ of Definition 8.3.4 on the perfect space X′ (transported to X by Theorem 8.3.5).
items.note: VB1 ('Define bundles as finite locally free O_X modules on the existing curve; compare with finite projective modules on annuli and Frobenius descent. Prove rational/pro-étale/v descent'; node VB1/v-descent-for-bundles-and-cohomology) on the glued curve of RF1. It follows from Theorem 8.7.7 locally and descent of φ^a-modules over ℛ̃ along rational coverings (Corollary 6.3.13, item 212). The statement writes ℛ̃_X though Definition 8.3.4 defines ℛ̃ on perfect spaces, here X′.

items.name: Global sections of the twists O(n) (Corollary 8.7.9)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), for n ∈ ℤ: H^0(Proj(P_R), O(n)) = H^0(FF_R, O(n)) = P_{R,n} if n ≥ 0, and = 0 if n < 0.
items.note: VB1 ('Compute O(n) sections and first cohomology with actual Frobenius maps and signs'; node VB1/cohomology-of-twists, FS II.2.5(i): H^0(X_S, O(λ)) = 0 for λ < 0) and RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map (P_n := H^0(X_S, O(n))). KL's P_{R,n} is {x ∈ ℛ̃⁺_R : φ^a(x) = p^n x}, equal to the same set in ℛ̃_R by Corollary 5.2.12 (items 194, 211).

items.name: Étale ℚ_{p^a}-local systems are the pointwise semistable degree-0 bundles on FF_X (Corollary 8.7.10)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), fix a morphism X → Spa(ℚ_{p^a}, ℤ_{p^a}). Then the category of étale ℚ_{p^a}-local systems on X is functorially equivalent to the category of vector bundles on FF_X which are pointwise semistable of degree 0, i.e. whose restriction to FF_{H(x)} is semistable of degree 0 for every x ∈ X.
items.note: KL's proof combines Remark 4.2.18, Theorem 8.5.12 (local systems ↔ pure φ-modules over ℛ̃_{X′}, stated for (c, d)-pure φ-modules) and Theorem 8.7.8. For a > 1 the input actually needed is the φ^a / ℚ_{p^a} analogue of Theorem 8.5.12, obtained from Theorem 8.5.6 with d = a, Corollary 8.4.7 and Theorem 8.3.5 (finding E139).

items.name: Change of a: the finite étale covers FF^{(ad)} → FF^{(a)} and the bundles O(n, d) (Definition 8.7.11)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), write P^{(a)}_{R,n}, P^{(a)}_R, U^{(a)}_R, FF^{(a)}_R, FF^{(a)}_X to record a. For a positive integer d, P^{(a)}_{R,n} ⊆ P^{(ad)}_{R,nd} inside ℛ̃_R, giving a morphism of graded rings P^{(a)}_R → P^{(ad)}_R (degree n to degree nd) and a morphism of schemes Proj(P^{(ad)}_R) → Proj(P^{(a)}_R), which is finite étale of degree d, the quotient by the automorphism induced by φ^a. The corresponding morphism U^{(ad)}_R → U^{(a)}_R is an isomorphism, so FF^{(ad)}_R → FF^{(a)}_R is finite étale of degree d, the quotient by the action of φ^{a*}. For n, d ∈ ℤ with gcd(n, d) = 1 and d > 0, O(n, d) is the rank-d vector bundle on FF^{(a)}_R obtained by pushing forward O(n) on FF^{(ad)}_R.
items.note: Node VB0/scalar-extension-adjunction (pullback and pushforward along π_{E′|E} : X_{E′} → X_E match the up and down isocrystal functors; here E′ = ℚ_{p^{ad}} over E = ℚ_{p^a}) and RF3/isocrystal-line-bundles-and-sign (the stable bundles O(λ)); FS use O(λ) = f_*O_{X_{C,E′}}(s) in the proof of II.2.14. The finite étale map of schemes Proj(P^{(ad)}_R) → Proj(P^{(a)}_R) is not stated in the atlas. The printed text has P^{(d)} for P^{(a)} twice (source issue).

items.name: Classification of vector bundles over an algebraically closed field (Corollary 8.7.12)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5) with R = L an algebraically closed analytic field, every vector bundle on Proj(P_L) or on FF_L is (nonuniquely) isomorphic to a direct sum ⊕_i O(n_i, s_i) for some n_i, s_i ∈ ℤ with gcd(n_i, s_i) = 1 and s_i > 0.
items.note: Node VB2:classification/dieudonne-manin-classification-of-bundles (FS II.2.14). KL deduce it from Theorem 8.7.7 and the Dieudonné–Manin decomposition over ℛ̃_L (Proposition 4.2.16, item 183, planned in PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.1/RD.2), not by the FS argument.

items.name: φ^a-cohomology is the coherent cohomology of the schematic and adic curves (Theorem 8.7.13)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), let M be a φ^a-module over ℛ̃_R corresponding to the vector bundle V on FF_R (Theorem 8.7.8), and also write V for the corresponding bundle on Proj(P_R). Then there are isomorphisms, natural in M and R, H^i_{φ^a}(M) ≅ H^i(Proj(P_R), V) ≅ H^i(FF_R, V) for all i ≥ 0; all three groups vanish for i ≥ 2.
items.note: Nodes VB2:ampleness/gaga-equivalence (H^i(X^alg, E^alg) ≅ H^i(X, E) for all i, FS II.2.7) and RF0:annuli/stein-exhaustion-and-higher-acyclicity (RΓ(X_S, E) = [H^0(Y_S, E) → H^0(Y_S, E)] via φ − 1, zero above degree 1); VB1 ('Construct H^0 and H^1 and prove higher vanishing'). KL's proof: H^i(Proj(P_R), V) is Yoneda Ext^i(O, V) among quasicoherent sheaves (Thomason–Trobaugh B.8 and Hilton–Stammbach IV.9.1, black-box items), compared with φ^a-modules for i = 0, 1 by Theorem 6.3.12 and vanishing for i ≥ 2 by Remark 8.7.6(b); on FF_R, Čech cohomology for the cover by the annuli [rq^{−1/2}, r] and [rq^{−1}, rq^{−1/2}], acyclic by Theorem 5.3.9.

items.name: Sufficiently positive twists are globally generated with vanishing H^1 (Corollary 8.7.14)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), for V a quasicoherent finite locally free sheaf on Proj(P_R) there exists N ∈ ℤ such that for all n ≥ N, H^0(Proj(P_R), V(n)) generates V(n) and H^1(Proj(P_R), V(n)) = H^1(FF_R, V(n)) = 0.
items.note: Node VB2:ampleness/quantitative-global-generation (FS II.2.6, which FS attribute to KL15 Proposition 6.2.4). KL deduce it from Theorem 8.7.13 and Propositions 6.2.2 and 6.2.4 (item 210).

items.name: FF preserves étale, finite étale and faithfully finite étale morphisms (Lemma 8.7.15)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), if Y → X is a morphism of perfectoid adic spaces which is étale (resp. finite étale, faithfully finite étale), then the induced morphism FF_Y → FF_X is also étale (resp. finite étale, faithfully finite étale).
items.note: Nearest: RF1 (functoriality in S and pullback along T → S) and FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F3 (étale and finite étale sites of a single curve X_F over a field); no stage states that the relative curve sends (finite) étale maps of the base to (finite) étale maps. The proof tilts to Y′ → X′ and uses Proposition 5.5.4 (item 204, missing).

items.name: The morphism of étale topoi FF_X → X (Remark 8.7.16)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), Lemma 8.7.15 promotes the continuous map |FF_X| → |X| to a morphism of étale topoi from FF_X to X; this morphism behaves like a circle bundle (Remark 5.4.7).
items.note: Nearest: RF1/diamond-formula-and-map-to-base, which constructs only the map of topological spaces |X_S| → |S| and records that there is no adic morphism X_S → S. Remark 5.4.7 is in item 202.

items.name: Globally ample and ample vector bundles on Proj(P_R) (Definition 8.8.2)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), a vector bundle F on Proj(P_R) is globally ample if for every quasicoherent sheaf of finite type G on Proj(P_R) there exists n_0 ∈ ℤ such that F^{⊗n} ⊗ G is generated by global sections for all n ≥ n_0 (by Corollary 8.8.5 it suffices to check G = O(e) for all e ∈ ℤ). F is ample if there is a strong rational covering {(R, R⁺) → (R_i, R_i⁺)}_i such that the pullback of F to each Proj(P_{R_i}) is globally ample.
items.note: VB2:ampleness plans only positive twists E(n) of bundles on X_S (FS II.2.6); no stage defines ampleness of an arbitrary bundle on the relative curve. Mathlib has no ample sheaves or global generation on schemes. Suggested home: VB2:ampleness.

items.name: Ampleness is insensitive to tensor powers (Lemma 8.8.3)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), for a vector bundle F on Proj(P_R) and a positive integer m, F is globally ample (resp. ample) if and only if F^{⊗m} is globally ample (resp. ample).
items.note: Not planned; part of the ampleness theory of Definition 8.8.2 (suggested home VB2:ampleness).

items.name: O(e) is globally ample for e > 0, and finite-type sheaves are quotients of sums of O(e_i) (Lemma 8.8.4, Corollary 8.8.5)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5): the line bundles O(e) on Proj(P_R) are globally ample for all e > 0. Consequently every quasicoherent sheaf of finite type on Proj(P_R) is a quotient of a vector bundle ⊕_{i=1}^m O(e_i) for some m ≥ 0 and e_1, …, e_m ∈ ℤ.
items.note: For G a vector bundle, global generation of G(n) for n ≫ 0 is VB2:ampleness/quantitative-global-generation (FS II.2.6) via GAGA; the case of an arbitrary quasicoherent sheaf of finite type, proved by the Proj argument on the affine opens D_+(f_1), D_+(f_2), is not planned. Part II (Theorem 4.6.12) reuses it for pseudocoherent sheaves. The printed proof treats only U_1 (source issue).

items.name: Cohomological criterion for global ampleness (Proposition 8.8.6)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), for a vector bundle F on Proj(P_R) the following are equivalent. (a) F is globally ample. (b) For every quasicoherent sheaf of finite type G on Proj(P_R) there exists n_0 ∈ ℤ such that H^1(Proj(P_R), F^{⊗n} ⊗ G) = 0 for all n ≥ n_0. (c) For each e ∈ ℤ there exists n_0 ∈ ℤ such that H^1(Proj(P_R), F^{⊗n}(e)) = 0 for all n ≥ n_0.
items.note: A variant of Hartshorne III.5.3 for the non-noetherian scheme Proj(P_R), resting on Remark 8.7.6 (cohomological dimension 1, affine Z_1 and U_1) and Fitting ideals. No stage plans a cohomological criterion for ampleness; the nearest is AdicSpacesPartII:F0/graded-cohomology-finiteness (Serre vanishing on proper noetherian schemes). Two source issues concern the proof (a circular citation in (a) ⇒ (c), and the dependence of n on e in (b) ⇒ (a)).

items.name: Positive twists of globally étale bundles are globally ample with vanishing H^1 (Corollary 8.8.7)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), let F be a globally étale vector bundle on Proj(P_R) (its φ^a-module admits a locally free étale model, Definition 7.3.4). Then for every positive integer n, H^1(Proj(P_R), F(n)) = 0 and F(n) is globally ample.
items.note: For F = O the vanishing is VB1/cohomology-of-twists (FS II.2.5(iii): H^1(X_S, O(λ)) = 0 for λ > 0, S affinoid); the globally étale (twisted) case and the global ampleness are not planned. Proof: Proposition 6.2.2 with N = 1 (item 210), Theorem 8.7.13, and criterion (c) of Proposition 8.8.6.

items.name: Non-vanishing loci of sections of globally ample line bundles are affine (Lemma 8.8.8)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), let F be a globally ample line bundle on Proj(P_R). Then for any s ∈ H^0(Proj(P_R), F), the open subscheme U_s of Proj(P_R) on which s generates F is affine.
items.note: Proof by Serre's cohomological criterion for affineness (Stacks Tag 01XG, black-box item), writing j_*G = lim_d H ⊗ F^{⊗d} and applying Proposition 8.8.6. Nearest: VB2:ampleness/schematic-curve-at-a-geometric-point (FS II.2.9: X_C^alg ∖ {x} is the spectrum of a principal ideal domain, at a geometric point only).

items.name: A globally ample line bundle recovers Proj(P_R) (Corollary 8.8.9)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), let F be a globally ample line bundle on Proj(P_R). Then there is a natural isomorphism Proj(P_R) ≅ Proj(P_F), where P_F = ⊕_{n≥0} H^0(Proj(P_R), F^{⊗n}).
items.note: Node VB2:ampleness/gaga-equivalence ('X^alg is independent of the chosen O_X(1) up to canonical isomorphism', FS II.2.7) applied to F; that a globally ample F satisfies its hypotheses (eventual global generation and vanishing of H^i, i > 0) is Proposition 8.8.6 with Remark 8.7.6(b), which are missing.

items.name: The slope polygon of a bundle on Proj(P_R) and pointwise ampleness (Definition 8.8.10)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), let F be a vector bundle on Proj(P_R) and M the φ^a-module over ℛ̃_R corresponding to it (Theorem 6.3.12). The slope polygon of F is the function on ℳ(R) (and on Spa(R, R⁺) by retraction) given by the fibrewise Harder–Narasimhan polygon; it agrees with the slope polygon of M (Remark 4.2.18). F is pointwise ample at β ∈ ℳ(R) if all slopes of F at β are positive; by Theorem 7.4.5 this is an open condition on ℳ(R). F is pointwise ample if it is pointwise ample at every β.
items.note: The fibrewise slope polygon and its semicontinuity are items 221 and 224 (VB4/semicontinuity-of-HN-polygon); positivity of all slopes as a notion of ampleness is not in the atlas (suggested home VB4).

items.name: Tensor powers of a pointwise ample bundle eventually dominate any bundle (Lemma 8.8.11)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), for any pointwise ample vector bundle F on Proj(P_R) and any vector bundle G on Proj(P_R) there exists n_0 ∈ ℤ such that F^{⊗n} ⊗ G is pointwise ample for all n ≥ n_0.
items.note: Uses that the slope polygon is bounded (Proposition 7.4.6, item 225, missing) and that the slopes of F lie in a discrete subset of ℚ.

items.name: Ample bundles over an analytic field have vanishing H^1 (Lemma 8.8.12(a))
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5) with R = L an analytic field, let F be an ample vector bundle on Proj(P_L). Then H^1(Proj(P_L), F) = 0.
items.note: Over a geometric point, H^1(X_C, O(λ)) = 0 for λ > 0 is VB1/cohomology-of-twists (FS II.2.5(iii)) and the splitting into O(λ)'s is VB2:classification; KL's L need not be algebraically closed. Proof: reduce by the slope filtration (Theorem 4.2.13, item 182) to M pure of slope s > 0, enlarge a so that as ∈ ℤ, and apply Theorem 8.7.13 and Corollary 8.8.7.

items.name: Ample bundles over an analytic field are globally generated (Lemma 8.8.12(b))
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5) with R = L an analytic field, let F be an ample vector bundle on Proj(P_L). Then F is generated by H^0(Proj(P_L), F).
items.note: Proof: by (a) and the slope filtration reduce to M pure of slope s > 0 with as ∈ ℤ after enlarging a; then H^0_{φ^a}(M) generates M by Proposition 6.2.4 (item 210) and Theorem 8.7.13. Not planned in this generality (nearest VB2:ampleness and VB2:classification at geometric points).

items.name: Dévissage: extending a nonnegative bundle by O(−1) keeps it nonnegative at a point (Lemma 8.8.13)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), let F be a vector bundle on Proj(P_R) whose slopes at some β ∈ ℳ(R) are all nonnegative but not all zero. Then there exists a short exact sequence 0 → O(−1) → G → F → 0 of vector bundles on Proj(P_R) such that the slopes of G at β are also all nonnegative.
items.note: A dévissage in the style of R. Liu [96]: the extension class is the image under H^0(Z_1, i^*F^∨) → H^1(Proj(P_R), F^∨(−1)) of a section on the affine Z_1 = V_+(f_1) that is nonzero on the positive-slope part F_+ of F at β (Theorem 4.2.13 at β); nonsplitting of 0 → O(−1) → G_+ → F_+ → 0 gives deg ≥ 0 for every quotient of G_+. Two misprints and the degree normalization affect the proof (source issues).

items.name: Resolving a pointwise nonnegative bundle by a bundle étale at the point (Corollary 8.8.14)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), let F be a vector bundle on Proj(P_R) whose slopes at some β ∈ ℳ(R) are all nonnegative. Then there exists a short exact sequence 0 → H → G → F → 0 of vector bundles on Proj(P_R) such that G is étale at β.
items.note: Induction on deg(F_β) using Lemma 8.8.13, plus Theorem 7.3.7 (item 220, missing).

items.name: Ample if and only if pointwise ample (Theorem 8.8.15)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), a vector bundle F on Proj(P_R) is ample if and only if it is pointwise ample (all its slopes at every β ∈ ℳ(R) are positive).
items.note: Not planned: VB2:ampleness has only the twists E(n) (FS II.2.6) and VB4 the semicontinuity of HN polygons. Proof: if F^{⊗n}(−1) is globally generated its smallest slope is ≥ 0; conversely, locally around β, Lemma 8.8.11 and Corollary 8.8.14 give G ↠ F^{⊗n}(−1) with G globally étale after a rational localization, and Corollary 8.8.7 makes G(1), hence F^{⊗n}, globally ample. Remark 8.8.16: it is unknown whether pointwise ample (equivalently ample) implies globally ample, e.g. for L^{⊗n}(e) with e, n > 0 and L étale but not globally étale.

items.name: Ample vector bundles on FF_X and their locality on the base (Definition 8.8.17)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), a vector bundle F on FF_X is ample if for every choice of (A, A⁺), (R, R⁺) and every morphism f : Spa(A, A⁺) → X, the bundle f^*F on FF_R corresponds via Theorem 8.7.7 to an ample vector bundle on Proj(P_R). By Theorem 8.8.15 this holds if and only if the slopes of F, as functions on X, are everywhere positive. Consequently: if X = Spa(A, A⁺), a vector bundle on Proj(P_R) is ample if and only if the corresponding vector bundle on FF_X is ample; if f : Y → X is a surjective morphism of perfectoid adic spaces and f^*F is ample then F is ample, so ampleness is local on the base; and ampleness is open on the base, even on its real quotient: if the restriction of F to FF_{H(x)} is ample for some x ∈ X, there is a partially proper open neighbourhood U of x in X such that the restriction of F to FF_U is ample (Theorem 7.4.5).
items.note: Nearest: VB4 (Harder–Narasimhan polygons of bundles on X_S in families; node VB4/semicontinuity-of-HN-polygon). The printed third consequence says 'F is a vector bundle on X' for FF_X (source issue).

items.name: The line bundle L_X of the canonical divisor and its section t_X (Definition 8.8.18)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), let z ∈ W(R⁺) be primitive of degree 1 generating ker θ (Remark 8.7.2). The inclusion ℛ̃^{[q^{−1/2}, q^{1/2}]}_R → z^{−1}ℛ̃^{[q^{−1/2}, q^{1/2}]}_R induces an inclusion O → L of vector bundles on FF_R. Since this construction is canonically independent of z, it globalizes to an inclusion O_X → L_X of line bundles on FF_X, corresponding to a section t_X ∈ H^0(FF_X, L_X) whose divisor is the image of the canonical section X → FF_X. L_X is pure of slope 1/a (printed 'slope 1', correct for a = 1; see source issue) and hence ample by Theorem 8.8.15.
items.note: RF2:untilts constructs the divisor of an untilt on Y_S and X_S ('descend the Cartier divisor'); L_X is the line bundle of that Cartier divisor with its canonical section. VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence (FS II.2.3: 0 → O → O(1) → O_{S^♯} → 0 when the untilt is cut out by a section of O(1); II.2.4: (BC(O(1)) ∖ 0)/E^× = Div^1) identifies it with O(1) locally on S.

items.name: L_X is an étale twist of O(1) (Lemma 8.8.19)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5) with X = Spa(A, A⁺), write z = [z̄] + p z_1. Let M be the φ^a-module over ℛ̃_R free on one generator v with φ^a(v) = z_1^{−1} z v; it is globally étale. The convergent product u = ∏_{n≥0} φ^{an}(1 + p^{−1} z_1^{−1}[z̄]) ∈ ℛ̃⁺_R satisfies φ^a(u) = p z_1 z^{−1} u in ℛ̃_R, so uv defines an inclusion ℛ̃_R → M(1) of φ^a-modules, and M(1) is the φ^a-module corresponding to L_X. Hence the φ^a-module corresponding to L_X is globally pure of slope 1/a, i.e. globally (1, a)-pure (printed 'slope 1'; see source issue).
items.note: Nearest: VB3:positive-basic-examples/fundamental-exact-sequence (FS II.2.3–II.2.4), which identifies the line bundle of the divisor with O(1) only where the untilt is cut out by a section of O(1); the global identification L_X = M(1) with an explicit rank-one étale M is not planned. With Corollary 8.8.7 it makes L_X globally ample, which Lemma 8.9.3(a) uses.

items.name: Conjecture: zero loci of fibrewise nonzero sections of positive line bundles are affine and perfectoid (Conjecture 8.8.20, Remark 8.8.21)
items.statement: Conjecture, not proved in the source. Under Hypothesis 8.7.1 (a ≥ 1 an integer, q = p^a; (A, A⁺) a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and (R, R⁺) the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 3.6.5; X a perfectoid adic space over ℚ_p and X′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_p corresponding to it by Theorem 8.3.5), let F be a line bundle on Proj(P_R) such that deg(F) > 0 and F(−a·deg(F)) is globally étale (printed F(−deg(F)), with deg(F) : X → ℤ; see the normalization source issue); F is then globally ample by Corollary 8.8.7. (a) If t ∈ H^0(Proj(P_R), F) has nonzero restriction to FF_x for all x ∈ Spa(R, R⁺), then the closed subscheme Z of Proj(P_R) cut out by t is affine (this would follow from Lemma 8.8.8 given a second section s whose zero locus is disjoint from that of t). (b) With Z as in (a), and assuming in addition that t has only simple zeros on each fibre, so that Z is reduced (without this (b) is false; see source issue), the coordinate ring of Z, normed by identifying it with the global sections of the subspace of FF_R cut out by t, is a perfectoid Banach algebra over ℚ_p. Remark 8.8.21: for R = L an analytic field this is attributed to [45]; for deg(F) = 1 it should follow by reversing the proof of Lemma 8.8.19 and rescaling the norm on R as in Remark 2.3.11(d); the case F(−deg F) étale but not globally étale is unclear.
items.note: Stated as a conjecture. Nearest: RF2:untilts (degree one: an untilt is a closed Cartier divisor whose ring is the perfectoid untilt, FS II.1.4) and RF2:integral-divisors/product-equation-and-affineness (FS VI.1.2: degree-d relative Cartier divisors on X_S are affinoid locally on S, cut out by products of primitive elements, and are not perfectoid when legs coincide). Neither states affineness of the scheme-theoretic Z ⊂ Proj(P_R) over a general base.

items.name: The complement of the untilt divisor in Proj(P_R) is affine (Lemma 8.9.3(a))
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.9.1 (Hypothesis 8.7.1 with X = Spa(A, A⁺)), with Z the image of the canonical section Spec(A) → Proj(P_R) and L_X transported to Proj(P_R) by Theorem 8.7.7 (Convention 8.9.2), the open subscheme Proj(P_R) − Z of Proj(P_R) is affine.
items.note: Proof: Z is the divisor of the section t_X of L_X, which is globally ample (Lemma 8.8.19 with Corollary 8.8.7), so Lemma 8.8.8 applies. Nearest: VB2:ampleness/schematic-curve-at-a-geometric-point (FS II.2.9: the complement of a classical point of X_C^alg is the spectrum of a principal ideal domain, at a geometric point only). Suggested home: RF4:vector-bundles, as the B_e side of the B-pair description.

items.name: The untilt divisor is a Cartier divisor inside an affine open (Lemma 8.9.3(b))
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.9.1 (Hypothesis 8.7.1 with X = Spa(A, A⁺)), with Z the image of the canonical section Spec(A) → Proj(P_R) and L_X transported to Proj(P_R) by Theorem 8.7.7 (Convention 8.9.2), the closed subscheme Z of Proj(P_R) is a Cartier divisor contained in an open affine subscheme of Proj(P_R).
items.note: Proof: following Proposition 6.2.4, choose t_L ∈ P_{L,1} whose Newton polygon avoids slope 1, so Z ⊆ D_+(t_L). The Cartier property on the adic curve is RF2:untilts/closed-cartier-divisor-norm-estimate; the scheme-theoretic statement is not planned. Part II (Definition 4.8.2) sharpens it to an affine open on which Z is principal.

items.name: The relative period rings R_1 = B_e, R_2 = B^+_dR, R_3 = B_dR of A (Definition 8.9.4)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.9.1 (Hypothesis 8.7.1 with X = Spa(A, A⁺)), with Z the image of the canonical section Spec(A) → Proj(P_R) and L_X transported to Proj(P_R) by Theorem 8.7.7 (Convention 8.9.2): by Lemma 8.9.3(a), Proj(P_R) − Z is an affine scheme Spec(R_1); by Lemma 8.9.3(b), the completion of Proj(P_R) along Z is an affine scheme Spec(R_2); and Spec(R_1) ×_{Proj(P_R)} Spec(R_2) is an affine scheme Spec(R_3). R_2 is the ker(θ)-adic completion of ℛ̃^{int,1}_R and R_3 = R_2[z^{−1}] for any z generating ker(θ).
items.note: (R_1, R_2, R_3) are relative versions of Fontaine's (B_e, B^+_dR, B_dR) for A. Nearest: RF2:untilts/BdR-completion-and-filtration (B^+_dR as the completion along a degree-one divisor and B_dR = B^+_dR[1/I_S]); R_1 = B_e (functions on the complement of the untilt divisor in the schematic curve) is planned nowhere (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1 has B_e = B_cris^{φ=1} over a field only). Part II, Definition 4.8.2, names these rings B_{e,R}, B^+_{dR,R}, B_{dR,R} but lists them as 'R_1, R_2, R_12' in the order B^+_dR, B_e, B_dR, which does not match this definition (R_1 = B_e, R_2 = B^+_dR, R_3 = B_dR). R_2, R_3 have relative counterparts (completion along the untilt divisor on the adic curve); R_1 = B_e (the affine complement in Proj(P_R)) and the scheme-theoretic description are not planned. Already reflected in the item note. Evidence: RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/BdR-completion-and-filtration: 'For d = 1 the rings of the previous construction are B^+_dR = B^+_{Div^1}(S) and B_dR = B^+_dR[1/I_S].'

items.name: B-pair cohomology computes the cohomology of flat quasicoherent sheaves (Theorem 8.9.6(a), Remark 8.9.5)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.9.1 (Hypothesis 8.7.1 with X = Spa(A, A⁺)), with Z the image of the canonical section Spec(A) → Proj(P_R) and L_X transported to Proj(P_R) by Theorem 8.7.7 (Convention 8.9.2) and R_1, R_2, R_3 as in Definition 8.9.4: for any flat quasicoherent sheaf V on Proj(P_R), the cohomology of the complex 0 → Γ(Spec(R_1), V) ⊕ Γ(Spec(R_2), V) → Γ(Spec(R_3), V) → 0, whose arrow is the difference of the two restriction maps, is naturally identified with H^i(Proj(P_R), V).
items.note: Proof from Beauville–Laszlo (Proposition 1.3.6, item 17) on an affine neighbourhood of Z. Remark 8.9.5: for R = L the morphism Spec(R_1 ⊕ R_2) → Proj(P_L) is faithfully flat, so it can be used to define quasicoherent sheaves and compute their cohomology; in general flatness of Spec(R_2) → Proj(P_R) is unknown. RF4:vector-bundles plans the Beauville–Laszlo gluing but not the cohomology of the B-pair complex; Berger's B-pairs are not in the atlas.

items.name: Vector bundles on Proj(P_R) are relative B-pairs (Theorem 8.9.6(b)–(c))
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 8.9.1 (Hypothesis 8.7.1 with X = Spa(A, A⁺)), with Z the image of the canonical section Spec(A) → Proj(P_R) and L_X transported to Proj(P_R) by Theorem 8.7.7 (Convention 8.9.2) and R_1, R_2, R_3 as in Definition 8.9.4: (b) the morphism Spec(R_1 ⊕ R_2) → Proj(P_R) is an effective descent morphism for the category of quasicoherent finite locally free sheaves over schemes; (c) the category of vector bundles on Proj(P_R) is equivalent to the category of triples (V_1, V_2, ι) with V_1 a finite projective R_1-module, V_2 a finite projective R_2-module and ι : V_1 ⊗_{R_1} R_3 ≅ V_2 ⊗_{R_2} R_3 an isomorphism of R_3-modules.
items.note: Node RF4:vector-bundles/beauville-laszlo-module-gluing ('a bundle off D, a bundle on its formal neighborhood, and an isomorphism on the punctured neighborhood determine a bundle') on the adic curve X_S; with GAGA (Theorem 8.7.7, VB2:ampleness) this is KL's statement on Proj(P_R). It is the relative form of Berger's B-pairs [12]; the B-pair language is not in the atlas. Proof: Proposition 1.3.6 (item 17).

items.name: Thomason–Trobaugh: quasicoherent cohomology of a quasicompact semiseparated scheme is computed inside QCoh
items.statement: For a scheme Z which is quasicompact and semiseparated (covered by finitely many open affine subschemes, any two of which have affine intersection), the category of quasicoherent sheaves on Z has enough injectives, and the resulting derived functors of Γ agree with sheaf cohomology defined using the full category of sheaves of abelian groups. It applies to Proj(P_R), which is quasicompact (Lemma 6.3.7) and separated.
items.locator: §8.7, proof of Theorem 8.7.13, p. 179 (Thomason–Trobaugh [124], Proposition B.8) (arXiv 1301.0792v5)
items.note: Node SchemeKTheoryOperations:S.1/coherator: for X quasi-compact with affine diagonal ('quasi-compact and semi-separated in TT's language'), D(QCoh(O_X)) → D_QCoh(O_X) is an equivalence (Stacks 08DB), which contains this statement. Mathlib has quasicoherent sheaves of modules (SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent) but no cohomology of them.

items.name: Hilton–Stammbach: Yoneda Ext equals derived-functor Ext
items.statement: In an abelian category, the Yoneda groups of n-fold extensions of A by B are naturally isomorphic to Ext^n(A, B) computed as derived functors (when enough injectives exist); in particular Ext^1(A, B) classifies extensions 0 → B → E → A → 0.
items.locator: §8.7, proof of Theorem 8.7.13, p. 179 (Hilton–Stammbach [75], Theorem IV.9.1) (arXiv 1301.0792v5)
items.note: Mathlib defines Ext in the derived category (CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext), computes it by injective resolutions (CategoryTheory.InjectiveResolution.extEquivCohomologyClass) and has the class of a short exact sequence (CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact.extClass), but not the bijection between extension classes and Ext^1 (or Ext^n), which KL use to compare H^1(Proj(P_R), V) with extensions of φ^a-modules. Suggested home: FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.3.

items.name: EGA III 1.4.1: Čech cohomology of an affine cover computes quasicoherent cohomology on a separated scheme
items.statement: Let X be a separated scheme, 𝔘 a covering of X by open affine subschemes and F a quasicoherent sheaf on X. Then the Čech cohomology Ȟ^i(𝔘, F) is naturally isomorphic to H^i(X, F) for all i; in particular, if 𝔘 has two members then H^i(X, F) = 0 for i ≥ 2.
items.note: tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-b-coherent-cohomology-over-k-genus-riemannroch-serre-duality plans 'acyclicity of affines, Čech ≃ derived on a separated scheme' for coherent sheaves on schemes over a field k; Proj(P_R) is a non-noetherian scheme not of finite type over a field. Mathlib has no cohomology of quasicoherent sheaves on schemes.

items.name: Serre's cohomological criterion for affineness
items.statement: A quasicompact scheme U with H^1(U, G) = 0 for every quasicoherent sheaf of ideals G (for U quasicompact and quasiseparated, equivalently for every quasicoherent sheaf of finite type, as KL use it) is affine.
items.locator: §8.8, proof of Lemma 8.8.8, p. 182 (Stacks Project [121], Tag 01XG as cited) (arXiv 1301.0792v5)
items.note: No stage plans it and Mathlib has no quasicoherent cohomology. AdicSpacesPartII:R2/topological-invariance-of-affinoid records that no such criterion holds for rigid analytic spaces; KL apply it on the scheme Proj(P_R). The reduction from all quasicoherent sheaves to those of finite type uses that cohomology on a qcqs scheme commutes with filtered colimits.

items.name: Pro-objects and the pro-category Ĉ (Definition 9.1.1)
items.statement: For a category C, a pro-object over C is a pair (I, F) in which I is a directed poset and F is a contravariant functor from I to C (written lim← F(i)). The pro-objects over C form a category Ĉ with Hom((I, F), (I′, F′)) = lim←_{i′∈I′} lim→_{i∈I} Hom(F(i), F′(i′)). Ĉ admits inverse limits (modulo set-theoretic difficulties), and X ↦ ({0}, 0 ↦ X) is a natural embedding C → Ĉ. When C has a forgetful functor X ↦ |X| to topological spaces, it is extended to Ĉ by |lim←_{i∈I} X_i| = lim←_{i∈I} |X_i|.
items.locator: §9.1, Definition 9.1.1 and the paragraph after it, pp. 188–189 (arXiv 1301.0792v5)
items.note: Mathlib has the dual construction: Ind C (ind-objects among presheaves on C, Kashiwara–Schapira ch. 6), with Ind.yoneda : C ⥤ Ind C fully faithful and filtered colimits in Ind C; pro-objects over C are (Ind Cᵒᵖ)ᵒᵖ, and the lim–colim formula for Hom is the Pro-Coyoneda lemma colimitCoyonedaHomIsoLimit. Mathlib indexes by small filtered categories rather than directed posets (equivalent up to cofinality), and |lim X_i| = lim |X_i| is the limit in TopCat. The atlas already treats Pro(X_ét) as the dual of Mathlib's Ind (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism, DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-category-of-finite-t0-spaces). Source cited: SGA 4 [5, Exposé I, §8.10].

items.name: Étale, finite étale, faithfully finite étale and pro-étale morphisms of pro-objects of X_ét (Definition 9.1.2)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis of §9.1: X is a preadic space (Definition 8.2.3). Let X̂_ét be the pro-category (Definition 9.1.1) of the small étale site X_ét (Definition 8.2.19). A morphism U → V in X̂_ét is étale (resp. finite étale, faithfully finite étale) if it arises by base extension from an étale (resp. finite étale, faithfully finite étale) morphism Y₀ → X₀ in X_ét; these classes are stable under composition and base change. A morphism U → V in X̂_ét is pro-étale if U admits a pro-étale presentation, i.e. is (over V) a cofiltered inverse limit lim← U_i of objects U_i étale over V such that U_i → U_j is faithfully finite étale for all i ≥ j with j sufficiently large.
items.note: Nearest layer: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-morphism plans exactly these classes (Scholze 2013, Definition 3.9), but only for X a locally noetherian analytic adic space; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-generalized plans Kedlaya–Liu's étale site of an arbitrary analytic Yoneda-adic (= preadic) space, but no node builds the pro-category or the pro-étale morphisms over that site. Stability under composition and base change is argued as in Scholze 2013, Lemma 3.10(i)–(ii) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-base-change). Route: AdicEtaleGeometry A1, extending its pro-étale nodes from locally noetherian X to the preadic spaces of A1/etale-site-generalized.

items.name: Pro-étale morphisms are stable under base change, surjectively on underlying spaces (Lemma 9.1.3(a))
items.statement: Standing hypothesis of §9.1: X is a preadic space (Definition 8.2.3). Let U → V be a pro-étale morphism in X̂_ét and W → V an arbitrary morphism in X̂_ét. Then U ×_V W → W is pro-étale, and the map |U ×_V W| → |U| ×_{|V|} |W| is surjective.
items.note: Nearest: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-base-change (Scholze 2013, Lemma 3.10(i)) for locally noetherian analytic X only. The proof uses surjectivity of inverse limits of surjections of compact spaces, Remark 2.3.15(c) (PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/61, missing).

items.name: Pro-étale over pro-étale is pro-étale (Lemma 9.1.3(b))
items.statement: Standing hypothesis of §9.1: X is a preadic space (Definition 8.2.3). For pro-étale morphisms U → V → W in X̂_ét, the composition U → W is pro-étale.
items.note: Nearest: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-composition (Scholze 2013, Lemma 3.10(vi)), for locally noetherian analytic X only.

items.name: The pro-étale site X_proét of a preadic space (Definition 9.1.4, with Remark 9.1.7)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis of §9.1: X is a preadic space (Definition 8.2.3). X_proét is the full subcategory of X̂_ét consisting of the objects pro-étale over X. It is a site in which a family {U_i → Y}_i is a covering if, for some (equivalently, any) pro-étale presentations U_i = lim←_j U_{i,j} over Y and some (equivalently, any) indices j(i) such that U_{i,j″} → U_{i,j′} is faithfully finite étale for all j″ ≥ j′ ≥ j(i), the family {U_{i,j(i)} → Y}_i is a set-theoretic covering. The embedding X_ét → X̂_ét defines a morphism of sites X_proét → X_ét. If X is stably adic, the coverings are exactly the families {U_i → Y}_i for which {|U_i| → |Y|}_i is jointly surjective. (Remark 9.1.7: X_proét has fibre products by Lemma 9.1.3, but without a locally noetherian hypothesis one cannot argue as in [113, Lemma 3.10(vii)] that it has all finite projective limits, nor apply the topos-theoretic results of [113, Proposition 3.12].)
items.note: Nearest: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-site-corrected, A1/corrected-covers-pretopology and A1/proetale-projection-nu (Scholze 2013 §3 with the 2016 erratum) for locally noetherian X. Two differences: Kedlaya–Liu allow arbitrary preadic X, and (Remark 9.1.7) without a noetherian hypothesis X_proét has fibre products (Lemma 9.1.3) but not necessarily all finite limits, so Scholze's topos-theoretic results (Lemma 3.10(vii), Proposition 3.12) are not available. Their covering condition is Scholze's uncorrected one: members are towers over jointly surjective étale maps indexed by arbitrary cofiltered categories, so (for instance) an open surjection of profinite sets without a continuous section gives a covering, which A1's corrected convention excludes (A1/profinite-set-objects (d)); the two agree for countable presentations. Kedlaya–Liu's arguments (Čech computations along towers, Lemmas 9.1.9, 9.2.8) do not use the splitting property that motivated the correction (Scholze's Proposition 3.7, Lemma 3.16), so the difference is not recorded as a source issue. Route: AdicEtaleGeometry A1.

items.name: Underlying spaces of objects of X_proét are locally spectral (Remark 9.1.5)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis of §9.1: X is a preadic space (Definition 8.2.3). For any Y ∈ X_proét admitting a pro-étale presentation in which the underlying space of each term is qcqs, |Y| is a spectral space (an inverse limit of spectral spaces, Corollary 8.1.3). Consequently |Y| is a locally spectral space for every Y ∈ X_proét.
items.note: The input 'inverse limits of spectral spaces are spectral' (Corollary 8.1.3, chapter 8) is planned in DiamondsAndVStacks:D0 (limits of spectral spaces); the statement about objects of X_proét needs Kedlaya–Liu's site, which no layer plans.

items.name: Quasicompact opens of objects of X̂_ét are étale subobjects (Lemma 9.1.6(a))
items.statement: Let X be a stably adic space. For U ∈ X̂_ét and W ⊆ |U| a quasicompact open subset, there exist V ∈ X̂_ét and an étale map V → U such that |V| → |U| induces a homeomorphism |V| ≅ W. Moreover, if U ∈ X_proét, one can take V ∈ X_proét, and then any morphism V′ → U in X_proét with image contained in W factors through V.
items.note: Scholze 2013, Lemma 3.10(iii), for locally noetherian X, is summarised in AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-site-corrected; nothing plans the stably adic case. Proof: as Scholze's, using Lemma 9.1.3 and openness of étale maps (Lemma 8.2.17(b); AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-open-map).

items.name: Pro-étale maps are open (Lemma 9.1.6(b))
items.statement: Let X be a stably adic space. For any pro-étale morphism U → V in X̂_ét, the map |U| → |V| is open.
items.note: Nearest: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-maps-open (Scholze 2013, Lemma 3.10(iv)) for locally noetherian analytic X only.

items.name: Surjective (finite) étale maps to objects of X_proét come from X_ét (Lemma 9.1.6(c))
items.statement: Let X be a stably adic space. Any étale (resp. finite étale) map U → V in X̂_ét with V ∈ X_proét and |U| → |V| surjective is the base extension of some surjective étale (resp. finite étale) morphism in X_ét.
items.note: Nearest: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-surjective-etale-descent (Scholze 2013, Lemma 3.10(v)) for locally noetherian analytic X only.

items.name: Continuous maps to a topological space form a pro-étale sheaf (Lemma 9.1.9)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis of §9.1: X is a preadic space (Definition 8.2.3). For any topological space T, the functor F_T : Y ↦ Map_cont(|Y|, T) is a sheaf on X_proét. If T is discrete, F_T is the usual constant sheaf associated to T.
items.note: No node states it. Nearest: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-sheaves-of-modules (locally constant functions form an étale sheaf), PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/period-sheaves-on-profinite-products (values Hom_cont(S, F(U)) on U × S), and AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/torsor-spa-orbits, which cites this proof for the quotient-map step (Spa of a faithfully finite étale algebra maps openly onto Spa, Lemma 8.2.17(b)). The proof also uses Proposition 8.2.21 (chapter 8) and that inverse limits of surjective open maps are quotient maps. Route: AdicEtaleGeometry A1 or ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0, with the site.

items.name: Étale ℤ_p- and ℚ_p-local systems on X_proét (Definition 9.1.10)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis of §9.1: X is a preadic space (Definition 8.2.3). An étale ℤ_p-local system (resp. étale ℚ_p-local system) on X_proét is a sheaf of ℤ_p-modules (resp. ℚ_p-vector spaces) on X_proét which is locally of the form F_T (Lemma 9.1.9) for T a finite free ℤ_p-module (resp. a finite-dimensional ℚ_p-vector space) carrying its usual p-adic topology.
items.note: Nearest: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/lisse-zp-sheaf (Scholze 2013, Definition 8.1: lisse Ẑ_p-sheaves, locally Ẑ_p ⊗ M) for locally noetherian X over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p); the ℚ_p-version and the preadic generality are not planned. The analogous notions for ℤ_{p^d}, ℚ_{p^d} are used in §9.3.

items.name: Étale local systems on X and on X_proét agree (Lemma 9.1.11)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis of §9.1: X is a preadic space (Definition 8.2.3). Pullback along X_proét → X_ét defines equivalences between the category of étale ℤ_p-local systems (resp. étale ℚ_p-local systems) on X in the sense of Definition 8.4.3 and the category of étale ℤ_p-local systems (resp. étale ℚ_p-local systems) on X_proét (Definition 9.1.10).
items.note: Nearest: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/lisse-sheaves-etale-proetale-equivalence (Scholze 2013, Proposition 8.2, cited in the proof), for ℤ_p-coefficients and locally noetherian X over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p). The proof reduces to local systems on Spa(A, A⁺) trivialised by a faithfully finite étale tower, descends the tower to Spec(A) (Lemma 8.2.17(a)) and applies Bhatt–Scholze's Theorem 1.4.11 (PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/28, missing; route EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2).

items.name: Pro-étale cohomology of a local system (Definition 9.1.12)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis of §9.1: X is a preadic space (Definition 8.2.3). For V an étale ℤ_p- or ℚ_p-local system on X, the pro-étale cohomology H^i_proét(X, V) is the sheaf cohomology H^i(X_proét, V′) of the local system V′ on X_proét corresponding to V under Lemma 9.1.11.
items.note: Nearest: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/proetale-etale-comparison and PadicHodgeTheory:P8/lisse-sheaves-etale-proetale-equivalence (locally noetherian X).

items.name: Scholze's pro-étale site of a locally noetherian adic space (black box: Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, §3)
items.statement: For X a locally noetherian adic space, Scholze defines pro-X_ét, étale/finite étale/pro-étale morphisms and X_proét (Definition 3.9), and proves (Lemma 3.10): (i) base change along étale, finite étale and pro-étale maps exists and is of the same type, with |U ×_V W| → |U| ×_{|V|} |W| surjective; (ii) composites of étale (finite étale) maps are étale (finite étale); (iii) quasicompact opens of |U| are represented by étale maps; (iv) pro-étale maps are open; (v) surjective (finite) étale maps to objects of X_proét come from X_ét; (vi) pro-étale over pro-étale is pro-étale; (vii) X_proét has finite projective limits; and (Proposition 3.12) the topos is algebraic with coherent affinoid presentations.
items.locator: §9.1: Definitions 9.1.2, 9.1.4, Lemmas 9.1.3, 9.1.6 and Remark 9.1.7 follow or cite [113, §3, Lemma 3.10 and Proposition 3.12], pp. 188–190 (arXiv 1301.0792v5)
items.note: Scholze's erratum to [113] (math.uni-bonn.de/people/scholze/pAdicHodgeErratum.pdf) deletes Proposition 3.7(i) (splitting of open surjections of profinite sets), Proposition 3.8 and the last sentence of Proposition 3.13 (points). It also restricts the covers in Definitions 3.3, 3.4 and 3.9 to transfinite composites of pullbacks of finite étale surjections (unchanged for countable limits). KL Definition 9.1.4 uses the unrestricted (original) notion of covering. None of the claims deleted by the erratum is reproduced or used in KL §9.1–9.2 (see notes).

items.name: Lisse ℤ_p-sheaves on X_ét and X_proét agree (black box: Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Proposition 8.2)
items.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian adic space over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) and L_• a lisse ℤ_p-sheaf on X_ét. Then L̂ = lim ν^*L_n is a lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf on X_proét, R^j lim ν^*L_n = 0 for j > 0, and L_• ↦ L̂ is an equivalence of categories.
items.locator: §9.1, cited in the proof of Lemma 9.1.11 ('See also [113, Proposition 8.2]'), p. 191 (arXiv 1301.0792v5)
items.note: Node: PadicHodgeTheory:P8/lisse-sheaves-etale-proetale-equivalence. Kedlaya–Liu's Lemma 9.1.11 is the version for arbitrary preadic X and ℚ_p-coefficients.

items.name: The structure presheaves O, O°, O⁺ on X_proét and the spectral seminorm (Definition 9.2.2, Remark 9.2.3)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.2.1: X is a preadic space over an analytic field K of residue characteristic p (K may have characteristic 0 or p). For Y = lim← Y_i ∈ X_proét put O(Y) = lim→_i Γ(Y_i, O_{Y_i}), O°(Y) = lim→_i Γ(Y_i, O°_{Y_i}), O⁺(Y) = lim→_i Γ(Y_i, O⁺_{Y_i}). The spectral seminorm on O(Y): choose j such that Y_i → Y_j is faithfully finite étale for all i ≥ j; for f ∈ O(Y) choose i ≥ j with f ∈ O_{Y_i}(Y_i) and let the spectral seminorm of f be its spectral seminorm in O_{Y_i}(Y_i). Equivalently (Remark 9.2.3), each point of |Y| defines a multiplicative seminorm on O(Y), and the spectral seminorm is their supremum.
items.note: Nearest: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/proetale-structure-sheaves-and-valuations (O_X = ν^*O_{X_ét}, O_X⁺, and the valuations f ↦ |f(x)| on sections; Scholze 2013, Definition 4.1 and Lemma 4.2) for locally noetherian X over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p); on qcqs objects ν^*O agrees with Kedlaya–Liu's colimit.

items.name: Perfectoid subdomains of X_proét (Definition 9.2.4)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.2.1: X is a preadic space over an analytic field K of residue characteristic p (K may have characteristic 0 or p). An element Y of X_proét is a perfectoid subdomain if it admits a pro-étale presentation lim← Y_i such that (a) there is an index j with Y_i → Y_j faithfully finite étale for all i ≥ j and Y_j a preadic affinoid space over K (then so is each Y_i, i ≥ j); and (b) the completion of O(Y) for the spectral seminorm is a perfectoid Banach algebra over K if K has characteristic 0, or a perfect (uniform) Banach algebra over K if K has characteristic p.
items.note: Nearest: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/affinoid-perfectoid-objects-and-etale-pullbacks (Scholze 2013, Definition 4.3: affinoid perfectoid objects, using the p-adic completion of lim→ R_i⁺) for locally noetherian X over a perfectoid field; Kedlaya–Liu use the spectral-seminorm completion, a tower over an affinoid stage, arbitrary preadic X and also characteristic p.

items.name: Stability of perfectoid subdomains (Definition 9.2.4(i)–(iii))
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.2.1: X is a preadic space over an analytic field K of residue characteristic p (K may have characteristic 0 or p). (i) If Y is a perfectoid subdomain and Z → Y is a morphism in X_proét which is the pullback of a rational subdomain embedding of elements of X_ét, then Z is a perfectoid subdomain (by Theorem 3.6.14). (ii) Any finite étale cover of a perfectoid subdomain is a perfectoid subdomain (by Theorem 3.6.21). (iii) The fibred product of two perfectoid subdomains is a perfectoid subdomain (by (i), (ii) and the local factorization of étale morphisms).
items.note: Inputs: Theorem 3.6.14 (PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/161, planned P2) and Theorem 3.6.21 (PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/166, planned P3). Nearest statement: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/affinoid-perfectoid-objects-and-etale-pullbacks (Scholze 2013, Lemmas 4.5–4.6) for locally noetherian X.

items.name: Perfectoid pro-finite étale covers exist; perfectoid subdomains form a basis (Lemma 9.2.5)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.2.1: X is a preadic space over an analytic field K of residue characteristic p (K may have characteristic 0 or p). If X = Spa(A, A⁺) for an adic Banach algebra (A, A⁺) over K, there exists Y = lim← Y_i ∈ X_proét which is a pro-finite étale covering of X and is a perfectoid subdomain of X_proét. Consequently, for arbitrary X, the perfectoid subdomains of X_proét form a neighborhood basis of X_proét.
items.note: The cover itself (a pro-finite étale torsor tower whose uniform completion is perfectoid, for complete Tate ℤ_p-algebras including characteristic p) is AdicEtaleGeometry:A4/finite-etale-torsor-tower and A4/perfectoid-uniform-completion (Scholze ECD Lemma 15.3). The basis statement inside Kedlaya–Liu's site is not planned (P8's analogue: Scholze 2013, Corollary 4.7, Proposition 4.8, in PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/affinoid-perfectoid-objects-and-etale-pullbacks). The printed proof ('Apply Lemma 3.6.26 to A^u') only covers K of characteristic 0 (source issue); A4's construction covers both characteristics. Status changed from planned (AdicEtaleGeometry:A4) to missing by the independent review: A4 plans the algebraic/perfectoid core (a finite étale torsor tower over a complete Tate ℤ_p-algebra with perfectoid uniform completion). The lemma's conclusions — that the tower is an object of Kedlaya–Liu's X_proét, a pro-finite étale covering there, a perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4, item 362, missing), and that perfectoid subdomains form a basis of X_proét for arbitrary preadic X — live on KL's site, which is missing (347–358); the item's note says 'The basis statement inside Kedlaya–Liu's site is not planned'. Recommend missing, citing A4 for the tower. If kept planned, the note must restrict the claim to the tower construction.

items.name: Reduction of properties of pro-étale coverings to rational coverings and towers (Proposition 9.2.6, corrected)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.2.1: X is a preadic space over an analytic field K of residue characteristic p (K may have characteristic 0 or p). Let (A, A⁺) be a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p and X = Spa(A, A⁺). Let B be the collection of perfectoid subdomains in X_proét which can be written as faithfully finite étale towers over perfectoid subdomains in X_ét (by Lemma 9.2.5 and the local factorization of étale morphisms these form a stable basis of X_proét). Let P be a property of coverings in X_proét of and by elements of B such that: (a) any covering admitting a refinement with property P has P; (b) any composition of coverings with property P has P; (c) for any Y ∈ B, any rational covering of Y has P; (d) for any Y ∈ B, any tower Y′ → Y of faithfully finite étale morphisms, viewed as a covering, has P. Then every covering in X_proét of and by elements of B has property P.
items.locator: §9.2, Proposition 9.2.6 and its proof, pp. 192–193 (the misprint 'subodmains' corrected in part II, Appendix A) (arXiv 1301.0792v5)
items.note: Pro-étale analogue of Proposition 8.2.20 (planned for the étale site in AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction, with its corrected reading, atlas finding AdicEtaleGeometry/E21). The proof (Proposition 8.2.20 plus (b), (d)) does not use characteristic 0, and Lemma 9.2.8 applies it also to perfect uniform 𝔽_p-algebras (source issue).

items.name: The completed structure presheaves Ô and Ô⁺ (Definition 9.2.7)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.2.1: X is a preadic space over an analytic field K of residue characteristic p (K may have characteristic 0 or p). The completed structure presheaf Ô = Ô_X on X_proét is defined by letting Ô(Y), for Y ∈ X_proét, be the completion of O(Y) for the spectral seminorm; the subpresheaf Ô⁺ ⊆ Ô is defined similarly (from O⁺).
items.note: Nearest: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/proetale-structure-sheaves-and-valuations (Scholze's Ô_X⁺ = lim O_X⁺/pⁿ, Ô_X = Ô_X⁺[1/p], a sheaf by construction) for locally noetherian X over ℚ_p; on perfectoid subdomains the two agree.

items.name: Cohomology of Ô and Ô⁺ on a perfectoid or perfect uniform affinoid (Lemma 9.2.8, with Remark 9.2.10)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.2.1: X is a preadic space over an analytic field K of residue characteristic p (K may have characteristic 0 or p). Let (A, A⁺) be a perfectoid adic Banach algebra over ℚ_p or a perfect uniform adic Banach algebra over 𝔽_p, and X = Spa(A, A⁺). (a) H⁰(X_proét, Ô) = A. (b) H^i(X_proét, Ô) = 0 for i > 0. (c) For i > 0, H^i(X_proét, Ô⁺) is annihilated by m_A; so Ô⁺ is almost acyclic in the sense of Proposition 8.3.2 (Remark 9.2.10).
items.locator: §9.2, Lemma 9.2.8 with proof and Remark 9.2.10, pp. 193–194 (arXiv 1301.0792v5)
items.note: Node: DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves (ECD Proposition 8.5: for X affinoid perfectoid, O and O⁺ are sheaves on the pro-étale site, H^i(X_proét, O) = 0 and H^i(X_proét, O⁺) almost zero for i > 0), stated for ECD's pro-étale site of a perfectoid space, which is the finer topology of Remark 9.2.16, where Kedlaya–Liu note the lemma remains true. For Kedlaya–Liu's own site the lemma is not planned; P8's analogue is PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/completed-structure-sheaf-on-affinoid-perfectoids (affinoid perfectoid objects over locally noetherian X). Proof: Čech acyclicity via Proposition 9.2.6 and Theorem 2.4.23 (PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/80), strict exactness of completed direct limits (Remark 3.1.6, item 115) and Proposition 3.6.9(b) (item 159). Status changed from planned (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2) to missing by the independent review: Lemma 9.2.8 is a statement about Kedlaya–Liu's pro-étale site X_proét of the preadic space X = Spa(A,A⁺) (Definition 9.1.4), which is missing (items 347–358 all missing; A1 plans only Scholze's site of a locally noetherian X). D2 plans the analogous statement on ECD's pro-étale site of a perfectoid space, i.e. the finer topology of Remark 9.2.16 (item 374), not KL's site; the item's note says so ('For Kedlaya–Liu's own site the lemma is not planned'). Recommend missing (route with 347–358), citing D2 as the planned analogue for the finer topology.

items.name: Ô agrees with its sheafification on perfectoid subdomains (Corollary 9.2.9)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.2.1: X is a preadic space over an analytic field K of residue characteristic p (K may have characteristic 0 or p). The completed structure presheaf Ô on X_proét agrees with its sheafification on perfectoid subdomains.
items.note: For locally noetherian X the corresponding value Ô_X(U) = R on affinoid perfectoid U is PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/completed-structure-sheaf-on-affinoid-perfectoids; for X perfectoid on ECD's site, DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves. Not planned for Kedlaya–Liu's site of a general preadic X.

items.name: The tilted structure sheaves Ō, Ō°, Ō⁺ (Definition 9.2.11)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.2.1: X is a preadic space over an analytic field K of residue characteristic p (K may have characteristic 0 or p). For K of characteristic 0, the sheaves Ō, Ō°, Ō⁺ on X_proét are defined via the perfectoid correspondence: for Y ∈ X_proét a perfectoid subdomain, (Ō(Y), Ō⁺(Y)) is the perfect uniform adic Banach algebra of characteristic p corresponding to (Ô(Y), Ô⁺(Y)) under Theorem 3.6.5.
items.note: Nearest: Scholze's Ô⁺_{X♭} = lim_Φ O_X⁺/p on X_proét (Definition 5.9), used in PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/period-sheaves-definitions, for locally noetherian X. Uses Theorem 3.6.5 (PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/156, planned P1).

items.name: Pro-sheafy affinoids (Definition 9.2.12)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.2.1: X is a preadic space over an analytic field K of residue characteristic p (K may have characteristic 0 or p). Let ν_X : X_proét → X_ét be the natural morphism. X = Spa(A, A⁺) is pro-sheafy if X is uniform and sheafy and the morphism O_X → ν_{X*}Ô_X is an isomorphism.
items.note: No layer defines the notion. Nearest: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-projection-nu (ν for locally noetherian X) and PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/pushforward-of-structural-de-rham-sheaf (ν_*Ô_X = O_{X_ét} for X smooth over a discretely valued field, Scholze 2013, Proposition 6.16), i.e. smooth rigid spaces are pro-sheafy. Remark 9.2.14 announces (without proof, deferred to a later paper) that reduced normal affinoid algebras over K are pro-sheafy, via Temkin's desingularization [123] and Andreatta–Brinon's imperfect period rings [2].

items.name: Perfectoid affinoids and analytic fields of characteristic 0 are pro-sheafy (Definition 9.2.12, examples, corrected)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.2.1: X is a preadic space over an analytic field K of residue characteristic p (K may have characteristic 0 or p). If A is perfectoid (or, in characteristic p, perfect uniform), X = Spa(A, A⁺) is pro-sheafy (by Lemma 9.2.8). If A = K with K of characteristic 0, X = Spa(K, K⁺) is pro-sheafy, by the Ax–Sen–Tate theorem. (As printed, the second example is asserted for every K of Hypothesis 9.2.1; it fails for imperfect K of characteristic p, see source issues.)
items.note: Ingredients planned: Ax–Sen–Tate (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/ax-sen-tate-invariants, for complete K of characteristic 0) and the perfectoid structure-sheaf computation (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves, on ECD's site); the notion of pro-sheafy on Kedlaya–Liu's site is not planned.

items.name: Split maps to a perfectoid algebra give pro-sheafiness (Remark 9.2.13)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.2.1: X is a preadic space over an analytic field K of residue characteristic p (K may have characteristic 0 or p). Suppose X = Spa(A, A⁺) and there exists a perfectoid Banach algebra B over K with a bounded homomorphism A → B which splits in the category of Banach modules over A. Then X is pro-sheafy. This holds for instance if A is strongly preperfectoid (choosing a perfectoid field admitting a Schauder basis over ℚ_p); and if A has this property, so does A{T₁, …, T_n}.
items.note: Stated without proof.
