The hypothesis is Hansen–Kedlaya's sousperfectoid condition; nearest layer AdicSpacesPartII:R5 (AdicSpacesPartII:R5/sousperfectoid-rings: sheafiness and stability of sousperfectoid rings), which does not consider ν_*Ô. Strongly preperfectoid: Definition 3.7.1 (PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/170, missing). Route: AdicSpacesPartII R5.

items.name: Kiehl glueing for the pro-étale topology (Theorem 9.2.15)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.2.1: X is a preadic space over an analytic field K of residue characteristic p (K may have characteristic 0 or p). Suppose X is perfectoid or perfect uniform. Then pullback of finite locally free O_X-modules to finite locally free Ô_X-modules on X_proét defines an equivalence of categories.
items.note: Proof: full faithfulness from Lemma 9.2.8; essential surjectivity by Theorem 8.2.22 and Proposition 8.2.20 reduces to descent along a countable faithfully finite étale tower A → B = Ô(Y), for which an A-linear bounded splitting B → A is built from almost purity (Theorem 5.5.9, PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/207) with splittings of norm ≤ p^{p^{−i}}. Not planned: PerfectoidSpaces:P9 plans descent of finite locally free modules along profinite towers over smooth rigid spaces, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-descent-perfectoid étale descent, PadicHodgeTheory:P8/vector-bundles-on-analytic-etale-and-proetale-sites the smooth locally noetherian case, and VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1 only quotes v-descent of vector bundles on perfectoid spaces (Scholze–Weinstein, Berkeley Lemma 17.1.8). Route: PerfectoidSpaces P9.

items.name: Scholze's finer pro-étale topology on perfectoid spaces (Remark 9.2.16)
items.statement: For X perfectoid or perfect uniform: a morphism f : Y → X of perfectoid spaces is pro-étale if there are a cofiltered inverse system {Y_i}_{i∈I} in X_ét and compatible morphisms Y → Y_i such that (a) the transition morphisms Y_j → Y_i are qcqs (for any U → Y_i with U a preadic affinoid space, Y_j ×_{Y_i} U is qcqs); (b) |Y| → lim← |Y_i| is a homeomorphism; (c) Y is covered by perfectoid affinoid subspaces Spa(A, A⁺) such that, for each i, over all perfectoid affinoid subspaces Spa(A_ij, A_ij⁺) of Y_i through which Spa(A, A⁺) → Y_i factors, the direct limit of the maps A_ij → A has dense image. A pro-étale covering of X is a family {U_i → X}_{i∈I} of pro-étale morphisms such that for every quasicompact open V ⊆ X there are a finite J ⊆ I and quasicompact opens V_j ⊆ U_j ×_X V (j ∈ J) with {V_j → V}_{j∈J} a set-theoretic covering. The acyclicity assertions of Lemma 9.2.8 and Lemma 9.3.4 remain true for this topology; it is unclear whether the proof of Theorem 9.2.15 adapts.
items.note: The covering condition is exactly ECD Definition 8.1 (DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/small-pro-etale-site-and-v-site); pro-étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces are PerfectoidSpaces:P6/pro-etale-map (ECD 7.8, locally affinoid pro-étale), and conditions (a)–(c) are the tilde-limit Y ∼ lim Y_i of Scholze–Weinstein [115, §2.4] (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison). The acyclicity claim is DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/pro-etale-etale-comparison-and-structure-sheaves (for Ô, Ô⁺; for the period sheaves of Lemma 9.3.4 see the source issue on that lemma).

items.name: Ax–Sen–Tate theorem (black box, [6])
items.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field of characteristic 0 and C the completion of an algebraic closure of K, with its continuous action of G_K. Then C^{G_K} = K; more generally, for a closed subgroup H ⊆ G_K, C^H is the completion of the fixed field of H.
items.note: Node: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/ax-sen-tate-invariants (stated for K/ℚ_p finite and 'more generally K complete of characteristic 0'). For K of characteristic p the invariants are the completed perfect closure of K, which is why the example in Definition 9.2.12 needs characteristic 0. Node: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/ax-sen-tate-invariants, whose statement is for K/ℚ_p finite; the general case (K any analytic field of characteristic 0, as used in Definition 9.2.12 for arbitrary analytic fields of characteristic 0) appears only as a parenthetical in the node's hypotheses list ('more generally K complete of characteristic 0 with algebraic closure dense in C'), so the design must promote it to the statement.

items.name: Witt-vector period sheaves Ã_X, Ã⁺_X, B̃_X (Definition 9.3.3, first part)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.3.2: X is a preadic space over ℚ_{p^d} for a positive integer d; Y ∈ X_proét denotes an arbitrary perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4) and Y′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} corresponding to Y; Ō, Ō⁺ are the tilted sheaves of Definition 9.2.11. Define sheaves on X_proét by Ã_X(Y) = W(Ō(Y)), Ã⁺_X(Y) = ℛ̃^{int,+}_{Ō(Y)} = W(Ō⁺(Y)), and B̃_X(Y) = W(Ō(Y))[p^{−1}].
items.note: Ã⁺_X is Scholze's A_inf = W(Ô⁺_{X♭}) (PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/period-sheaves-definitions, locally noetherian X over ℚ_p); the sheaves W(Ō) and W(Ō)[1/p] are not planned. Ring-level definitions: §5.1 (PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/188, missing).

items.name: Relative Robba period sheaves Ã^{†,r}_X, Ã^†_X, B̃^{†,r}_X, B̃^†_X, C̃⁺_X, C̃^r_X, C̃^I_X, C̃_X (Definition 9.3.3, second part)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.3.2: X is a preadic space over ℚ_{p^d} for a positive integer d; Y ∈ X_proét denotes an arbitrary perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4) and Y′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} corresponding to Y; Ō, Ō⁺ are the tilted sheaves of Definition 9.2.11. Define sheaves on X_proét by Ã^{†,r}_X(Y) = ℛ̃^{int,r}_{Ō(Y)}, Ã^†_X(Y) = ℛ̃^{int}_{Ō(Y)}, B̃^{†,r}_X(Y) = ℛ̃^{bd,r}_{Ō(Y)}, B̃^†_X(Y) = ℛ̃^{bd}_{Ō(Y)}, C̃⁺_X(Y) = ℛ̃⁺_{Ō(Y)}, C̃^r_X(Y) = ℛ̃^r_{Ō(Y)}, C̃^I_X(Y) = ℛ̃^I_{Ō(Y)} and C̃_X(Y) = ℛ̃_{Ō(Y)}, the relative extended Robba rings of Definition 5.1.1.
items.note: The rings are PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/188 (missing); over a perfectoid base the nearest are the rings of the relative annuli Y_{S,I} (RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF0:annuli). No layer plans them as sheaves on a pro-étale site. Route: with the chapter 8 relative ϕ-module theory, a Part II of RelativeFarguesFontaine or PadicHodgeTheory P8.

items.name: The period sheaves are acyclic on perfectoid subdomains (Lemma 9.3.4, corrected for Ã⁺_X)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.3.2: X is a preadic space over ℚ_{p^d} for a positive integer d; Y ∈ X_proét denotes an arbitrary perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4) and Y′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} corresponding to Y; Ō, Ō⁺ are the tilted sheaves of Definition 9.2.11. Standing hypothesis 9.3.2: X is a preadic space over ℚ_{p^d} for a positive integer d; Y ∈ X_proét denotes an arbitrary perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4) and Y′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} corresponding to Y; Ō, Ō⁺ are the tilted sheaves of Definition 9.2.11. The sheaves Ã_X, Ã^{†,r}_X, Ã^†_X, B̃_X, B̃^{†,r}_X, B̃^†_X, C̃^r_X, C̃^I_X, C̃_X of Definition 9.3.3 have vanishing higher cohomology on every perfectoid subdomain Y (these are exactly the rings for which Theorem 5.3.3 gives acyclicity for rational coverings). For C̃⁺_X = ℛ̃⁺_{Ō} acyclicity is asserted by the paper but not established by the cited argument: Theorem 5.3.3 omits ℛ̃^{int,+}, ℛ̃^{bd,+} and ℛ̃⁺ even for rational coverings. For Ã⁺_X = W(Ō⁺) the higher cohomology on Y is only almost zero (killed by [x] for every topologically nilpotent x ∈ Ō⁺(Y)), as for Ô⁺ in Lemma 9.2.8(c). (As printed, all the sheaves of Definition 9.3.3 are asserted to be acyclic on Y; see source issues.) For Ã⁺_X = W(Ō⁺) the higher cohomology on Y is only almost zero (killed by [x] for every topologically nilpotent x ∈ Ō⁺(Y)), as for Ô⁺ in Lemma 9.2.8(c). (As printed, all the sheaves of Definition 9.3.3 are asserted to be acyclic on Y; see source issues.)
items.locator: §9.3, Lemma 9.3.4 and its proof ('Imitate the proof of Lemma 9.2.8'), p. 196 (arXiv 1301.0792v5)
items.note: Nearest: PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/period-sheaves-on-affinoid-perfectoids (Scholze 2013, Theorem 6.5: A_inf almost acyclic, B_inf, B_dR⁺ acyclic on affinoid perfectoids of locally noetherian X). The Robba-type sheaves are not planned.

items.name: ϕ^d-modules over the perfect period sheaves; pure and étale points (Definition 9.3.5)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.3.2: X is a preadic space over ℚ_{p^d} for a positive integer d; Y ∈ X_proét denotes an arbitrary perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4) and Y′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} corresponding to Y; Ō, Ō⁺ are the tilted sheaves of Definition 9.2.11. The sheaves Ã_X, Ã⁺_X, Ã^†_X, B̃_X, B̃^†_X, C̃⁺_X, C̃_X carry actions of ϕ and are called perfect period sheaves. A ϕ^d-module over one of them is a sheaf of finite projective modules over it equipped with an isomorphism with its ϕ^d-pullback. A ϕ^d-module M over C̃_X is pure (resp. étale) at x ∈ X if its restriction to some perfectoid subdomain is pure (resp. étale) at some lift of x; then the same holds for every lift of x to every perfectoid subdomain (Corollary 7.3.10).
items.note: Pointwise purity and étaleness over a perfect uniform base: PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/217 and /220. Nearest atlas layer: bundles on X_S for perfectoid S (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1, VB4); ϕ-modules over pro-étale period sheaves of a general preadic X are not planned.

items.name: Pure and étale loci are open and partially proper (Theorem 9.3.6)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.3.2: X is a preadic space over ℚ_{p^d} for a positive integer d; Y ∈ X_proét denotes an arbitrary perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4) and Y′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} corresponding to Y; Ō, Ō⁺ are the tilted sheaves of Definition 9.2.11. For M a ϕ^d-module over C̃_X, the pure locus (resp. the étale locus) of M is a partially proper open subset of X. In particular, by Lemma 8.2.12, if X is taut, then so are the pure locus and the étale locus.
items.note: Proof: locally X = Spa(A, A⁺); take A → B as in Lemma 3.6.26 (PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/169), apply Corollary 7.3.8 on ℳ(B) (item 220) and descend along the quotient map ℳ(B) → ℳ(A) (Remark 2.3.15(b)). Over a perfectoid base the openness of the pure locus also follows from semicontinuity of the Harder–Narasimhan polygon (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB4/semicontinuity-of-HN-polygon), but the statement for general X is not planned.

items.name: Étale ℤ_{p^d}-local systems are ϕ^d-modules over Ã_X and Ã^†_X (Theorem 9.3.7)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.3.2: X is a preadic space over ℚ_{p^d} for a positive integer d; Y ∈ X_proét denotes an arbitrary perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4) and Y′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} corresponding to Y; Ō, Ō⁺ are the tilted sheaves of Definition 9.2.11. The following categories are equivalent via functors which preserve rank and are natural for pullbacks on X: (a) étale ℤ_{p^d}-local systems over X; (b) ϕ^d-modules over Ã_X; (c) ϕ^d-modules over Ã^†_X.
items.note: Immediate from Theorem 8.5.5 (chapter 8) and Lemma 9.1.11. Nearest planned: PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology:PG.1 (Fontaine's equivalence over a field); the perfect-ring case over W_n(R) is Proposition 3.2.7 (PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/125, missing).

items.name: ϕ^d-modules over Ã_X and Ã^†_X on a perfectoid subdomain come from the ring (Corollary 9.3.8)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.3.2: X is a preadic space over ℚ_{p^d} for a positive integer d; Y ∈ X_proét denotes an arbitrary perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4) and Y′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} corresponding to Y; Ō, Ō⁺ are the tilted sheaves of Definition 9.2.11. If X = Y is itself a perfectoid subdomain, base extension from ϕ^d-modules over Ẽ^{int}_{Ō(Y)} = W(Ō(Y)) (resp. ℛ̃^{int}_{Ō(Y)}) to ϕ^d-modules over Ã_X (resp. Ã^†_X) is an equivalence of categories.
items.note: Combines Theorem 8.5.3 (chapter 8) with Theorem 9.3.7.

items.name: The graded period sheaf P_X and vector bundles over FF_X (Definition 9.3.9, corrected)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.3.2: X is a preadic space over ℚ_{p^d} for a positive integer d; Y ∈ X_proét denotes an arbitrary perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4) and Y′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} corresponding to Y; Ō, Ō⁺ are the tilted sheaves of Definition 9.2.11. Define the sheaf of graded rings P_X = ⊕_{n≥0} P_{X,n} by P_{X,n}(Y) = {x ∈ C̃_X(Y) : ϕ^d(x) = pⁿx}. A vector bundle over FF_X is a sheaf of graded P_X-modules whose restriction to each Y has the form ⊕_{n≥0} Γ(FF_Y, V(n)) for some vector bundle V on FF_Y, where V(n) = V ⊗ O(n); morphisms are morphisms of graded modules whose restrictions to each Y arise from morphisms of vector bundles. (Printed: Γ(FF_Y, V^{⊗n}); see source issues.)
items.note: For a perfectoid (or perfect uniform) base, the graded ring P and Proj(P) are PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/211 (planned RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness) and FF_R is chapter 8. The sheafified notion over a general preadic X is not planned.

items.name: Vector bundles on FF_Y agree with vector bundles over FF_X when X = Y (Remark 9.3.10)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.3.2: X is a preadic space over ℚ_{p^d} for a positive integer d; Y ∈ X_proét denotes an arbitrary perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4) and Y′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} corresponding to Y; Ō, Ō⁺ are the tilted sheaves of Definition 9.2.11. If X = Y is a perfectoid subdomain, then FF_Y is an adic space, and base extension from vector bundles on FF_Y to vector bundles over FF_X in the sense of Definition 9.3.9 is an equivalence of categories.
items.note: Sketched: follows from Theorem 9.2.15 via Theorem 5.3.9 (PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/198) and a splitting argument.

items.name: The de Rham period sheaves B⁺_{dR,X} and B_{dR,X} (Definition 9.3.11, first part)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.3.2: X is a preadic space over ℚ_{p^d} for a positive integer d; Y ∈ X_proét denotes an arbitrary perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4) and Y′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} corresponding to Y; Ō, Ō⁺ are the tilted sheaves of Definition 9.2.11. B⁺_{dR,X}(Y) is the ker(θ)-adic completion of B̃^{†,1}_X(Y) = ℛ̃^{bd,1}_{Ō(Y)}, and B_{dR,X} is the localization of B⁺_{dR,X} obtained by inverting a generator of ker(θ). These correspond on Y to the rings R₂, R₃ of Definition 8.9.4.
items.note: The same sheaves (B_dR⁺ = lim B_inf/(ker θ)ⁿ, B_dR = B_dR⁺[1/t]) are planned for locally noetherian X over ℚ_p in PadicHodgeTheory:P8:local-rational/period-sheaves-definitions and /de-rham-period-sheaf, and at an untilt of a perfectoid space in RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts/BdR-completion-and-filtration; not for a general preadic X.

items.name: The sheaf B_{e,X} (Definition 9.3.11, second part)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.3.2: X is a preadic space over ℚ_{p^d} for a positive integer d; Y ∈ X_proét denotes an arbitrary perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4) and Y′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} corresponding to Y; Ō, Ō⁺ are the tilted sheaves of Definition 9.2.11. B_{e,X}(Y) is the coordinate ring of the open affine subscheme of Proj(P_X(Y)) obtained by removing the zero locus of the canonical section Y → FF_Y (the divisor of the untilt Y); on Y it is the ring R₁ of Definition 8.9.4.
items.note: Not planned anywhere (the affine complement of ∞ in the Fargues–Fontaine curve, B_e = B_cris^{ϕ=1} classically); nearest RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3/graded-algebra-and-algebraic-curve-map.

items.name: B-pairs over X (Definition 9.3.11, third part)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.3.2: X is a preadic space over ℚ_{p^d} for a positive integer d; Y ∈ X_proét denotes an arbitrary perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4) and Y′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} corresponding to Y; Ō, Ō⁺ are the tilted sheaves of Definition 9.2.11. A B-pair over X is a triple (M_e, M⁺_dR, M_dR) in which M_e is a finite projective B_{e,X}-module, M⁺_dR a finite projective B⁺_{dR,X}-module and M_dR a finite projective B_{dR,X}-module, with isomorphisms M_dR ≅ M_e ⊗_{B_{e,X}} B_{dR,X} ≅ M⁺_dR ⊗_{B⁺_{dR,X}} B_{dR,X}.
items.note: B-pairs appear nowhere in the atlas. Over a point, the Beauville–Laszlo description of modifications at a divisor is RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF4:vector-bundles/meromorphic-modification-at-a-divisor (and item PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/17). B-pairs are not in any stage text of the atlas; note that the accepted PAPER-DING-25 route 6 routes Berger's B-pairs over a p-adic field (the functor M ↦ W(M) and H^i_{(φ,Γ)}(M) ≅ H^i(G_K, W(M))) to PadicHodgeTheory:P7 (see item 404). The relative/sheaf version stays missing.

items.name: ϕ^d-modules over C̃_X, vector bundles on FF_X and B-pairs on X are equivalent (Theorem 9.3.12)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.3.2: X is a preadic space over ℚ_{p^d} for a positive integer d; Y ∈ X_proét denotes an arbitrary perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4) and Y′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} corresponding to Y; Ō, Ō⁺ are the tilted sheaves of Definition 9.2.11. The categories of ϕ^d-modules over C̃_X, of vector bundles on FF_X (Definition 9.3.9), and of B-pairs on X are functorially equivalent.
items.note: Immediate from Theorems 8.7.8 and 8.9.6 (chapter 8). For a perfectoid base the first equivalence is PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/212 (planned VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness, RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF3) with the GAGA theorem VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness/gaga-equivalence; the B-pair description is not planned.

items.name: Étale ℚ_{p^d}-local systems as étale ϕ^d-modules and slope-zero bundles (Theorem 9.3.13)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.3.2: X is a preadic space over ℚ_{p^d} for a positive integer d; Y ∈ X_proét denotes an arbitrary perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4) and Y′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} corresponding to Y; Ō, Ō⁺ are the tilted sheaves of Definition 9.2.11. The following categories are equivalent via functors which preserve rank and are natural for pullbacks on X: (a) étale ℚ_{p^d}-local systems over X; (b) étale ϕ^d-modules over B̃_X; (c) étale ϕ^d-modules over B̃^†_X; (d) étale ϕ^d-modules over C̃_X; (e) vector bundles on FF_X which are pointwise semistable of degree 0.
items.note: Immediate from Theorems 8.5.12, 8.7.7 and Lemma 9.1.11. For X perfectoid, (a) ⇔ (e) is Fargues–Scholze II.2.20 with E = ℚ_{p^d}, planned in VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB4/slope-zero-local-systems (the stage VB4 states 'the equivalence between everywhere slope-zero bundles and pro-étale E-local systems'); the ϕ-module descriptions (b)–(d) and general preadic X are not planned.

items.name: ϕ^d-modules over C̃_X on a perfectoid subdomain come from ℛ̃ (Corollary 9.3.14)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.3.2: X is a preadic space over ℚ_{p^d} for a positive integer d; Y ∈ X_proét denotes an arbitrary perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4) and Y′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} corresponding to Y; Ō, Ō⁺ are the tilted sheaves of Definition 9.2.11. If X = Y is a perfectoid subdomain, base extension from ϕ^d-modules over ℛ̃_{Ō(Y)} to ϕ^d-modules over C̃_X is an equivalence of categories.
items.note: Printed proof: 'Immediate from Theorem 9.3.13 and Remark 9.3.10'; for non-étale modules the argument needs Theorem 9.3.12 with Theorem 8.7.8 (source issue). Used for all (ϕ, Γ)-modules in Theorem 9.5.8.

items.name: Pure ϕ^d-modules over B̃_X and B̃^†_X on a perfectoid subdomain come from the ring (Corollary 9.3.15)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.3.2: X is a preadic space over ℚ_{p^d} for a positive integer d; Y ∈ X_proét denotes an arbitrary perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4) and Y′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} corresponding to Y; Ō, Ō⁺ are the tilted sheaves of Definition 9.2.11. If X = Y is a perfectoid subdomain, base extension from pure ϕ^d-modules over Ẽ_{Y′} (resp. ℛ̃^{bd}_{Y′}) to pure ϕ^d-modules over B̃_X (resp. B̃^†_X) is an equivalence of categories.
items.note: From Theorem 9.3.13 and the fact that étale ℚ_p-local systems arise adic-locally from isogeny ℤ_p-local systems (Corollary 8.4.7).

items.name: ϕ-cohomology of ϕ^d-modules over period sheaves (Definition 9.4.1)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.3.2: X is a preadic space over ℚ_{p^d} for a positive integer d; Y ∈ X_proét denotes an arbitrary perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4) and Y′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} corresponding to Y; Ō, Ō⁺ are the tilted sheaves of Definition 9.2.11. For M a ϕ^d-module over a perfect period sheaf, H^i_{ϕ^d}(M) is the i-th hypercohomology of the complex 0 → M --(ϕ^d − 1)--> M → 0 of sheaves on X_proét.
items.note: Ring-level ϕ-cohomology: Remark 1.5.5 ff. (PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/30, planned VB0, PG.0); the sheaf hypercohomology version is not planned.

items.name: Pro-étale cohomology of ℤ_{p^d}-local systems is ϕ-cohomology (Theorem 9.4.2)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.3.2: X is a preadic space over ℚ_{p^d} for a positive integer d; Y ∈ X_proét denotes an arbitrary perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4) and Y′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} corresponding to Y; Ō, Ō⁺ are the tilted sheaves of Definition 9.2.11. Let E be an étale ℤ_{p^d}-local system on X, and let M over Ã_X and M^† over Ã^†_X be the ϕ^d-modules attached to E by Theorem 9.3.7. Then for i ≥ 0 there are isomorphisms, functorial in E and X, H^i_proét(X, E) → H^i_{ϕ^d}(M^†) → H^i_{ϕ^d}(M).
items.note: Proof: M^† → M induces quasi-isomorphisms on kernel and cokernel sheaves of ϕ^d − 1 (Theorem 8.6.2); the sequence 0 → E → M → M → 0 (9.4.2.1) is exact by Corollary 3.1.4 (PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/113) and Proposition 7.3.6 (item 219). Not planned; nearest: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists (ii) (rational, trivial coefficients, perfectoid base).

items.name: Cohomology of B-pairs (Definition 9.4.4)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.3.2: X is a preadic space over ℚ_{p^d} for a positive integer d; Y ∈ X_proét denotes an arbitrary perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4) and Y′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} corresponding to Y; Ō, Ō⁺ are the tilted sheaves of Definition 9.2.11. For M = (M_e, M⁺_dR, M_dR) a B-pair over X, H^i_B(M) is the i-th hypercohomology of the complex 0 → M_e × M⁺_dR → M_dR → 0, (x, y) ↦ x − y, of sheaves on X_proét.
items.note: Not planned (no B-pairs in the atlas). Not planned ; note that the accepted PAPER-DING-25 route 6 routes Berger's B-pairs over a p-adic field (the functor M ↦ W(M) and H^i_{(φ,Γ)}(M) ≅ H^i(G_K, W(M))) to PadicHodgeTheory:P7 (see item 404). The relative/sheaf version stays missing.

items.name: Pro-étale cohomology of ℚ_{p^d}-local systems via ϕ-modules and B-pairs (Theorem 9.4.5)
items.statement: Standing hypothesis 9.3.2: X is a preadic space over ℚ_{p^d} for a positive integer d; Y ∈ X_proét denotes an arbitrary perfectoid subdomain (Definition 9.2.4) and Y′ the perfect uniform adic space over 𝔽_{p^d} corresponding to Y; Ō, Ō⁺ are the tilted sheaves of Definition 9.2.11. Let V be an étale ℚ_{p^d}-local system over X, and let M over B̃_X, M^† over B̃^†_X, M_C over C̃_X (étale ϕ^d-modules) and the B-pair M_B = (M_e, M⁺_dR, M_dR) be attached to V by Theorem 9.3.13. Then for i ≥ 0 there are isomorphisms, functorial in V and X, H^i_proét(X, V) → H^i_{ϕ^d}(M) → H^i_{ϕ^d}(M^†) → H^i_{ϕ^d}(M_C) → H^i_B(M_B).
items.note: Proof reduces to isogeny ℤ_{p^d}-local systems and uses exact sequences 0 → V → M → M → 0 etc. (Corollaries 3.1.4, 5.2.4, Proposition 7.3.6) and Theorems 8.7.13, 8.9.6(a). The special case V = ℚ_p over a perfectoid base, RΓ_proét(S, ℚ_p) ≅ RΓ(X_S, O), is planned in VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1/cohomology-of-twists (ii); the general statement is not.

items.name: Cyclotomic coefficient rings with ϕ and Γ = ℤ_p^× (Definition 9.5.1)
items.statement: Setting of §9.5: K is a finite extension of ℚ_p; the rings are those of §4.1 (Robba rings in a variable T with ϕ(1 + T) = (1 + T)^p). Put A_{ℚ_p} = o_{ℰ_{ℚ_p}}, A^†_{ℚ_p} = ℛ^{int}_{ℚ_p}, B_{ℚ_p} = ℰ_{ℚ_p}, B^†_{ℚ_p} = ℛ^{bd}_{ℚ_p}, C_{ℚ_p} = ℛ_{ℚ_p}, and Ã_{ℚ_p} = o_{ℰ̃_{ℚ_p}}, Ã^†_{ℚ_p} = ℛ̃^{int}_{ℚ_p}, B̃_{ℚ_p} = ℰ̃_{ℚ_p}, B̃^†_{ℚ_p} = ℛ̃^{bd}_{ℚ_p}, C̃_{ℚ_p} = ℛ̃_{ℚ_p}. Besides ϕ, these carry the action of Γ = ℤ_p^× given by γ(1 + T) = (1 + T)^γ = Σ_{n≥0} (γ choose n) Tⁿ.
items.note: KL write only 'with notation as in §4.1'. §4.1 allows an arbitrary Frobenius lift, so the cyclotomic lift ϕ(1 + T) = (1 + T)^p is implicit (it is forced by requiring ϕ to commute with the stated Γ-action). The item's parenthetical is an editorial reading, not printed text.

items.name: The cyclotomic perfectoid field, the rings ∗_K and (ϕ, Γ)-modules (Definition 9.5.2, Remark 9.5.3)
items.statement: Setting of §9.5: K is a finite extension of ℚ_p; the rings are those of §4.1 (Robba rings in a variable T with ϕ(1 + T) = (1 + T)^p). Let F be the completion of ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}); F is perfectoid (characteristic 0, not discretely valued, ϕ surjective on o_F/(p)). By the henselian property of A^†_{ℚ_p}, Lemma 2.2.4 (or Krasner's lemma) and the perfectoid correspondence for analytic fields (Theorem 3.5.3) there are distinguished equivalences of tensor categories FÉt(ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞})) ≅ FÉt(F) ≅ FÉt(Ã^†_{ℚ_p}/(p)) ≅ FÉt(A^†_{ℚ_p}/(p)) ≅ FÉt(A^†_{ℚ_p}). For K finite over ℚ_p, the finite étale ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞})-algebra K ⊗_{ℚ_p} ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}) corresponds to a finite étale A^†_{ℚ_p}-algebra A^†_K. For ∗ ∈ {A, A^†, B, B^†, C, Ã, Ã^†, B̃, B̃^†, C̃} put ∗_K = ∗_{ℚ_p} ⊗_{A^†_{ℚ_p}} A^†_K, with the induced ϕ and Γ. A (ϕ, Γ)-module over ∗_K is a ϕ-module with an action of Γ continuous for the weak topology (on A_K, Ã_K, B_K, B̃_K) or the LF topology (on the other rings). (Remark 9.5.3: this differs from the usual convention, which takes a connected component and Γ_K ≅ Gal(K(μ_{p^∞})/K); the two are related by induction and restriction between Γ_K and Γ.)
items.note: PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology:PG.0 plans the coefficient rings A_K, B_K, their overconvergent variants, finite-extension functoriality and the field-of-norms Galois equivalence; FÉt(F) ≅ FÉt(F♭) is PerfectoidSpaces:P3/fontaine-wintenberger. The atlas uses the standard (connected, Γ_K) convention; Kedlaya–Liu's induced convention is not stated. The printed presentation of o_F/(p) is wrong (source issue).

items.name: Fontaine's equivalence and Cherbonnier–Colmez overconvergence (Theorem 9.5.4(a)–(e), black box)
items.statement: Setting of §9.5: K is a finite extension of ℚ_p; the rings are those of §4.1 (Robba rings in a variable T with ϕ(1 + T) = (1 + T)^p). The following categories are canonically equivalent: (a) continuous representations of G_K on finite free ℤ_p-modules; (b) (ϕ, Γ)-modules over A_K; (c) (ϕ, Γ)-modules over Ã_K; (d) (ϕ, Γ)-modules over A^†_K; (e) (ϕ, Γ)-modules over Ã^†_K.
items.locator: §9.5, Theorem 9.5.4 (a)–(e) and its proof, p. 201 (citing Fontaine and Cherbonnier–Colmez via [89, §2]) (arXiv 1301.0792v5)
items.note: External: Fontaine's theory of étale (ϕ, Γ)-modules ((a) ⇔ (b)) and Cherbonnier–Colmez overconvergence ((a) ⇔ (d)), in the standard Γ_K convention (Remark 9.5.3). PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology:PG.1 ('Construct D(T) = (A ⊗ T)^{H_K} and its inverse via φ-fixed vectors on the enlarged coefficient ring') and PG.2 (Cherbonnier–Colmez); the perfect-ring variants (c), (e) are not stated separately there.

items.name: ℤ_p-representations of G_K as ϕ-modules over the pro-étale period sheaves of Spa(K, o_K) (Theorem 9.5.4(f)–(g))
items.statement: Setting of §9.5: K is a finite extension of ℚ_p; the rings are those of §4.1 (Robba rings in a variable T with ϕ(1 + T) = (1 + T)^p). The category of continuous representations of G_K on finite free ℤ_p-modules is canonically equivalent to (f) the category of ϕ-modules over Ã_{Spa(K,o_K)}, and to (g) the category of ϕ-modules over Ã^†_{Spa(K,o_K)}.
items.note: From Theorem 9.3.7 with d = 1 and X = Spa(K, o_K). Not planned (needs the §9.1–9.3 sheaves).

items.name: Étale (ϕ, Γ)-modules over the rational rings (Definition 9.5.5)
items.statement: Setting of §9.5: K is a finite extension of ℚ_p; the rings are those of §4.1 (Robba rings in a variable T with ϕ(1 + T) = (1 + T)^p). For ∗ = B, B^†, C, B̃, B̃^†, C̃, a (ϕ, Γ)-module over ∗_K is étale if its underlying ϕ-module is étale, i.e. descends to a ϕ-module over A_K, A^†_K, A^†_K, Ã_K, Ã^†_K, Ã^†_K respectively. The Γ-action acts on some such descent, but not necessarily on all of them.
items.note: PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology:PG.0 ('Define an étale φ-module by the appropriate φ-linearization plus a stable lattice') and PG.2 (étale objects in the Robba realization); the extended-ring versions are not stated.

items.name: ℚ_p-representations of G_K and étale (ϕ, Γ)-modules over B_K, B^†_K, C_K (Theorem 9.5.6(a)–(d))
items.statement: Setting of §9.5: K is a finite extension of ℚ_p; the rings are those of §4.1 (Robba rings in a variable T with ϕ(1 + T) = (1 + T)^p). The following categories are canonically equivalent: (a) continuous representations of G_K on finite-dimensional ℚ_p-vector spaces; (b) étale (ϕ, Γ)-modules over B_K; (c) étale (ϕ, Γ)-modules over B^†_K; (d) étale (ϕ, Γ)-modules over C_K.
items.note: (a)–(c) from Theorem 9.5.4; (c) ⇔ (d) from Proposition 4.1.8 (PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/175, planned RD.2). Planned: PG.1 ('Extend to V'), PG.2 ('Compare integral, bounded overconvergent and Robba realizations ... Separate equivalence for étale objects').

items.name: ℚ_p-representations of G_K and étale (ϕ, Γ)-modules over the extended rings B̃_K, B̃^†_K, C̃_K (Theorem 9.5.6(e)–(g))
items.statement: Setting of §9.5: K is a finite extension of ℚ_p; the rings are those of §4.1 (Robba rings in a variable T with ϕ(1 + T) = (1 + T)^p). The category of continuous representations of G_K on finite-dimensional ℚ_p-vector spaces is canonically equivalent to the categories of étale (ϕ, Γ)-modules over (e) B̃_K, (f) B̃^†_K, (g) C̃_K.
items.note: (e)–(f) from Theorem 9.5.4 (c), (e); (f) ⇔ (g) from Theorem 8.5.6 (chapter 8). The perfect-ring (ϕ, Γ)-module equivalences are not stated in PG.1–PG.2; the descent of étale ϕ-modules from ℛ̃ to ℛ̃^{bd} over a perfect field without Γ is PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/182 (planned PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.2). Route: PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology PG.2.

items.name: ℚ_p-representations of G_K as étale ϕ-modules over the pro-étale sheaves of Spa(K, o_K) (Theorem 9.5.6(h)–(j))
items.statement: Setting of §9.5: K is a finite extension of ℚ_p; the rings are those of §4.1 (Robba rings in a variable T with ϕ(1 + T) = (1 + T)^p). The category of continuous representations of G_K on finite-dimensional ℚ_p-vector spaces is canonically equivalent to the categories of étale ϕ-modules over (h) B̃_{Spa(K,o_K)}, (i) B̃^†_{Spa(K,o_K)}, (j) C̃_{Spa(K,o_K)}.
items.note: From Theorem 9.3.13 with d = 1. Not planned.

items.name: B-pairs over a p-adic field (Definition 9.5.7, after Berger [12])
items.statement: Setting of §9.5: K is a finite extension of ℚ_p; the rings are those of §4.1 (Robba rings in a variable T with ϕ(1 + T) = (1 + T)^p). Let ℂ_p be a completed algebraic closure of ℚ_p. For K ⊆ ℂ_p finite over ℚ_p, a B-pair over K is a B-pair over Spa(ℂ_p, o_{ℂ_p}) (Definition 9.3.11) equipped with a continuous semilinear action of G_K.
items.note: Berger's B-pairs appear nowhere in the atlas (its Berger sources are the 2002 and Astérisque 319 papers, not [12]). Route: PadicHodgeTheory (P7/R06.2, where Berger's Robba-ring dictionary lives) or PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology PG.2. Review (status changed from missing to planned): Berger's B-pairs over a p-adic field K are routed to PadicHodgeTheory:P7 by an accepted source route (PAPER-DING-25 route 6), whose item PAPER-DING-25/2.1-bpairs (status planned, P7) defines the B-pair W(M) = (W_e(M), W^+_dR(M)) of a (φ,Γ)-module after Berger; BHS-19 route 4 (accepted) also routes Berger's W^+_dR/W_dR to P7. Kedlaya–Liu's Definition 9.5.7 (a B-pair over Spa(ℂ_p, o_ℂp) with continuous semilinear G_K-action) is Berger's notion. The P7 stage description itself does not yet mention B-pairs (the source addition is pending), so the item's note 'B-pairs appear nowhere in the atlas' is out of date. Caveat for the parent: this rests on an accepted source route, not on stage/packet text. Reviewer S2 (parent) accepts this with the caveat that the plan is an accepted source route (PAPER-DING-25 route 6, verified in PAPER-DING-25.review.json: verdict accept) whose addition to the P7 stage text is pending; the Definition-level notion (a pair (W_e, W^+_dR) with the gluing isomorphism and G_K-action) is what DING-25/2.1-bpairs uses.

items.name: (ϕ, Γ)-modules over C_K and C̃_K are B-pairs (Theorem 9.5.8(a)–(c); Berger [12, Théorème 2.2.7])
items.statement: Setting of §9.5: K is a finite extension of ℚ_p; the rings are those of §4.1 (Robba rings in a variable T with ϕ(1 + T) = (1 + T)^p). The following categories are canonically equivalent: (a) (ϕ, Γ)-modules over C_K; (b) (ϕ, Γ)-modules over C̃_K; (c) B-pairs over K.
items.note: (a) ⇔ (c) is Berger's theorem [12, Théorème 2.2.7] (external); (b) ⇔ (c) by the same argument. Not planned: the atlas has the étale Robba realization (PG.2) and Berger's (φ, N)-module dictionary (PadicHodgeTheory:P7/berger-dcris-dst-dictionary) but no B-pairs. Route: PadicHodgeTheory P7 or PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology PG.2. 2) and Berger's (φ, N)-module dictionary (PadicHodgeTheory:P7/berger-dcris-dst-dictionary) but no B-pairs; note that the accepted PAPER-DING-25 route 6 routes Berger's B-pairs over a p-adic field (the functor M ↦ W(M) and H^i_{(φ,Γ)}(M) ≅ H^i(G_K, W(M))) to PadicHodgeTheory:P7 (see item 404). The relative/sheaf version stays missing.

items.name: (ϕ, Γ)-modules as equivariant vector bundles on Fargues–Fontaine curves (Theorem 9.5.8(b) ⇔ (d), (c) ⇔ (e))
items.statement: Setting of §9.5: K is a finite extension of ℚ_p; the rings are those of §4.1 (Robba rings in a variable T with ϕ(1 + T) = (1 + T)^p). Let F be the completion of ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞}). The category of (ϕ, Γ)-modules over C̃_K is equivalent to (d) the category of continuous Γ-equivariant vector bundles over FF_{Spa(F ⊗_{ℚ_p} K, (F ⊗_{ℚ_p} K)°)}, and the category of B-pairs over K to (e) the category of continuous G_K-equivariant vector bundles over FF_{Spa(ℂ_p, o_{ℂ_p})}.
items.note: From Theorem 8.7.7. Equivariant bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve are not planned (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals has the curve and its bundles without group actions).

items.name: (ϕ, Γ)-modules over C̃_K as ϕ-modules and B-pairs on Spa(K, o_K) (Theorem 9.5.8(f)–(g))
items.statement: Setting of §9.5: K is a finite extension of ℚ_p; the rings are those of §4.1 (Robba rings in a variable T with ϕ(1 + T) = (1 + T)^p). The category of (ϕ, Γ)-modules over C̃_K is equivalent to (f) the category of ϕ-modules over C̃_{Spa(K,o_K)} and to (g) the category of B-pairs over Spa(K, o_K) (Definition 9.3.11).
items.note: (b) ⇔ (f) by Corollary 9.3.14, (f) ⇔ (g) by Theorem 8.9.6. Not planned.

items.name: Compatibility with Herr's and Liu's (ϕ, Γ)-cohomology (Remark 9.5.9)
items.statement: Setting of §9.5: K is a finite extension of ℚ_p; the rings are those of §4.1 (Robba rings in a variable T with ϕ(1 + T) = (1 + T)^p). Using Remark 9.4.3, the computation of pro-étale cohomology by ϕ-cohomology (Theorems 9.4.2, 9.4.5) agrees, for X = Spa(K, o_K), with the computations of Galois cohomology by classical (ϕ, Γ)-modules of Herr [72, 73] and of the second author [96].
items.note: Stated without proof. Herr's comparison is planned (PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology:PG.3); Liu's Robba-ring cohomology and duality [96] is not a source of the atlas; the agreement with §9.4 is not planned. Liu's Robba-ring cohomology is routed to PG.3/PG.7 by the accepted PAPER-DING-25 route 5 and PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 route 7 ('the Herr complex and Liu's Euler characteristic formula'); the agreement with §9.4 is still not planned

items.name: Herr's complex computes Galois cohomology (black box, [72, 73])
items.statement: For K finite over ℚ_p and D the étale (ϕ, Γ_K)-module of a continuous ℤ_p- or ℚ_p-representation V of G_K, the cohomology of the Herr complex D^Δ → D^Δ ⊕ D^Δ → D^Δ, x ↦ ((ϕ − 1)x, (γ − 1)x), (a, b) ↦ (γ − 1)a − (ϕ − 1)b, is canonically isomorphic to the continuous Galois cohomology H^i(G_K, V) (with Tate duality compatibilities in [73]).
items.note: Stage PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology:PG.3 (nodes PG.3/herr-complex, /herr-differentials; the quasi-isomorphism to continuous cochains is in the stage description).

items.name: The perfectoid property is not local for rational coverings (Remark 3.6.27)
items.statement: (Asserted without proof, adapting Buzzard–Verberkmoes, Proposition 13.) There is an adic Banach algebra (A, A⁺) over a perfectoid field which admits a rational covering by perfectoid algebras but is not perfectoid; this is a counterexample to Scholze's covering conjecture (Perfectoid spaces: a survey, Conjecture 2.16). Whether the conjecture holds when (A, A⁺) is additionally assumed uniform or stably uniform is left open.
items.note: Added by the independent review. The characteristic-0 counterpart of item 121 (Proposition 3.1.16). The remark cites the covering conjecture under the wrong reference (finding E36, in the authors' errata). No stage or packet node states the counterexample.

items.name: Reduced normal affinoids are pro-sheafy (Remark 9.2.14)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 9.2.1: if X = Spa(A, A⁺) with A a reduced normal affinoid algebra over K, then X is pro-sheafy (Definition 9.2.12). The paper only sketches the proof (reduce to A smooth over K by Temkin's resolution of singularities for affinoid algebras, then build imperfect period rings generalizing Andreatta–Brinon) and defers it to a later paper.
items.note: Added by the independent review. A claim whose proof the paper defers; recorded so that nothing relies on it as proved here. No stage or packet node states it.

items.name: ϕ^d-modules over the perfect period sheaves evaluate on perfectoid spaces over X (Remark 9.3.17)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 9.3.2: any ϕ^d-module over one of the sheaves of Definition 9.3.3 other than Ã⁺_X (for which Lemma 9.3.4 fails, finding E85) may be evaluated at any perfectoid space mapping to X, not just at perfectoid subdomains.
items.note: Added by the independent review. The remark says this follows from Lemma 9.3.4, so it inherits the correction of finding E85.

routes.reason: IG.0 constructs the profinite fundamental group of the finite étale site and its equivalence with finite continuous sets; §1.4 of Kedlaya–Liu is the next step on the same objects: Z_p-, isogeny Z_p- and Q_p-local systems on a scheme, their equivalence with continuous representations, the examples separating isogeny Z_p- from Q_p-local systems, and descent of isogeny local systems along finite étale covers (Lemma 1.4.8, with the lattice schemes L_m(T)). Nothing else in the atlas plans étale local systems on schemes, and the perfectoid chapters of the paper use them through Remark 1.4.3. The route also takes Lemma 1.2.3, which identifies R-algebra maps out of a finite étale algebra with idempotents of the tensor product: the representability behind FÉt(R) being a Galois category, which Mathlib does not yet provide. (De Jong’s étale fundamental groups of non-archimedean analytic spaces, item 282, go with the analytic local systems of route 21.)

SF.2 owns the sites and the cohomology of schemes: it says it will "own Zariski, etale, fppf and pro-etale site comparisons", "construct sheaf cohomology" and "distinguish torsion, l-adic and rational coefficients in every export". The pro-étale site of a scheme (Definition 1.4.10, weakly étale morphisms with fpqc coverings and the sheaves F_T of continuous maps) is therefore planned there (item 27, named). Bhatt–Scholze’s theorem that Z_p- and Q_p-local systems are the locally free F_{Z_p}- and F_{Q_p}-modules of finite rank on X_proét (Theorem 1.4.11, item 28) is the l-adic coefficient export of that site. Two standard scheme-cohomology inputs of §§8.7–8.8 belong here too: Čech cohomology of a finite affine cover computes the cohomology of a quasicoherent sheaf on a separated scheme (EGA III 1.4.1, used for Proj(P_R) in Remark 8.7.6; Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge Layer B plans this only for coherent sheaves over a field), and Serre’s cohomological criterion for affineness (proof of Lemma 8.8.8). The extraction had sent items 27–28 to EnhancedDerivedSheaves E2, which only imports the replete-topos results of the same Bhatt–Scholze paper; the review moved them, and moved items 344–345 here from route 23.

PG.0 sets up semilinear ϕ- and Γ-actions and étale ϕ-modules. Kedlaya–Liu §1.5 gives the general conventions (a ϕ-action is an isomorphism ϕ^*M ≅ M, ϕ-cohomology as Ext over S{ϕ}) and a lemma used throughout their later chapters: every finitely generated ϕ-module is a quotient of a finite free one, and finite projective ϕ-modules are direct summands of free ones.

TB.0 constructs the Berkovich spectrum of a Banach algebra and compares strictly affinoid algebras with Huber spectra. Kedlaya–Liu §§2.3–2.4 give that comparison for any Banach ring with a uniform unit: the retraction Spa(A, A^+) → M(A) exhibiting M(A) as the maximal Hausdorff quotient, rational subspaces of M(A) and encircling neighbourhoods, Hausdorff localizations, the surjectivity and openness statements, and the hierarchy of uniform, topologically nilpotent and trivial-spectrum conditions. These are the general form of TB.0’s comparison. Chapter 8 adds the real quotient of a preadic space and its partially proper opens (Definition 8.2.11), and that the real quotient of a taut space is its maximal Hausdorff quotient with partially proper opens again taut (Lemma 8.2.12).

AdicSpacesPartII extends the Tau Ceti AdicSpaces roadmap, which cannot be re-planned; its R0 (morphisms and affinoid products) and R3 (coherent and locally free sheaves) are where these belong. Kedlaya–Liu §§2.2 and 2.5–2.8 supply: norms on finite projective modules and completed tensor products over analytic fields; the parts of the dictionary between adic and rigid affinoids that the packet nodes do not state (Lemma 2.5.4, Proposition 2.5.14, Remark 2.5.22); glueing squares and Kiehl glueing of finite projective modules for arbitrary sheafy rings (Theorem 2.7.7); and projectivity over uniform rings. The non-noetherian vector-bundle theory is what later chapters and the relative Fargues–Fontaine curve use. Corollary 2.5.13 must be taken with A^+ = A° (finding E11). The route also takes the nonarchimedean functional-analysis basics of §§2.1–2.2 that neither library has: strict and (almost) optimal homomorphisms, the unit-ball subring o_A with m_A and κ_A, and the canonical equivalence class of norms on a finite module over a Banach ring (Lemma 2.2.6). Chapter 8 adds Theorem 8.2.22(a)–(b): Tate acyclicity of vector bundles for the adic and finite étale topologies on an arbitrary sheafy affinoid, and the equivalence of finite projective modules with locally free O_X- and O_{X_fét}-modules, beyond the strongly sheafy and perfectoid cases R3 plans. Review: many statements of §§2.2–2.8 are already written as packet nodes of this roadmap and of AdicEtaleGeometry, several citing Kedlaya–Liu by number (R0/banach-completed-tensor-field-exactness, R0/reduced-affinoid-supremum-norm, R1/gerritzen-grauert, R1/classical-points-constructible-density, R3/glueing-square, R3/matrix-factorisation-strict-surjection, R3/sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing, A3/rational-inclusion-reduction, A1/affinoid-system-approximation). Items 48, 83 and 98–102 are therefore planned and stay named here as planned; items 81, 85–87 and 93 (planned at A3, R1 and A1) left the route; items 91, 94 and 95 (clopen sets, finite-stage approximation, Proposition 2.6.4) moved to route 6 with the A1 affinoid-system node. What remains missing: norms on finite projective modules and the canonical norm class over an arbitrary Banach ring (items 45, 49, 50), completed tensor products over analytic fields not of countable type (item 34, 37), the rigid dictionary items 88 and 92, projectivity over uniform rings (item 105), the uniform-ring consequences of Remark 2.8.3 (item 104, with finding E143), and Theorem 8.2.22(a)–(b) beyond the sheafy finite étale case (items 262–263).

A1 owns finite étale algebras over complete Tate pairs and their local-to-global recognition. Kedlaya–Liu prove the inputs for arbitrary adic Banach algebras: henselian pairs from direct limits of Banach rings, full faithfulness and (for fields) essential surjectivity of FÉt(A) → FÉt(Â), the equivalences FÉt(A) ≅ FÉt(completed direct limit) and FÉt(A) ≅ FÉt(A^u), and effective descent of finite étale algebras and étale Z_p-local systems along rational coverings (Theorem 2.6.9, Corollary 2.6.10). Chapter 9 adds the pro-étale site of an arbitrary preadic space in the same generality (§9.1: pro-étale morphisms of pro-objects, X_proét, continuous-map sheaves, local systems and their cohomology) and its structure sheaves (§9.2: O, Ô, Ō and their tilts on perfectoid subdomains, pro-sheafy affinoids, Kiehl glueing for the pro-étale topology, Theorem 9.2.15). The layers plan these only for locally noetherian spaces. Review: items 96 and 97 (Proposition 2.6.8, Theorem 2.6.9) are planned by the packet nodes A1/finite-etale-approximation and A1/finite-etale-rational-descent, which cite them, and stay named here; item 110 (FÉt(A) ≅ FÉt(A^u)) is planned at A4, which A1 names as the owner of the uniformization comparison, and moved to route 15. The route also takes items 91, 94 and 95 (clopen sets and idempotents, the finite-stage behaviour of affinoid systems, Proposition 2.6.4), which the node A1/affinoid-system-approximation plans only in part, and three §§8.2 and 9.2 items the extraction had marked planned in special cases: Lemma 8.2.17(b) for an arbitrary preadic space (item 256; A1/etale-open-map assumes X locally strongly sheafy), Lemma 9.2.5 on the paper’s pro-étale site (item 364; A4 plans only the torsor tower) and Lemma 9.2.8 (item 367; DiamondsAndVStacks D2 plans the analogue on the finer site of Étale cohomology of diamonds).

LI.1 owns the general commutative algebra the campaign needs and does not find in Mathlib, and names finite presentation, flatness, determinants and Fitting ideals among its areas. Kedlaya–Liu §§1.1–1.3 use five such facts that the pinned Mathlib lacks: the equivalence of finite projective with pointwise free of locally constant rank and with Zariski-locally free for finitely generated modules (and the reduced case); Fitting ideals and their characterization of finite projective modules of constant rank; distinct idempotents are not congruent modulo an ideal in the Jacobson radical, and that radical extends along integral maps; and descent of finite projectivity along faithfully flat maps, which Mathlib’s own descent file records as missing (Stacks 058B). Review: the trace-pairing criterion (item 6) is planned by the packet node AdicSpacesPartII:R3/etale-iff-trace-pairing-perfect and left the route.

LI.2 assigns the general compactness and continuity lemmas that later stages consume. Remark 2.3.15(c)–(e) collects the facts about inverse limits of compact Hausdorff spaces that the paper applies to spectra of completed direct limits (Proposition 2.6.4): emptiness of preimages detected at a finite stage, finite open covers and disconnections pulled back from a finite stage. Mathlib has nonemptiness and the clopen statement only for profinite limits; the argument for (e) needs the corrected choice of stage (finding E5).

P5 proves finite étale approximation from the henselian-pair theorem of Gabber–Ramero 5.4.53, and the paper’s Theorem 1.2.8 (planned there) uses its Definition 1.2.6 of a henselian pair by lifting coprime factorizations. Mathlib defines henselian pairs by lifting simple roots and proves the equivalence of the characterizations only for local rings, so the equivalence for pairs (Gabber’s Remark 1.2.7) belongs with P5.

P1 builds perfectoid Tate rings, tilts and marked untilts and names Kedlaya–Liu among its primary sources; §§3.3–3.6 prove the correspondence through Witt-vector norms and primitive elements (Theorems 3.3.7, 3.5.3, 3.6.5). The missing items are the functoriality of the correspondence in the Banach setting, which P1’s equivalence of categories needs: strict maps, completed tensor products and quotients of perfect uniform algebras (Remark 3.1.6), density and strictness under tilting (Lemma 3.4.7, Proposition 3.6.9, Theorem 3.6.17), and completion along a finitely generated ideal containing p (Proposition 3.6.19, whose proof is completed in part II, Theorem 3.3.18(v)). Review: item 163 (Theorem 3.6.17(b), perfectoidness under dense-image maps) is planned by the packet node PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-dense-image-criterion, which cites it, and moved to route 11 as a named planned item. Items 134, 155 and 156 must carry the unit condition z̄₀ ∈ R^× (findings E23 and E114).

P2 defines perfectoid spaces as adic spaces locally modelled on perfectoid pairs and proves their sheaf theorem. Proposition 3.1.16 (a sheafy F_p-algebra covered by perfect uniform ones is perfect; essentially Buzzard–Verberkmoes, Corollary 10) is the positive half of the question whether being perfectoid is local, whose general form (Scholze’s covering conjecture) fails. P2 needs it to know which affinoid objects its local definition admits. Theorems 3.6.14–3.6.15 are the paper’s source for P2’s tilting homeomorphism and sheafiness. Chapter 8 adds the global perfectoid correspondence between perfectoid spaces and pairs (X, I) of a perfect adic space and a primitive ideal sheaf (Theorem 8.3.5). Review: the route also takes Remark 3.6.27 (item 410), the counterexample in characteristic 0 to the covering conjecture, asserted without proof after Buzzard–Verberkmoes; it is the negative half of the question Proposition 3.1.16 answers positively, and it names item 163 (planned at P2).

P3 proves that finite étale algebras over perfectoid rings are perfectoid and that tilting is an equivalence on them, and compares the perfectoid finite étale category with the algebraic one. Kedlaya–Liu prove this by reduction to fields through Witt vectors instead of almost mathematics (Theorems 3.5.6, 3.6.21). The missing inputs are the characteristic-p side (finite étale algebras over a perfect ring are perfect, and FÉt is unchanged by perfection and completed perfection, Lemma 3.1.5 and Theorem 3.1.15), the descent direction (Proposition 3.5.9 with Lemma 3.5.8, Proposition 3.6.22), and Ω_{o_L/o_K} = 0 for perfectoid K (Theorem 3.5.11). Chapter 5 adds the period-ring side of the same equivalence: finite étale algebras over R, W(R), ℛ̃^int_R and the φ^{−1}-equivariant ones over ℛ̃^{int,r}_R correspond, compatibly with the untilt ℛ̃^{int,r}_R/(z) and Theorem 3.6.21 (Proposition 5.5.3, Corollary 5.5.6). The route also names P3’s planned almost purity theorem, which the paper proves from this comparison without toric coordinates (Theorem 5.5.9). Review: items 114 (finite étale algebras over a perfect ring are perfect) and 120(b) are stated by the packet nodes P3/etale-over-perfect-is-perfect and P3/finite-etale-under-completed-perfection; 114 is now planned and stays named, 120 stays missing for its part (a).

PG.1 proves Fontaine’s equivalence between étale ϕ-modules and Galois representations, including finite torsion coefficients, over a field. Kedlaya–Liu §3.2 proves the same equivalence over any perfect F_p-algebra R (Katz’s nonabelian Artin–Schreier–Witt theory): lisse Z/p^n-sheaves on Spec R correspond to finite projective ϕ-modules over W_n(R) (Proposition 3.2.7, with Lemma 3.2.6 and the authors’ corrections), with the Lang-torsor variant for unipotent groups (Proposition 3.2.9), projectivity of ϕ-modules (Lemma 3.2.12, Proposition 3.2.13), and the description of ϕ-invariants by idempotents (Lemma 3.1.3, Corollary 3.1.4). The later chapters use this relative version for local systems on perfectoid spaces. Chapter 8 continues this relative version: étale ℤ_{p^d}-local systems on Spec(R) and on a perfectoid space correspond to ϕ^d-modules over W(R), ℛ̃^int_R and the tilt (Theorems 8.5.3, 8.5.5), isogeny and (c, d)-local systems to globally étale and globally pure ϕ-modules (Theorem 8.5.6, Definition 8.5.7, Theorem 8.5.8 with its completeness hypothesis restored), and étale cohomology to ϕ^d-cohomology (Theorems 8.6.2, 8.6.4).

RF0 constructs W(R) for perfect R with its Teichmüller representatives, universal property and topology, and then the relative period annuli. The annuli are cut out by the Gauss seminorms λ(α^r) on W(R) of Definition 3.3.2, which transport points of M(R) to M(W(R)) (Lemma 3.3.3; Kedlaya, Nonarchimedean geometry of Witt vectors, §4). No layer plans these seminorms for a perfect ring; the Tau Ceti AdicSpaces layer 6 has them only over a perfect field.

A4 constructs a perfectoid pro-finite-étale cover of an analytic Tate pair for diamondification and proves that its uniform completion is perfectoid. Lemma 3.6.26 gives an explicit such cover of any uniform Banach Q_p-algebra by adjoining p-power roots of 1 + t and of unity, with M(B) → M(A) surjective and A → B isometric; it is used for the uniformity of preperfectoid tensor products (Proposition 3.7.3) and in the later chapters on the pro-étale topology. Review: the route also names item 110 (Proposition 2.8.16, FÉt(A) ≅ FÉt(A^u), with Lemmas 2.8.14–2.8.15), planned by the packet node A4/uniform-completion-etale-comparison; Lemmas 2.8.14–2.8.15 and the gaps E112–E113 in their proofs belong with it.

R5 constructs sousperfectoid spaces, the class of non-perfectoid adic spaces that inherit sheafiness from a perfectoid cover. Preperfectoid algebras (Scholze–Weinstein), whose base change to a perfectoid field is perfectoid, are the closest earlier class: Kedlaya–Liu §3.7 proves that they are stably uniform and sheafy, closed under finite étale extension, and (in the strong and relative variants) under completed tensor products. Chapters 8–9 add preperfectoid, strongly preperfectoid and relatively perfectoid spaces (Definition 8.3.1) and the pro-sheafiness of affinoids split into a perfectoid algebra (Remark 9.2.13). Review: the route also takes Remark 9.2.14 (item 411), that reduced normal affinoids are pro-sheafy, which the paper asserts and defers to a later paper.

RF0:annuli builds the rings of the relative period annuli Y_{S,I} of a perfectoid S as rational localizations of Spa W(R⁺), and RF1 glues Y_S over the base and forms X_S = Y_S/φ^ℤ; route 14 already sends the Witt-vector norms λ(α^r) on W(R) to RF0. Kedlaya–Liu §5 build the same rings from those norms (the relative extended Robba rings ℛ̃^{int,r}_R, ℛ̃^{bd,r}_R, ℛ̃^{[s,r]}_R, ℛ̃^r_R, ℛ̃_R and ℛ̃⁺_R) and prove the properties the curve needs: their norms, topologies and functoriality; convexity, units and φ-invariants; restriction maps, intersections and splittings; the sheaf property and Kiehl glueing over Spa(R, R⁺) and over covers of the interval; relative perfectoidness (after R. Rodriguez); the maps between Gel’fand spectra and the radius fibration onto (0, ∞) with the quotient X_R; finite étale functoriality; and reduction modulo a primitive element. Lemma 6.1.4 (generators of a φ^a-bundle generate its global sections) belongs with the glueing statements. The layers do not state these properties: they construct the annuli through adic charts. Under Hypothesis 5.0.1 (kept to the end of the paper) R is a perfect uniform Banach F_p-algebra over an analytic field, that is, a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p, so the paper works in the same generality as the layers’ affinoid perfectoid S; the items are missing because the layers do not state them, not because the paper is more general. The route also names the lifting of rational localizations (Definition 5.3.10–Corollary 5.3.12), which RF0:integral-Y plans. Chapter 8 adds the sheaves of relative period rings on a perfect adic space (Definition 8.3.4) and the étale functoriality of the relative curve FF_X with its morphism of étale topoi FF_X → X (Lemma 8.7.15, Remark 8.7.16). Review: item 200 (glueing over covers of the interval, Theorem 5.3.16 with Lemma 6.1.4’s context) is planned at VB1 and RF0:annuli and stays named.

VB2:ampleness compares bundles on X_S with the Proj curve of RelativeFarguesFontaine RF3 and uses the regular noetherian dimension-one structure of the schematic curve at a geometric point. Kedlaya–Liu §6.3 prove the same comparison (planned there; Under Hypothesis 5.0.1 (kept to the end of the paper) R is a perfect uniform Banach F_p-algebra over an analytic field, that is, a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p, so the paper works in the same generality as the layers’ affinoid perfectoid S; the items are missing because the layers do not state them, not because the paper is more general) and add two facts about the Proj description that the layer does not state: for an analytic field L the rings P[f^{−1}]_0 are Prüfer, so coherent sheaves on Proj(P) correspond to finitely presented φ^a-modules over ℛ̃_L (Theorem 6.3.14); and the norms on the spaces of twisted invariants M(n)^{φ^a} = Γ(Proj P, V(n)) are well defined up to equivalence, which defines continuous group actions on φ^a-modules (Lemma 6.3.17, Definition 6.3.18), used for the relative (φ, Γ)-modules of §9. Chapter 8 adds the ampleness theory on Proj(P_R) that VB2:ampleness uses but plans only for positive twists: Proj(P_R) is covered by two affines with vanishing higher cohomology (Remark 8.7.6), globally ample and ample bundles, O(e) globally ample for e > 0, the cohomological criterion for global ampleness, positive twists of globally étale bundles, and affineness of non-vanishing loci (Definition 8.8.2 to Lemma 8.8.8).

VB4 studies bundles on X_S in families over a perfectoid S: semicontinuity of the Harder–Narasimhan polygon, the relative HN filtration on loci of constant polygon, and slope-zero bundles as local systems (Fargues–Scholze II.2.19–II.2.20). Kedlaya–Liu §7 prove the first two for φ^a-modules over ℛ̃_R by another method, which needs statements the layer does not have: approximation lemmas that spread a good basis at a point of ℳ(R) to a neighbourhood (Lemmas 7.1.1–7.1.2, 7.4.4); pure models, with the openness of the pure and étale loci and the equivalence of pointwise purity with purity (§7.3, Proposition 7.3.6); boundedness of the slope polygon and its local constancy on an open dense set (Proposition 7.4.6, Corollary 7.4.7); splitting off a constant vertex of a varying polygon (Lemma 7.4.8, Theorem 7.4.9); and pointwise detection of H^1 for negative slopes (Corollary 7.4.11). The route also names VB4’s planned semicontinuity and constant-polygon filtration (Theorem 7.4.5, Corollary 7.4.10), which the paper proves in the layer’s generality. Under Hypothesis 5.0.1 (kept to the end of the paper) R is a perfect uniform Banach F_p-algebra over an analytic field, that is, a perfectoid Tate ring of characteristic p, so the paper works in the same generality as the layers’ affinoid perfectoid S; the items are missing because the layers do not state them, not because the paper is more general. Chapter 8 adds purity in families from the local-system side — independence of (c, d), pointwise purity implies purity over ℰ̃_R, ℛ̃^bd_R and ℛ̃_R, descent and detection of purity along surjective maps (Remark 8.5.10, Lemma 8.5.11, Corollaries 8.5.13–8.5.16, Lemma 8.6.3), with the Tate-curve counterexamples (Examples 8.5.17–8.5.18) as acceptance tests — and pointwise ampleness: the slope polygon of a bundle on Proj(P_R), 'ample iff pointwise ample, iff all slopes positive' (Definition 8.8.10 to Theorem 8.8.15), ample bundles on FF_X and L_X (Definition 8.8.17, Lemma 8.8.19). Review: the route also takes Theorem 8.5.12 (item 293), étale (c, d)-ℚ_p-local systems on a perfectoid space and (c, d)-pure φ-modules on its tilt; VB4 plans only c = 0.

D0 builds the spectral-space foundations the diamond roadmaps rest on (locally spectral spaces, spectral maps, the constructible topology, limits of spectral spaces), and this extraction marks §8.1's other statements as planned there. Hochster duality — the inverse spectral topology of Definition 8.1.4, under which a spectral space is again spectral — is the one statement of §8.1 it does not name, and it belongs with them.

H0 constructs torsion local systems, stalks and Čech-to-derived comparisons on analytic adic étale sites, (its stage text says "torsion local systems"; its packet node H0/torsion-local-systems also defines lisse ℤ_ℓ-sheaves, ℓ = p included, on locally strongly sheafy spaces). §8.4 extends this to étale ℚ_p-local systems on an arbitrary preadic space: a surjective étale cover acquires a faithfully finite étale factor near each point (Lemma 8.4.1), ℚ_p-local systems are locally isogeny ℤ_p-local systems and are described by descent data of them (Lemma 8.4.2, Proposition 8.4.6, Corollary 8.4.7), local systems on Spec(A) and on Spa(A, A⁺) agree integrally but not rationally (Remarks 8.4.5, 8.4.8), and extensions of isogeny local systems stay inside the ℚ_p-local systems (Remark 8.4.9). These are statements about local systems on the étale site that H0 constructs. Review: the route also takes Definition 8.4.3 itself (item 275), which the extraction had marked planned at H0 although H0 covers only locally strongly sheafy spaces and the paper allows any preadic space, and de Jong’s étale fundamental groups of non-archimedean analytic spaces (item 282), the input of Definition 8.4.3 and Remark 8.4.8, which had been routed to the scheme-theoretic Galois categories of IG.0.

RF2:untilts constructs the divisor of an untilt on X_S with B⁺_dR as the completion along it, and RF4:vector-bundles proves Beauville–Laszlo patching of bundles along that divisor; this extraction marks Theorem 8.9.6(b)–(c) (vector bundles as relative B-pairs) as planned there. §8.9 supplies the rest of that picture over a base X = Spa(A, A⁺): the complement of the untilt divisor in Proj(P_R) is affine and the divisor is Cartier inside an affine open (Lemma 8.9.3), the relative period rings B_e, B⁺_dR, B_dR of A (Definition 8.9.4), and the comparison of B-pair cohomology with quasicoherent cohomology (Theorem 8.9.6(a), Remark 8.7.6). Conjecture 8.8.20, on zero loci of fibrewise nonzero sections of positive line bundles, is recorded with them as a conjecture, not a target; as printed its part (b) fails for sections with repeated zeros (see sourceIssues).

LI.3 unifies the homological algebra the campaign uses: resolutions, derived functors and sheaves. The proof of Theorem 8.7.13 uses that Yoneda Ext agrees with derived-functor Ext (Hilton–Stammbach IV.9.1). Mathlib has Ext in derived categories and the class of a short exact sequence (ShortComplex.ShortExact.extClass) but not the bijection with Yoneda extension classes. Review: the two scheme-cohomology inputs the extraction also routed here (Čech computation of quasicoherent cohomology on a separated scheme, Serre’s criterion for affineness) moved to route 2, SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2, which owns scheme cohomology.

P8 constructs the relative period sheaves on the analytic pro-étale site. §§9.3–9.4 construct the other family of relative period sheaves on the pro-étale site of an arbitrary adic space over ℚ_p: the Witt-vector sheaves Ã_X, Ã⁺_X, B̃_X and the relative Robba sheaves Ã†, B̃†, C̃ (Definition 9.3.3, with Lemma 9.3.4 corrected), ϕ^d-modules over them with their pure and étale loci (Theorem 9.3.6), and prove that étale ℤ_{p^d}- and ℚ_{p^d}-local systems are étale ϕ^d-modules, vector bundles on FF_X and B-pairs on X (Theorems 9.3.7, 9.3.12, 9.3.13), with the comparison of pro-étale cohomology with ϕ-cohomology and B-pair cohomology (Theorems 9.4.2, 9.4.5). P8 imports the curve side (bundles on FF_X, slope-zero comparison) from VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB1/VB4 and RelativeFarguesFontaine RF1 rather than restating it.

review.reason: The page image of p. 37 reads: "Choose any i ∈ I. By (a), the images V_{1,i}, V_{2,i} of U_1, U_2 in X_i are closed and disjoint; they may thus be covered by disjoint open neighborhoods W_{1,i}, W_{2,i}." The disjointness fails for an arbitrary i. Re-derived counterexample: I = {1 ≤ 2}, X_1 = {pt}, X_2 = {a, b} (discrete), X = lim X_i = {a, b}. U_1 = {a}, U_2 = {b} is a disconnection of X, but both images in X_1 are {pt}. The suggested repair is right. If π_i(U_1) ∩ π_i(U_2) ≠ ∅ for every i, these nonempty compact sets form an inverse system (π_{ij} maps the j-th into the i-th). By (c) its limit has a point x, and x_i ∈ π_i(U_k) for every i and k = 1, 2. A closed subset C of X equals ⋂_i π_i^{-1}(π_i(C)): a point outside C has a basic neighbourhood π_i^{-1}(V) missing C, so its i-th coordinate lies outside π_i(C). Hence x ∈ U_1 ∩ U_2, a contradiction. So some i has disjoint images, and the rest of the argument goes through: the pullbacks of W_{1,j}, W_{2,j} contain U_1 and U_2, are disjoint and cover X, so they equal U_1 and U_2. The conclusion of (e) is correct. The authors' errata (part II Appendix A, kl2.txt 9555–9700) do not mention it, so known: new is right.

review.reason: Page 50 image: 'Corollary 2.5.13. Suppose that A is reduced. Then no two distinct rational subspaces of Spa(A, A+) have the same intersection with Maxspec(A). Proof. We may reduce to the case where A is reduced. By Corollary 2.5.6, we may further reduce to the case A+ = A◦.' Re-derivation: take A = K{T} (reduced) and A^+ = o_K + m_K·o_K{T} = {f ∈ o_K{T} : f mod m_K ∈ k}. This A^+ is open (it contains m_K·A°) and integrally closed: the reduction of an element integral over A^+ lies in k[T] and is integral over k, so it is constant. Let U = {v : v(1) ≤ v(T)} and V = {v : v(T) ≤ 1}; both are rational. On Maxspec(A) (classical points x with |T(x)| ≤ 1), U ∩ Maxspec = U ∩ V ∩ Maxspec = {|T(x)| = 1}. Now let v be the rank-2 point v(Σ a_i T^i) = max_i |a_i|γ^i, with γ > 1 infinitesimal (value group R_{>0} × γ^Z, ordered lexicographically). v is continuous, v(T) = γ > 1, and v(aT^i) = |a|γ^i < 1 for |a| < 1, so v ≤ 1 on A^+ and v ∈ Spa(A, A^+). Then v ∈ U \ V, so U ≠ U ∩ V: two distinct rational subspaces with the same classical points. The printed corollary is therefore false, and the reduction via Corollary 2.5.6 is invalid, because Corollary 2.5.6 concerns the norm, and the passage from A^+ to A° changes Spa. The corrected statement (A^+ = A°) follows from Lemma 2.5.12: apply its one-element case to U ∩ U' ⊆ U and to U ∩ U' ⊆ U'. One flaw in the entry: its correction says '(so that A is reduced)', which is false (see new issue); drop it.

sourceIssues.printed: The source declares four conditions equivalent for a Banach ring A: (a) its norm is equivalent to a power-multiplicative norm; (b) it is equivalent to the spectral seminorm; (c) some c > 0 satisfies |x²| ≥ c|x|² for every x ∈ A; and (d) A◦ is a bounded subring.
sourceIssues.correction: Conditions (a)–(c) are equivalent and define uniform Banach rings. Condition (d) follows from them and implies that the spectral norm defines the same topology, but it does not imply (a)–(c); it does when A has a topologically nilpotent unit z with |z||z^{−1}| = 1.

review.reason: Page 59 image lists (a)–(d) as equivalent, with (d) 'The subring A◦ of A is bounded.' The authors' errata (part II Appendix A, p. 189) record exactly this correction. Re-check of the counterexample: f(x) = |x| for |x| ≤ 1 and |x|(1 + log|x|) for |x| > 1, on a nontrivially valued K. It is a nondecreasing function of |x|, so it is nonarchimedean. It is submultiplicative, since (1 + log a + log b) ≤ (1 + log a)(1 + log b) for a, b ≥ 1 and the mixed cases are easy. Its spectral seminorm lim f(x^n)^{1/n} = |x|, so A° = o_K is bounded and (d) holds. But f(x)/|x| = 1 + log|x| is unbounded, so (a) and (b) fail, and f(x²)/f(x)² → 0 as |x| → ∞, so (c) fails.

review.reason: Lemma 3.5.8 (p. 84, image checked) states only H^1(G, 1+m_K) = 0 for K perfect of char p with G acting faithfully and isometrically. In the proof of 3.5.9 the cocycle f(g) = g(w)/w, w = z_1^{-1}z = z_1^{-1}[z̄] + p, takes values in U = ker(W(o_L)^× → W(κ_L)^×) = 1 + W(m_L), which is not 1+m_L; the lemma as stated does not apply. I re-checked the proposed fix: U → (W(o_L)/p)^× = o_L^× has image 1+m_L and kernel U_1 = U ∩ (1+pW(o_L)), so U/U_1 ≅ 1+m_L; for n ≥ 1, 1+p^n x ∈ U iff x ∈ W(m_L) (p^n x has components x_i^{p^n}), and 1+p^n x ↦ x mod p gives U_n/U_{n+1} ≅ m_L additively (surjective via 1+p^n[a]); H^1(G, m_L) = 0 because a cocycle h with max|h(g)| = δ < 1 is dx with |x| ≤ (1+ε)δ < 1 by the almost-optimal exactness shown in the proof of 3.5.8. U is abelian, the n-th correction lies in U_n ⊂ 1+p^nW(o_L), and W(o_L) is p-adically complete, so the product converges to y. Also needed (implicit in the paper): G acts faithfully and isometrically on L (a g trivial on L is trivial on W(o_L) and hence on E = Frac(W(o_L)/I)). The rest of the proof (G-invariant generator w/y, K = L^G, F' ⊆ E^G = F with [E:F'] = #G = [E:F]) checks out. Not in the errata, so 'new' is right.

review.reason: p. 100 reads '…this conjecture is made in [112, Conjecture 2.16]'; in the v5 bibliography [112] = Scholze, Perfectoid spaces, Publ. IHÉS 116 ([114] = Scholze's ICM 2014 paper). The IHÉS paper's only numbered conjectures are 1.13 and 9.3 (weight-monodromy, checked in arXiv:1111.4914). Scholze, Perfectoid spaces: a survey (arXiv:1303.5948v1), Conjecture 2.16 is exactly the covering conjecture ('(A,A+) complete affinoid K-algebra … cover by rational subsets with O_X(U_i) perfectoid … then A is perfectoid'), checked. The errata cite '[114, Conjecture 2.16]' in the published (Astérisque) numbering and redirect it to part II's [110] = the survey.

review.reason: p. 102: Theorem 3.7.4 asserts first that any rational localization of (A, A^+) is again preperfectoid; the proof ('By Theorem 3.6.14, A_K is stably uniform; by Remark 2.8.12, so is A.') only treats stable uniformity. sourceIssues.printed: For every positive integer a, it identifies the φ^a-fixed elements in both Ẽ_L and R̃_L with the unramified extension of Q_p whose residue field is F_{p^a}.
sourceIssues.correction: … constitute W(L^{φ^a})[p^{−1}], where L^{φ^a} = {x ∈ L : x^{p^a} = x}; this is the unramified extension of Q_p with residue field F_{p^a} exactly when F_{p^a} ⊆ L (for instance when L is algebraically closed).
sourceIssues.reason: Ẽ_L = W(L)[p^{−1}], so its φ^a-invariants are W(L^{φ^a})[p^{−1}], and the proof (via Lemma 4.2.4) shows that R̃_L has the same invariants. Take L the completed perfection of F_p((t)), a perfect analytic field with residue field F_p. An x ∈ L with x^{p²} = x is 0 or a root of unity of order dividing p² − 1, prime to p, and such roots of unity inject into the residue field F_p; so L^{φ²} = F_p and the φ²-invariants of Ẽ_L are Q_p, not Q_{p²}. The uses of the lemma (Proposition 4.3.3, and the proof of Theorem 7.3.7, where L is a completed algebraic closure) take L algebraically closed or a = 1, so they are unaffected.

review.reason: Page 106 image: Hypothesis 4.2.1 says only 'let L be a perfect analytic field of characteristic p with norm α'. An analytic field is complete for a nontrivial multiplicative norm (§2.2, tex l.1497). So L need not be algebraically closed or contain F_{p^a}. Page 108 image, Lemma 4.2.10: 'for any positive integer a, the elements of Ẽ_L and R̃_L fixed by φ^a constitute the unramified extension of Q_p with residue field F_{p^a}'. Re-derivation: φ^a(Σ p^i[x̄_i]) = Σ p^i[x̄_i^{p^a}], and Teichmüller expansions are unique, so (W(L)[1/p])^{φ^a} = W(L^{φ^a})[1/p]. For R̃_L, φ^a-invariance gives λ(α^s)(x) = λ(α^{p^a s})(x), so x is bounded near 0 and lies in R̃^bd_L ⊂ Ẽ_L by Lemma 4.2.4. Conversely W(L^{φ^a}) ⊂ R̃^int_L, since its Teichmüller coordinates have norm ≤ 1. So both invariant rings equal W(L^{φ^a})[1/p]. Counterexample: L = completed perfection of F_p((t)), with residue field F_p. The roots of X^{p²} − X in L are 0 and roots of unity of order prime to p. These reduce injectively into the residue field (X^{p²} − X is separable mod the maximal ideal), so L^{φ²} = F_p and the φ²-invariants are Q_p ≠ Q_{p²}. The case a = 1 (Q_p) is correct. The authors' errata (part II, Appendix A) do not mention it. The uses of the lemma are with L algebraically closed: Proposition 4.3.3 (L′ algebraically closed) and Theorem 7.3.7 (L a completed algebraic closure). So the entry is right as written.

review.reason: The page image p. 162 has the printed text of the first bullet of Definition 8.2.16. Lemma 2.3.13 (p. 34 text: 'the map M(B ⊗̂_A C) → M(B) ×_{M(A)} M(C) is surjective') is about Gel'fand spectra only. For surjectivity of |Y ×_X Z| → |Z| one needs, for every point z ∈ |Z| (possibly of higher rank), some point of the fibre product over z. Lemma 2.3.13 gives such a point only over the maximal (rank-one) generalization of z. Lifting it to z needs an extension of valuations, e.g. a valuation on a compositum of H(y) and H(z) that extends v_z and is ≤ 1 on the image of the + ring. Chevalley extension does this, but the argument is not in the paper. The assertion is true, so this is a citation gap affecting the proof only. The entry's phrasing 'over y and z themselves' asks for more than surjectivity needs (only some point over z is needed), but the gap is the same.

sourceIssues.printed: It asserts a categorical equivalence via the real quotient functor between taut adic spaces over an analytic field K that are locally of finite type and Hausdorff strictly K-analytic spaces as in Berkovich [15]. It describes the former as spaces covered by adic spectra of affinoid K-algebras.
sourceIssues.correction: '(i.e., covered by open subspaces Spa(A, A°) with A an affinoid algebra over K)', that is, locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°) in Huber's sense, as in Huber [79, Proposition 8.3.1].
sourceIssues.reason: An adic spectrum Spa(A, A⁺) of an affinoid algebra A may have any ring of integral elements A⁺ (Hypothesis 2.5.1 allows A⁺ ≠ A°), and the real quotient forgets A⁺. For A = K{T}, Spa(A, A°) and Spa(A, o_K + m_K·A°) (Remark 2.4.9) are affinoid, hence taut, and both have real quotient M(K{T}); they are not isomorphic, since by Lemma 8.2.9 an isomorphism would give a topological automorphism of A carrying A° into the strictly smaller ring o_K + m_K·A°, whereas topological automorphisms preserve the power-bounded subring A°. So the functor is not an equivalence on the category the parenthetical describes.

review.reason: The page image p. 161 reads '… taut adic spaces locally of finite type over an analytic field K (i.e., covered by the adic spectra of affinoid algebras over K) and Hausdorff strictly K-analytic spaces …'. In this paper 'adic spectrum' means Spa(A, A⁺) for any ring of integral elements A⁺ (§2.4), and Remark 2.4.9 itself uses the pair (K{T}, o_K + m_K·o_K{T}). My own re-derivation: A⁺′ = o_K + m_K A° is open (it contains A°° = m_K A°) and integrally closed in A, because an element integral over it lies in A°, and its reduction in A°/A°° = k[T̄] is integral over k, hence constant. Every continuous rank-one valuation on K{T} has |T| ≤ 1 because T is power-bounded, so both X = Spa(A, A°) and X′ = Spa(A, A⁺′) have real quotient M(K{T}) (quotient map by Definition 2.4.8). Both are affinoid, hence qcqs and taut, and both are sheafy since A is strongly noetherian. X ≅ X′ over K would, by Lemma 8.2.9, give a continuous automorphism of A carrying A° into A⁺′ ⊊ A°, which is impossible because automorphisms preserve A°. Fullness fails concretely: id of M(K{T}) does not lift to X′ → X, since T would have to go into A⁺′. So the functor is not fully faithful on the class the parenthetical describes. With Huber's meaning of 'locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°)', A⁺ must contain the integral closure of the image of K°⟨T⟩, which is A°, so the proposition as Huber states it [79, Prop. 8.3.1] is correct. The defect is the gloss, which is part of the statement. The correction is right.

sourceIssues.printed: Any such space is in fact an adic space, and even a stably adic space: thanks to Theorem 3.6.14 and Theorem 3.6.21, the subspaces which are themselves perfect/perfectoid/preperfectoid/strongly preperfectoid/relatively perfectoid form a basis for the étale topology.
sourceIssues.correction: For the preperfectoid classes cite Theorem 3.7.4 and Proposition 3.7.5, and supply the missing steps. (i) For the strongly preperfectoid and relatively perfectoid classes, stability under rational localization and finite étale extension follows by applying Theorems 3.6.14 and 3.6.21 after base change to each perfectoid field, resp. algebra. (ii) Closure of the preperfectoid basis under fibred products: given preperfectoid A1 → A2, A1 → A3 with witnessing perfectoid fields K1, K2, K3, pick a point of M(K1 ⊗̂ K2 ⊗̂ K3), which is nonempty by Lemma 2.3.13. Its residue field contains all three fields, and its completed algebraic closure L is a perfectoid field. Each Ai ⊗̂ L = (Ai ⊗̂ Ki) ⊗̂_{Ki} L is perfectoid, so (A2 ⊗̂_{A1} A3) ⊗̂ L is perfectoid by Proposition 3.6.11 (as corrected in part II, Theorem 3.3.13). Uniformity of A2 ⊗̂_{A1} A3 follows because Q_p → L admits a bounded Q_p-linear retraction, so the tensor product embeds strictly into its uniform base change to L.
sourceIssues.reason: Theorems 3.6.14 and 3.6.21 concern perfectoid algebras (and, through the correspondence, perfect uniform ones). For the other three classes a stable basis needs stability under rational localization, finite étale extension and fibred products over basis objects (Definition 8.2.19). §3.7 proves the first two only for preperfectoid algebras (Theorem 3.7.4, Proposition 3.7.5) and stability under completed tensor products only for the strongly preperfectoid and relatively perfectoid classes (Proposition 3.7.6, whose proof 'does not work in the preperfectoid case because we need to know that the same perfectoid field can be used for all three rings').

review.reason: The page image p. 169 reads 'suppose that A is an integral affinoid algebra over an analytic field. Then on one hand Spec(A) is normal and noetherian, so Zp-ILoc(Spec(A)) = Qp-Loc(Spec(A)) by Remark 1.4.9.' Remark 1.4.9 (p. 23) assumes X normal. My own re-derivation of the nodal example A = K{x,y}/(y² − x²(1+x)), char K ≠ 2, follows. (1) f is y-distinguished of degree 2, so A is free of rank 2 over K{x}. A factorization of f would force (a/x)² = 1+x in K{x}, impossible because 1+x has a simple zero at x = −1 in the disc, so f is prime (K{x,y} is a UFD) and A is a domain. (2) t = y/x satisfies t² = 1+x. If t ∈ A then A → K{t} would be surjective, but A is singular at the maximal ideal (x,y) (f ∈ m², so dim m/m² = 2 > 1), so A is not normal. (3) Following Example 1.4.6, the crosswise double cover B = {(g1,g2) ∈ K{t}² : g1(1) = g2(−1), g2(1) = g1(−1)} is finite étale over A: it is finite, is an isomorphism onto the normalization away from the node, and at the node both complete local rings are K[[u,v]]/(uv). Glueing trivial rank-1 local systems on B by 1 and p across the two nodes gives a Q_p-local system with monodromy p, which is not an isogeny Z_p-local system. Its descent V ⊕ τ*V is then in Qp-Loc(Spec A) but not in Zp-ILoc(Spec A), because pullback preserves Zp-ILoc and V is a direct summand. So the displayed equality is false for integral non-normal A. The remark's conclusion (non-essential-surjectivity) is unaffected, since Example 8.5.17 is smooth.

For an incomplete R_0 the statement fails: take d = 1, c = 0, K the completed perfection of 𝔽_p((t)), R the completed perfection of K⟨T⟩ and R_0 = K[T] with the restricted norm, whose completed direct perfection is R.
