So the unipotent rank-2 isogeny ℤ_p-local system attached to it is a nonsplit extension of ℚ_p by ℚ_p over Spec K[T] that splits over Spec R, and base change from (b) to (a) is not fully faithful. The extension is nonsplit even in the isogeny category: if p^m[tT] = F(y) − y with y ∈ W(K[T]), then y − p^m z ∈ W(R)^{F=1} = ℤ_p (z = −Σ_k [(tT)^{p^k}], Spec R connected), so y = p^m z + a with a ∈ ℤ_p, and the m-th Witt component of y is (±Σ_k (tT)^{p^k})^{p^m} + a_m, which is not a polynomial.

Nontriviality must hold after inverting p (Hom/Ext in the isogeny category are tensored with Q), which the entry's reason does not argue; I checked it: if p^m[tT] = F(y) - y with y in W(K[T]), then y - p^m z lies in W(R)^{F=1} = Z_p (R^{F=1} = F_p, Spec R connected), so y = p^m z + a, a in Z_p; the m-th Witt component of p^m z + a is z_0^{p^m} + a_m with z_0 = ±sum_k (tT)^{p^k} (lower components of p^m z vanish, so the Witt addition polynomial contributes nothing else), which is not a polynomial - contradiction. Hence the rank-2 unipotent isogeny local system is nonsplit over Spec K[T] and split over Spec R: (b)->(a) is not full. With R0 complete (e.g. K<T>) the series converges in R0 itself, consistent with the correction. Not in the authors' errata.

sourceIssues.printed: The remark asserts that, for a Banach ring A over an analytic field K, a semivaluation whose values on A^+ are bounded by 1 is continuous precisely when its restriction to K gives a valuation equivalent to K's norm.

The correct criterion is the one in the preceding sentence: v (bounded by 1 on A^+) is continuous iff for every x with v(x) ≠ 0 there is n with v(ϖ^n) < v(x), ϖ a pseudo-uniformizer of K, i.e. v(ϖ) is cofinal in the value group.
sourceIssues.reason: A = K⟨T⟩, A^+ = o_K⟨T⟩. sourceIssues.printed: For (d), the proof regards perfectness as evident and reduces the task to establishing that R/I has a spectral seminorm which is a norm. It concludes that ȳ = 0 because ȳ has quotient norm below ε.
sourceIssues.correction: Uniformity needs the quotient norm to be equivalent to the spectral seminorm, not just the spectral seminorm to be a norm. The same argument gives this. For any ȳ ∈ R/I and any lift y_n of ȳ^{p^n}, y_n^{p^{−n}} lifts ȳ (I is perfect) and |y_n^{p^{−n}}| = |y_n|^{p^{−n}}. So the quotient norm of ȳ is at most (quotient norm of ȳ^{p^n})^{p^{−n}}, which tends to the spectral seminorm. Hence the quotient norm equals the spectral seminorm and is power-multiplicative.
sourceIssues.reason: A Banach ring whose spectral seminorm is a norm need not be uniform (the spectral norm can be strictly weaker than the Banach norm). As written, the proof shows only that the spectral seminorm is a norm.

sourceIssues.reason: Same formula and same slip as Remark 3.6.16. The factors f_j^{i_j−⌊i_j⌋} and g^{n−Σ(i_j−⌊i_j⌋)} have fractional exponents in [0,1) and [0,n], so their norms are bounded by max{1,|f_j|} and max{1,|g|}^n, not by |f_j| and |g|^n. Example: n = 1, g = 1, h_1 = 0, k = 1 (so h_1f_1 + kg = 1), f_1 = f with 0 < |f| < 1, and y = T^{1/p} (Gauss norm 1). Then z = f^{1/p} and |z| = |f|^{1/p} > |f| = c|y|. Any uniform bound suffices for the surjectivity of S → S', so the remark's conclusion stands. Its final claim, that the quotient norm can be brought within any c > 1 of the spectral norm, also needs the re-chosen h_i, k to have norm tending to 1, which the remark does not address.

sourceIssues.printed: The proof claims convergence of Σ_l a_il to a_i ∈ R̃^∞_R with w = Σ_i a_i v_i, thereby establishing the claim.

sourceIssues.reason: By construction w = Σ_i (Σ_{j<l} b_ij + a_il) v_i for every l, with b_ij ∈ R̃^∞_R and a_il ∈ R̃^{[p^{−l},p^l]}_R. The estimate max_i λ(α^t)(a_{i(l+1)}) ≤ p^{−1} max_i λ(α^t)(a_il) (t ∈ [p^{−l},p^l]) makes a_il → 0 on every fixed [p^{−k},p^k] and makes the b_il (which are within p^{−1}c_l^{−1}λ(α^t)(a_il) of a_il) summable, so the coefficient of v_i is Σ_l b_il. The a_il do not even lie in a common ring, and Σ_l a_il is not the coefficient: already a_{i1} ≈ a_{i0} − b_{i0}, so a_{i0} + a_{i1} + ⋯ ≠ Σ_l b_il in general.

sourceIssues.printed: The source calls A Tate when it has a topologically nilpotent unit z. It claims that each c ∈ (0, 1) gives A a Banach ring structure through α(x) = inf{cⁿ : n ∈ Z, z⁻ⁿx ∈ A0}.
sourceIssues.correction: Require z ∈ A0 (always achievable by replacing z with a power, since z is topologically nilpotent), and A complete and Hausdorff for "Banach ring". Then α is a submultiplicative nonarchimedean norm defining the topology.
sourceIssues.reason: Without z ∈ A0 the set {n : z⁻ⁿx ∈ A0} need not be downward closed, and α can violate the triangle inequality. Take A = ℚ_p(√p), A0 = {a + b√p : a ∈ ℤ_p, b ∈ pℤ_p} (an open bounded subring, a ring of definition), z = √p and c = 1/2. Then α(1) = 1 (n = 0 is allowed), α(√p) = 1/2 (n = 1), but α(1 + √p) = 4: z⁻ⁿ(1 + √p) ∈ A0 only for n ≤ −2 (for n = −1 it is p + √p, whose √p-coefficient 1 is not in pℤ_p). So α(1 + √p) > α(1) + α(√p). Already recorded in the atlas as AdicSpacesPartII/E39 (confirmed by REV-AdicSpacesPartII); the extraction had not listed it. It is separate from the finding on the second paragraph of the same remark.
